The gap between today and ideal is exactly this: substrate and backend logic are landing at a good clip, but each move's packet promised a specific owner-visible artifact (a message, a page field, an endpoint) and about a third of those consumer artifacts are still missing even when the underlying computation is honest.

audits.ideal: A world-class fleet would have: (1) every read endpoint fail per-metric, never per-request — a partial success (6337 real works) is never swallowed into a false global 'unavailable' by one unrelated query's exception; (2) a producer-complete identity spine — the LLM tool contract that creates a booking is generated from (or kept in lockstep with) the same schema the migration defines, so a shipped party/connection model is reachable from the very first live booking, not just from hand-crafted test payloads; (3) a blind-spot registry that grows with every connector-backed module as a matter of course (a lint/CI check flags a module with no declared pattern), so 'what can't this session see' is a fleet-wide guarantee, not a Health-only demo; and (4) every proactive-drafting domain named in a shipped design (finance, email) actually producing prepared actions before the move is marked done, so the approval spine's 'bound to the motivating insight' promise is fleet-wide on day one.
audits.jarvis_gap: Today's fleet ships real substrate and correct mechanisms for all five run-12 moves under audit — attachments truly reach the model as content blocks with fail-closed vision dispatch (move 7), the journey/connection-verdict derivation is genuinely computed and door-gated (move 8), the taste ledger's per-play evidence pipeline and resolver are real and LLM-free (move 10), prepared actions are genuinely parked, dedup'd, and replayed off the approval spine with the reach_out_draft legacy path fully retired (move 11), and the blind-spot/continuity dispatch seams are correctly wired and fail-closed (move 13). But four of five moves stop at the substrate-to-one-producer boundary: travel's new identity model is invisible to the actual booking-ingestion LLM contract so it never populates on real trips; the blind-spot registry only ever names Health; task continuity has zero adopters; and prepared actions has one live producer instead of the three promised. Worse, a genuinely serious live regression sits on the taste tab: the very consumer the packet demanded ('a Taste tab that queries the owner') actively lies to the owner right now, showing a false 'failed to load' / all-zero KPI over a ledger that in fact holds thousands of real rows — the exact 'failure never impersonates health' violation the north star names, just inverted (failure impersonates absence over real health/data).

Live-confirmed: (a) `GET /api/butlers/finance/mcp/tools` returns 105 tools and `schedule_toggle` is NOT among them (only schedule_list/create/update/delete/trigger/costs) while the dashboard toggle button calls it; (b) `GET /api/approvals/actions?limit=50` returns `origin: null` on all 50 rows — no prepared action has ever been produced in the live instance since #4120 shipped; 37/50 are executed `telegram_send_message`; (c) `GET /api/approvals/suggestions` returns 0 rows despite that approval volume; (d) `GET /api/butlers/{health,finance,relationship,travel}/schedules` shows no `continuity` field on the wire and no schedule anywhere declares it; (e) `GET /api/system/insights/delivery-state` = {queued 2, delivered 99}; `GET /api/switchboard/insights` shows 2 pending finance candidates, both `prepared_action_id: null`; (f) `GET /api/attention/ledger/summary` shows 82 attention events across 9 origins with zero `coalesced` and no owner-response dimension. Source-confirmed (exact mechanism read): the dead engagement writer and the resulting budget clamp, the travel prepared-action door gap, sync_schedules clobber of owner edits, the all-args fingerprint basis, the digest channel majority vote, and `LINK_KINDS` excluding prepared actions. Nothing was written; no POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE issued.
audits.jarvis_gap: Run 12 shipped three proactivity substrates — prepared actions (#4120), situation-scoped attention (#4032), and the task-continuity ledger (core_229/#4123) — and one week later the live instance shows zero prepared actions ever parked (`origin` is NULL on every recent approval row), zero schedules opted into continuity anywhere in the roster, and zero fleet cases open. Meanwhile the fleet's proactive bandwidth is silently clamped: `compute_effective_budget` divides by `insight_engagement.engaged`, and the only function that ever sets that column true, `check_and_update_engagement`, has no production caller at all — so every window containing a delivery scores 0% engagement and the daily budget collapses to one insight regardless of the owner's configuration. The owner's single steering verb on the dashboard — pause this recurring task — calls an MCP tool that does not exist, and any owner or butler edit to a TOML-sourced schedule's cron or enabled flag is reverted at the next daemon start without a word. The ideal is a fleet that parks a concrete draft next to every insight it raises, arbitrates channel-and-silence from a policy object the owner can read, learns cadence from what its own last run concluded, and hands the owner a weekly statement of everything it did unasked with one-keystroke verbs to grant, narrow, or forbid. Today the fleet can only tell the owner things; it cannot yet do them, and the owner cannot steer it without opening a database.
audits.ideal: A world-class proactive fleet runs on one loop the owner can see end to end. Every domain butler's deterministic scan produces a typed insight AND, where a bounded remedy exists, a prepared draft parked on the approval spine and bound to that insight by a declared insight→draft mapping with explicit refusal rules (never draft an irreversible external side effect, never draft on evidence older than the producer's own freshness window, never draft a second time for the same real-world identity). The Switchboard arbitrates egress from a readable delivery-posture policy — per (butler, category, urgency) a channel, a hold window, or deliberate silence — and every delivery records which clause decided it. Situation posture governs volume: a draft attached to an open fleet case is silent while the case is calm, pushed when it turns urgent, withdrawn when it closes. Recurring tasks read their own last conclusion and propose their own next cadence, which the owner accepts or overrides in a layer no config sync can clobber. Once a week the fleet renders a receipt: here is what I did unasked, what it cost, how you responded — with three verbs on every line: snooze this reason until a date, never again for this class, or always just do it within this ceiling. The autonomy ladder counts action shapes, not message texts, so it actually reaches its own threshold. Nothing in that loop fabricates a denominator, and no button on it points at a tool that does not exist.

findings.title: Insight budget is permanently clamped to one per day by an engagement writer that has no production caller
findings.detail: `compute_effective_budget` (broker.py:417-465) reduces the configured daily insight budget from the ratio `COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE engaged) / COUNT(*)` over `insight_engagement` in a 14-day window; rate < 0.25 returns 1. `record_engagement_rows` (broker.py:509-529) inserts every delivered candidate with `engaged=FALSE`. The ONLY function that ever flips that column is `check_and_update_engagement` (broker.py:531-580), and a repo-wide grep finds it referenced only inside broker.py's own definition and tests/core/test_engagement_detection.py — no scheduler job, no daemon hook, no scheduled_jobs.py registration. Therefore any 14-day window with at least one delivery yields rate 0.0 and the effective budget is 1, forever, regardless of the owner's configured budget. Live: 99 delivered candidates with 2 still queued. The same dead column also backs `check_total_disengagement_auto_off` (broker.py:663+), which is likewise uncalled — a latent fabricated verdict that would tell the owner "I've paused proactive insights since you haven't found them useful" (broker.py:657-659) on the basis of a signal nothing writes. Shape: an aggregate that denominates nothing, throttling the fleet's entire proactive bandwidth.
findings.evidence: roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py:417-465, :509-529, :531-580, :657-659, :663; live GET /api/system/insights/delivery-state {delivered:99,queued:2}

findings.title: Travel parks a prepared action and links it to the insight, but the broker can never render its door
findings.detail: `_raise_connection_door` (roster/travel/tools/connections.py:256-311) proposes an insight candidate with `prepared_action_id=action_id` and then parks the matching prepared action (`acknowledge_connection_risk`). At delivery, `_resolve_prepared_action_statuses` (broker.py:859-886) looks the origin butler up in `_PREPARED_ACTION_STATUS_QUERIES` (broker.py:811-813), which contains exactly one key: `"relationship"`. For a travel candidate the lookup returns None and the loop `continue`s, so no status entry is recorded; `_decorate_candidate_with_door(c, None)` (broker.py:846-857) then returns both `door=None` and `terminal_line=None` and the message ships as bare text. The owner is told "Your connection at X now looks broken — only N minutes available" with no verb, while a live pending action sits in `pending_actions` waiting for a decision that the digest never offers. The computed prepared_action_id is written, joined, and then discarded at the render seam.

findings.title: Owner and butler edits to a TOML-sourced schedule are silently reverted at every daemon start
findings.detail: `sync_schedules` computes `needs_update` as true when the DB row's cron, dispatch_mode, prompt, job_name, job_args, complexity differ from TOML OR when `not existing["enabled"]` (src/butlers/core/scheduler.py:805-814), and the resulting UPDATE forces `source = 'toml', enabled = true` along with the TOML cron (scheduler.py:854-870, :893-910). `schedule_update` (core_tools/_scheduling.py:161-215) and the generic `_schedule_update` (scheduler.py:2832) write cron/enabled without setting `source='db'` and without any TOML-ownership guard. Consequence: a butler that reschedules itself, or an owner who disables a proactive digest, gets that decision reverted at the next restart with only an INFO log line ("Updated TOML schedule: %s"). There is no owner-visible record that a steering decision was overwritten.

findings.title: The autonomy ladder is unreachable for the fleet's most-approved tool because the fingerprint spans the message body
findings.detail: `fingerprinted_args` (src/butlers/modules/approvals/autonomy_tracker.py:41-78) narrows the fingerprint basis to `ToolMeta.arg_sensitivities` entries marked True, and falls back to ALL arguments when a module declares none. So `telegram_send_message` is fingerprinted over `{chat_id, text}` and every distinct message body is a distinct pattern, which can never accumulate the default 5 approvals the promotion threshold requires (openspec/specs/autonomy-tracker/spec.md, Promotion Threshold Detection). The whole promotion ladder — the system's only path to 'you keep saying yes, shall I just do it?' — is structurally dead for the action shape the owner approves most.

findings.detail: In the digest path, `delivery_channel` is chosen as `Counter(candidate_channels).most_common(1)[0][0]` across the selected candidates (broker.py:1748-1758) and then forced onto every candidate at record time (`channel=delivery_channel or _c.get("channel")`, broker.py:1835, :1921). A Finance candidate that deliberately requested `email` is delivered over telegram whenever two other candidates in the same cycle asked for telegram, and the stored engagement/cooldown row records the overridden channel, not the requested one. Separately, `notify()` resolves an unspecified channel from the target entity's preference and then falls through to the literal `"telegram"` (src/butlers/core_tools/_notifications.py:453-465), with `_SUPPORTED_CHANNELS` limited to telegram|email — there is no 'dashboard only' and no 'hold' channel, so 'do not interrupt me for this' is not expressible anywhere in the egress path.

findings.title: The Switchboard's binding infrastructure contract does not mention proactive egress arbitration at all
findings.detail: The 1943-line insight broker — attention budget, cooldowns, clustering, engagement ratchet, auto-off, prepared-action doors — lives in `roster/switchboard/`, and the attention ledger names it as one of the fleet's two primary owner-egress paths (src/butlers/core/attention_ledger.py:31-40). The Switchboard MANIFESTO lists Responsibilities as ingress ownership, classification, routing execution, durable buffer, agent registry, connector registry and butler-to-staffer routing; the word 'insight' appears exactly once, as an SLA row ('Insight delivery cycle | Daily at 08:00 UTC'), and 'attention', 'budget' and 'proactive' appear nowhere. Under non-negotiable rule 6 the governing document is binding and must describe the service's responsibilities, SLAs, failure modes and escalation; the fleet's entire proactive-egress authority currently sits in a manifesto blind spot, which is why no document names who may decide the owner's attention budget.
findings.evidence: roster/switchboard/MANIFESTO.md:15-40 (Responsibilities, Non-Responsibilities, SLAs); roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py (1943 lines); src/butlers/core/attention_ledger.py:31-40; about/heart-and-soul/vision.md:106-111 (rule 6)
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: a load-bearing subsystem whose governing document never claims it, so no manifesto amendment is triggered when its behavior changes

moves.title: Prepared-action producer contract: five butlers park a draft next to the insight, with declared refusal rules and one status resolver
moves.why: vision.md:130-136 — 'Butlers surface timely, relevant insights without being asked'; the fleet currently only *says*. #4120 shipped the spine and one week later `origin` is NULL on all 50 most recent approval rows (live) — two producers exist, neither has fired in the live instance, and travel's cannot render a door at all (finding 3). Owner-visible payoff within a week: every digest line that has a bounded remedy arrives with 'reply approve' attached, so the check-in the owner meant to send, the subscription they meant to cancel, and the connection they meant to acknowledge become one keystroke instead of one session.
moves.manifesto: Serves Finance ('We will never let a subscription renew without warning you first' — MANIFESTO.md:20), Travel ('never let you miss a check-in window' — MANIFESTO.md:15), Relationship ('never forgetting what matters' — MANIFESTO.md:42), Health (medication supply), Home. The producer contract itself (who may park, and the refusal rules) belongs in a new `openspec/specs/prepared-actions` capability; the requirement that each butler's producer set is manifesto-derived is a per-butler alignment statement, not an amendment.
moves.integration_points: New spec `openspec/specs/prepared-actions/spec.md` (producer contract + refusal rules). `src/butlers/modules/approvals/park.py:126-179` — `park_prepared_action` gains a required `producer` identifier and a `refusal_checked` assertion. New core migration replacing the per-butler SECURITY DEFINER dict at `roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py:811-813` with one `public.resolve_prepared_action_status(butler text, action_id uuid)` and a switchboard-readable grant, so the resolver table stops being an allowlist of one. `roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py:859-886` reads the generic resolver. Producers: `roster/finance/jobs/*` (subscription-renewal → draft `finance_mark_subscription_for_cancellation`; overdue bill → draft `notify` reminder), `roster/travel/tools/connections.py:256-311` (already parks; only needs the resolver), `roster/health/jobs/*` (medication supply below refill threshold → draft `notify` to the owner with the real quantity from #4115), `roster/relationship/jobs/relationship_jobs.py:556-600` (existing template, becomes the reference implementation), `roster/home/jobs` (maintenance-due → draft `ha_call_service` only when the verb is in the reversible allowlist). Read surface: `GET /api/approvals/actions` already exposes `origin`; add `producer` and `insight_id`.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: a deterministic scan derives a candidate, evaluates the refusal rules, parks one draft with a semantic `deduplication_key`, and links it to the candidate via `prepared_action_id`; the digest renders 'approve/dismiss'. Refusal rules (each must be evaluated and the reason recorded on the candidate metadata, never silently skipped): (R1) never park an action whose `reversibility` is irreversible AND whose `blast_radius` is external — those stay informational; (R2) never park when the motivating evidence's `observed_at` is older than the producer's declared freshness window — a stale draft is a fabricated intent; (R3) never park a second draft for the same real-world identity while one is live — enforced by approvals_013's partial unique index, and a UniqueViolation is resolved to the incumbent id, not treated as an error (the pattern already at relationship_jobs.py:585-600); (R4) never park an action whose tool the butler does not itself register (a draft must be executable by its own producer); (R5) never park during an open owner 'never again for this class' directive (move 2). Failure: resolver query raises → status None → plain text plus a recorded resolver-failure reason, never a dead button (broker.py:879-886 already does this; the generic resolver keeps that contract). Concurrency: two scan ticks race → unique index wins, both converge on one id. Idempotence: same key, same week → no new row, no re-notify. Rollback: the producer registry is per-butler config; removing a producer stops new drafts and the nightly orphan sweep expires the live ones.
moves.verification: (1) A behavior test per producer that runs the real scan against a seeded schema and asserts exactly one `pending_actions` row with `origin='prepared'`, the expected `deduplication_key`, and a matching `insight_candidates.prepared_action_id`. (2) A refusal test per rule that seeds the refusing condition and asserts zero rows parked AND a recorded refusal reason on the candidate. (3) An end-to-end broker test that runs `delivery_cycle` with one candidate per producing butler and asserts every one renders a door — the test that would have caught finding 3, and that fails today for travel. (4) A resolver test asserting `public.resolve_prepared_action_status` is callable from the switchboard role for every producing butler's schema.
moves.slice_plan: S1 generic status resolver + broker reads it + travel's existing door starts rendering (this alone closes finding 3 and is shippable in a day). S2 the spec: producer contract, the five refusal rules, the recorded-refusal requirement. S3 Finance producers (subscription cancellation draft, overdue-bill reminder draft) — the manifesto promise with the most direct payoff. S4 Health medication-refill draft. S5 Home maintenance draft behind the reversible-verb allowlist.

moves.title: Owner steering directives: snooze-by-reason, never-again-for-this-class, and a standing 'just do it' grant with a ceiling
moves.why: The pursuit question's second half — 'how does the owner steer proactivity without reading logs?' The honest answer today is: they cannot. The only steering control the dashboard renders is a dead tool (finding 2), the autonomy ladder that would learn 'always just do it' can never reach its own threshold (finding 6, live: 37 approvals of one tool, 0 suggestions), and the sole aggregate steering signal is a column nothing writes (finding 1). Owner-visible payoff within a week: three verbs on every proactive line — 'not until March', 'never for this class', 'always, up to this ceiling' — each with a visible expiry and a visible ceiling.
moves.manifesto: Implies a Switchboard MANIFESTO amendment (finding 9): add a Responsibility 'Proactive egress arbitration — owns the owner's attention budget, the directive ledger, and the standing-autonomy ceiling', with SLAs (a directive takes effect on the next cycle) and failure modes (directive-store unavailable → default to the most conservative posture, never to unrestricted delivery). Rule 6 requires this before the authority can legitimately live there.
moves.integration_points: New `public.proactivity_directives` (id, scope_kind ∈ {producer, category, tool_shape, entity}, scope_key, verb ∈ {snooze, forbid, grant}, reason TEXT NOT NULL, until TIMESTAMPTZ NULL, ceiling JSONB NULL, created_by, created_at, revoked_at) with RLS mirroring `public.fleet_cases`. Consumers: `roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py` eligibility step (a forbidden class never becomes a candidate; a snoozed class is filtered with a recorded reason, not dropped); `src/butlers/modules/approvals/gate.py:770` (a `grant` directive auto-approves within its ceiling and records the directive id on `pending_actions.approval_rule_id`'s sibling column); `src/butlers/modules/approvals/park.py` refusal rule R5. Ceiling shape: `{max_per_week, max_cost_usd, blast_radius_max, reversibility_min, expires_at}` — a grant without an expiry is rejected at write time. Replaces the exact-args promotion ladder as the *primary* path: `openspec/specs/autonomy-tracker/spec.md` and `openspec/specs/autonomy-suggestions/spec.md` are amended so the fingerprint basis for a suggestion is the declared tool shape (tool_name + safety-critical args only, with `arg_sensitivities` newly declared on the telegram and email modules), and a confirmed suggestion writes a `grant` directive with a ceiling rather than an unbounded exact-match rule. API: `GET /api/proactivity/directives`, `POST /api/proactivity/directives`, `DELETE /api/proactivity/directives/{id}` (revoke, never hard delete).
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: owner presses 'never again' on a digest line → a `forbid` directive scoped to that producer+category with the reason captured → the next scan records the candidate as refused-by-directive and the digest says nothing. Grant path: owner presses 'always just do it' → a `grant` with a mandatory ceiling and expiry → the next matching action auto-approves, the execution is recorded against the directive, and the week's counter increments. Ceiling breach: the (N+1)th action in a week, or one exceeding cost/blast-radius/reversibility, falls back to parked-and-pushed with the reason 'grant ceiling reached'. Failure: directive table unreachable → gate defaults to requiring approval and the broker defaults to delivering nothing new for granted classes (fail closed on autonomy, fail closed on volume). Concurrency: two sessions consume the last unit of a weekly ceiling → the counter is incremented inside the gate's decision transaction with a row lock, so exactly one auto-approves. Idempotence: writing the same (scope_kind, scope_key, verb) revokes-and-supersedes rather than stacking. Rollback: revoke restores the prior posture immediately; a revoked grant does not un-execute past actions, and the receipt (move 5) shows what it did while live.
moves.verification: (1) A gate test asserting an action inside the ceiling auto-approves and the (N+1)th parks with reason 'grant ceiling reached'. (2) A gate test asserting a grant with no expiry is rejected at write time. (3) A broker test asserting a forbidden class produces zero candidates and one recorded refusal reason. (4) A fail-closed test: directive store raises → gate requires approval, broker withholds. (5) A concurrency test firing two simultaneous gate decisions against a ceiling of 1 and asserting exactly one auto-approval. (6) A regression test that `telegram_send_message` with two different `text` values and the same `chat_id` produces ONE fingerprint once `arg_sensitivities` is declared — the assertion that fails today.
moves.slice_plan: S1 declare `arg_sensitivities` on the telegram and email modules (unblocks finding 6 with a two-line change plus a test). S2 the directives table + read API + broker `forbid`/`snooze` consumption. S3 the gate's `grant` path with the ceiling and its counter. S4 amend the two autonomy specs so suggestions emit ceiling-bounded grants. S5 the Switchboard manifesto amendment through the improvement-proposal spine (#4125).

moves.title: Delivery posture: channel, hold, and silence as one policy object the owner can read, with a per-delivery deciding clause
moves.why: architecture.md's connectors-as-cost-boundary doctrine says transport is a connector concern, but *whether and where to interrupt* is an owner concern with no home: `notify()` falls through to the literal 'telegram' (finding 7), digests override a producer's requested channel by majority vote, and there is no expressible 'dashboard only' or 'hold until morning'. Owner-visible payoff within a week: 'Home digests go to the dashboard, Finance anomalies to Telegram, everything else waits until 08:00' — written once, readable as a table, and every delivered message can name the clause that routed it.
moves.manifesto: Switchboard amendment (same one as move 2 — 'Proactive egress arbitration'), plus it makes Messenger's stated boundary honest: Messenger 'does not initiate autonomous behavior' (roster/messenger/MANIFESTO.md:27), so the decision of *where* must be owned upstream and named, not defaulted to a literal in a core tool.
moves.integration_points: New `public.delivery_posture` (id, match JSONB over {origin_butler, category, priority_min, blast_radius}, channel ∈ {telegram, email, dashboard, hold}, hold_until_local_time, precedence INT, created_at, revoked_at). Consumers: `src/butlers/core_tools/_notifications.py:453-465` replaces the `or "telegram"` fallback with a posture resolution that returns a (channel, reason) pair; `roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py:1748-1758` replaces the majority vote with per-candidate posture resolution and splits a cycle into per-channel deliveries rather than forcing one; `src/butlers/core/attention_ledger.py` `record_attention_event` gains `posture_rule_id` so every row names the clause that decided it, and the existing 'deferred' outcome gains reason 'posture_hold' distinct from quiet hours. New channel: `dashboard` is a terminal posture that records `delivered` with channel='dashboard' and surfaces on the attention/timeline read path — the fleet's first way to say something without interrupting. API: `GET /api/proactivity/posture` returns the ordered rule table; `GET /api/attention/ledger` rows gain the deciding rule.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: a Home energy digest matches a posture rule routing it to `dashboard`; the ledger records delivered/dashboard/rule-id; no push fires. Hold: a low-priority Finance note at 23:00 matches `hold until 08:00 local`; ledger records deferred with reason 'posture_hold' and the retry envelope fires at 08:00. No rule matches: the fleet-default rule (precedence lowest, always present, seeded by migration) applies and is named in the ledger — there is never an unattributed channel choice. Failure: posture table unreachable → resolve to the seeded default rule and record `posture_rule_id=NULL, reason='posture_unavailable'`, so the ledger shows the degradation instead of impersonating a decision. Concurrency: two rules match → highest precedence wins, ties broken by lowest id, deterministic. Idempotence: a held notification retried at 08:00 re-resolves posture and does not double-deliver (the delivery envelope's existing dedup key holds). Rollback: revoke a rule; the default rule can never be revoked.
moves.verification: (1) A `notify()` test asserting that with no matching rule the channel comes from the seeded default AND the ledger row names it — the assertion that fails today, where the channel comes from a string literal. (2) A broker test with three candidates requesting {email, telegram, telegram} asserting two deliveries on two channels, not one telegram digest — the current majority-vote behavior fails it. (3) A hold test asserting outcome 'deferred' with reason 'posture_hold', distinct from a quiet-hours defer. (4) A degraded test asserting posture-store failure records `posture_unavailable` rather than a fabricated rule id. (5) A dashboard-channel test asserting the message is readable on the attention read path and no push was attempted.
moves.slice_plan: S1 the table + seeded default rule + `notify()` resolution with the reason on the ledger (kills the hardcoded literal). S2 broker per-candidate resolution replacing the majority vote. S3 the `dashboard` terminal channel and its read surface. S4 the `hold` posture riding the existing deferred-notification retry envelope. S5 the owner-readable rule table on the dashboard.

moves.title: Cadence sovereignty: recurring tasks propose their own next cadence from their last conclusion, and no config sync overwrites the owner
moves.why: core_229 shipped a ledger that lets a recurring task remember what it concluded, and one week later not one schedule in the roster opts in (finding 5) — the memory has no consumer and the read API does not even expose it. Meanwhile any cadence the owner or a butler does set on a TOML task is reverted at the next daemon start with an INFO log (finding 4). Owner-visible payoff within a week: the weekly relationship-maintenance run that concluded 'nothing changed, three weeks running' proposes going fortnightly, the owner accepts with one keystroke, and the change survives a restart.
moves.manifesto: Serves every domain manifesto's cadence promises (Relationship's 'life moves in cycles' framing, MANIFESTO.md:21-29; Finance's 'we will not let overdue obligations pile up silently', MANIFESTO.md:20) and enforces vision.md rule 5's own distinction: identity lives in git, *operational tuning* lives in the database. Today the sync violates that rule in the DB's direction — git overwrites operational tuning. No amendment needed; this is rule 5 enforced.
moves.integration_points: `src/butlers/core/scheduler.py:805-814, :854-870, :893-910` — `sync_schedules` learns an override layer: new `scheduled_tasks.owner_override JSONB` (keys: cron, enabled, set_by, set_at, reason). A field present in `owner_override` is excluded from the `needs_update` comparison and preserved by the UPDATE; the TOML value is still stored as `toml_cron` so the surface can show 'git says 0 9 * * 1, you say 0 9 */14 * 1'. `src/butlers/core_tools/_scheduling.py:161` — `schedule_update` writes through `owner_override` when the row's source is 'toml'. Register the missing `schedule_toggle` core tool in the same file (closing finding 2) writing `owner_override.enabled`. New core tool `propose_cadence(task_name, cron, rationale)` alongside `carry_forward` in `src/butlers/core_tools/_continuity.py`, writing a structured `cadence_proposal` column on `public.task_continuity` (core_229 successor migration) — the daemon never applies it; it parks a prepared action (move 1's spine) for the owner. Opt in `continuity = true` on the fleet's narrative recurring prompts in each `roster/*/butler.toml` (relationship-maintenance, weekly-health-summary, monthly-finance-digest, destination-outlook, trip-document-expiry). Expose `continuity`, `owner_override` and the live carry-forward on `GET /api/butlers/{name}/schedules`.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: a continuity task's run calls `carry_forward` plus `propose_cadence('0 9 */14 * 1', 'no new signal in three consecutive runs')`; a prepared action is parked; the owner approves; `owner_override.cron` is written; the next `sync_schedules` leaves it alone and the schedules surface shows both the git value and the override with its reason. Failure: `propose_cadence` with an uncronable expression → structured error, no row written, the task's `carry_forward` still lands. Concurrency: two runs of the same task propose different cadences → the prepared action's `deduplication_key` is `(butler, task_name, iso_week)`, so the second no-ops onto the first. Idempotence: re-approving an already-applied proposal is a no-op returning the same override. Rollback: clearing `owner_override.cron` returns the task to git authority at the next sync — and unlike today, that reversion is an explicit owner act with a record, not a restart side effect. Restart: an override survives; an unapplied proposal survives as a pending prepared action.
moves.verification: (1) A `sync_schedules` test that sets `owner_override.enabled=false` on a TOML row, runs sync, and asserts the row is still disabled — fails today (scheduler.py:813 forces it back on). (2) The same for cron. (3) A `schedule_toggle` tool test asserting the tool is registered and flips `owner_override.enabled` — the tool does not exist today, so `GET /api/butlers/{name}/mcp/tools` currently omits it. (4) A scheduler dispatch test asserting a `continuity=true` task receives the prior conclusion block AND that a task whose last run called `propose_cadence` has exactly one prepared action parked. (5) A schedules-API contract test asserting `continuity` and `owner_override` are on the wire.
moves.slice_plan: S1 register `schedule_toggle` and make the dashboard button work (finding 2, one day). S2 the `owner_override` column and the sync-respects-override change (finding 4). S3 opt five narrative recurring tasks into `continuity=true` and expose the flag on the read API (finding 5). S4 `propose_cadence` + the structured column + the prepared-action door. S5 the schedules surface showing git-value vs override-with-reason.

moves.title: The unasked receipt: a weekly statement of what the fleet did on its own, what it cost, and how the owner responded
moves.why: vision.md:120-137 measures success as 'the amount of mental labor the system reliably absorbs' — and there is no instrument that measures it. The attention ledger records 82 egress decisions across nine origins (live) with zero owner-response dimension; `insight_engagement.engaged` is written by nobody (finding 1); `pending_actions` knows decisions but not what they were worth. Owner-visible payoff within a week: one page that says 'this week I acted 14 times unasked, cost $0.83, you kept 12 and reversed 2' — with move 2's three verbs on every line, so reading the receipt IS the steering.
moves.manifesto: Switchboard amendment as in move 2 (the arbiter must be accountable for what it arbitrated). Distinct from bu-6jv4m.6 'proactive calm receipts', which is a *producer-side* scan-run and evidence-freshness registry (did every detector run before silence); this is the *owner-side* consequence ledger (what reached me, what it cost, what I did about it). They join on the candidate id but neither substitutes for the other.
moves.integration_points: New read-only aggregate `public.v_proactive_week` unioning: `public.attention_ledger` (egress decisions, outcome, reason, posture rule from move 3), `public.insight_candidates` (delivered/expired/filtered with reason), `pending_actions WHERE origin='prepared'` (parked/approved/rejected/expired plus `decided_by` and time-to-decision), auto-approved rows carrying a move-2 grant id, and per-action cost joined from the run-12 cache-honest spend ledger via `session_id`. Replaces the dead `insight_engagement.engaged` denominator with a real response outcome: a delivered line's response is one of {acted, dismissed, ignored, expired-unseen} derived from the prepared action's decision or the absence of one — which retires `check_and_update_engagement` (broker.py:531-580) rather than wiring it, and re-bases `compute_effective_budget` (broker.py:417-465) on the honest ratio. API `GET /api/proactivity/receipt?week=`. Surface: a weekly Dispatch page, keyboard-first, each row a door to move 2's verbs and to the originating session evidence.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: Sunday's receipt lists every proactive act grouped by producer, each with cost, channel, deciding posture clause, and owner response; totals are honest sums, and a producer with zero acts renders 'nothing this week' rather than being omitted. Failure: the spend join is unavailable → cost renders as 'unavailable', never as 0.00, and the total is labelled partial — a missing cost must never impersonate a free action. Missing response: an action still pending at week close is 'undecided', counted in its own bucket, never folded into 'ignored'. Concurrency: the view is read-only; a decision landing mid-render shifts the row on next read and no state is written. Idempotence: the receipt is derived, not materialized — regenerating last week's receipt after a late decision yields the corrected numbers with an 'amended' marker. Rollback: it is a view plus a page; dropping it changes no behavior, except that the budget re-base in `compute_effective_budget` must land with its own migration and test.
moves.verification: (1) A view test seeding one delivered-and-acted, one delivered-and-ignored, one parked-and-expired, one auto-approved-under-grant, and asserting each lands in the right bucket exactly once. (2) A denominator test asserting `compute_effective_budget` returns the configured budget when every delivery was acted upon — which fails today for every input (finding 1). (3) A degraded test asserting a missing spend join renders 'unavailable' and marks the total partial. (4) A Playwright keyboard test asserting j/k traversal and that each row's steering verb reaches the move-2 write path. (5) An amendment test asserting a decision recorded after week close changes the regenerated receipt and marks it amended.
moves.slice_plan: S1 the view + `GET /api/proactivity/receipt` (read-only, no behavior change). S2 re-base `compute_effective_budget` on the real response ratio and delete the dead engagement writer and the uncalled auto-off (finding 1). S3 the weekly page. S4 wire move-2 verbs onto each row. S5 the amended-receipt marker.

moves.title: Case-scoped drafts: a situation's posture decides whether its prepared actions stay silent, get pushed, or execute
moves.why: Run 12 shipped fleet cases with situation-scoped attention (#4032) and prepared actions (#4120) in the same release, and `LINK_KINDS` has no edge between them (finding 8). Today a prepared action is unconditionally silent by design (park.py:126-152) — correct for a routine reach-out draft, wrong for a draft attached to a situation that just escalated. Owner-visible payoff within a week: when a situation turns urgent, the drafts it already prepared surface with it instead of waiting for the next digest; when the owner closes the situation, its stale drafts disappear on their own instead of expiring as clutter.
moves.manifesto: Serves the case-owning butlers' promises directly (Travel's 'alert you to delays and gate changes' — MANIFESTO.md:15; Finance's 'we will not let overdue obligations pile up silently' — MANIFESTO.md:20) and belongs under RFC 0032's existing authority; no amendment needed beyond adding the link kind to the spec.
moves.integration_points: `src/butlers/core/fleet_cases.py:56` — add `"prepared_action"` to `LINK_KINDS`; `write_case_link` (fleet_cases.py:228-298) validates the ref against `pending_actions.id WHERE origin='prepared'`. `close_case` (fleet_cases.py:354) withdraws the case's still-pending drafts with `decided_by='system:case-closed'` (the withdrawal pattern already at roster/travel/tools/connections.py:315-325). `evaluate_case_attention` (fleet_cases.py:411-497) gains a second consequence: when posture is urgent, its linked drafts are promoted from silent to pushed by calling `emit_approval_push` (src/butlers/modules/approvals/notifications.py) once per draft, deduped by the case's existing attention dedup key so an urgent case cannot push the same draft twice. `park_prepared_action` (park.py:126-179) takes an optional `case_id` and writes the link in the same transaction as the insert. RFC 0032 and `openspec/specs/` updated with the fourth link kind and the posture→draft consequence table.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: a producer parks a draft with `case_id`; while posture is calm the draft is silent and reachable only through the digest door; posture flips to urgent → one push per linked draft with the case's correlation key as context; owner closes the case → remaining pending drafts are withdrawn with a system decider and the withdrawal is visible on the case's evidence trail. Failure: `emit_approval_push` fails for one draft → recorded on the attention ledger as `source='approvals', outcome='failed'` (core_227 already supports that source) and the other drafts still push. Concurrency: the TOCTOU fix already landed on `evaluate_case_attention` (#4097) covers the promotion path; the per-draft push is guarded by the same dedup key so two concurrent evaluations promote once. Idempotence: promoting an already-pushed draft is a no-op; withdrawing an already-decided draft is a no-op. Rollback: remove the link kind — drafts revert to unconditionally silent, which is today's behavior, and no data is lost.
moves.verification: (1) A fleet-case test asserting `write_case_link(link_kind='prepared_action')` is accepted and that a non-prepared pending action is rejected. (2) A close test asserting every still-pending linked draft is withdrawn with `decided_by='system:case-closed'` and that an already-decided one is untouched. (3) A posture test asserting exactly one push per linked draft on the calm→urgent transition, and zero on a second evaluation at the same posture. (4) A failure test asserting a failed push records `source='approvals', outcome='failed'` on the attention ledger and does not block the sibling pushes.
moves.slice_plan: S1 the link kind + validation + spec update. S2 `park_prepared_action(case_id=...)` writing the link transactionally. S3 close-withdraws-drafts. S4 posture-promotes-drafts with the deduped push. S5 the case read surface listing its drafts alongside its evidence.

findings.title: Finance and Relationship expose ZERO cross-butler tools: git identity says delegation/domain_events/fleet_cases, the running daemon registered none, and the drop is silent
findings.detail: roster/finance/butler.toml:11-22 declares core_groups including "delegation", "domain_events", "fleet_cases"; roster/relationship/butler.toml:11-21 declares "delegation" and "fleet_cases". The live runtime_config rows for both butlers were seeded 2026-04-07 with only [infra,state,scheduling,sessions,notifications,media,temporal] and never updated, and per vision.md rule 5 the DB wins. src/butlers/daemon.py:1254-1282: when core_groups is a list, `_core_tool(group)` returns `lambda fn: fn` for any group not in it — the tool is silently not registered, with no warning (the only warning path is name-gated groups, daemon.py:1267-1277). Live: GET /api/butlers/finance/mcp/tools returns 105 tools with no delegate_ask/delegate_receive/delegate_answer/receive_domain_event/*_case*; relationship 125 tools, same absence; health 160 tools with all of them present. Consequence: the fleet's money endpoint and its people endpoint cannot be asked a question, cannot receive a domain event, and cannot contribute case evidence. This single row of stale operational config explains every other cross-butler symptom below. Nothing anywhere compares seeded core_groups against the git identity that is supposed to define them.
findings.evidence: live GET /api/butlers/{finance,relationship,health}/mcp/tools; live GET /api/butlers/finance/runtime-config (core_groups=7 groups, seeded_at 2026-04-07T18:27:46Z, updated_at identical); roster/finance/butler.toml:11-22; roster/relationship/butler.toml:11-21; src/butlers/daemon.py:1251-1282; about/heart-and-soul/vision.md:92-101
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: git-declared identity silently narrowed by frozen operational config — the capability exists in the repo, never in the process, and no surface compares the two

findings.title: Five of the six domain-event deliveries that have EVER happened are failed_permanent on attempt 1, three of them after the bead that 'closed' the failure by pinning it as a regression test
findings.detail: Live GET /api/domain-events/deliveries (whole table, 6 rows): travel.trip_booked -> finance failed_permanent x5 (2026-08-04 x2, 2026-09-07 x3), attempt_count=1, error "receive_domain_event on 'finance' returned an incomplete success payload: None"; travel.trip_active -> health delivered x1 (2026-07-26). src/butlers/core_tools/_domain_events.py:344-380 classifies a route envelope whose result lacks task_id/task_name as non-retryable and terminal — correct honesty, wrong conclusion here: the target simply does not expose the tool (finding 1). bu-6jv4m.8 closed 2026-08-25 having added tests/core_tools/test_domain_event_incomplete_receiver.py to pin the shape, explicitly deferring recovery as "a separate owner-authorized action"; three fresh failures on 2026-09-07 prove the cause was never removed. No retry, no replay path, no owner-facing signal — travel.trip_booked has never once reached Finance, so no trip has ever produced a budget consequence.
findings.evidence: live GET /api/domain-events/deliveries?limit=200 (6 rows total); live GET /api/domain-events/subscriptions (2 active); src/butlers/core_tools/_domain_events.py:344-380; tests/core_tools/test_domain_event_incomplete_receiver.py:1-15; bd show bu-6jv4m.8 (CLOSED 2026-08-25)
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: a defect closed by pinning its shape in a test while the live cause keeps producing new instances

findings.title: The delegation dispatcher treats an empty route result as a successful dispatch, so the fleet's only cross-butler question has claimed 'the target acknowledged and scheduled itself to answer' for 26 days about a tool the target never exposed
findings.detail: src/butlers/core_tools/_delegation.py:77-95 classifies a route() envelope as failure only on a truthy `error` key; `{"result": None}` — the exact envelope the domain-event path at _domain_events.py:344-355 rejects as an incomplete success — is accepted, so dispatch_delegated_ask (_delegation.py:213-250) writes status='routed'. Two consumers of the same route primitive disagree about what a null result means; one fabricates. Live: /api/delegation/ledger holds exactly one row for all time — relationship -> finance, 2026-08-17, 'What is the household's typical gift or discretionary-budget guidance for a birthday like this?', status routed, answer null, wake_state not_applicable. Finance has no delegate_receive registered (finding 1), so no session was ever scheduled; the ledger's own tool docstring (_delegation.py:298-302) tells the asking butler routed means 'the target acknowledged and scheduled itself to answer'. Distinct from the known stalled-delegation sweep (bu-2jtfw.5): a sweep would close a lie, not stop it being written.
findings.evidence: live GET /api/delegation/ledger?limit=5 (total=1, asked_at 2026-08-17T23:06:41Z, status routed); src/butlers/core_tools/_delegation.py:77-95, 213-250, 296-302; src/butlers/core_tools/_domain_events.py:344-355
findings.taxonomy_shape: Failure impersonating health — a dispatch that reached nothing is recorded, and read back, as an acknowledged handoff

findings.title: Route-level capability checking exists but can never protect a cross-butler call: registry capabilities are derived from module names only
findings.detail: route() accepts required_capability and resolve_routing_target refuses with "Butler 'X' does not advertise required capability 'Y'" (roster/switchboard/tools/registry/registry.py:480-483, _supports_capability at :155). But capabilities are computed as `sorted(set(modules) | {"trigger"})` (registry.py:580) — module names, never registered core-tool groups. Live registry: finance advertises ['calendar','finance','memory','trigger']. No caller of route() for delegate_receive, receive_domain_event, or the fleet-case writes passes required_capability at all, and even if one did there is no capability string that corresponds to a core group. The honest refusal machinery is one field away from working and is wired to the wrong source.
findings.evidence: roster/switchboard/tools/registry/registry.py:155, 480-483, 570-590; live GET /api/switchboard/registry; src/butlers/core_tools/_delegation.py:213-224 (no required_capability); src/butlers/core_tools/_domain_events.py (fan-out dispatch, same)
findings.taxonomy_shape: Gate that is metadata — the eligibility check denominates modules, not the tool actually being called

findings.title: Every session's context preamble labels a machine inference as the owner's 'explicit' statement, and strips the writer and the age
findings.detail: context_bus.py:530-538 maps confidence>=1.0 to the literal label "explicit" — the word roster/general/modules/tools.py:110-118 reserves for the owner's own stated context ("Confidence is 1.0 (explicit)"). Deterministic producers write confidence=1.0 from keyword classification of a calendar title (src/butlers/jobs/context_producers.py:176-183, classify_calendar_signal on row['title']), from a trip row (:475-482), and from home presence (:756-761). format_context_preamble (context_bus.py:541-570) renders only `signal_type (value, label)` — no set_by_butler, no set_at, no expires_at. So every spawned session across the fleet reads `[User Context: meeting (Standup, explicit)]` and cannot distinguish the owner saying 'I am in a meeting' from a title-string guess, nor a signal set 30 seconds ago from one 23 hours into a 24-hour TTL.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/context_bus.py:530-538, 541-570; src/butlers/jobs/context_producers.py:176-183, 475-482, 756-761; roster/general/modules/tools.py:110-118; openspec/specs/context-bus/spec.md:10 (no provenance column), :167 (preamble requirement)
findings.taxonomy_shape: Writer's clock impersonating the world's clock, plus an inference wearing the owner's voice

findings.title: Two butlers can propose the same hour of the owner's life and neither the proposers nor the conflict policy can see it
findings.detail: calendar_event_proposals is a per-butler-schema staging table (alembic/versions/core/core_136_calendar_event_proposals.py:1-7) and lifestyle, health and relationship each own one (roster/{lifestyle,health,relationship}/butler.toml [modules.calendar]). _propose_event (src/butlers/modules/calendar.py:5513-5570) inserts with no overlap query of any kind — the only conflict handling in the module, find_conflicts (calendar.py:2900-2939), asks the Google freeBusy API, i.e. it denominates provider-committed events only and is blind to every pending proposal, including the butler's own. The cross-schema union exists only in the dashboard read path (src/butlers/api/read_models/calendar_workspace_v1.py:1118-1195, fan_out_with_status over butlers_with_module('calendar')). Result: Health can propose a physio slot and Lifestyle a dinner in the same hour, both arrive at the owner as accept-able proposals with the 'suggest' conflict policy reporting nothing.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/calendar.py:5513-5570, 2900-2939; alembic/versions/core/core_136_calendar_event_proposals.py:1-7; src/butlers/api/read_models/calendar_workspace_v1.py:1118-1195; roster/health/butler.toml:72-77, roster/lifestyle/butler.toml:55-60
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: contention on a scarce owner resource with no register — every claimant computes against a denominator that excludes the other claimants

findings.title: travel.trip_active claims to 'front-load medication prep' but cannot fire before the trip has already begun
findings.detail: src/butlers/jobs/context_producers.py:451-455 documents Health's seeded subscription as front-loading medication prep, and core_189_domain_event_bus_slice2_seed.py:33 is the seed. The publishing query (:459-470) selects only trips with status='active' or whose [start_date, end_date] window contains current_date, and the publish is memoized per trip id (:498-521). There is no lead-time path and no anticipatory event type anywhere in the bus, so the earliest Health can hear about a trip is day 0 — after the pharmacy visit that would have mattered. The bus has only a present tense.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/jobs/context_producers.py:451-455, 459-470, 487-521; alembic/versions/core/core_189_domain_event_bus_slice2_seed.py:33
findings.taxonomy_shape: Rendered clause not true — the contract's stated purpose is unreachable by its own trigger

findings.title: Fleet case evidence refs are documented as 'something a reader can open' but there is no grammar, no butler qualification, and no resolver in the codebase
findings.detail: contribute_case_evidence's ref parameter (src/butlers/core_tools/_fleet_cases.py:221-231) is an unconstrained string described as "a session id, a task name ... Something a reader can open"; core/fleet_cases.py:166-172 validates only non-emptiness. A session id carries no schema, so the same string means a different row in each of ten butler schemas, and grep finds no URI grammar or dereference helper anywhere (no butler://, bref, resolve_ref outside relationship's local entity lookup at roster/relationship/tools/relationship_lookup.py:91). GET /api/switchboard/cases/{id} (roster/switchboard/api/router.py:634-700) returns those strings verbatim. Only the three reserved LINK_KINDS values (core/fleet_cases.py:56-58) are resolvable, and only because their table is named in the tool description.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core_tools/_fleet_cases.py:221-231; src/butlers/core/fleet_cases.py:56-58, 166-172; roster/switchboard/api/router.py:634-700
findings.taxonomy_shape: The last hop has no door — the shared object cites evidence in a form nothing can open

findings.title: Zero fleet cases exist after all seven RFC 0032 slices landed, and no butler is told to open one
findings.detail: Live GET /api/switchboard/cases returns an empty page. All seven slices are marked landed (about/legends-and-lore/rfcs/0032-fleet-case-file.md:90-95) and the consumer PRs shipped (#4024/#4031/#4032/#4033/#4034). But grep across src/ and roster/ finds no deterministic caller of open_case/contribute_case_evidence outside the tool layer itself, and no butler.toml prompt, AGENTS.md, or MANIFESTO.md mentions the case file. Two of the ten butlers cannot call the tools at all (finding 1). The situation object is real in Postgres and has never existed in the owner's life.
findings.evidence: live GET /api/switchboard/cases?limit=5 (data: []); about/legends-and-lore/rfcs/0032-fleet-case-file.md:90-95; grep open_case|contribute_case_evidence over src/ roster/ (only core/fleet_cases.py, core_tools/_fleet_cases.py, _dispatcher.py:58-59)
findings.taxonomy_shape: Substrate shipped / consumer never — measured at the live read side

findings.title: The context bus vocabulary and its write permissions are compiled-in core constants, so no butler can introduce a shared signal without a core change, and the owner has no read or write surface at all
findings.detail: ContextSignal (src/butlers/context_bus.py:21-36), _WRITE_PERMISSIONS (:74-87) and _TTL_CONFIG (:93-107) are Python literals in core, mirrored as normative text in openspec/specs/context-bus/spec.md:25-66. Rule 2 says modules only add tools, so a butler that learns something new about the owner's state has no path to the shared bus short of a core edit plus a spec amendment. The live API has no /api/context endpoint of any kind (513 paths in the OpenAPI document, none matching context), so the owner cannot see what the fleet believes about them, nor declare anything except by messaging the general butler.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/context_bus.py:21-36, 74-87, 93-107; openspec/specs/context-bus/spec.md:25-66; live GET /openapi.json (no /api/context*)
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: shared vocabulary owned by core with no extension seam and no owner-facing mirror

audits.ideal: The fleet handles a situation together the way a good household staff does: one situation object that any specialist may open and every specialist may join; a shared vocabulary of typed questions and typed answers, so Travel asks Finance "how much is left for this trip?" and gets {amount, currency, as_of, basis: [claim ids], or a named refusal} rather than a paragraph; a register for every scarce thing the owner has exactly one of — an hour, an inbox thread, a reply, a decision — so two butlers contend in the register and only one proposal ever reaches the owner; a bus that carries not just where the owner is now but what the owner has declared about themselves (capacity, availability, mood) with the provenance to tell a declaration from an inference and the age to tell fresh from stale; a reference grammar in which every citation across a schema fence is a door the owner can open; and a machine-checked capability contract, so a question routed to a butler that cannot answer it fails loudly at the seam instead of being recorded as delivered. The owner's side of that spine is one artifact per situation with exactly one ask: "here is what we did, here is the one thing only you can decide", plus owner verbs that outrank every butler's opinion — close it, dismiss it, watch it quietly, I will handle this. And the honest limits are declared, not discovered: each manifesto names what it answers and what it refuses, so "no butler owns this question" is a real answer the fleet can give.
audits.jarvis_gap: Today the fleet cannot talk at all. Two of ten butlers — Finance, the money endpoint of every situation, and Relationship, the people endpoint — expose zero cross-butler tools because a runtime_config row frozen on 2026-04-07 silently overrides the git identity that grants them (finding 1). Every downstream number follows: the entire cross-butler traffic history is 6 domain-event deliveries (5 permanently failed to Finance, 3 of them after the bead that "closed" the failure), 1 delegated question (a money question, unanswerable by construction, recorded as "routed" for 26 days because the dispatcher reads an empty result as a successful handoff), and 0 fleet cases despite all seven RFC 0032 slices and five consumer PRs landing. There is no shared vocabulary for a typed answer, no register for the owner's contended hour, no tense but the present on the context bus, no provenance separating the owner's own words from a keyword guess, no grammar that makes a cross-schema citation openable, and no owner verb on a case. The case, the money claim and the journey are each real in exactly one schema; nothing yet makes them one situation the owner would recognise.
audits.live_verification: Dev stack reachable at http://127.0.0.1:42200 (513 OpenAPI paths). Live read-only probes: GET /api/butlers (10 agents ok); GET /api/butlers/{finance,relationship,health}/mcp/tools (105/125/160 tools — finance and relationship carry no delegate_*, no receive_domain_event, no *_case* tools; health carries all twelve); GET /api/butlers/{finance,relationship,health,travel,general}/runtime-config (finance and relationship pin a 7-group core_groups list seeded 2026-04-07 and never updated; everyone else null); GET /api/domain-events/deliveries?limit=200 (6 rows total, 5 failed_permanent travel.trip_booked->finance with three on 2026-09-07, 1 delivered); GET /api/domain-events/subscriptions (2 active); GET /api/domain-events/contracts (all permitted_subscribers empty); GET /api/delegation/ledger (total=1, routed since 2026-08-17); GET /api/switchboard/cases (empty); GET /api/system/conditions (infra ledger only); no /api/context* endpoint exists. Everything else — daemon core-group gate, delegation/domain-event route classifiers, calendar proposal insert and find_conflicts, context preamble and producers, fleet-case evidence ref contract, registry capability derivation — read at the exact decisive line and cited as source-confirmed. No writes of any kind were issued.

moves.title: Make the fleet able to speak: reconcile the registered tool surface with git identity, advertise core groups as capabilities, and refuse a cross-butler call the target cannot serve
moves.why: vision.md:92-101 rule 5 makes module selection and tool-surface identity a git concern; the live fleet contradicts it — finance and relationship silently dropped delegation/domain_events/fleet_cases (finding 1). architecture.md's MCP-only doctrine means the Switchboard route is the only channel, so a route that reaches a tool that is not there and reports success is the single most load-bearing lie in the system (findings 2, 3, 4). Owner-visible within a week: the birthday-gift budget question asked on 2026-08-17 gets an answer; every booked trip finally reaches Finance; Finance and Relationship can join a case.
moves.manifesto: roster/switchboard/MANIFESTO.md 'Agent registry: maintain liveness state for all registered agents' and 'Routing execution' — a registry that advertises modules but not the tools it will route to is not maintaining routability. No amendment needed; the contract already claims this.
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/core/runtime_config.py:145-170 (seed) + a core migration to re-seed core_groups for finance/relationship from git and a startup reconciliation that logs and surfaces divergence; src/butlers/daemon.py:1251-1282 (emit a named warning + a registry fact for every group present in git identity but absent from DB config, instead of a silent no-op decorator); roster/switchboard/tools/registry/registry.py:570-590 (capabilities = modules | registered core groups | {'trigger'}) and :155 _supports_capability; src/butlers/core_tools/_delegation.py:213-224 and the domain-event fan-out dispatch (pass required_capability='delegation' / 'domain_events' / 'fleet_cases'); src/butlers/core_tools/_delegation.py:77-95 (treat a null/absent result as failure, matching _domain_events.py:344-355); new field on GET /api/switchboard/registry and /api/butlers/{name} for declared-vs-registered groups.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: finance restarts with domain_events/delegation/fleet_cases registered; registry advertises them; delegate_ask to finance passes the capability gate; travel.trip_booked delivers. Failure: a butler whose DB config omits a git-declared group registers anyway but the daemon logs 'core group X declared in git, absent from runtime_config' and the registry row carries capability_drift=[X]; a route requiring X returns 'finance does not advertise required capability domain_events' and the delegation row is recorded 'unroutable/capability_absent', never 'routed'. Concurrency: two daemons reconciling the same butler race on one UPSERT keyed by butler_name; last writer wins and the value is identical. Idempotence: reconciliation is a set comparison — re-running changes nothing once converged. Rollback: the migration's downgrade restores the prior core_groups arrays verbatim from a saved column; the capability widening is additive and a registry consumer that ignores the new strings is unaffected.
moves.verification: tests/core_tools/test_domain_event_incomplete_receiver.py extended: an envelope of {'result': None} from a target that does not advertise the capability now fails BEFORE dispatch with capability_absent, and no delivery row reaches failed_permanent. New tests/test_core_group_identity_reconciliation.py: a runtime_config row missing a git-declared group yields a warning record and a registry capability_drift entry (fails on main). New tests/core_tools/test_delegation_route_classification.py: dispatch_delegated_ask against a route returning {'result': None} records status='failed', not 'routed' (fails on main — the live 2026-08-17 row is the fixture). Live seam after ship: GET /api/butlers/finance/mcp/tools contains delegate_receive and receive_domain_event; GET /api/domain-events/deliveries shows a delivered travel.trip_booked.
moves.slice_plan: S1 classifier fix + capability derivation from registered core groups + honest refusal (no schema change). S2 reconciliation: migration re-seeding finance/relationship, startup divergence detection, registry capability_drift field. S3 owner/operator surface: declared-vs-registered groups on the butler detail page and an attention row when they diverge; replay the five failed_permanent Travel->Finance deliveries under an explicit owner-authorized action.

moves.title: Typed answer contracts: a butler asks a question of a named shape and gets a machine-checkable answer with an as-of and a basis, or a named refusal
moves.why: The only cross-butler question ever asked is a money question ('typical gift or discretionary-budget guidance for a birthday') and the ledger can only ever hold prose (openspec/specs/cross-butler-delegation/spec.md 'Ledger Of Record', answer TEXT). With the money-claim object arriving (bu-2jtfw.12), Travel can bind a booking decision to Finance's number only if the number crosses the fence as {amount, currency, as_of, basis:[claim ids]}, not as a sentence. Owner-visible: 'Travel checked with Finance before booking — EUR 340 left as of this morning, from these three claims' instead of two butlers guessing separately. Distinct from the sibling-owned answerable-question registry: this types the ANSWER on the existing delegation ledger; it does not enumerate the owner's questions.
moves.manifesto: roster/finance/MANIFESTO.md:11-20 'Our Promise ... Reconcile the evidence' — an answer with a basis is the promise applied to a sibling instead of the owner. roster/travel/MANIFESTO.md 'Our Promise' (act on the owner's behalf with facts, not guesses). Implies a small Finance manifesto amendment: Finance answers sibling money questions with an evidence-bearing figure and refuses rather than estimating.
moves.integration_points: public.delegation_ledger + columns answer_contract (text), answer_payload (jsonb), refusal_code (text) via a core migration; src/butlers/core/delegation_ledger.py record_ask/record_answer (validate payload against the contract before accepting; the wake digest already hashes the answer — hash the canonical JSON); src/butlers/core_tools/_delegation.py:271-355 (delegate_ask gains answer_contract; delegate_answer validates or refuses); a contract registry module butlers.core.answer_contracts with v1 shapes money.available (amount, currency, as_of, basis[], horizon), time.availability (windows[], as_of), fact.boolean (value, as_of, basis[]) and refusal codes out_of_domain | no_evidence | stale_beyond_horizon | requires_owner; openspec/specs/cross-butler-delegation/spec.md new requirement 'Typed Answer Contracts'; GET /api/delegation/ledger exposes the typed fields (roster/switchboard/api/router.py).
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: travel asks with answer_contract='money.available'; finance's session calls delegate_answer with a payload that validates; the row stores payload + digest and the asker's return task reads a number. Failure: payload fails validation -> explicit error, row stays 'routed', no fabricated answer; target's domain does not cover the contract -> refusal_code=out_of_domain recorded as a terminal answer, and the asker is told nobody owns it rather than receiving a guess; evidence older than the contract's horizon -> stale_beyond_horizon with the as_of it does have. Concurrency: the existing wake protocol's immutable answer identity applies unchanged — a second differing typed answer is an integrity error (spec 'Duplicate or changed answer'). Idempotence: an identical payload replays the same digest and wake key. Rollback: answer_contract null = today's free-text behavior; the columns are additive and legacy rows stay readable.
moves.verification: New tests/test_delegation_typed_answers.py: a money.available payload missing currency is refused at delegate_answer (never stored); a refusal_code answer is terminal and discoverable over GET /api/delegation/ledger; the digest is computed over canonical JSON so key ordering cannot mint a second wake identity. roster/finance/tests/test_money_answer_contract.py against create_migrated_test_db(chains=['core','finance']): with zero synced accounts the answer is refusal_code=no_evidence, NOT an amount of 0 (the unverifiable-vs-zero distinction the cost-claim sweep already draws). Live seam after ship: replay the 2026-08-17 birthday question with answer_contract='money.available' and read the typed row back over the API.
moves.slice_plan: S1 contract registry + ledger columns + validation on answer, no callers changed. S2 delegate_ask accepts answer_contract; refusal codes; API exposure. S3 first two real callers: the briefing birthday seed asks money.available; Travel's booking flow asks before a booking above a threshold. S4 (after cost-claim slice 3) money.available answers cite cost_claim ids in basis[].

moves.title: Owner-hold register: one place where butlers contend for the owner's scarce hour before anything reaches the owner
moves.why: Three butlers own a calendar proposal table each, none can see the others, and the only conflict check asks Google freeBusy — which knows nothing about a pending proposal (finding 6). architecture.md's connectors-as-cost-boundary doctrine says the provider is not the arbiter of the owner's intent; the fleet is. Owner-visible within a week: two butlers never again ask for the same hour, and the loser's alternative arrives already knowing why. This is the first contention primitive; the inbox thread and the outbound reply are the same shape and follow it.
moves.manifesto: roster/switchboard/MANIFESTO.md 'Routing execution ... including fanout for multi-domain messages' extended to arbitration of a shared owner resource — the Switchboard is already the only role that arbitrates (RFC 0032 write authority). Implies one line in the Switchboard infrastructure contract: it arbitrates contention for singular owner resources, not only message routing.
moves.integration_points: new public.owner_holds (resource_kind in {calendar_slot, thread_reply, decision}, resource_key, window tstzrange, holder_butler, purpose, stake, expires_at, state) with the same RLS shape as core_217 (any butler INSERTs its own hold; Switchboard resolves) and a GIST exclusion constraint on (resource_kind, resource_key, window) WHERE state='held'; core tool group 'owner_holds' with request_hold / release_hold / read_holds routed through dispatch_via_switchboard_route exactly like _fleet_cases.py:81-104; src/butlers/modules/calendar.py:5513-5570 takes a hold before inserting a proposal and stamps hold_id on the row; src/butlers/api/read_models/calendar_workspace_v1.py:1118-1195 surfaces contended proposals; GET /api/switchboard/holds.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: health requests Tue 15:00-16:00 for 'physio follow-up'; the exclusion constraint grants it; lifestyle's request for the same window is refused with holder=health, purpose, expires_at, and lifestyle proposes 16:30 instead. Failure: the hold write fails -> the proposal is NOT created (fail closed; a proposal without a hold is exactly today's bug); the Switchboard is unreachable -> the calling butler gets a retryable error and its scheduled job retries next tick. Concurrency: two simultaneous requests for the same window — Postgres exclusion constraint decides, the loser reads the winner's row; no advisory lock needed. Idempotence: a repeat request with the same (holder, resource_key, window, purpose) returns the existing hold id. Expiry: every hold has expires_at (default = proposal TTL); a sweep releases expired holds and the released window is immediately grantable — a butler that dies never freezes the owner's calendar. Rollback: drop the table; calendar_propose_event's hold call is behind one feature check and degrades to today's behavior.
moves.verification: New tests/test_owner_holds_exclusion.py against two real butler roles: overlapping held windows raise, adjacent windows do not, an expired hold is grantable, a released hold is grantable. roster/health tests: calendar_propose_event with an existing lifestyle hold returns a refusal naming the holder and creates NO proposal row (fails on main, which creates it silently). Read-model test: the workspace proposals lane shows the hold's purpose on a contended entry. Live seam: GET /api/calendar/workspace?view=proposals with two seeded proposals in one hour shows one proposal and one refusal record, not two accept-able proposals.
moves.slice_plan: S1 table + RLS + exclusion constraint + core tool group + sweep (nothing owner-visible). S2 calendar proposals take holds; contended proposals refused with a named holder. S3 the workspace lane renders holds and their purposes. S4 second resource kind: thread_reply, so two butlers cannot both draft a reply to the same inbox thread.

moves.title: Declared owner state: a bus channel the owner writes in their own voice, with provenance that never lets an inference wear it
moves.why: The bus carries twelve situation signals, all machine-written, all rendered to every session as 'explicit' when confidence is 1.0 — the exact word reserved for the owner's own statement (finding 5) — and the owner has no surface at all to see or set them (finding 10). The single most useful thing the owner could tell the whole fleet at once is capacity: 'I'm wiped, keep it to what burns'. Owner-visible within a week: one declaration and every butler's tone, insight cadence and proposal volume changes, with the declaration visible and revocable.
moves.manifesto: roster/general/MANIFESTO.md (general is the owner's direct voice and is already the authorized writer for every signal). Serves the vision's 'automatically reduce frequency when the owner disengages' (vision.md:135-136) by letting the owner say so instead of being inferred at. No amendment needed; a context-bus spec amendment is required (openspec/specs/context-bus/spec.md Signal Vocabulary + Table Schema).
moves.integration_points: public.user_context + column origin (owner_declared | producer_inferred | butler_asserted, NOT NULL) via a core migration; src/butlers/context_bus.py:21-36 add ContextSignal.capacity with values low|normal|high and an owner-supplied note, :74-87 permissions (capacity: general only), :93-107 TTL (default 12h, max 72h), :530-570 preamble renders origin + writer + age and reserves the word 'explicit' for origin=owner_declared; src/butlers/jobs/context_producers.py all set_context calls stamp origin='producer_inferred'; roster/general/modules/tools.py:97-150 set_context stamps owner_declared; new GET/POST /api/context (read all active signals with origin and age; POST restricted to declaring capacity/dnd/sick on the owner's behalf) so the dashboard and chat share one path; consumers: roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py:1216-1220 (suppress/downgrade on capacity=low) and src/butlers/core/attention_ledger.py:529-549.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: the owner declares capacity=low for the evening; the preamble reads 'capacity (low, declared by you 10 minutes ago, expires 21:00)'; the broker holds routine insights and lets urgent ones through unchanged. Failure: an unauthorized butler writes capacity -> PermissionError, no row (existing _check_write_permission). A producer attempting origin='owner_declared' -> refused at the writer, so no inference can ever wear the owner's voice. Concurrency: UNIQUE(signal_type, set_by_butler) already makes the write an upsert; a producer and the owner cannot collide because only general may write capacity. Idempotence: re-declaring the same value refreshes expires_at and nothing else. Expiry: capacity always expires (no indefinite signals, spec TTL Semantics), and an expired declaration disappears from the preamble rather than lingering. Rollback: drop the column and the enum member; existing rows default to producer_inferred, which is the honest reading of every row written before this ships.
moves.verification: New tests/test_context_provenance.py: format_context_preamble renders writer, origin and age for every entry, and the word 'explicit' appears only for origin='owner_declared' (fails on main, where a calendar-title guess prints 'explicit'); a producer writing owner_declared raises. New tests/test_capacity_signal.py: capacity=low suppresses a routine insight candidate through the real broker path and does not suppress an urgent one; a capacity signal one second past expiry does not appear in get_active_context. Live seam: GET /api/context returns the active signals with origin and age (no such endpoint exists today).
moves.slice_plan: S1 origin column + producers/general stamping + preamble honesty (pure trust repair, no new vocabulary). S2 capacity signal + permissions + TTL + spec amendment. S3 GET/POST /api/context and the dashboard declaration control. S4 consumers: broker cadence, attention ledger threshold, proposal volume.

moves.title: The owner's side of a case: disposition verbs that outrank every butler's posture
moves.why: A case has four butler-facing verbs and zero owner-facing ones (roster/switchboard/api/router.py:500-700 is GET-only), and posture arbitration is documented as plain last-write-wins (RFC 0032 Decision, src/butlers/core_tools/_fleet_cases.py:34-38) — so a butler can re-escalate a situation the owner has already dismissed, forever. purpose-and-single-pane.md's earned calm requires that what the owner has settled stays settled. Owner-visible: 'I've got this' / 'not a thing' / 'keep watching but stay quiet' as one keystroke on a situation, and the fleet obeys.
moves.manifesto: roster/switchboard/MANIFESTO.md — the Switchboard is the sole write authority for fleet_cases, so it is the only role that can hold an owner ceiling. Implies an RFC 0032 amendment: the owner is a contributor whose posture is a ceiling, not a proposal, and an owner-set outcome is terminal.
moves.integration_points: public.fleet_cases + columns owner_posture_ceiling, owner_disposition, owner_disposition_at (core migration, same RLS fence: only butler_switchboard_rw writes, and the API writes as Switchboard); src/butlers/core/fleet_cases.py propose_posture clamps to the ceiling and returns 'clamped_by_owner' rather than silently applying; close_case refuses to reopen an owner-closed correlation_key; new POST /api/switchboard/cases/{case_id}/disposition on roster/switchboard/api/router.py with verbs close | dismiss | watch_quietly | mine_now, each writing an owner-attributed fleet_case_evidence row (contributor='owner') so the owner's action is evidence like everyone else's; src/butlers/core/fleet_cases.py evaluate_case_attention respects the ceiling before any quiet-hours bypass; frontend: the first case surface (there is none today).
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: the owner dismisses a case; state goes closed/outcome='dismissed_by_owner'; a later contribute_case_evidence for the same correlation_key opens a NEW case (the partial unique index already permits this) and its posture is capped at 'routine' for a cooldown window, so a genuinely new development can still surface but cannot shout. Failure: the disposition write fails -> explicit error, no partial state, the owner sees the case unchanged (never a fabricated 'dismissed'). Concurrency: an owner dismissal racing a butler's urgent proposal — both land, the ceiling is applied at read and at evaluate_case_attention, so the bypass does not fire; the proposal is preserved as evidence of what the butler wanted. Idempotence: the same disposition twice is a no-op returning the existing disposition_at. Rollback: drop three columns; postures revert to last-write-wins.
