moves.verification: New tests/test_case_owner_disposition.py against real roles: a non-switchboard role cannot write the ceiling; propose_case_posture('urgent') after an owner 'watch_quietly' yields posture='routine' with clamped_by_owner in the result (fails on main); evaluate_case_attention does not write an attention row or bypass quiet hours for a clamped case; a dismissed correlation_key's next evidence opens a new case at the capped posture. API test: POST disposition on an unknown case id is 404, never a 200 with a null. Live seam: after ship, GET /api/switchboard/cases/{id} exposes owner_disposition and the ceiling alongside the butler-proposed posture.
moves.slice_plan: S1 columns + ceiling enforcement in propose_posture and evaluate_case_attention + tests (no surface). S2 POST disposition endpoint with owner-attributed evidence rows. S3 the case surface itself: a situation view with the four verbs on j/k, deep-linked from the attention list. S4 cooldown policy for a re-opened dismissed correlation key.

moves.title: A fleet reference grammar and one resolver, so every cross-butler citation is a door
moves.why: fleet_case_evidence.ref is documented as 'something a reader can open' and is an unqualified string no code can dereference (finding 8); the same untyped-citation problem recurs in delegation answers, domain-event payloads and (imminently) money-claim basis lists. The north star requires every consequential clause to be a door on an unbroken signal-to-session-to-evidence spine; today the spine breaks at the schema fence, which is precisely where the fleet's collaboration happens. Owner-visible: on a situation, every line of 'what the fleet saw' is clickable and lands on the session, transaction, trip or fact that says it.
moves.manifesto: Serves architecture.md's MCP-only fence directly: a butler must not read a sibling's schema, so a reference is the only legal way to cite one, and an uninterpretable reference makes the fence a wall. roster/switchboard/MANIFESTO.md non-responsibility for domain logic is preserved — the Switchboard routes the resolve call, each butler resolves its own refs.
moves.integration_points: butlers.core.fleet_refs with a canonical form butler:<name>/<kind>/<id> (kinds drawn from a small closed set: session, task, transaction, trip, fact, claim, event, message) + parser/validator; src/butlers/core/fleet_cases.py:166-172 and src/butlers/core_tools/_fleet_cases.py:221-231 validate ref against the grammar (legacy rows stay readable, flagged unresolvable); a new core tool group 'fleet_refs' with resolve_ref returning {title, occurred_at, dashboard_path, sensitivity} for the caller's own schema only, routed through the Switchboard like every other cross-butler call (_switchboard_route_dispatch.dispatch_via_switchboard_route); GET /api/refs/{ref} on the dashboard API resolving in one hop; consumers: the case detail response (roster/switchboard/api/router.py:634-700) returns resolved titles + hrefs alongside the raw ref, and delegation typed answers' basis[] uses the same grammar.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: health contributes ref='butler:health/session/<uuid>'; the case view shows 'Health session, 2026-09-08 07:14' linking to /sessions/<id>. Failure: the named butler is down or the row is gone -> the reference renders as 'unresolvable (health/session/<id>) — checked 30s ago', never silently dropped and never a fabricated title. Sensitivity: a resolver may return {resolvable: true, redacted: true} rather than a title, so a health ref can prove existence without leaking a diagnosis (memory read-ceiling doctrine, bu-2jtfw.3). Concurrency: resolution is a pure read; N refs resolve in one batched fan-out with per-butler failure isolation like fan_out_with_status. Idempotence: trivially idempotent; results cached with an explicit as-of shown in the UI. Rollback: refs remain free strings; the resolver is additive and the raw ref keeps rendering.
moves.verification: New tests/test_fleet_ref_grammar.py: parser round-trips every kind, rejects unqualified strings, and contribute_case_evidence refuses a malformed ref while accepting a legacy row read. New tests/test_ref_resolution.py: a resolver for a butler that is down returns an explicit unresolvable marker (never an empty success); a redacted-sensitivity ref returns existence without content; a batch of 20 refs across 4 butlers isolates one failing butler. Live seam: GET /api/refs/butler:health/session/<a real session id> returns a title and a dashboard path; the case detail response carries resolved entries.
moves.slice_plan: S1 grammar + validation on new evidence writes (legacy tolerated). S2 resolve_ref core tool per butler + batched resolution helper. S3 GET /api/refs and resolved refs in the case detail payload. S4 adopt in delegation typed-answer basis[] and money-claim evidence.

audits.live_verification: Dev stack reachable and used read-only throughout (http://127.0.0.1:42200). Live-confirmed: (a) /api/memory/stats — 262 rules fleet-wide, candidate_rules=262, established=proven=anti_pattern=0; every /api/memory/rules row has applied_count=0, success_count=0, effectiveness_score=0.0, last_applied_at=null; (b) /api/memory/entities — 626 entities; (c) /api/relationship/entities/concentration — ~88 active relational entity_facts rows (owner alone holds 41 `knows` targets), every row src=interaction_sync, conf=1.0, verified=false, last_seen=null, and the `predicate` query param is ignored (always returns "knows"); (d) /api/memory/catalog/search probed with 5 unrelated queries (works at / colleague / friend / married / owes, 40 rows) — the ONLY non-null graph_coverage on any row is the owner's {relationships_known: 6, relationships_withheld: 1}; every other entity returns null, i.e. public.entity_graph_edges is effectively empty against 626 entities and ~88 relational facts; (e) /api/memory/entities/{id} omits graph_coverage entirely and returns dunbar_tier/dunbar_score = null for an entity the list route ranks tier 5 / score 50.47; (f) /api/butlers/{name}/runtime-config for all 12 butlers — relationship=[infra,state,scheduling,sessions,notifications,media,temporal], finance=same, switchboard=[infra,notifications,module_mgmt,switchboard_routing,switchboard_backfill], all seeded 2026-04-07 with updated_at == seeded_at; the other nine are core_groups=null; (g) /api/memory/stats meta.graph_health returns per-pool episode-retention ratios, not entity-graph facts. Source-confirmed (exact decisive mechanism read): the rule/fact context formatters, the assert-fact `unchanged` short-circuit, the core_groups gate in daemon.py, the walk/path projection of tool output, and the absence of production callers for all three graph backfills. Nothing inferred-only in the findings below except where graded.
audits.jarvis_gap: Today the knowledge graph is a beautifully specified substrate with almost no matter in it and no door on either end. `public.entity_graph_edges` has correct write-behind contracts, withheld stubs, merge repoint and retraction cascade — and holds roughly seven live edges against 626 entities and ~88 active relational facts, because the one idempotent re-assert path that runs daily (`relationship_assert_fact` → `AssertOutcome.unchanged`) skips projection entirely and all three backfill functions written to heal exactly this have no production caller. The two zero-LLM traversal tools that would let a butler use the graph are not registered on the relationship butler at all — its DB-frozen April core_groups allowlist omits `graph` (and `delegation`, and `fleet_cases`) — and when they do run they return bare UUIDs and predicates with the source pointer stripped, so nothing downstream can name a person or cite a fact. The rule substrate is worse: every one of 262 rules is injected into live prompts labeled "effectiveness: 0.00" without an id, so no session can call `memory_mark_helpful`, `memory_confirm`, or `memory_forget` on anything it was shown; the feedback loop is severed at a single format string, and the resulting 0/0 is rendered as if it were a measurement. The ideal is a graph that the owner can interrogate in names ("how do I know her?", "who connects me to that firm?") and that every session is silently grounded on at spawn — and a rule ledger whose maturity is earned against evidence the daemon recorded deterministically, not against a counter nothing increments.

findings.title: The injected memory block carries no identifiers, so every memory feedback and correction tool is unreachable from context
findings.detail: `_format_fact_line` (src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/context.py:152-157) and `_format_rule_line` (:160-164) render content, subject/predicate, maturity and a confidence/effectiveness numeral — and no `id`. That block is what `fetch_memory_context` returns and `_compose_system_prompt` splices into every spawned session (src/butlers/core/spawner.py:1946-1953, src/butlers/core/spawner_context.py:118-150). Meanwhile `memory_confirm`, `memory_forget`, `memory_mark_helpful` and `memory_mark_harmful` all take a `memory_id`/`rule_id` as their only handle (src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/feedback.py:31-56). A session is therefore shown 262 rules and dozens of facts it can neither confirm, retract, nor rate — the entire write-back half of the memory contract is severed by one format string. Contrast the consolidation prompt, which does emit ids (src/butlers/modules/memory/prompt_template.py:44-58, `- **{fid}**: …`). This is the root cause behind the ledger's 'rule maturity unreachable' entry, and it applies to facts too.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/context.py:152-164; src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/feedback.py:31-56; src/butlers/core/spawner.py:1946-1953; src/butlers/modules/memory/prompt_template.py:44-58; live /api/memory/rules (applied_count=0 on every row)
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: the rendered clause is a door in every other surface but the prompt block hands the agent no handle — a write-back loop severed at the formatter

findings.title: Never-measured rules are injected as "effectiveness: 0.00" — a fabricated measurement over a zero denominator
findings.detail: `_format_rule_line` emits `(maturity: {maturity}, effectiveness: {effectiveness:.2f})` with `effectiveness_score` defaulting to 0.0 (context.py:160-164). Live, all 262 rules have applied_count=0 and effectiveness_score=0.0, so every rule the fleet injects reads to the model as 'this guidance was tried and scored zero' rather than 'never applied'. The Active Rules section is also *sorted* by that same fictional score (context.py:308-317), so the ordering is noise. PR #4044 fixed the exactly analogous fake `(confidence: 0.00)` on the fact line for never-confirmed facts but left the rule line untouched; this is the surviving instance.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/context.py:160-164, 306-317; live /api/memory/stats (candidate_rules=262, established/proven/anti_pattern=0) and /api/memory/rules (effectiveness_score 0.0, last_applied_at null)
findings.taxonomy_shape: run-11 shape: an aggregate that denominates nothing (0/0 rendered as a measured 0.00)

findings.title: `relationship_assert_fact`'s idempotent `unchanged` path skips graph projection, so public.entity_graph_edges can never self-heal
findings.detail: Both mutating outcomes project: the supersession path calls `project_entity_graph_edge` (roster/relationship/tools/relationship_assert_fact.py:822-830) and the insert path at :861. The `unchanged` branch — same triple, same provenance — returns at :765 after appending evidence only, with no projection call. `project_entity_graph_edge` is explicitly idempotent (`ON CONFLICT (source_schema, source_table, source_id) DO UPDATE`, src/butlers/core/entity_graph_edges.py:70-79), so adding the call there is free. The consequence is structural: `run_interaction_sync` re-mints the owner's `knows` edges on every tick through this writer (roster/relationship/jobs/relationship_jobs.py:1717-1745), and every one of them lands on the `unchanged` branch, so a relational fact that existed before the RFC-0031 write-behind landed is never projected and no amount of re-running heals it. Live: ~88 active relational entity_facts rows (owner alone holds 41 `knows` targets) against a graph where the only entity with any coverage at all is the owner at 6 known / 1 withheld.
findings.evidence: roster/relationship/tools/relationship_assert_fact.py:747-765 vs :822-830 and :861; src/butlers/core/entity_graph_edges.py:47-88; roster/relationship/jobs/relationship_jobs.py:1661-1748; live /api/relationship/entities/concentration and /api/memory/catalog/search graph_coverage probe
findings.taxonomy_shape: run-12 shape: computed then discarded at the seam — here, the write-behind is skipped on the only path that actually recurs

findings.title: All three entity-graph backfill functions have no production caller — no job, no script, no route
findings.detail: `backfill_relationship_entity_facts_edges` (src/butlers/core/entity_graph_edges.py:223), `backfill_memory_facts_edges` (:463) and `backfill_commitment_edges` (:520) exist, are idempotent, and are referenced only from tests (tests/modules/memory/test_memory_migration_integration.py:2390-2434, tests/integration/test_commitments_entity_graph_edges.py:245, roster/relationship/tests/test_relationship_assert_fact.py:370-390). A repo-wide grep outside .git returns no other reference: no scheduled task, no `src/butlers/scripts/` entry point, no API route. RFC 0031's Slice-2 substrate therefore only ever contains edges written since the write-behind landed, and combined with the `unchanged` gap above, that is close to nothing.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/entity_graph_edges.py:223,463,520; grep across repo returns only test callers; live graph_coverage null on 39 of 40 sampled catalog rows
findings.taxonomy_shape: run-12 shape: substrate shipped / consumer never — here the healing consumer of the substrate's own migration story

findings.title: core_groups is frozen at the first-boot seed: the graph-owning butler cannot call the graph tools, and the declared sole writer of fleet cases cannot write them
findings.detail: `_core_tool(group)` registers a core tool only when `_core_groups is None or group in _core_groups`, and `_core_groups` is read from the DB-backed RuntimeConfigAccessor cache, falling back to the git seed only when the cache is cold (src/butlers/daemon.py:1252-1282). Live, relationship's runtime_config row is `[infra,state,scheduling,sessions,notifications,media,temporal]`, seeded 2026-04-07 with `updated_at == seeded_at` — it lacks `graph`, `delegation` and `fleet_cases`, all three of which its git butler.toml has since added (roster/relationship/butler.toml:11-21). Switchboard's live row lacks `fleet_cases` even though its own git comment declares it 'the sole writer of fleet_cases/fleet_case_links (RLS)' (roster/switchboard/butler.toml). Finance is likewise missing `domain_events`, `delegation`, `fleet_cases`. The daemon warns only about name-gated groups (`switchboard_routing`/`switchboard_backfill`, daemon.py:1263-1276) — there is no warning for a group that exists in code, is declared in git, and is absent from the DB allowlist, and no drift check anywhere. The consequence for this lens is exact: `entity_graph_walk`/`entity_graph_path` are documented as 'always registered on every butler' (src/butlers/core_tools/_graph.py:9-12) but are not registered on the butler that owns the entity graph.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/daemon.py:1252-1282; src/butlers/core_tools/_graph.py:9-12,59,118; roster/relationship/butler.toml:11-21; live GET /api/butlers/{relationship,finance,switchboard}/runtime-config
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: git declares a capability, the database silently withholds it, and no seam compares the two — capability drift with no observer

findings.title: Walk/path tool output strips both the entity's name and the edge's provenance, so a graph answer can never be spoken or cited
findings.detail: `walk_entity_graph` SELECTs `entity_id, hop, e.id, e.subject_entity_id, e.predicate, e.object_entity_id` (src/butlers/core/entity_graph_edges.py:357-368) — it never joins `public.entities` for `canonical_name`/`entity_type`, and it never carries the `(source_schema, source_table, source_id)` triple that the table stores and that `memory_catalog_fetch` needs to reach the underlying fact. `_edge_dict` then narrows even that to four fields (src/butlers/core_tools/_graph.py:46-53). The docstring calls `via_edge` 'a receipt, not a summary' (:88-92) but a receipt with no name and no source pointer cannot be shown to the owner or verified by the session — the model must issue N extra `memory_entity_get` calls just to say a name, which defeats the tool's zero-LLM-cost premise.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/entity_graph_edges.py:337-373, 375-415; src/butlers/core_tools/_graph.py:46-53, 88-92, 140-169
findings.taxonomy_shape: run-11 shape: the last hop has no door (and here, no name either)

findings.title: graph_coverage is computed on catalog search only, has zero frontend consumers, and is absent from the entity detail route that should own it
findings.detail: `coverage_for_entities` is called exactly once in the API — inside `search_memory_catalog`, attaching `graph_coverage` to each catalog row (src/butlers/api/routers/memory.py:1546-1573). `grep -rn 'graph_coverage' frontend/src` returns nothing, and `grep -rn 'catalog/search' frontend/src` returns nothing: the whole endpoint has no dashboard consumer. Meanwhile `GET /api/memory/entities/{entity_id}` — the route behind EntityDetailPage, the one place an owner asks 'what do you know about this person' — never calls it; the live response has no `graph_coverage` key at all. RFC 0031 Slice 4's 'N relationships known, M withheld' statement is currently addressed to nobody.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/memory.py:1460-1490, 1546-1573 vs :1915-1921 (get_entity); frontend/src grep for graph_coverage and catalog/search both empty; live GET /api/memory/entities/{id}
findings.taxonomy_shape: run-12 shape: substrate shipped / consumer never

findings.title: The same entity has two Dunbar truths depending on which route you ask
findings.detail: `list_entities` enriches every person row from `_compute_entity_dunbar_map` (src/butlers/api/routers/memory.py:1872-1896); `get_entity` (:1915-1921) never calls it, so the `EntityDetail` model's `dunbar_tier`/`dunbar_score` fields are always null. Live: `GET /api/memory/entities?limit=6` returns Lee Hui Min at tier 5 / score 50.47, and `GET /api/memory/entities/7c1eadf3-…` for the same id returns tier null / score null. The Dunbar model is the relationship manifesto's declared foundation for prioritising owner attention ('Attention flows inward'), so the detail page silently drops the one signal the manifesto says governs everything.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/memory.py:1715-1755, 1872-1896, 1915-1921; roster/relationship/MANIFESTO.md § The Dunbar Model; live list vs detail for 7c1eadf3-1f2a-46b7-9ff7-fc59cb17db45
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: one subject, two routes, two answers — enrichment applied on the index and dropped on the detail

findings.title: memory stats `meta.graph_health` reports episode retention, not entity-graph health
findings.detail: The `graph_health` block on `GET /api/memory/stats` is assembled from the retention observation tracker and emits `reapable_expired_episodes` / `retention_eligible_episodes` / `reapable_expired_ratio` per pool (src/butlers/api/routers/memory.py:626-678); it contains nothing about `public.entity_graph_edges`. Live it reports `coverage: complete` for all ten pools — while the entity graph itself holds roughly seven edges. A reader checking 'graph health' is told the graph is complete when the word means a different graph entirely.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/memory.py:626-678; live GET /api/memory/stats meta.graph_health; openspec/specs/memory-graph-health/spec.md
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: a health name that denominates a different subject than the reader's question

findings.title: Confidence decay silently rewrites an asserted certainty, contradicting a binding manifesto clause, and recency is double-counted in the composite score
findings.detail: The relationship manifesto states as doctrine: 'A fact's confidence is its certainty at the moment it was asserted: it is immutable (changed certainty is a new, superseding assertion) … an old observation does not lower its confidence; the butler renders the two as separate signals and never lets the passage of time silently rewrite what was once asserted.' The memory module does the opposite: `_effective_confidence` returns `confidence * exp(-decay_rate * days_since_last_confirmed)` and that decayed value is the number printed to the session as `(confidence: …)` (src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/context.py:140-157), and it drives the fading/expired lifecycle. The composite retrieval score then adds `0.2*recency + 0.1*effective_confidence` (docs/modules/memory.md § Retrieval), counting recency twice while never exposing staleness as its own axis. Adjacent to but distinct from the in-flight credence-at-birth work (bu-djjig, deferred out of PR #4044): that concerns the value written, this concerns time rewriting it at read.
findings.evidence: roster/relationship/MANIFESTO.md § 'Confidence and staleness are different axes'; src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/context.py:130-157; docs/modules/memory.md § Retrieval and § Decay and Hygiene
findings.taxonomy_shape: run-11 shape: the writer's clock impersonating the world's clock, here in violation of a binding manifesto clause (non-negotiable rule 6)

findings.title: The relational graph is one undifferentiated `knows` predicate, all machine-minted, all unverified, all confidence 1.0
findings.detail: Live `/api/relationship/entities/concentration` returns predicate `knows` for every item, `src=interaction_sync`, `conf=1.0`, `verified=false`, `last_seen=null` on all ~88 rows; the `?predicate=` query parameter is accepted and ignored (the response still says `knows`). Every edge in the registry is an adjacency derived from message-volume thresholds (roster/relationship/jobs/relationship_jobs.py:910-913, 1661-1748), not a typed relationship, so the graph cannot answer 'who is my sibling', 'who works with me', or 'who introduced us'. Every derived edge is also stamped conf=1.0 — the machine's threshold heuristic asserts the same certainty as an owner statement.
findings.evidence: live GET /api/relationship/entities/concentration (and with ?predicate=friend-of, which returns knows); roster/relationship/jobs/relationship_jobs.py:905-913, 1661-1748
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: a graph whose only edge type is 'adjacency' presented under a typed-predicate registry — vocabulary declared, one term used

moves.title: Every injected memory carries a door: ids and honest never-applied rendering in the context block
moves.why: North star: 'every consequential clause is a door on an unbroken signal-to-session-to-evidence spine.' Today the memory block spliced into every session prompt is the one surface in the fleet with no handles at all (context.py:152-164), which is why 262/262 rules sit at applied_count=0 and why no butler has ever confirmed or retracted a fact it was shown. Owner-visible within a week: memory stops being write-only — the Memory page's Confirm/Retract counters and last_confirmed_at start moving because sessions can finally name what they read, and rules stop advertising a score of 0.00 they never earned. Serves module-memory's own feedback requirement (openspec/specs/memory-retention-policy/spec.md:57) which is currently unsatisfiable in practice.
moves.manifesto: Serves every butler that loads memory; directly serves roster/relationship/MANIFESTO.md ('A Friend Who Never Forgets' — a memory that cannot be corrected is not a memory) and the module-memory spec's confirm/mark requirements. No amendment implied.

moves.title: Rule practice ledger: define what "helped" means and measure it deterministically
moves.why: This is the ledger's open design question (rule maturity unreachable, 226/226 candidate — now 262/262 live). The answer is not a better prompt: it is that the *daemon* knows, deterministically, which rules it injected into which session, and the fleet already records what happened next (session terminal state, the turn-closure ledger, the friction ledger, correction-driven retraction events in `memory_events`, approval outcomes). Vision non-negotiable 4 says the daemon is deterministic infrastructure and judgment lives in sessions — so the receipt is daemon-side and the *adjudication* is an explicit, auditable rule, never an LLM guess. Owner-visible within a week of shipping slice 2: a 'Rules the fleet actually ran on' view that says, for each rule, how many sessions carried it, how many of those ended in friction or correction, and how many the owner approved — replacing 262 identical zeroes with a real, denominated record. It also makes the anti-pattern demotion path (storage.py:3143-3150), which has never fired, reachable.
moves.manifesto: Serves every butler with memory; the honesty requirement comes from about/heart-and-soul/vision.md § What Success Looks Like ('the measure is the amount of mental labor the system reliably absorbs'). moves.integration_points: New per-schema table `rule_injections(session_id, rule_id, injected_at, section, rank, butler)` written by the memory module's context assembly under the caller's session id (module migration, memory `migrations/` — modules may declare migrations, non-negotiable rule 2 respected) plus `rule_outcomes(rule_id, session_id, verdict, basis, evidence_ref, adjudicated_at)`; `src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/context.py` (emit receipts alongside the rendered block); `src/butlers/core/spawner_context.py`/`spawner.py:1946-1953` to thread the session id into assembly; adjudication as a module-default deterministic maintenance job next to `ann_observability.py`/`reembedding.py`, reading the session log, turn-closure ledger, friction ledger and `memory_events`; `src/butlers/modules/memory/storage.py:3009-3082` (mark_helpful) and :3088-3180 (mark_harmful) rewritten to consume adjudicated rows rather than raw tool calls; `GET /api/memory/rules` gains injection/outcome counts; frontend Memory rules view; openspec/specs/module-memory + memory-retention-policy.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: a session is spawned, three rules are injected, three receipt rows are written in the same transaction as nothing else (append-only, no FK to the session row so a receipt cannot block a spawn); the nightly adjudicator joins each receipt to that session's terminal state and finds (a) an explicit `memory_mark_helpful` citation → verdict=cited_helpful, (b) a friction report or correction-driven retraction naming the session → verdict=harmful, (c) a clean completion with no counter-signal → verdict=carried_without_incident (counts toward exposure, NOT toward success), (d) session still running or terminal state unknown → no row written yet. Only (a) and (b) move success/harmful counters; (c) moves an `exposure_count` that gives effectiveness a visible denominator and is rendered as such. Failure: adjudicator cannot read a ledger → it writes no rows for that window and records the gap; it never infers a verdict from absence. Concurrency: receipts are append-only with a unique `(session_id, rule_id)`; the adjudicator claims a window with an advisory lock and is safe to run concurrently with spawns. Idempotence: `(rule_id, session_id)` unique on outcomes — a re-run of the adjudicator over the same window is a no-op; counters are recomputed from outcome rows, never incremented in place. Rollback: stop the job and drop the two tables; `applied_count`/`effectiveness_score` are recomputed-from-rows so they return to zero honestly rather than keeping stale values.
moves.verification: (1) Integration test at the spawn seam: spawn a fake session with a seeded rule, assert one receipt row with the real session id, then drive a friction report naming that session and assert the adjudicator writes verdict=harmful and the rule's harmful_count/maturity move to anti_pattern. (2) A determinism test: run the adjudicator twice over the same window and assert byte-identical outcome rows and unchanged counters. (3) A 'no verdict from absence' test: a session with no counter-signal produces exposure only, and `effectiveness_score` stays null (not 0.0) until at least one adjudicated success or harm exists. (4) An API test asserting `GET /api/memory/rules` reports exposure_count and a null effectiveness for never-adjudicated rules. (5) A migration test asserting counters recompute from rows.
moves.slice_plan: S1 receipt table + session-id threading + receipts written at assembly (no behaviour change; immediately answers 'which rules is the fleet actually carrying?'). S2 the adjudicator job with the two hard verdicts (cited_helpful, harmful) and exposure counting; counters recomputed from rows; null-not-zero effectiveness. S3 owner surface: rules ranked by exposure with outcome breakdown, 'never carried' and 'carried but never adjudicated' as first-class states. S4 promotion/demotion thresholds re-specified against adjudicated evidence and the anti_pattern path proven with a test. S5 retire the raw `memory_mark_helpful` counter write in favour of a citation that the adjudicator reads.

moves.title: The graph self-heals: projection parity sweep and an edge-coverage denominator that names what is missing
moves.why: RFC 0031's substrate, walk tools, catalog coverage, merge repoint and retraction cascade have all shipped — over a graph that live holds roughly seven edges against 626 entities and ~88 active relational facts, because the only recurring write path skips projection on `unchanged` and all three backfills have no caller. Every downstream answer therefore looks complete and is not: `entity_graph_path` returning `{found: false}` today means 'the projection never ran', not 'you are unconnected' — failure impersonating health at the read side, which the north star forbids by name. Owner-visible within a week: the graph goes from ~7 edges to the full relational corpus, `graph_coverage` starts returning real numbers on the surfaces that already ask for it, and a parity figure states plainly how many eligible source rows are still unprojected.
moves.manifesto: Serves roster/relationship/MANIFESTO.md (the Dunbar model needs real edges to weight) and the fleet-wide identity model (docs/concepts/identity-model.md). No amendment implied. Adjacent to the open change `openspec/changes/relational-edges-single-home` (which decides *where* relational edges are written and backfills entity_facts); this move is strictly downstream of that — the projection of entity_facts into public.entity_graph_edges and its observability — and should cite it as a dependency rather than duplicate it.
moves.integration_points: roster/relationship/tools/relationship_assert_fact.py:747-765 (add the idempotent projection to the `unchanged` branch); src/butlers/core/entity_graph_edges.py:223/463/520 (the three backfills) wired into a new deterministic core maintenance job — projection is core write-behind, not a module tool, so it belongs beside the existing core sweeps rather than in `modules/memory`; a new parity query (`eligible source rows` per source_table vs `projected` vs `withheld`) exposed on `GET /api/memory/stats` as a genuine `entity_graph` block distinct from the existing episode-retention `graph_health` (src/butlers/api/routers/memory.py:626-678, which should be renamed to `episode_retention_health`); frontend memory/butler console; openspec/specs/memory-graph-health (or a new `entity-graph-projection` capability) and about/legends-and-lore/rfcs/0031.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: the sweep runs on a bounded schedule, calls each backfill with a limit, and reports `{scanned, projected, withheld, skipped_unresolvable}`; the parity block reports projected/eligible per source table with the shortfall named. Failure: a backfill raises → the sweep records the failing source and continues with the others; parity for that source is reported `unknown`, never 0 and never 'complete'. Concurrency: each backfill is `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`/`DO UPDATE` on the natural key and safe against a concurrent live write of the same row; the sweep takes an advisory lock so two daemons cannot both drain. Idempotence: proven by the existing tests — a second run projects zero new rows. Rollback: disable the schedule; already-projected edges stay valid (they are exact projections of live source rows) and the retraction cascade already removes them when the source dies.
moves.verification: (1) A regression test at the assert-fact seam: assert the same triple twice, delete the projected edge between the calls, and assert the second (unchanged) call restores it — this is the exact live gap. (2) A parity test: seed N relational entity_facts and M memory edge-facts, run the sweep, assert projected == eligible and the parity block reports zero shortfall. (3) A degraded test: make one backfill raise and assert the parity block reports `unknown` for that source and `complete` for the others, with the API's degraded envelope set. (4) A live-shaped smoke assertion that `GET /api/memory/stats` no longer uses the name `graph_health` for episode retention.
moves.slice_plan: S1 the one-line projection fix on the `unchanged` branch plus its regression test (this alone starts healing the graph on the next interaction_sync tick). S2 the bounded projection sweep wired to all three backfills, with per-source results in the task's last_result. S3 the parity denominator on the stats API and the `graph_health` rename. S4 console surface: 'N relationships projected, M eligible, K withheld' with the shortfall as a door.

moves.title: The graph speaks in names and cites its source
moves.why: `entity_graph_walk`/`entity_graph_path` are the only zero-LLM way to answer 'how do I know her?' and they return bare UUIDs with the provenance triple stripped (core_tools/_graph.py:46-53; the SQL never joins public.entities and never selects source_schema/source_table/source_id). A session must therefore issue one lookup per hop just to speak a name, and can never cite the fact behind an edge — so the tool is unusable in a sentence and unverifiable in a receipt. Owner-visible within a week: a butler can answer 'how do I know Chloe?' with 'through Amy Lam — relationship butler, entity_facts row asserted 2026-07-04 from a WhatsApp thread', in one tool call, with a clickable source. This is the missing precondition the deferred graph dossier route (bu-8cdl1.8) is waiting on, and it is what makes move 6's context pack renderable.
moves.manifesto: Serves roster/relationship/MANIFESTO.md ('Richness' and 'Connection' — context always at hand, without scrambling) and the north star's evidence spine. No amendment implied.
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/core/entity_graph_edges.py `walk_entity_graph` (:337-373) and `find_entity_graph_path` (:375-415) — join `public.entities` for canonical_name/entity_type and select the stored `source_schema/source_table/source_id` and `updated_at`; src/butlers/core_tools/_graph.py `_edge_dict` (:46-53) and both tool returns; a new `entity_graph_explain(from_entity_id, to_entity_id)` core tool in the same `graph` group that narrates the shortest path as an ordered, named, cited chain and returns `{found: false, searched_hops: N}` when there is none; `memory_catalog_fetch` is the existing follow-the-pointer verb the citations resolve through, so no new read authority is introduced (the withheld-stub exclusion in the CTE is untouched); openspec/specs (module-memory / a graph traversal requirement) and RFC 0031 'Traversal Shape'.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: each edge receipt carries `{predicate, subject:{id,name,type}, object:{id,name,type}, source:{schema,table,id}, as_of}`; `entity_graph_explain` returns the ordered chain plus a coverage statement ('3 relationships known for this entity, 1 withheld'). Failure: an entity row missing from public.entities renders `name: null, name_status: 'unresolved'` — never a fabricated label and never a silent drop of the hop. A source pointer whose row is gone renders `source_status: 'retracted'` rather than a dead link. No path found returns `{found: false, searched_hops: N, coverage: {...}}` so the caller can distinguish 'no relationship' from 'nothing projected yet' — which, given move 3, is the difference that matters most right now. Concurrency: read-only. Idempotence: pure reads. Rollback: revert the projection of extra fields; callers that only read id/predicate are unaffected.
moves.verification: (1) A tool-level test asserting a two-hop walk returns canonical names and a resolvable source triple for every hop, and that feeding that triple to `memory_catalog_fetch` returns the underlying record. (2) An unresolved-entity test asserting `name_status: 'unresolved'` and no dropped hop. (3) A withheld test asserting a sensitivity-withheld edge is still absent from traversal and is only counted in the coverage statement. (4) An `entity_graph_explain` test asserting the not-found response carries `searched_hops` and coverage, so 'unprojected' is distinguishable from 'unconnected'. (5) A query-plan/row-count guard that the entities join does not turn a bounded walk into an unbounded scan.
moves.slice_plan: S1 names and source triple on walk/path output (pure widening, no new tool). S2 `entity_graph_explain` with the cited chain and the coverage-qualified not-found. S3 hand the enriched shape to the pending dossier route so it can render without a second round trip.

moves.title: Declared capability vs granted capability: a core_groups drift observer and reconcile verb
moves.why: The graph tools are documented as 'always registered on every butler' and are not registered on the relationship butler, because its runtime_config row was seeded on 2026-04-07 and has never been touched since, while git kept adding groups. Live, three butlers are affected and one of them — switchboard — is missing `fleet_cases` despite its own git config declaring it the sole writer of fleet_cases/fleet_case_links. Nothing anywhere compares git's declared groups to the DB's granted groups, and the daemon's only warning covers name-gated groups. Vision non-negotiable 5 draws the git-identity / DB-tuning line explicitly; a seed that silently ossifies turns a git declaration into a lie. Owner-visible within a week: the Butlers console states, per butler, 'declared 10, granted 7, 3 withheld since first boot' with the missing names, and the graph tools actually become callable where the graph lives.
moves.manifesto: Serves about/heart-and-soul/vision.md non-negotiable 5 and roster/switchboard/MANIFESTO.md (the staffer infrastructure contract naming its responsibilities). No amendment implied; if anything it is the enforcement the rule already assumes.
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/daemon.py:1252-1282 (the `_core_tool` gate and the existing name-gated warning block) — extend to a full three-way diff of {groups defined in code} × {groups declared in git seed} × {groups granted in runtime_config}; src/butlers/core/runtime_config.py:39-166 (seeding); `GET /api/butlers/{name}/runtime-config` gains a `capability_diff` field; frontend ButlerDetailPage runtime-config tab; a reconcile verb that adopts git-declared groups the DB lacks (owner-initiated, audited, never automatic — the DB stays the operational authority); openspec/specs/core-daemon or the runtime-config capability spec.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: on startup the daemon logs, and the API reports, `declared_not_granted: ['graph','delegation','fleet_cases']`, `granted_not_defined: []`, `defined_not_declared: [...]`; the console shows a warning chip and a reconcile action. Failure: runtime_config unreadable → the daemon falls back to the git seed as today and the diff reports `unknown`, never 'complete'. Concurrency: reconcile is a single guarded UPDATE with an updated_at bump; a concurrent dashboard edit loses only if it targets the same row and is reported, not silently overwritten. Idempotence: reconcile applied twice is a no-op (set semantics); the diff is a pure read. Rollback: the reconcile records the prior group list in the audit row so the owner can restore it; the observer alone changes no behaviour. Ordering trap to test: a group granted in the DB but no longer defined in code must be reported, not crash registration.
moves.verification: (1) A daemon test with a runtime_config row missing a group the code defines and git declares: assert the startup diff names it and that the tool is genuinely absent from the MCP surface (assert on the registered tool list, not on the log line). (2) An API test asserting `capability_diff` for a drifted butler matches the live shape observed here (relationship missing graph/delegation/fleet_cases). (3) A reconcile test asserting idempotence, the audit row, and that a group not defined in code is refused rather than written. (4) A repo-level test asserting that for every butler.toml declaring core_groups, every named group exists in the code's group vocabulary — catching the reverse drift.
moves.slice_plan: S1 the three-way diff at startup plus the `capability_diff` API field (observation only, zero behaviour change). S2 console surface with the withheld names. S3 the audited reconcile verb. S4 decide per butler whether the April allowlists were ever intentional — the likely answer is that all three should simply carry the groups their git config declares.

moves.title: Entities in play: a graph-grounded context pack at spawn
moves.why: `memory_context` is injected into every session (spawner.py:1946-1953) and has five sections, none of which is about *who or what the trigger is about*: Profile Facts, Task-Relevant Facts, Active Rules, Recent Episodes, Fleet Knowledge (context.py:213-224). A butler handling 'Chloe asked about dinner' gets loose facts that mention Chloe and must re-derive her identity every single time — the exact 'which Chloe?' problem the entity anchor was built to solve (docs/modules/memory.md § Facts). Owner-visible within a week: butlers stop asking who someone is, stop conflating two people with the same first name, and start naming a person's tier and known relationships in their first sentence — because the session was handed them before it started, at zero LLM cost. This is also the first consumer that makes the graph load-bearing rather than optional, and it degrades honestly: with move 3 unshipped it says 'no projected relationships' rather than implying isolation.
moves.manifesto: Serves roster/relationship/MANIFESTO.md ('Connection': 'You're not scrambling to recall context') and every domain butler that talks about people. No amendment implied. Respects specialist ownership: the pack carries entity identity and graph adjacency only — never another butler's domain content, which continues to come through the existing Fleet Knowledge section under the held catalog ceiling.
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/context.py (new `## People & Things In Play` section + a re-slice of `_PROFILE_FACTS_FRAC.._FLEET_KNOWLEDGE_FRAC` at :35-39, which PR #4044 is already normalising — sequence behind it); src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/entities.py `memory_entity_resolve` for trigger-prompt resolution; src/butlers/core/entity_graph_edges.py `walk_entity_graph` (1 hop) and `coverage_for_entities` for the adjacency and the coverage statement — so this move depends on move 4 for names and on move 5 for the relationship butler to have the group at all; the Dunbar map behind `/api/relationship/entities/concentration` for tier (read through the existing sanctioned path, not a cross-schema query); openspec/specs/module-memory § context assembly; docs/modules/memory.md § Context Assembly table.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: names in the trigger prompt resolve to entities; each resolved entity renders one block — canonical name, type, aliases, entity_id (a door, per move 1), Dunbar tier where known, up to K one-hop named neighbours with predicates, and 'N relationships known, M withheld'. Failure: resolution is ambiguous → the section names both candidates explicitly with their distinguishing facts and instructs no silent pick; resolution finds nothing → the section is omitted entirely rather than rendering an empty heading (matching `_fill_section`'s existing rule at :208-210). Graph unreachable or unprojected → 'relationships: not projected' rather than 'no relationships' — the honest-absence distinction the north star requires. Sensitivity: the section obeys the same read ceiling PR #4044 introduces for the other sections and reports `withheld: N`. Concurrency: read-only. Idempotence: deterministic ordering (tier desc, then coverage desc, then entity_id asc) so the same trigger yields the same block. Rollback: remove the section and restore the four/five-way budget split; no persisted state.
moves.verification: (1) A composition test: a trigger naming two people yields two blocks with correct names, tiers and one-hop neighbours, and the whole block still fits the token budget. (2) An ambiguity test: two entities share an alias → both are named, neither is silently chosen. (3) An honest-absence test: an entity with zero projected edges renders 'not projected', and after seeding an edge renders the count — asserting the two states are textually distinguishable. (4) A ceiling test: a confidential edge is withheld and counted, never rendered. (5) An end-to-end spawn test asserting the section reaches the composed system prompt and that the entity_id in it is accepted by `memory_entity_get`.
moves.slice_plan: S1 resolution + identity block only (names, aliases, entity_id, tier) — this alone kills 'which Chloe?'. S2 one-hop named adjacency with the coverage statement, gated behind move 4's enriched walk output. S3 budget re-slice and spec/doc update. S4 opt-in extension to non-person entities (organizations, places) once the graph carries typed edges.

audits.ideal: A JARVIS-grade knowledge substrate has three properties this one lacks. First, it is *populated by construction*: every write path that can name two entities projects an edge, the projection is idempotent so the recurring no-op write is also the self-heal, a bounded sweep continuously reconciles source rows to edges, and a parity denominator states out loud how many eligible rows are not yet projected — so a traversal that finds nothing is provably 'unconnected' and never quietly 'unprojected'. Second, it is *speakable and citable*: every traversal result carries canonical names, the predicate, the provenance triple that resolves back to the originating fact under the held read ceiling, and an as-of stamp, so the owner can be told 'you know her through Amy Lam, asserted by the relationship butler on 4 July from a WhatsApp thread' and can open the receipt; withheld knowledge is counted honestly for the butler and revealable to the owner, who owns the instance. Third, it is *grounded into every session automatically* — the daemon resolves the entities a trigger is about and hands the session their identity, tier, one-hop named neighbourhood and coverage statement before the first token, at zero LLM cost, so no butler ever re-derives who someone is. Over that substrate, the rule layer earns its authority the same way: the daemon records deterministically which rules it injected into which session, an auditable adjudicator joins those receipts to outcomes the fleet already records — friction reports, correction-driven retractions, approval verdicts, explicit session citations — and maturity moves only on adjudicated evidence, with exposure as the visible denominator and 'never carried' and 'carried but never adjudicated' as first-class states rather than a rendered 0.00. Every clause the owner reads in that world is a door, every capability git declares is a capability the database granted, and the difference between 'we do not know' and 'we never looked' is always on the page.

audits.jarvis_gap: Run 12 tiered this lens **solid** on the strength of the plumbing (ingest.v1, `operational_role`, replay drain, discretion, heartbeat liveness, RFC 0018 scope discipline) and it has since gained real ground: the vision lane shipped (#4122), captionless media envelopes landed (#4128, `contracts.py:255-270`), the Switchboard connector API was retired (#4129), the OAuth scope registry landed in code (`src/butlers/api/oauth_scope_registry.py`). I am tiering it **down to functional** because this run's read-side evidence shows three fabrications the plumbing quality cannot excuse. First, the fleet's headline perception number is a clock: every connector's "lifetime counters" are Prometheus `_created` series values, so the live dashboard renders Gmail as having ingested **1,789,149,468** messages — which is exactly 2026-09-11T17:57:48Z, the connector process's start time — and the fleet KPI totals 8,945,736,607 (`heartbeat.py:343-370`; live `GET /api/ingestion/connectors/gmail/...`; `ConnectorDetailView.tsx:349-372`). Second, the ingestion boundary has no world clock at all: `ingest.v1` carries no source-event time and the Switchboard stamps `received_at = datetime.now(UTC)` (`roster/switchboard/tools/ingestion/ingest.py:793`), so Home Assistant's real state timestamp survives only as a substring inside the dedupe key (live: `external_event_id="ha:sensor.bedroom_air_quality_humidity:2026-09-12T17:40:09.635647+00:00"`, `received_at=17:40:10.316825`) — which makes the entire dormant backfill subsystem unsound before it runs, because an imported 2019 receipt would date to 2026. Third, a source's whole life-cycle is undocumented at the edges: `connector_registry.capabilities` is written by every heartbeat and read by nothing; the backfill jobs table, its two MCP tools and its six REST endpoints (with `rate_limit_per_hour` and `daily_cost_cap_cents`) have zero frontend and zero jobs; disconnect soft-deletes one row while leaving the credential live, the provider grant intact, the data unmentioned and every `expected_signal` it fed permanently `producer_unregistered`; and the Telegram user client has been offline since 2026-07-18 with `/api/switchboard/cases` empty, because no deterministic producer opens a fleet case for a dead sense. A JARVIS knows *when* a thing happened, *how far back it can see*, *what each sense costs to keep warm*, *what breaks when a sense dies*, and *what remains after a sense is retired*. Butlers today knows only that bytes arrived.
audits.live_verification: Dev stack reachable; all live checks were GETs against http://127.0.0.1:42200. Live-confirmed: `/api/ingestion/connectors/available` returns 13 profiles with no `live_listener`; `/api/ingestion/connectors/summaries` returns 19 registry rows (telegram_user_client last heartbeat 2026-07-18, spotify:unconfigured 2026-08-25, google_health:degraded 2026-06-07); `/api/ingestion/connectors/cross-summary` returns total_messages_ingested=8945736607 with aggregates_available=false; per-connector detail returns counter_messages_ingested=1789149468 (gmail), 1789145711 (spotify), 1789146253 (owntracks), 1789145788 (google_health) and counter_source_api_calls=7156587834 (gmail, = 4x epoch) — each equal to a process-start epoch; `/api/switchboard/backfill` returns zero jobs; `/api/switchboard/cases` returns zero fleet cases; `/api/ingestion/events?limit=2` shows HA source time discarded into external_event_id while received_at is the pipeline clock. Source-confirmed: heartbeat `_created` sample pollution, `received_at = now()` at ingest, capabilities write-with-no-reader, disconnect semantics, v_qa_connector_state deleted_at filter, cost_usd lazy write-back, calendar-private mutation idempotency ledger, butler-side SMTP/REST transport. Inferred: nothing load-bearing; the Google Photos Library API restriction (March 31 2025, app-created data only; Picker API for library selection) was verified by web search, not by code.

findings.title: Every connector's lifetime counters are Prometheus `_created` timestamps — the dashboard renders 1.79 billion ingested messages for a mailbox that saw 2 today
findings.detail: `_collect_counters` iterates `metric.samples` and filters only on label values, never on `sample.name`. prometheus_client emits both `<name>_total` and `<name>_created` samples for every Counter (and `PROMETHEUS_DISABLE_CREATED_SERIES` is set nowhere in the repo), so the `_created` sample's value — the counter's creation time in epoch seconds — is added into `messages_ingested`, `messages_failed`, `source_api_calls`, `checkpoint_saves` and `dedupe_accepted`. Live: gmail `counter_messages_ingested = 1789149468` = 2026-09-11T17:57:48Z (its process start); `counter_source_api_calls = 7156587834` = 4x that epoch (four label combinations). The values are persisted verbatim by the heartbeat tool, summed into the fleet KPI (`total_messages_ingested = 8945736607`), and rendered under the label 'lifetime counters' on the connector detail page. The one place the number looks sane — `today_messages_ingested` — is a MAX-MIN delta per instance-day, which cancels the constant and therefore hides the defect from the only surface anyone sanity-checks.

findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: instrument artifact published as measurement — a writer-side bookkeeping value (counter creation time) is summed into an owner-facing quantity and rendered with full authority, while the one derived view that would expose it (a same-day delta) algebraically cancels the error

findings.title: `ingest.v1` has no source-event clock: the Switchboard stamps `received_at = now()` and the real event time survives only inside the dedupe-key string
findings.detail: `IngestPayloadV1`/`IngestRequestContextV1` carry no `occurred_at`; `public.ingestion_events` has only `received_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()`; and the ingest tool sets `received_at = datetime.now(UTC)` on acceptance. Home Assistant proves the source time is known and thrown away: its `external_event_id` embeds `2026-09-12T17:40:09.635647+00:00` while the row's only timestamp is 17:40:10.316825. Consequence beyond ordering jitter: every historical import is mis-dated by construction, so the entire backfill subsystem cannot be correct; the Chronicler's manifesto promise of 'point events: things that happened at an instant' with recorded boundary precision has no field to read; and Finance's 'answers come from your actual email history' dates a 2019 receipt to whenever the pipeline saw it.
findings.evidence: roster/switchboard/tools/ingestion/ingest.py:793,798; roster/switchboard/tools/routing/contracts.py:242-270,374; alembic/versions/core/core_001_foundation.py:148,170-177; roster/chronicler/MANIFESTO.md:19-24; roster/finance/MANIFESTO.md:26; live GET /api/ingestion/events?limit=2
findings.taxonomy_shape: Run 11 shape: writer's clock impersonating the world's clock — new instance, at the ingestion boundary itself rather than at a read surface

findings.title: Connector retirement is one soft-deleted row: the credential stays live, the provider grant is never revoked, the data is never accounted for, and every signal that source fed becomes permanently unmeasurable
findings.detail: `POST .../disconnect` parks an approval whose only effect is `connector_registry.deleted_at = now()`. Provider-side revocation is explicitly declined (Spotify: 'Does not call Spotify or revoke provider-side authorization'; Google Health: the refresh token is deliberately not revoked). Nothing states what ingested data remains (ingestion_events, connectors.filtered_events, spotify_track_plays, owntracks_points, health measurements) or what will be deleted. And because `v_qa_connector_state` filters `deleted_at IS NULL`, `_connector_measurability` finds no rows and returns `producer_unregistered` — so a retired source turns every `expected_signals` row it fed into a permanent `unmeasurable`, indistinguishable from a source that was never installed. Sovereignty (vision rule 1) is exactly the promise that the owner can see and control what remains.

findings.title: A complete backfill subsystem — jobs table, two MCP tools, six REST endpoints, rate limit and daily cost cap — has no owner door and no jobs
findings.detail: `create_backfill_job` validates target categories, a date window, `rate_limit_per_hour` and `daily_cost_cap_cents`; `backfill_pause/cancel/resume/list` exist; `backfill.poll`/`backfill.progress` are Switchboard-owned MCP tools; `/api/switchboard/backfill` plus five lifecycle routes are mounted. Zero frontend files reference any of them, live `GET /api/switchboard/backfill` returns an empty list, and only gmail and google_drive pass `get_capabilities` to the heartbeat at all. The one cost fence in the entire connector layer (`daily_cost_cap_cents`, default 500) exists only inside this dormant path.

findings.title: `connector_registry.capabilities` is written by every heartbeat and read by nothing
findings.detail: The heartbeat envelope defines an optional `capabilities` dict, the Switchboard tool persists it (`capabilities = EXCLUDED.capabilities`) and logs it, and the base spec makes it part of the contract. No API response model exposes it (the detail payload's 24 keys do not include it), and no frontend file references it. The question 'which of my sources can reach into their own history?' is therefore recorded on every check-in and answerable by nobody.

findings.title: `ingestion_events.cost_usd` is populated only as a side effect of a human opening the event detail, so any cost aggregate denominates over 'events someone clicked'
findings.detail: The per-event cost column is written back by `ingestion_event_set_cost_usd` inside the event-detail handler's session rollup — nowhere else. Events nobody inspects keep `cost_usd = NULL` forever (live: the two most recent events return `cost_usd: null`). The column is already sortable on the events list (`sort=cost`, 'highest cost_usd first, NULLS LAST'), which presents a ranking over the inspected subset as a ranking over all traffic. This is the substrate a per-source cost boundary would want, and it is currently self-selecting.

findings.title: No deterministic producer opens a fleet case for a sense that has gone silent: a source dead for eight weeks leaves the case ledger empty
findings.detail: `public.fleet_cases` rows are created only by `open_case` called from the LLM-facing core tool and by the owner_conditions backfill. Nothing in the connector layer, the heartbeat tool, the expected-signals evaluator or the ingestion API opens or contributes to a case. Live, `telegram:user:@Tzeusy` last heartbeat 2026-07-18 (liveness `offline`, registry `state` still the string `healthy`), `spotify:unconfigured` 2026-08-25, `google_health:degraded` 2026-06-07 — and `/api/switchboard/cases` returns an empty page. The mechanism built precisely for 'a situation that needs the owner' never learns that a sense died.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/fleet_cases.py:151,631; src/butlers/core_tools/_fleet_cases.py:165-207; live GET /api/ingestion/connectors/summaries and GET /api/switchboard/cases?limit=10
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: the alarm has no wire to the sensor — a landed attention substrate whose only producers are LLM sessions, so deterministic infrastructure failures never reach it

findings.title: The write side has no transport boundary: butler-side modules open SMTP and call provider REST directly, and the one real idempotency ledger is private to calendar.py
findings.detail: Vision rule 7 says a butler 'must never contain Telegram polling logic, Gmail API calls'. `src/butlers/modules/email.py` opens smtplib to smtp.gmail.com; `calendar.py` calls https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3 and https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token; `telegram.py` calls https://api.telegram.org/bot{token}. Each reinvents auth, retry and receipts. The single disciplined pattern — `_prepare_workspace_mutation` with an idempotency key, a projection-action ledger and applied/noop/failed/pending replay semantics — lives inside calendar.py and is referenced by no other module, so every future source's write path starts from zero.

findings.title: `live_listener` is a shipped connector with its own capability spec but is absent from the deployable-connector catalog
findings.detail: `src/butlers/connectors/live_listener/` is a full package (connector, envelope, filter_gate, vad, transcription, checkpoint, metrics) with `openspec/specs/connector-live-listener/spec.md`, and `discretion.py` names `live_listener` as a channel. The hardcoded catalog behind `GET /api/ingestion/connectors/available` — documented as 'the list of connector profiles the framework can deploy' — has 13 entries and does not include it. moves.title: How far back can you see? A source coverage window with named gaps, and backfill promoted to an owner verb
moves.why: Chronicler's manifesto promises to answer 'how much time did I spend listening to music?' and Finance's promises answers 'from your actual email history, not your memory' (roster/chronicler/MANIFESTO.md:8-10,30; roster/finance/MANIFESTO.md:26) — but no source records when its observation actually begins, so every such answer silently denominates over 'since we installed the connector', and the blind-spot preamble (#4123) tells a session what it cannot see without ever telling it since when. Meanwhile a complete backfill subsystem sits dormant with no door (finding 4). Owner-visible payoff inside a week: a coverage bar on every connector ('Gmail: 2026-03-28 → now, 2 gaps totalling 9h'), a 'reach further back' verb with a date window and a cost cap, and butlers that answer 'first time I have data for that is March' instead of confidently answering from a two-month window.
moves.manifesto: Chronicler (MANIFESTO.md:8-10,19-24 — provenance and boundary precision on every projected row); Finance (MANIFESTO.md:26). Implies one amendment to the Switchboard staffer infrastructure contract: coverage publication becomes an ingestion SLA, not a connector courtesy.
moves.integration_points: New `connectors.source_coverage` (connector_type, endpoint_identity, stream_key, covered_from, covered_to, gap ranges as tstzrange[], evidence_kind, updated_at) written by `src/butlers/connectors/cursor_store.py:save_cursor` alongside the checkpoint; `src/butlers/connectors/heartbeat.py` publishes `capabilities.backfill` and coverage summary (fixing finding 5 by giving capabilities a reader); new `GET /api/ingestion/connectors/{type}/{identity}/coverage` in `src/butlers/api/routers/ingestion_connectors.py`; existing `/api/switchboard/backfill` + `roster/switchboard/tools/backfill/{controls,connector}.py` gain a frontend (`frontend/src/components/ingestion/connectors/`) and a coverage-derived default window; `src/butlers/core/blind_spot_declarations.py` and `src/butlers/core/expected_signals.py` cite coverage so a session is told the horizon, not just the outage; spec deltas to `openspec/specs/connector-base-spec` (new requirement: Coverage Publication Obligation) and `connector-replay-queue`.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: connector persists cursor → coverage row extends covered_to; owner opens connector page, sees window + gaps, requests 2019-01-01→2024-12-31, job is created pending, connector polls it, progress ticks, coverage rows merge and gaps shrink. Failure: source refuses history (provider API cannot page back) → capability advertised false, the verb is absent rather than disabled-with-a-tooltip, and coverage records `horizon_reason='source_has_no_history_api'`. Concurrency: two overlapping backfill windows on one identity — the job store rejects the second with the overlapping job id; a backfill running while live ingestion advances writes disjoint coverage ranges merged by tstzrange union, never a lock on the live path. Idempotence: re-running an identical window is a no-op because dedupe_key already exists and coverage union is idempotent; a partially-completed job resumes from its own cursor. Rollback: a job cancelled mid-flight leaves coverage as the union of what actually landed (never the requested window) — the requested window is not evidence.
moves.verification: tests/connectors/test_source_coverage.py::test_cursor_save_extends_coverage_and_records_gap_on_restart_hole; tests/api/test_connector_coverage_route.py::test_coverage_absent_returns_named_unavailable_not_empty_window; roster/switchboard/tests/test_backfill_coverage.py::test_cancelled_job_coverage_reflects_landed_rows_not_requested_window; tests/core/test_blind_spot_declarations.py::test_preamble_states_horizon_for_every_declared_producer; a live read seam: GET coverage for gmail must not claim covered_from earlier than the oldest ingestion_events.occurred_at for that identity.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 0 (hard prerequisite): move 'The world's clock at the ingestion boundary' must land first — backfill without occurred_at mis-dates everything it imports. 1) coverage table + cursor_store writer + read route + connector-page coverage bar. 2) capabilities surfaced on the detail payload; backfill verb rendered only where capabilities.backfill is true. 3) backfill console (create/pause/resume/cancel/progress) over the existing REST. 4) generalize the connector-side poll loop from gmail to google_calendar, spotify, steam, google_health. 5) blind-spot preamble and expected_signals cite the horizon.

moves.title: The world's clock at the ingestion boundary: `occurred_at` with declared clock provenance
moves.why: Finding 2. `ingest.v1` has no field for when the observed thing happened; the Switchboard stamps `received_at = now()`; Home Assistant's real timestamp survives only as a substring of the dedupe key. Every non-message source — a Steam session, a health measurement, a bank posting, a photo, a backfilled 2019 receipt — has a true event time the connector already holds and drops. Owner-visible payoff: the timeline stops showing imported history as 'today', Chronicler's point events land at the instant they happened with a recorded precision, and 'what did I spend in January' can mean January.
moves.manifesto: Chronicler (MANIFESTO.md:19-24 — point events at an instant, and 'how precise the boundary is' recorded as provenance). No amendment needed; this is the field that manifesto clause has been describing without a home.
moves.integration_points: `roster/switchboard/tools/routing/contracts.py` — add `occurred_at: datetime | None` and `occurred_at_source: Literal['source_stated','connector_derived','receipt_only']` to IngestPayloadV1/IngestRequestContextV1 with tz-aware validators mirroring the existing `_validate_tz_aware`; `roster/switchboard/tools/ingestion/ingest.py:793` keeps `received_at` as the pipeline clock and stores occurred_at beside it; new core migration adding `occurred_at TIMESTAMPTZ` + `occurred_at_source TEXT` + index to `public.ingestion_events` (partitioning stays on received_at); every connector's envelope builder (home_assistant, gmail, telegram_bot, whatsapp, steam, spotify, owntracks, google_health, google_calendar, activitywatch, discord_user); Chronicler adapters and `roster/chronicler/` projection reads; `openspec/specs/connector-base-spec` ingest.v1 envelope requirement.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: HA publishes state.last_changed as occurred_at with source='source_stated'; the event sorts and projects at 17:40:09, not 17:40:10. Failure: a source that states no time → occurred_at is NULL and occurred_at_source='receipt_only'; readers MUST render 'observed at' rather than 'happened at', and MUST NOT substitute received_at into a 'happened' claim. Skew: a source-stated time more than a configured window in the future (or before the account's creation) is recorded verbatim plus `clock_skew_flagged` — never silently clamped, because a lying source is a fact about the source. Concurrency: dedupe is unchanged (dedupe_key), so two connectors reporting the same event with different occurred_at collapse to the first accepted row and the divergence is recorded on the losing attempt. Idempotence: replay of a stored envelope re-derives the identical occurred_at because it is in the payload, not the clock. Rollback: the column is additive and nullable; readers fall back to received_at only through one named helper so the fallback is greppable and testable.
moves.verification: roster/switchboard/tests/test_ingest_occurred_at.py::test_receipt_only_never_substitutes_pipeline_clock_into_happened_claim; tests/connectors/test_home_assistant_envelope.py::test_state_last_changed_becomes_occurred_at_source_stated; tests/connectors/test_envelope_contract_matrix.py::test_every_shipped_connector_declares_an_occurred_at_source (parametrized over the connector catalog — also the test that would have caught finding 9); roster/chronicler/tests/test_projection_boundary_precision.py::test_point_event_uses_occurred_at_and_records_precision.
moves.slice_plan: 1) contract + migration + ingest storage, receipt_only for everyone (no behavior change). 2) home_assistant, google_health, spotify, steam, owntracks declare source_stated (these are the sources whose event time is most wrong today). 3) chat/email connectors declare source_stated from message date headers. 4) Chronicler and the timeline read occurred_at; the 'observed at' vs 'happened at' distinction becomes a rendered contract. 5) spec delta + a lint that a new connector cannot ship without an occurred_at declaration.

moves.title: What each sense costs: a per-source cost boundary ledger and an admission budget at the gate
moves.why: architecture.md:277-300 makes connectors THE computational cost boundary, and the doctrine is enforced today by exactly one gate (group participant count). Nothing measures the boundary: the source-API counter is an epoch timestamp (finding 1), per-event cost is populated only when a human clicks (finding 6), and the only cost cap in the layer is buried in dormant backfill config. So the owner cannot answer 'what is this sense costing me?' and the fleet has no way to throttle a noisy source rather than a butler. Owner-visible payoff: a cost column on the connector roster ('WhatsApp: 4,100 admitted events, 61 sessions, $3.40 this week; HA: 380k events, 0 sessions, $0'), and a per-source weekly admission budget that degrades the noisy sense to summary-only instead of letting it drain the fleet.
moves.manifesto: about/heart-and-soul/architecture.md:277-300 (the cost boundary principle). The Switchboard staffer infrastructure contract (roster/switchboard/MANIFESTO.md) has no cost clause at all — this implies a manifesto amendment adding per-source admission accounting and budget enforcement as a named Switchboard responsibility with an SLA and a failure mode. Deliberately scoped to the perception boundary, not the per-butler spend ceiling that the spend-governance lane owns.
moves.integration_points: `src/butlers/connectors/heartbeat.py:343-370` (filter `_created` samples — slice 1 of this move); `src/butlers/api/routers/ingestion_events.py:760-779` (move cost_usd write-back out of the detail handler into the session-close path so every event is priced); new `public.source_cost_rollup` materialization joining ingestion_events → sessions → the spend ledger by request_id; new `GET /api/ingestion/connectors/{type}/{identity}/cost` and a column on `/summaries`; budget config in `switchboard.runtime_config` enforced in the connector filter gate (`src/butlers/connectors/*_filter.py`, base gate in connector-base-spec 'Source Filter Gate'); `openspec/specs/connector-base-spec` new requirement: Per-Source Admission Budget.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: every admitted event is priced when its sessions close; the roster shows 7-day cost per source; a source crossing 80% of its weekly budget raises an attention item; at 100% the gate admits only batch summaries and records `budget_exhausted` on every dropped event in connectors.filtered_events (never a silent drop). Failure: pricing unavailable (spend ledger degraded) → cost renders as a named unavailable, never as $0, and the budget gate fails OPEN with a recorded `budget_unenforced` reason, because starving perception on a metering outage is worse than overspending. Concurrency: two connector processes for one identity share one budget row — enforcement uses a single atomic decrement, and the loser of the race is throttled, not double-counted. Idempotence: re-pricing an already-priced event is a no-op keyed by request_id; the rollup is recomputable from scratch. Rollback: budgets ship disabled (NULL = unlimited) and the ledger is read-only until the owner sets one.
moves.verification: tests/connectors/test_heartbeat_counters.py::test_created_series_samples_excluded (assert against a real prometheus_client Counter that counters equal increments, not epoch); tests/api/test_source_cost_rollup.py::test_unpriced_events_render_unavailable_not_zero; tests/connectors/test_admission_budget.py::test_exhausted_budget_records_filtered_reason_for_every_dropped_event; tests/connectors/test_admission_budget.py::test_metering_outage_fails_open_and_records_budget_unenforced; live read seam: after slice 1, cross-summary total_messages_ingested must be < 1e6 for this instance.
moves.slice_plan: 1) fix the counter seam and backfill nothing (the historical rows are known-garbage; stamp a `counters_epoch_polluted_before` marker so old heartbeat_log deltas are not trusted). 2) price every event at session close; kill the click-triggered write-back. 3) source_cost_rollup + roster column + detail panel. 4) budget config + gate enforcement + attention item. 5) Switchboard manifesto amendment.

moves.title: A silent sense opens a case that names the promise it broke
moves.why: Finding 8: the Telegram user client has been offline since 2026-07-18 and the fleet case ledger is empty, because cases are only ever opened by an LLM session. Vision's success markers require the system to surface what matters unasked (vision.md:136) and the north star forbids failure impersonating health. The missing half is consequence: the owner does not care that a heartbeat stopped, he cares that Relationship stopped seeing his personal Telegram interactions. `expected_signals.producer_endpoint_identity` (core_211) already maps signals to exact source identities, so the promise-to-sense map is computable today. Owner-visible payoff within a week: one case that reads 'Telegram user client dark 56 days — Relationship interaction history has no personal-Telegram evidence since 18 Jul', with the last good observation as its opening evidence.
moves.manifesto: Switchboard staffer infrastructure contract (failure modes and escalation are its defining clauses per vision.md:24-29); Relationship (MANIFESTO.md:30 interaction history) and Home/Health as the promise-holders the case names. RFC 0032 fleet cases is the substrate.
moves.integration_points: New deterministic sweep `src/butlers/jobs/source_lapse.py` (zero-LLM context-producer shape, mirrors butlers.jobs.context_producers) reading `public.v_qa_connector_state` + `public.expected_signals` + `switchboard.connector_registry`; `src/butlers/core/fleet_cases.py:631` `open_case` gains a deterministic caller with a stable correlation_key (`source_lapse:{connector_type}:{endpoint_identity}`); evidence rows via `public.fleet_case_evidence`; the consequence sentence derives from expected_signals rows whose `producer_endpoint_identity` matches, joined to the declaring butler; surfaces on the existing `/api/switchboard/cases` read API and attention strip.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: a runtime_instance whose liveness has been offline beyond its declared cadence opens one case; the case lists each expected_signal it feeds and each butler that declared it; when the source returns, the sweep posts a resolution contribution and closes the case with the outage duration recorded. Failure: liveness itself unreadable → no case is opened and the sweep records `lapse_evaluation_unavailable` (an unreadable instrument must not manufacture an outage). Concurrency: correlation_key makes reopening idempotent — `find_open_case` before `open_case`, exactly as the core tool already does. Idempotence: a sweep run adds at most one evidence row per source per run, keyed by (case_id, evaluated_at bucket). Rollback: the sweep is a schedule row; disabling it stops case creation and leaves existing cases inspectable. Deliberate scope guard: a `checkpoint`-role row can never open a case (registry_roles semantics), and a source in `retired` state (see the retirement move) opens none either.
moves.verification: tests/jobs/test_source_lapse_sweep.py::test_offline_runtime_instance_opens_one_case_with_named_consequence; ::test_unreadable_liveness_opens_no_case_and_records_reason; ::test_checkpoint_role_never_opens_a_case; ::test_returning_source_closes_case_with_outage_duration; live seam after ship: /api/switchboard/cases must contain a case for telegram:user:@Tzeusy.
moves.slice_plan: 1) the promise map (expected_signals → declaring butler → owner-readable consequence string) as a pure function with tests. 2) the sweep opening and closing cases. 3) consequence rendered on the connector roster and the attention strip. 4) escalation: a case older than a configured age gets an owner signal through the existing approval/notify spine.

moves.title: The camera roll as dated, placed observation: a self-hosted photo-library source
moves.why: With the vision lane shipped (#4122) and captionless media envelopes accepted (#4128), the owner's photo library is the single largest untapped personal signal and the only one that pays four butlers at once: receipts and price tags → Finance, meals → Health, whiteboards and book pages → Education and the capture() ledger (#4121), faces → Relationship, EXIF time+place → Chronicler and Travel corroboration. Google Photos is not the route: since 2025-03-31 the Library API returns only app-created data and library access requires the interactive Picker API — so the sovereign route (vision.md:60-63) is a self-hosted library (Immich or equivalent) the owner already runs, read over its own API on the LAN. Owner-visible payoff: photograph a receipt, and Finance has the transaction with the merchant, amount and the place you were standing.
moves.manifesto: Chronicler (MANIFESTO.md:19-24 — dated evidence with provenance and boundary precision; it explicitly has no connector of its own and reads what others capture); Finance (MANIFESTO.md:14,30 — a second source of transaction evidence, searchable spending); Health and Relationship as downstream readers. No new butler and no amendment: the connector is Switchboard-owned transport, the observations route through existing triage.
