moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: new asset since cursor → metadata envelope with occurred_at, GPS, content hash, lazy blob ref → triage routes a receipt-shaped image to Finance, which calls attachment_view and records a transaction bound to the photo as evidence. Failure: library unreachable → heartbeat degraded with reason, cursor unmoved, expected_signal absent (and, with the lapse move, a case). Volume gating (the cost-boundary duty): a 40k-asset library must not admit 40k events — the connector admits on owner-declared rules (favourites, named albums, screenshots-with-text, assets whose EXIF places them outside home) and records every non-admitted asset in filtered_events with its reason, so the coverage window stays honest about what was skipped and why. Concurrency: two library syncs advancing the same cursor are serialized by the registry row; a re-import after a library restore dedupes on content hash. Idempotence: same photo, new asset id → one event. Rollback: disconnect follows the retirement move — blobs the connector fetched are enumerated in the retention statement.

moves.title: One external-action contract so every new source is two-way on day one
moves.why: Finding 7 (and vision rule 7, vision.md:113-118): the read side has a rigorous transport boundary, and the write side has none. email.py opens SMTP to smtp.gmail.com, calendar.py calls the Google REST API, telegram.py calls the Bot API — each with its own auth, retry, and error story, and only calendar.py has a real idempotency ledger (its `_prepare_workspace_mutation` / projection-action machinery, unreferenced anywhere else). So 'what can my butlers actually DO?' has no answer, no receipt, and no reversal, and every new source costs a bespoke write path. Owner-visible payoff: one Actions surface listing every real-world verb the fleet holds, each execution leaving a receipt with the external id, and every irreversible one bound to the approval spine that already exists (#4120 prepared actions).
moves.manifesto: about/heart-and-soul/vision.md:113-118 (rule 7 — transport is connector responsibility) read as covering egress, which today it does not; the Switchboard staffer contract owns the boundary. Implies either an RFC extending rule 7 to actions or an explicit documented carve-out — the current silence is what let three modules grow their own transport.
moves.integration_points: New `src/butlers/actions/` core primitive: an ActionSpec registry (source, verb, args schema, reversibility, consequence class), an `external_actions` ledger table (idempotency_key, request_id, motivating insight/case id, status applied/noop/failed/pending, external_id, receipt payload, reversal_of), and a shared executor generalizing `calendar.py:9527-9552`; module write tools become thin ActionSpec declarations (`modules/email.py`, `calendar.py`, `spotify.py`, `telegram.py`, `home_assistant` service calls with their existing risk map); approval binding through the existing pending_actions/park_pending_action path; `GET /api/actions` + receipts on the session detail page; new `openspec/specs/external-action-contract/spec.md`.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: a session calls an action verb → executor mints an idempotency key from (verb, request_id) → consequence class decides direct-execute vs approval-park → provider call → ledger row applied with the external id → receipt rendered on the session and on the motivating insight. Failure: provider 5xx → status failed with the provider's own error preserved verbatim; a timeout with unknown outcome is `indeterminate`, never retried blind, and surfaced to the owner as such. Concurrency: two sessions issuing the same verb for the same request_id → the second gets the first's stored result flagged idempotent_replay (calendar's proven semantics, now shared). Idempotence: replay of an applied action returns the receipt without a provider call. Rollback: reversible actions record a reversal verb and the ledger links reversal_of; irreversible ones must declare so and are approval-gated by construction — an ActionSpec with neither a reversal nor an irreversibility declaration fails registration at daemon start.
moves.verification: tests/actions/test_action_registry.py::test_spec_without_reversal_or_irreversibility_declaration_fails_registration; tests/actions/test_executor_idempotence.py::test_duplicate_verb_same_request_id_returns_receipt_without_provider_call; ::test_indeterminate_timeout_is_never_auto_retried_and_is_owner_visible; tests/modules/test_calendar_actions_migrated.py::test_calendar_mutations_use_shared_ledger_and_preserve_existing_semantics; tests/actions/test_approval_binding.py::test_irreversible_action_parks_on_approval_spine.
moves.slice_plan: 1) lift calendar's ledger into src/butlers/actions/ with its tests intact and re-point calendar.py at it (behavior-preserving). 2) ActionSpec registry + registration-time validation + the /api/actions read surface. 3) migrate telegram, spotify, HA service calls. 4) migrate email send (also the moment to decide whether SMTP moves behind a connector-owned egress process, per rule 7). 5) receipts bound to the motivating insight/case, closing the loop with #4120.

moves.title: Retiring a sense honestly: revoke, state what remains, and retire the signals it fed
moves.why: Finding 3. Disconnect today soft-deletes one row while the credential stays live, the provider grant stays granted, the ingested data goes unmentioned, and every expected_signal that source fed silently becomes `producer_unregistered` — the same state as a source that never existed. Sovereignty (vision.md:60-63) is precisely the promise that the owner knows what he holds and what he has given away. Owner-visible payoff: retiring Spotify produces a receipt — 'authorization revoked at the provider; credential deleted; 41,220 play rows and 3 blobs retained under the Taste ledger; 2 Chronicler signals now marked source retired' — and nothing afterwards claims those signals are merely unmeasurable.
moves.manifesto: about/heart-and-soul/vision.md:60-63 (rule 1, full sovereignty) and rule 6's binding-manifesto clause, since retirement withdraws evidence that butler promises depend on; Switchboard staffer contract owns the lifecycle ceremony.
moves.integration_points: `src/butlers/api/routers/ingestion_connectors.py:1947-2072` (disconnect) gains a pre-flight retention inventory and a post-approval retirement pipeline; provider revocation via the existing OAuth clients (`src/butlers/api/routers/spotify.py:820`, `google_health.py:919` — the deliberate non-revocation there becomes an explicit owner choice, not a hidden default); credential deletion through the entity_info/secrets passport path; new `retired` value on `connector_registry` (or `retired_at`) that `v_qa_connector_state` exposes rather than filters, so `src/butlers/core/expected_signals.py:49-83` can return a distinct `producer_retired` reason; a retirement receipt row + render on the connector page and the audit log; spec delta to connector-base-spec ('THEN the record persists in connector_registry for historical visibility' — extended with retirement semantics).
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: owner requests disconnect → pre-flight shows exactly what will be revoked, what will be deleted, and what will be retained and where (row counts per table, blob counts) → approval → revoke at provider, delete credential, mark retired, write receipt, mark dependent expected_signals `producer_retired`. Failure: provider revocation call fails → the retirement completes locally but the receipt says 'provider authorization could NOT be revoked — revoke manually at <url>' and the connector stays flagged until the owner confirms; a partial retirement is never reported as clean. Concurrency: a heartbeat arriving after retirement does not resurrect the row — it is rejected with `identity_retired` and recorded, because a process that did not get the memo is a fact worth seeing. Idempotence: re-retiring is a no-op returning the original receipt. Rollback: a retired identity can be re-adopted only by an explicit re-connect that mints a new credential and records the gap in the coverage window, never by a silent heartbeat.
moves.verification: tests/api/test_connector_retirement.py::test_preflight_inventory_counts_every_table_the_source_wrote; ::test_provider_revocation_failure_produces_partial_receipt_not_success; ::test_retired_source_signals_read_producer_retired_not_unregistered; ::test_post_retirement_heartbeat_is_rejected_and_recorded; tests/core/test_expected_signals.py::test_retired_reason_is_distinct_from_unregistered.
moves.slice_plan: 1) the retention inventory as a read-only pre-flight (owner sees the truth before anything changes). 2) `producer_retired` plumbed through v_qa_connector_state and expected_signals. 3) provider revocation + credential deletion + the receipt. 4) heartbeat rejection for retired identities. 5) an owner-initiated 'and delete the data' option, honouring the memory retention-policy machinery rather than inventing a second deletion path.

audits.ideal: A world-class connector layer would make every external source a *declared instrument* rather than a pipe. Each source would publish, on every heartbeat, four facts the owner and every session can read: what it is authorized to observe (scopes and consent, already half-built), how far back it can see and where its coverage has holes, what it costs to keep warm (external calls, admitted events, and the downstream sessions those events caused, fenced by an admission budget enforced at the gate the doctrine already names as the cost boundary), and what it can *do*, not just report — a registry of real-world verbs with idempotency keys, receipts carrying the external id, declared reversibility, and approval binding for anything irreversible. Every event it emits would carry two clocks — when the world produced it and when the pipeline saw it — with the provenance of the first stated, so history can be imported without lying about its date and the Chronicler can honour its own promise of point events at an instant with recorded precision. Backfill would be an ordinary owner verb with a cost cap and a receipt, not a dormant subsystem; a source falling silent would deterministically open a fleet case that names the butler promise it just broke rather than waiting for a session to notice; and retirement would be a ceremony that revokes at the provider, deletes the credential, states exactly what data remains and where, and marks the signals it fed as *retired* rather than quietly unmeasurable. In that system the owner adds a new sense — a self-hosted photo library, a bank feed, a code-forge — by declaring it once, and coverage, cost, consequence, actions and retirement all come for free.

audits.ideal: A JARVIS-grade spawn is a witnessed contract. Before the model runs, the daemon deterministically composes an identity segment whose every source is named and hashed, an envelope the session can read (model, tier, deadline, tool-call ceiling), a perception layer that states what is currently unmeasurable and what this butler already did in the last day, and a capability card that tells the session, per tool, whether calling it will execute, park for owner approval, or be refused — before a token is spent guessing. After the model runs, the same seam emits a receipt: the exact prompt-layer inventory by digest, the effects the session actually produced in the world with their settlement status, and the measured difficulty of the work. Those receipts close two loops the owner can see: identity drift (a butler running instructions that are not its git identity raises a condition rather than waiting to be noticed) and routing fit (a task that routinely exhausts its ceiling proposes its own tier change through the improvement-proposal spine instead of quietly failing at 12% a week). Tiers name purposes that actually differ — a local lane that keeps private message content on the owner's own hardware, a reasoning lane for repair, a workhorse lane for everything else — and the dashboard can state, in one line per tier, which model each resolves to right now. Nothing in this requires the daemon to reason: every layer is a deterministic projection of state the system already holds, which is precisely what doctrine Rule 4 reserves for the daemon.
audits.jarvis_gap: Today the spawn seam is a good gate chain wrapped around an unwitnessed prompt. Since run 12 two real perception layers landed — the blind-spot preamble (#4123) and the task-continuity ledger — but the first declares patterns for exactly one module (blind_spot_declarations.py:23-25) and the second only serves named scheduled tasks, so the marginal perception a routed session gained in a week is approximately zero. What is still invisible to the session: which of its own tools will park for approval before it spends a turn composing the payload (gate.py:124-165 injects _why but never says the tool is gated, while roster/shared/AGENTS.md:73-77 instructs it to use "advertised" metadata that is not advertised); what it already did in the last day; and what instructions it is actually running under. What is invisible to the owner is worse: the composed prompt leaves no digest, no source identity, no layer inventory anywhere (spawner.py:1916-1979 -> :2097), the only owner-facing prompt view asserts "No system prompt configured." for all thirteen agents while each runs ~21KB of roster identity (butler_management.py:160-201; ButlerManagementTab.tsx:273), and one save in that editor silently replaces that identity wholesale (skills.py:186-195). On the routing side the classification the Switchboard pays for on every segment resolves cheap and workhorse to the same gpt-5.6-luna (live catalog; 401/500 recent sessions), and SPECIALTY doubles as both the self-healing lane and the connector-discretion lane, so private WhatsApp, Telegram and live-listener content is classified by the cloud reasoning model while the enabled local 9B sits at priority 10 and never runs. The gap to the ideal is not more gates; it is receipts — of identity, of capability, of effects, of fit — and one honest separation of purpose from capability in the catalog.
audits.live_verification: Live (read-only, http://127.0.0.1:42200): /api/butlers (13 agents online); /api/sessions/aggregate?period=week (23,658 sessions, 88.7% success, 3.34B input tokens); /api/sessions?limit=500 (complexity x model distribution: 401 sessions on gpt-5.6-luna across cheap+workhorse); /api/settings/models (full enabled catalog per tier, extra_args, priorities, session_timeout_s, routing scores); /api/butlers/{finance,switchboard,messenger,health}/model-overrides (all empty); /api/butlers/finance/prompt ({"prompt":"","version":0}); /api/permissions (all cells inherited, no explicit rows); /api/approvals?limit=200 (200 rows; 1 pending with push_outcome=failed; 176 messenger auto-approved owner-target) and /api/approvals/rules (total 0); /api/spend (by_butler contains the WhatsApp group JID; by_model gpt-5.6-sol). Statically confirmed from source: prompt composition and its absence of provenance, fail-open override fetch, approval gate wrapping and schema injection, discretion dispatcher tier and ledger butler_name, resolve_model priority semantics, blind-spot registry, undelivered-reply guardrail, spend grouping. No writes of any kind were issued. Stack reachable throughout.

moves.title: Effective-prompt receipt and roster-drift sentinel: every session records which instruction bytes ran, and the fleet raises a condition when a butler is not running its git identity
moves.why: Vision Rule 5 (about/heart-and-soul/vision.md:92-101) makes git roster content the source of butler identity and Rule 6 (:103-111) makes the manifesto binding — yet skills.py:186-195 lets one database row replace the whole roster chain, spawner.py:1916-1979 composes six more layers, and nothing anywhere records what was actually sent (grep for prompt digest/sha in src/ returns nothing; open PR #4043 adds only chars/4 token estimates). docs/plans/system-prompt-authority-decision.md maps the ten entry points and proposes an ownership contract, but proposes no per-session record and no drift detector, so even after that packet lands nobody can prove which prompt a given session ran. Owner payoff inside a week: the butler detail page stops saying "No system prompt configured." and instead shows the resolved identity chain with each include's path and digest; every session detail answers "which instructions produced this answer"; and the roster board flags any butler whose live identity segment is not its git identity.
moves.manifesto: Serves doctrine directly rather than one butler: vision.md Rules 5 and 6, plus openspec/specs/butler-base-spec (CLAUDE.md as System Prompt Entry Point) and openspec/specs/core-spawner (System Prompt Composition). It implies the amendment already drafted in docs/plans/system-prompt-authority-decision.md § Proposed governing amendment contract — this move is its observability half and should be specified alongside it, not instead of it.
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/core/spawner_context.py:110-150 (_compose_system_prompt returns a ComposedPrompt carrying per-layer {layer_id, source_ref, bytes, sha256} instead of a bare string; PR #4043's ComposedPrompt is the natural host); src/butlers/core/skills.py:166-198 + process_system_prompt_base (return the resolved include set: each file path plus its blob digest, and whether the shared include was present); src/butlers/core/spawner.py:1916-1979, :2097 (persist the inventory beside the session row); new forward core migration public.session_prompt_provenance(session_id PK, butler_name, composed_sha256, identity_source ENUM roster|overlay|generated_default, overlay_version, include_refs JSONB, layer_inventory JSONB, roster_head_sha256) with per-schema RLS matching sessions; new GET /api/butlers/{name}/prompt/effective returning the resolved chain + layer inventory (src/butlers/api/routers/butler_management.py, beside :160-201); frontend/src/components/butler-detail/ButlerManagementTab.tsx:228-297 (render identity segment vs overlay as two distinct blocks; the edit modal at :297 gains an explicit consequence statement); src/butlers/core/infra_conditions.py for the drift condition; SessionDetailPage prompt-provenance row.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: spawn composes layers, digests each, writes one provenance row in the same transaction as the session row; identity_source='roster', roster_head_sha256 == composed identity digest, no condition. Overlay present: identity_source='overlay', overlay_version recorded, drift condition raised at INFO with the butler named — a deliberate overlay is visible, not alarming. Failure: the override fetch fails open (spawner_context.py:214-254) — provenance records identity_source='roster' plus degraded_reason='overlay_unavailable', so the silent identity swap becomes readable; a provenance write failure never blocks the spawn but sets the session's provenance to 'unrecorded' rather than fabricating a digest. Concurrency: two sessions spawning while the owner saves a new overlay version each record the version they actually read; no shared mutable state. Idempotence: provenance is keyed by session_id and written once; a redispatch after failover keeps the same row because the prompt is composed once outside the failover loop (spawner.py:1975 precedes the loop at :2079). Rollback: the table and the endpoint are additive; dropping the reader restores today's behavior with no data loss, and the composition function's string output is unchanged.

moves.title: Gate-honest tool surface: mark gated tools as gated, and give sessions preflight_effect() so they learn execute/park/deny before spending a turn
moves.why: roster/shared/AGENTS.md:73-77 instructs every session to supply "its advertised _why" on approval-gated tools, but gate.py:124-165 advertises only the four dossier parameters and never says the tool is gated, and gate.py:510-541 leaves the description untouched. With zero standing rules live (GET /api/approvals/rules -> total 0), every non-owner-targeted call among messenger's seven gated tools (roster/messenger/butler.toml:77-97) parks after the session has already composed the payload. The Messenger manifesto makes it the sole owner of outbound delivery with a 48h approval expiry and medium risk tier (roster/messenger/MANIFESTO.md:17, 78-79) — an owner-facing promise its own sessions cannot see. Owner payoff inside a week: sessions say "I have prepared this; it needs your approval" in the same turn instead of discovering the gate; fewer half-finished outbound attempts; and the session can choose the owner-targeted path (auto-approved) when that is the right answer.
moves.manifesto: roster/messenger/MANIFESTO.md (outbound delivery ownership and approval SLAs), roster/home/MANIFESTO.md via the PROTECTED actuation classes, roster/relationship and roster/switchboard gated tools. No amendment needed — this makes an existing binding contract legible to the agent bound by it.
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/modules/approvals/gate.py:124-165 (extend the schema injection to a deterministic description suffix naming risk tier, expiry hours, and the owner-target exemption) and :510-541 (apply it at wrap time); new core tool preflight_effect(tool_name, args) in src/butlers/core_tools/ (a new _preflight.py registered in the infra group, src/butlers/daemon.py:154 area) that composes the existing pure helpers — approvals/gate.py match_standing_rule (:230-289), _unpinned_safety_critical_args (:167-213), _extract_channel_identity (:290+), butlers.identity.resolve_contact_by_channel, and butlers.core.permissions.check_permission — and returns {'verdict': 'would_execute'|'would_park'|'would_deny', 'rule_id', 'risk_tier', 'expiry_hours', 'unpinned_args', 'permission'} with no writes; src/butlers/core/spawner_context.py adds one deterministic capability line to the composed prompt ('N of your tools are approval-gated; M permissions are revoked'), sourced from ApprovalConfig.gated_tools and public.permissions; specs: openspec/specs/core-modules (Approval metadata remains authoritative) and the in-flight openspec/changes/add-runtime-tool-surface-discovery/specs/core-tool-discovery/spec.md:259-268, which preserves the approval path but does not advertise it — this move belongs in that change's spec surface as a sibling requirement.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: a messenger session calls preflight_effect('telegram_send_message', {chat_id: <non-owner>}) and gets would_park with risk_tier=medium, expiry 48h; it drafts, calls the tool once, and reports the parked state to the owner in the same turn. Owner target: preflight returns would_execute (the gate's owner auto-approve branch), matching the 176 live auto-approved messenger actions. Failure: contact resolution or the rules query fails — preflight returns verdict='unknown' with the reason and never claims would_execute; the real gate remains the only authority, so an optimistic or pessimistic preflight can never widen or narrow what actually happens. Concurrency: a standing rule created between preflight and the call changes only the direction of surprise (would_park -> executes); preflight is read-only so there is no lock to hold and no lease to leak. Idempotence: pure read; repeated calls with identical args return identical verdicts and write nothing (no PendingAction, no autonomy_approval_history row, no fingerprint). Rollback: the description suffix is generated at registration and disappears when the module is disabled; the tool is registered in one group and can be removed without touching the gate.
moves.verification: tests for gate registration asserting every gated tool's rendered description contains the tier/expiry/exemption clause and that ungated tools are untouched; a preflight-vs-gate equivalence test that, for a table of (tool, args, rules, contact role, permission) cases, asserts preflight's verdict equals the gate wrapper's actual branch — the real seam, not a parallel reimplementation; a no-side-effect test asserting preflight leaves pending_actions, autonomy_approval_history and the approval event log byte-identical; a roster/messenger integration test that a non-owner send preceded by preflight parks exactly one action.
moves.slice_plan: S1: description suffix at wrap time (pure registration change, no new tool). S2: preflight_effect as an infra core tool plus the equivalence test against the gate branch table. S3: the spawn-time capability line in the composed prompt. S4: shared AGENTS.md updated to point at preflight_effect so the 'advertised metadata' instruction finally has a referent.

moves.title: Session effects manifest: one per-session record of what actually changed in the world, and a 24h effects digest every session reads at spawn
moves.why: The system already knows every consequential thing a session did — it is scattered across pending_actions, home actuation receipts, notify delivery outcomes, calendar writes and captured tool calls — and joins none of it. spawner_guardrails.py:198-239 proves the seam exists and works for exactly one case (an interactive reply attempted and never delivered), while a session that never attempted is exempted at :229-231 and recorded as a success. Nothing tells the next session what the last one already did, so duplicate outreach is structurally possible and invisible. Owner payoff inside a week: every session detail carries a plain "what changed" list with settlement status (executed / parked / failed / unverified), and butlers stop repeating an act they already performed because the spawn preamble states it.
moves.manifesto: Serves the whole roster; the sharpest instances are roster/messenger/MANIFESTO.md:17 (sole owner of outbound delivery — its effects are the fleet's most consequential) and roster/home/MANIFESTO.md's PROTECTED actuation classes, whose receipts already exist per roster/home/migrations/002_home_actuation_receipts.py but have no cross-butler home. No amendment implied; it is the evidence spine the manifestos already assume.
moves.integration_points: new forward core migration public.session_effects(id, session_id FK, butler_name, tool_name, effect_class ENUM read|internal_write|external_write|irreversible, target_ref, status ENUM executed|parked|failed|unverified, receipt_ref, occurred_at) with per-schema RLS; classification is deterministic from data already held — ApprovalConfig risk tier + Module.tool_metadata() ToolMeta.arg_sensitivities (src/butlers/modules/base.py) + the notify delivery outcome the guardrail already parses (spawner_guardrails.py:229-239); written at src/butlers/core/spawner.py:2621-2660 from the captured tool_calls, next to session_complete; read back into the prompt by a new fetch_recent_effects_digest in src/butlers/core/spawner_context.py composed as one more enumerated layer; API GET /api/sessions/{id}/effects and a session-detail panel; specs openspec/specs/core-sessions (session record contents) and openspec/specs/core-spawner (composition layer list).
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: a session sends one approved message and creates one calendar event; two rows land with status executed and their receipt refs; the next spawn of that butler reads 'in the last 24h you sent 1 message to <entity> and created 1 event'. Parked: the gated call returns pending_approval and the row lands status=parked with the pending_actions id — the owner sees the intent even though nothing left the system. Failure: tool-call capture is partial (a runtime that reports no tool calls) — the manifest records effect_class='unknown' with a degraded flag rather than asserting zero effects, because 'nothing happened' and 'we could not see' must not share a rendering. Concurrency: two sessions of the same butler run under the semaphore (spawner.py:447-452); each writes its own rows keyed by session_id, and the digest reader takes a snapshot at spawn, so a sibling's later effect simply appears in the next digest. Idempotence: rows are derived once from the final tool_calls list, keyed (session_id, tool_call_id); a replay or failover retry that re-invokes the same logical session cannot double-write. Rollback: additive table plus one prompt layer behind a runtime_config flag (mirroring blind_spot_preamble_enabled at spawner.py:1955-1971); disabling the flag restores today's prompt byte-for-byte.
moves.verification: a spawner test asserting that a session whose tool_calls include one gated call returning pending_approval produces exactly one parked row with the right pending_actions ref; a test that a runtime reporting zero tool calls produces a degraded manifest, never an empty one; extend tests/core covering _check_undelivered_interactive_reply so an undelivered notify appears as status=failed in the manifest and still fails the session; a real-Postgres round trip for RLS and the 24h digest query; a prompt-composition test that the digest layer is byte-identical no-op text when the window is empty (cache stability, the same discipline the blind-spot layer documents).
moves.slice_plan: S1: deterministic effect classification as a pure function over (tool_calls, ApprovalConfig, ToolMeta) with a table-driven test. S2: migration + write at session_complete + GET /api/sessions/{id}/effects. S3: session-detail panel. S4: the 24h digest layer at spawn behind a runtime_config flag.

moves.title: Tier-fit calibration: measure how hard the work actually was, show what each tier resolves to today, and let the fleet propose its own re-tiering
moves.why: openspec/specs/complexity-classification promises "cost-efficient model selection proportional to task difficulty", but live evidence shows the cheap and workhorse tiers resolving to the same gpt-5.6-luna for 401 of the last 500 sessions, local and legacy holding zero enabled entries, and every tier sharing session_timeout_s=1800 — so the classification the Switchboard pays for on every segment buys a reasoning-effort flag and nothing the owner can see. Meanwhile the evidence needed to judge fit is already recorded per attempt (model_dispatch_attempts duration and tool_call_count, sessions success/duration/tokens, guardrail terminations) and is used only to rank candidates WITHIN a tier (model_routing.py:1577-1585), never to question the tier itself. Owner payoff inside a week: a Models-tab line per tier reading 'cheap -> gpt-5.6-luna (effort high) — same model as workhorse', and a weekly proposal such as 'chronicler memory-consolidation has hit its ceiling 4 of 5 runs at workhorse; move it to reasoning?' arriving on the improvement-proposal spine for one-tap approval.
moves.manifesto: roster/switchboard/MANIFESTO.md:18 (message classification is Switchboard's named responsibility, with a <5s p99 classification SLO at :37) — this move is what makes that classification consequential. It rides the merged unified improvement-proposals spine (#4125) rather than implying a new butler.
moves.integration_points: read side: public.model_dispatch_attempts (duration_ms, tool_call_count, outcome — written at src/butlers/core/spawner.py:2685-2700), public.sessions (complexity, success, duration_ms, tokens), guardrail terminations from spawner_guardrails._check_tool_call_budget/_check_token_budget; new rollup view or table public.tier_fit_observations keyed (butler_name, trigger_source, task_name, classified_tier) with n, ceiling-hit rate, p50/p95 duration against catalog session_timeout_s, failover count, success rate; a scheduled core job (src/butlers/jobs/) emitting proposals through the improvement-proposal spine; API GET /api/settings/models/tier-resolution returning, per tier, the entry resolution would pick right now (reusing model_routing.resolve_model's ordering, not a reimplementation) plus a collapsed-tier flag when two tiers share a model_id; frontend SettingsModelsPage tier header; specs openspec/specs/complexity-classification (add a Tier Fit Observation requirement) and openspec/specs/core-sessions.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: a task with n>=5 runs at one tier and a ceiling-hit rate above threshold produces one proposal naming the task, the evidence, and the suggested tier; the owner approves and the scheduled task's complexity changes. Insufficient data: fewer than the minimum runs yields no verdict and the surface says 'insufficient history (n=3, need >= 5)' — reusing the exact honesty the catalog's routing_score_insufficient_data already shows live. Failure: the rollup query fails — the tier board renders unavailable rather than zero, and no proposal is emitted (an absent proposal is safe; a fabricated one is not). Concurrency: the job is idempotent per window and takes an advisory lock; a proposal already open for the same (task, tier) is updated with fresh evidence rather than duplicated. Idempotence: proposals are keyed by (butler, task_name, from_tier, to_tier, window) so re-running the job the same day changes nothing. Rollback: the observation table and the tier-resolution endpoint are read-only additions; disabling the job stops proposals with no state to unwind, and no proposal ever changes routing without owner approval.
moves.verification: a pure test over synthetic attempt/session rows asserting the verdict thresholds and the insufficient-data refusal; a test that the tier-resolution endpoint's answer equals what resolve_model actually returns for the same catalog state (equivalence at the real seam) including the collapsed-tier flag for the live cheap/workhorse case; a job test asserting idempotence across two runs in one window and non-duplication against an open proposal; a real-Postgres test of the rollup under a mixed-tier week.
moves.slice_plan: S1: GET /api/settings/models/tier-resolution + the Models-tab line (immediately shows the cheap==workhorse collapse; no new tables). S2: the observation rollup and its honesty states. S3: the proposal job on the improvement-proposal spine. S4: owner approval applying a tier change to a scheduled task.

moves.title: Separate purpose from capability in the catalog so the local lane is reachable: private message triage stops going to the cloud reasoning model
moves.why: public.model_catalog's complexity_tier is doing two incompatible jobs. SPECIALTY is both the self-healing lane (src/butlers/core/healing/dispatch.py:667,1285) and the connector-discretion lane (discretion_dispatcher.py:181-194, :345-355), and resolution is strictly by priority within a tier (model_routing.py:1564-1585), so healing-codex (gpt-5.6-sol, priority 30) always beats discretion-qwen3.5-9b (ollama/qwen3.5:9b, priority 10). Live /api/spend confirms the consequence: the WhatsApp group identity's discretion spend is priced against gpt-5.6-sol. Every WhatsApp, Telegram, live-listener and Home Assistant discretion call — the most private content the system touches — goes to an external reasoning CLI while the owner's enabled local model never runs. Vision Rule 1 (vision.md:60-64) makes sovereignty non-negotiable and the anti-patterns list (:146-147) warns against designs that require the network at daemon level. Owner payoff inside a week: private chat triage runs on the owner's own hardware, healing keeps the model it needs, and the tier vocabulary starts meaning capability again.
moves.manifesto: Doctrine-level (vision.md Rule 1 sovereignty; Rule 4 daemon determinism, since purpose is a deterministic property of the caller, not a judgment). Touches openspec/specs/complexity-classification (the six-tier enum is capability; purpose is a second, orthogonal axis) and openspec/specs/core-spawner model resolution. It also removes the latent hazard that an emptied cheap tier falls through to specialty and lands trivial work on the healing reasoning model.
moves.integration_points: forward core migration adding public.model_catalog.purpose_lane TEXT NULL (values: general, discretion, healing, classification) with a partial unique/priority ordering per (complexity_tier, purpose_lane), backfilled from the existing aliases (healing-codex -> healing, discretion-qwen3.5-9b -> discretion, trivial-* -> general); src/butlers/core/model_routing.py:1564-1660 (resolve_model / resolve_model_with_effective_tier gain a purpose_lane parameter that filters candidates before priority ordering, defaulting to general and falling back to general only when the requested lane is empty, never the reverse); callers src/butlers/connectors/discretion_dispatcher.py:345-355 (purpose_lane='discretion'), src/butlers/core/healing/dispatch.py:667,1285 (purpose_lane='healing'), roster/switchboard/tools/routing/structured_classify.py; src/butlers/api/routers/model_settings.py:520 (catalog list and the Models tab gain the lane column); also fix src/butlers/connectors/discretion_dispatcher.py:562 so the ledger's butler_name is the constructor's butler_name and the connector identity lands in a separate column, which is what puts a WhatsApp JID in /api/spend by_butler today.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: a WhatsApp discretion call resolves ollama/qwen3.5:9b; a healing dispatch resolves gpt-5.6-sol; neither can select the other's entry. Empty lane: the requested lane has no enabled entry — resolution falls back to the general lane in the same tier with a recorded fallback reason, so a missing local model degrades to today's behavior loudly rather than silently. Failure: the local runtime is down — same-tier failover inside the discretion lane runs first, then the recorded general fallback; the ledger row names the lane and the fallback so the owner can see when privacy degraded. Concurrency: resolution is a read plus the existing round-robin counter, which becomes per (tier, lane) so one lane's traffic cannot starve another's rotation. Idempotence: pure resolution; the migration is a backfill of a nullable column and re-running it is a no-op. Rollback: purpose_lane NULL means 'general', so old code ignoring the column resolves exactly as today; reverting the callers restores current routing without touching rows.
moves.verification: a resolution test table asserting that (SPECIALTY, discretion) never returns a healing entry and vice versa, and that an empty lane falls back to general with the reason recorded; a test that the round-robin counter is keyed per (tier, lane); an integration test that DiscretionDispatcher's resolved model_id for a whatsapp identity is the ollama entry given the live-shaped catalog fixture; a ledger test asserting butler_name is the rostered name and the connector identity lands in its own column, plus an /api/spend test that by_butler contains only rostered names; a real-Postgres migration test covering the alias backfill and idempotent re-run.
moves.slice_plan: S1: migration + backfill + catalog API/UI column (no resolution change; the owner can see the lanes). S2: resolve_model lane filtering with general fallback, behind the default that preserves today's answer for unlaned callers. S3: repoint the discretion and healing callers, with the ledger identity split. S4: /api/spend by_butler key-space test and the Models-tab lane rendering.

findings.title: Curriculum receipt claims "Ready — the curriculum was created" on the mere existence of an empty mind_maps row
findings.detail: _correlate_curriculum settles the receipt from `SELECT id FROM education.mind_maps WHERE created_at >= $1 ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1` — a row, any row. It never counts nodes, never requires a teaching flow, and never checks status. The receipt then settles `status='completed'`, and the read side renders badge "Ready" plus "The curriculum for C++ was created". Live on main: GET /api/education/curriculum-requests/latest returns status=completed, mind_map_id=aa778538-29e8-4211-b06c-7a59881d73af, calibration_ready_at=null, calibration_notice_outcome=null, settled 2026-08-23; GET /api/education/mind-maps shows that map with "nodes":[], "edges":[]; GET /api/education/flows returns exactly one flow and it is not this map. So the only "Ready" curriculum the owner has is an empty title with no flow, no calibration and no proof anyone was told. Critically, the pending change openspec/changes/education-mind-map-lifecycle-integrity does NOT reach this seam: its dashboard-education-api delta covers the status endpoint and the receipt lock, not the correlation query, so once maps are created `draft` the correlation will happily settle "completed" against a draft empty map too.
findings.evidence: roster/education/api/router.py:1002-1035 (_correlate_curriculum), roster/education/api/router.py:1145-1171 (_run_curriculum_request settle), frontend/src/components/education/CurriculumRequestReceiptPanel.tsx:192-208 ("Ready" badge + "was created"); openspec/changes/education-mind-map-lifecycle-integrity/specs/dashboard-education-api/spec.md:51,250-262 (no correlation requirement); live GET /api/education/curriculum-requests/latest and /api/education/mind-maps
findings.taxonomy_shape: gates as metadata / rendered clause not true — a completion claim whose only test is that a row exists

findings.title: Zero review cards have ever been scheduled in the instance's life; the butler's central promise has never executed once
findings.detail: Confirmed on main as instructed. education has 14 rows in scheduled_tasks and not one carries the `review-` prefix that spaced_repetition_record_response creates (`_REVIEW_SCHEDULE_PREFIX = "review-"`). GET /api/education/quiz-responses returns total 0 — no diagnostic, teach or review response has ever been recorded. All 5 mind maps have zero nodes and zero edges. GET /api/education/analytics/cross-topic returns topics [] with portfolio_mastery 0.0. Meanwhile daily-spaced-repetition-nudge has run every day (last_run 2026-09-12T09:14Z), weekly-progress-digest weekly, nightly-analytics nightly, and daily_briefing_contribution daily — four schedules maintaining the appearance of a learning system over an empty evidence base. The manifesto's promise ("After you learn something, we schedule spaced repetition reviews... When the time comes, you get a brief quiz on exactly the right concept") has never been kept once.
findings.evidence: live GET /api/butlers/education/schedules (14 rows, no `review-*`), live GET /api/education/quiz-responses (total 0), live GET /api/education/mind-maps (5 maps, nodes:[] each), live GET /api/education/analytics/cross-topic; roster/education/tools/spaced_repetition.py:31,266-303; roster/education/MANIFESTO.md "Our Promise"
findings.taxonomy_shape: substrate shipped / consumer never — the scheduling engine exists and has never been reached

findings.title: Mastery advances on rows with no owner utterance and no proof a question was ever asked
findings.detail: quiz_responses.user_answer is nullable and mastery_record_response accepts user_answer=None while still applying the full recency-weighted quality and driving the status machine. session_id is nullable too, and nothing binds a row to a delivered question, an owner message, or a grading rubric — question_text is whatever the session typed. Three self-authored rows with quality>=4 and response_type='review' graduate a node to `mastered` (mastery.py:107-114), which in turn can auto-complete the whole mind map (mastery.py:266-285). Mastery in this butler is a declaration the session makes about itself, not evidence about the owner.
findings.evidence: roster/education/migrations/001_education_tables.py:86-98 (user_answer TEXT nullable, session_id UUID nullable); roster/education/tools/mastery.py:122-190 (accepts user_answer=None), :107-114 (graduation rule), :266-285 (auto-complete)
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: mastery as declaration — a claim about the owner's mind admitted with zero owner-authored evidence and no delivery proof

findings.title: Velocity and "Est. Completion" read the writer's clock: nodes are bucketed by updated_at as a stand-in for when they were mastered
findings.detail: _compute_velocity counts a node as mastered-in-week-N if mastery_status='mastered' and updated_at falls in that bucket. There is no mastered_at column anywhere in the schema. updated_at is bumped by every mastery_score write (mastery.py:252-262) and by every spaced-repetition write of ease_factor/next_review_at/last_reviewed_at (spaced_repetition.py:231-253) — so a concept mastered a year ago and merely reviewed today counts as mastered this week. estimated_completion_days = ceil(unmastered / velocity * 7) is derived from that number and rendered on the dashboard as the "Est. Completion" KPI, and the weekly digest prompt asks the session to report "an estimated completion date".
findings.evidence: roster/education/tools/analytics.py:264-297 (_compute_velocity), :93-99 (estimated_completion_days); roster/education/tools/mastery.py:252-262; roster/education/tools/spaced_repetition.py:231-253; frontend/src/components/education/MasterySummaryCards.tsx:12,48-51; roster/education/butler.toml weekly-progress-digest prompt
findings.taxonomy_shape: writer's clock impersonating the world's clock

findings.title: Two graders with different demotion rules and no atomicity between the score ledger and the review schedule
findings.detail: mastery_record_response refuses to demote a mastered node at all (`if current_status == "mastered": return None`), while spaced_repetition_record_response demotes mastered→reviewing on quality<3. Both are separately registered MCP tools operating on the same node with independent transactions; recording a review answer correctly requires the session to call both, and nothing enforces it. A session that calls only mastery_record_response updates the score and never schedules the next review (the node's next_review_at goes stale forever); a session that calls only spaced_repetition_record_response reschedules with no quiz_responses row, so the answer leaves no evidence and analytics/retention never see it.
findings.evidence: roster/education/tools/mastery.py:76-79 vs roster/education/tools/spaced_repetition.py:460-474; roster/education/modules/tools.py registers both independently (module docstring roster/education/modules/__init__.py:31-35)
findings.taxonomy_shape: built twice, unified never — two writers for one domain event

findings.title: Two "pending review" denominators; the briefing hides exactly the retention checks the manifesto promises
findings.detail: The daily briefing contribution counts pending reviews with `AND n.mastery_status NOT IN ('mastered','unseen')`, so an overdue retention check on a concept the owner has already mastered never appears in the briefing. The Telegram daily nudge and the dashboard Reviews tab both use spaced_repetition_pending_reviews, which filters on next_review_at alone and therefore includes mastered nodes. The manifesto's whole retention claim ("come back, at exactly the right moment, to make sure it still does") lives entirely in the set the briefing excludes.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/jobs/briefing.py:1095-1106 vs roster/education/tools/spaced_repetition.py:313-368 and roster/education/api/router.py:476-525; roster/education/butler.toml daily-spaced-repetition-nudge
findings.taxonomy_shape: one word, two denominators on one owner surface

findings.title: "Avg Mastery 0%" is rendered over zero concepts
findings.detail: mastery_get_map_summary returns COALESCE(AVG(mastery_score),0.0) with no reference to total_nodes, and MasterySummaryCards renders Math.round(avg*100)+'%' unconditionally. Live for the only active curriculum: total_nodes 0, mastered_count 0, avg_mastery_score 0.0 — so the page reads "Total Concepts 0 / Mastered 0 / Avg Mastery 0% / Est. Completion —". A 0% that means "nothing exists to measure" is typographically identical to a 0% that means "you have mastered none of your forty concepts".
findings.evidence: roster/education/tools/mastery.py:361-403; frontend/src/components/education/MasterySummaryCards.tsx:41-52; live GET /api/education/mind-maps/aa778538-29e8-4211-b06c-7a59881d73af/mastery-summary
findings.taxonomy_shape: an aggregate that denominates nothing

findings.title: Concept entities are written into the shared identity graph in a form nothing can ever join, and no caller reads them
findings.detail: mind_map_node_create creates a public.entities row per concept with canonical_name = '<map title> > <label>', entity_type 'other', and aliases '{}' — so the concept "RAII" is stored as "C++ > RAII" with no alias for the bare term and no type that says it is a concept. No mention of RAII anywhere else in the fleet can ever resolve to it. Worse, nothing reads it back: grep for mind_map_nodes.entity_id across src/, roster/ and frontend/ finds only the migration and the writer itself — no API field, no UI, no tool. And no education writer ever calls project_entity_graph_edge (the only callers are core commitments, memory storage, and relationship's fact writer), so a concept is an isolated vertex with zero edges in public.entity_graph_edges. audits.ideal: A world-class learning butler would treat mastery as an evidentiary claim with a chain of custody, not a number a session may set. Every retention check would exist as a durable review card with a lifecycle — scheduled, asked, delivered (proven against the attention ledger, not the flow state), answered by the owner in their own words, graded against a recorded rubric by a named model — so that "what have I actually retained" is answered by counting answered cards, and "what did you ask me that never reached me" is answerable at all. Graduation to `mastered` would require at least one free-recall answer (explain it back, not recognise it) separated in time from the teaching, and mastery would decay in the open: a concept whose verification interval has lapsed reads "mastered, unverified for 94 days", never a flat "mastered". Every aggregate would refuse a zero denominator and every mastery timestamp would come from a recorded transition event, never from a row's updated_at. Concepts would be first-class entities in the shared graph under their own names, joined by edges, so the butler could say "RAII, which you are learning, came up in Tuesday's session and in the C++ talk on your calendar Thursday" — turning the owner's week into retrieval practice. The owner would state learning goals as standing intents with a horizon and a cadence, and the butler would report honestly against them, unprompted: what has never been tested, what has gone cold, what the measured rate says about the stated deadline. And review would be answerable wherever the owner is — a keyboard-first answer box on the dashboard, a Telegram reply, a chat turn — each landing on the same card with the same evidence. Above all it would refuse: no mastery without owner-authored evidence, no percentage over an empty set, no "curriculum ready" without a concept in it, no retention claim older than its own interval.
audits.jarvis_gap: Today Education is a complete claim apparatus over an empty evidence base, and it has been for the life of the instance. Five mind maps, zero nodes; zero quiz responses ever recorded; not one `review-*` schedule ever created; one teaching flow, for a map named `__probe_not_used__`. Against that void the read side is confident: the receipt panel says "Ready — The curriculum for C++ was created" because a mind_maps row exists (router.py:1002-1035), the mastery cards say "Avg Mastery 0%" over zero concepts, the daily briefing job asserts a current topic every morning, and four schedules — nightly analytics, weekly digest, weekly stale-flow, daily nudge — keep running maintenance on nothing. Where the machinery does exist it cannot bear weight: mastery can be graduated by three rows a session wrote itself with user_answer NULL; velocity and estimated completion are computed from `updated_at`, a writer's clock, because no `mastered_at` event was ever recorded; the score ledger and the review scheduler are two unatomic tools with contradictory demotion rules; the briefing and the nudge disagree about what "pending review" means, and the disagreement precisely excludes the retention checks the manifesto sells. The one bridge to the rest of the owner's life — a public.entities row per concept — was built in a form nothing can join ("C++ > RAII", type 'other', no alias) and is read by nothing at all. The gap to JARVIS is not polish: the butler cannot currently distinguish "you have retained this" from "a session said so", and it has never once asked the owner a question.

findings.detail: roster/relationship/butler.toml:180 enables only 4 of the module's 9 tool groups (`contacts`, `interactions`, `management`, `tracking`). `src/butlers/modules/base.py:35-45` (`group_enabled`) then silently skips every tool in `contacts_extended`, `social`, `notes`, `relationships`, and `entity`. findings.title: The Dunbar census is denominated in contact rows, not people — a duplicate contact row consumes a support-clique slot
findings.detail: compute_dunbar_scores groups by `(cem.contact_id, cem.entity_id)` while joining facts on entity_id (dunbar.py:339-361), so one person with N contact rows yields N identical scored rows. get_tier_ranking then assigns tiers by `enumerate(scored_entries)` rank position (dunbar.py:455-477), so each duplicate takes a rank slot and pushes real people outward. Live: /api/relationship/dunbar/ranking returns 180 entries for 176 distinct entities; tier 5 shows 6 rows for 5 distinct people (Lee Hui Min occupies ranks 1 and 2 with identical score 50.43 under two contact_ids and one entity_id). The frontend compounds it: plex-layout.ts:161-167 counts `tierCounts[tier] += 1` per entry and pushes one node per entry keyed by entityId. The MANIFESTO makes this count load-bearing — 'If the system shows 20 people at the support-clique level, that's honest feedback about social overextension, not a setting to adjust' — so the fabricated margin is exactly the number the owner is told to read as truth.

findings.title: Email is structurally one-sided and the butler is never told: the owner's sent mail is walked but never ingested, so email-only people are scored to tier 1500
findings.detail: The Gmail connector enumerates the SENT mailbox only to collect RFC822 Message-IDs for the `reply_to_outbound` policy tier (gmail.py:728-790, _SENT_IDS_TTL at :169-170); it never emits the owner's outgoing mail as an ingestion event. Passive interaction sync therefore writes only `direction='incoming'` facts for email, and the reciprocity gate multiplies incoming-only contacts to score 0.0 (dunbar.py:241-245,259,317-337) → tier 1500 → excluded from every cadence, insight, and reconnect path. A person the owner emails weekly is silently classified 'recognizable'. Meanwhile stale_contacts.py:21-24 maps source_channel 'email' → connector:gmail as if it were a two-sided producer. Nothing declares the blind spot: MODULE_BLIND_SPOT_SIGNAL_PATTERNS contains only `health` (blind_spot_declarations.py:23-25), so no Relationship session preamble states that the owner's half of email is invisible.

findings.title: The parked reach-out draft is a constant string wearing the authority of a composed message
findings.detail: run_insight_scan parks a `notify` pending action whose body is `f"Hey {contact_name}, it's been a while since we caught up -- how have you been?"` (relationship_jobs.py:574-576) and hands it to the approval spine with a `why` and a real third-party send door. Nothing the butler knows about the person — the notes it stores, the pending gift it just counted, the upcoming date, the last interaction summary — reaches the words the owner is asked to approve for sending. audits.ideal: A world-class relationship butler treats the owner's social life as a living ledger of obligations, not a contact list with decay. It knows, per person and per thread, whose turn it is to speak and how long the ball has sat in the owner's court — a presence claim it can make honestly even when it cannot make absence claims. It knows the shape of the owner's groups because it derives them from the threads the fleet already ingests, and it can say a circle has gone quiet or that the owner has gone quiet inside it. It derives occasions rather than waiting to be told them — ordinals ('turns 40', 'ten years married'), first-met anniversaries, life-event anniversaries with the right tone for a loss — and it sets lead time by what preparation costs, so a gift-shaped occasion surfaces three weeks out bound to the gift idea captured in March. It remembers provenance: who introduced whom, who referred what, which thanks are still owed, and which two people in the graph should meet. When it drafts words for a third party it composes from what it actually knows and shows the owner exactly which other people and which sensitivity-classed facts that draft would disclose, refusing sends that cross a declared boundary. And it is exact about its own perception: for each person it names which channel could attest, which precondition is missing, and one door that fixes it — declaring, in every session preamble, that it cannot see the owner's sent email at all. Every promise in the manifesto has a registered verb the runtime actually exposes, and every count it shows the owner is denominated in people.
audits.jarvis_gap: Today the substrate is unusually good and the output is close to zero. Relationship has 176 real people, a decay-scored Dunbar ranking, direction-weighted reciprocity, entity facts with evidence and coverage, dedup and merge review, deterministic passive interaction sync from Telegram/WhatsApp/Gmail/Calendar, and a rich entity workbench — and yet 180 of 180 contacts report stale_contact_state='unmeasurable', cadence_available is false, the weekly relationship-maintenance job is instructed by its own prompt to stay silent, and the single attention surface renders a permanent 'ranking source unavailable' card blaming a source that returns HTTP 200. Beneath that, the butler at runtime cannot create a note, add an important date, record a gift, form a group, assert a typed relationship, log a life event, or call relationship_lookup, because butler.toml enables four of nine tool groups; and it cannot delegate or open a fleet case because its runtime_config was seeded in April and git changes to core_groups never land. The graph is one machine-minted predicate: live concentration shows knows=41 and works-at=20 against friend-of=0, family-of=0, colleague-of=0, participant-of=0, co-attended=0. Reciprocity exists only as a scoring multiplier, never as an owner-facing obligation; there is no notion of whose turn it is, no group as a social unit, no derived occasion, no introduction memory, and no boundary on what the fleet may repeat about one person to another. The gap to JARVIS is not perception — the messages are already in the database with real timestamps and owner-tagged senders — it is that nothing turns them into something the owner is told.
audits.live_verification: Live, read-only, against http://127.0.0.1:42200. Stack reachable; relationship butler status ok (port 41102). Verified live: GET /api/relationship/dunbar/ranking (180 entries / 176 distinct entities; tier rows {5:6, 50:6, 150:10, 500:9, 1500:149} vs distinct-entity {5:5, 50:6, 150:10, 500:9, 1500:146}; 3 duplicated entities; cadence_available=false; unmeasurable_count=32 while all 180 per-entry states read 'unmeasurable'); GET /api/relationship/contacts/overdue ({"contacts":[],"cadence_available":false,"unmeasurable_count":0}); GET /api/relationship/entities/concentration with pred= for each registered relational predicate (knows=41, works-at=20, member-of=4, managed-by=2, manages=2, child-of/parent-of/partner-of/invited-by/rental-agent/rental-location=1, and co-attended, colleague-of, family-of, friend-of, manages-property, participant-of, purchased-from, subscribed-to, visited all 0); GET /api/butlers/relationship/mcp/tools (125 registered tools — none of the 40 tools in the disabled contacts_extended/social/notes/relationships/entity groups, and no delegation or fleet-case tools); GET /api/butlers/relationship/runtime-config and /api/butlers/finance/runtime-config (core_groups missing delegation/fleet_cases/domain_events that git declares, seeded_at 2026-04-07). Postgres is not a local container, so no direct SQL was run; message_inbox turn-state claims in Move 1 are source-confirmed from the interaction_sync query and connector owner-tagging code, not live-sampled. Frontend claims are source-confirmed against the .tsx plus the live API payload that drives them.

moves.title: Turn-state ledger: whose move is it, per person and per thread
moves.why: The manifesto's identity is 'the one who follows through… the one who notices when someone has been quiet' — but the only quietness the butler models is decay, which is an absence claim and is therefore gated to silence for 180/180 people (live cadence_available=false). Whose-turn-is-it is a PRESENCE claim: a message exists, from them, after the owner's last message, unanswered for N days. Presence needs no producer-attested absence authority, so it is honest and emittable today with the exact data interaction_sync already reads (switchboard.message_inbox, real received_at, owner sender tagged). This is the inverse of the run-11 deferred 'waiting-on-them producer' (what others owe the owner); this is what the owner owes others, which nothing anywhere models. Owner-visible payoff in week one: the Plex rail stops saying 'ranking source unavailable' and starts saying 'Chloe has been waiting 6 days on WhatsApp; Papa 2 days', each with the real last message time and a door into the thread and the person.
moves.manifesto: roster/relationship/MANIFESTO.md — 'Connection' and 'the one who follows through'; it also satisfies the Dunbar section's 'attention flows inward' by tier-ordering the debt. No amendment needed. Touches Messenger only as a reply door, not as transport knowledge (vision rule 7 preserved: the ledger stores thread identity, never transport mechanics).
moves.integration_points: New job `run_turn_state_sync` in roster/relationship/jobs/relationship_jobs.py reusing the sanctioned cross-schema read already at relationship_jobs.py:1076-1131 (switchboard.message_inbox under RFC 0010) but WITHOUT the (received_at)::date collapse and the synthetic hour offsets at :1273-1274 — turn state needs real timestamps. Owner-side observability comes from whatsapp_user_client.py:993-1000,1801-1822 (`raw.is_from_me`) and telegram_user_client.py:1103-1150 (owner sender tagging) → both_sides_observed=true; gmail is excluded (gmail.py:728-790 never ingests SENT) → both_sides_observed=false and no debt row. New MCP tools `turn_state_list(scope, limit)` and `turn_state_get(entity_id)` in roster/relationship/modules/tools.py group `interactions` (an enabled group — see Move 2). New API GET /api/relationship/turn-state and an `awaiting_reply` block on GET /api/relationship/entities/{id} consumed by frontend/src/pages/EntityDetailPage.tsx and by a new 'Waiting on you' section in the Plex AttentionRail (PlexPage.tsx:1274-1340). New insight-scan category `reply-debt` in run_insight_scan with dedup_key `relationship:reply-debt:{entity_id}:{yyyy-Www}`. New spec capability openspec/specs/relationship-turn-state/spec.md; amend openspec/specs/butler-relationship/spec.md tool inventory and schedule inventory.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: a WhatsApp DM where their last message is 2026-09-06T11:04Z and the owner's last is 2026-09-05T20:12Z yields last_speaker='them', unanswered_since=2026-09-06T11:04Z, both_sides_observed=true; the owner replies, the next tick flips last_speaker='owner' and nulls unanswered_since. Failure: switchboard.message_inbox unreadable → the job records errors and the API returns the degraded envelope of docs/api_and_protocols/response-conventions.md with an explicit unreadable_thread_count; it MUST NOT return an empty list, because 'no one is waiting' is the dangerous lie here. One-sided channel: a Gmail-only thread stores both_sides_observed=false and is reported under an 'owner's half not observable' bucket rather than as zero debt. Concurrency: one pg_advisory_xact_lock per run; upsert on the natural key so a tick overlapping the existing interaction-sync tick cannot double-write. Idempotence: the derivation is a pure function of a bounded received_at window, so replay converges; re-running after the owner replies is monotone (unanswered_since only advances or clears). Rollback: drop the table and unregister the job and the two tools; no other subsystem reads it (the insight category and rail section are additive and fail closed to today's behaviour).

moves.title: Tool-surface truth: make the manifesto's promises registered verbs, and make config drift impossible to hold silently
moves.why: Live, the Relationship butler cannot record a gift, add a birthday, write a note, form a group, assert a typed relationship, log a life event, or call relationship_lookup — 40 implemented tools in five groups are unregistered by one line of butler.toml, while the MANIFESTO, openspec/specs/butler-relationship/spec.md, the gift-brainstorm skill, and the relationship-maintenance prompt all speak as though they exist. Separately its runtime_config, seeded 2026-04-07 and never re-read, silently drops the `delegation` and `fleet_cases` core groups git declares, so it cannot ask another butler a question or contribute to a fleet case. Vision rule 6 says the governing document is binding, not decoration; today it is decoration enforced by nothing. moves.title: Disclosure boundary: show and gate what a draft would reveal about someone who is not the recipient
moves.why: notify(entity_id=<contact>) resolves a third party's channel from relationship.entity_facts and sends butler-composed words to a real person, gated only by a `_why` dossier — nothing inspects the body. The butler holds facts classified pii and confidential and notes 'capturing everything that matters' about people who never consented to being quoted to each other, and the fleet now parks prepared outreach automatically. The single-user sovereignty rule protects the owner's data from the outside world; nothing protects one person in the owner's life from another. Owner-visible payoff in week one: every prepared send shows an itemised 'this message reveals: Ana's new job (confidential), Ben's phone number' block, so the owner can actually let the butler send things.
moves.manifesto: No butler currently promises discretion — this implies a Relationship MANIFESTO amendment ('Discretion: what the butler knows about one person is not currency to spend with another; a message to Y is composed only from what Y may hear') and a matching clause in the Messenger contract for the egress leg. Vision rule 6 requires the amendment before the capability, so the amendment is slice 1.

Sensitivity classes already exist on memory facts (src/butlers/modules/memory/migrations/001_memory_schema.py:53,134,315) and on relationship entity facts. New deterministic check `resolve_disclosures(body, recipient_entity_id)`: resolve capitalised name spans against public.entities (reuse roster/relationship/tools/_entity_resolve.py and the HIGH-confidence discipline from commitments.py), and match body spans against active facts with sensitivity != 'normal' for any resolved entity. Result is a typed `disclosures[]` array on the pending_actions dossier, rendered by the approvals surface (frontend approvals components) and by the prepared-action door on the insight digest. New registered predicate `disclosure-boundary` (object = JSON literal: scope 'any' | entity-id list) on relationship.entity_predicate_registry; an active boundary that a draft would cross fails the send closed with a stated reason instead of parking it. Spec: new capability openspec/specs/third-party-disclosure-boundary/spec.md; amend openspec/specs/core-notify/spec.md.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: a draft to Ben mentioning 'Ana' resolves Ana as a non-recipient entity → the approval card lists the disclosure; the owner approves; the send proceeds and the executed action records the disclosure list as evidence. Boundary hit: Ana carries disclosure-boundary scope 'any' → the send is refused with status='blocked_by_disclosure_boundary' and a named reason; the butler is told why, so it can recompose. Ambiguity: a name span that resolves at less than HIGH confidence is reported as 'possible mention: <span>' and still requires acknowledgement — under-reporting is the dangerous direction, so ambiguity escalates rather than passes. Failure: the entity store is unreadable → the send fails closed (never sends unchecked), consistent with notify's existing fail-closed behaviour when an identifier cannot be resolved. Concurrency: the check runs inside the same park transaction as the dossier write, so a boundary asserted mid-flight either precedes the park (blocks) or follows it (the boundary re-check at dispatch time blocks then). Idempotence: the check is a pure function of (body, recipient, facts-at-time); the dispatch-time re-check is the authority. Rollback: remove the hook; parked dossiers keep their disclosures array as inert metadata.
moves.verification: tests/contracts/test_channel_egress_ownership.py extension: no non-owner send can be dispatched without a disclosures array on its dossier. src/butlers/tests (or roster/relationship/tests) test_disclosure_boundary.py: a body naming a non-recipient entity yields exactly one disclosure item; a confidential fact quoted verbatim is flagged; a HIGH-confidence boundary blocks and a MEDIUM-confidence name still requires acknowledgement; an unreadable entity store blocks rather than sends. Frontend approvals test: the disclosure block renders and the approve control is disabled until acknowledged. Live seam: no live write test — this move is verified at the park/dispatch seam in tests only, since firing a real third-party send is out of bounds.

audits.live_verification: Dev stack UP (docker ps: 17 butlers-dev-* containers, 26h uptime; dashboard-api-hotreload marked unhealthy). LIVE-CONFIRMED: (1) GET http://127.0.0.1:42200/api/system/backups returns 15 nightly artifacts, newest 2026-09-12T02:07Z at 1,868,913,619 bytes, last_run {result:"success",reason:"ok"}, and restore_drill {checked_at:null, result:"pending", detail:null} — no restore has ever been proven, ever, against any of the 15 dumps. (2) `docker exec butlers-dev-backup-cron-1 ls -la /backups` — 15 artifacts totalling ~25.5 GB, plus last_run.json; growth ~18 MB/day. (3) First (cold) GET /api/system/backups did NOT return inside 120 s and a concurrent GET /api/butlers returned nothing in 15 s (curl code 000); after warm-up both return in 10-30 ms — the endpoint gunzips up to 7 artifacts (~12.6 GB) synchronously on the event loop. (4) `gzip -dc` of the real 2026-09-12 dump: line 29 is `ALTER SCHEMA calendar OWNER TO butlers;` before any table exists, and the dump contains `COPY chronicler.butler_secrets` — plaintext Tier-1 credentials inside an unencrypted artifact. SOURCE-CONFIRMED (not runnable read-only): the restore-drill executor role's inability to satisfy those ALTER OWNER statements, the drill's ON_ERROR_STOP=1 abort, the exclusion of public.fleet_cases from every dump, and the QA patrol's four checks. The protected restore-drill Compose fragment (docker-compose.restore-drill.yml) is not part of the dev stack, so the drill itself could not be executed here — and has never run.
audits.jarvis_gap: Today the system produces an honest backup and cannot prove a single one of them is a recovery. The producer half is genuinely good work — atomic publish, gzip integrity verification, a truthful `last_run.json` receipt written from an EXIT trap, a fixed failure vocabulary, a QA finding on the night a run dies, and a documented omission set. Everything downstream of "a file exists" is unearned. Fifteen 1.8 GB dumps sit in a Docker volume on the same host as the database they protect; nothing off-host attests to a second copy; the drill that would prove recoverability has never run and, when it runs, aborts on line 29 of its own artifact because the executor role is deliberately not a member of the dump's owner role while psql runs with `ON_ERROR_STOP=1` — its pass state is unreachable by construction. If it could pass, "pass" would mean `count(*) > 0` over information_schema.tables with no denominator, and the manual script certifies "RESTORE VERIFIED — structurally sound" on three table-existence checks and two row-count comparisons. Two application-plane tables (`public.fleet_cases`, `public.fleet_case_links`) are silently omitted from every dump in violation of deployment-hardening's own "omissions SHALL be limited to the trusted-bootstrap control plane" clause, while their NOT-NULL child `fleet_case_evidence` is dumped — so a restore lands referentially broken. The artifact carries every butler's plaintext credentials while the 7-table `/api/data/export` gets AES-256-GCM. And the /system tile renders a green "Healthy" badge over all of it, at the cost of taking the whole dashboard API offline for two minutes on a cold read. The ideal system is one where the owner can answer, in five seconds and without a shell, "where are my copies, when was one last proven to restore my brain, what did you do while you were blind, what dies if Google turns me off, and what would leak if this file walked out the door." Today it can answer none of those.
audits.ideal: A JARVIS-grade personal system treats recovery as a continuously re-earned claim, not a cron job. Every night it publishes a role-neutral artifact plus a machine-readable manifest of exactly what it contains — relation by relation, row count by row count, omission by omission with a reason code — and then proves the claim by restoring into a scratch database and reconciling restored content against that manifest, so "proven recoverable" carries a denominator (312/312 relations, 4.1M/4.1M rows) and an age the owner can read on /system. It knows where its copies live: a `backup_replicas` ledger holds an attestation receipt per location, so the fleet can say "the only copies of your life die with this host" or "an off-host copy is 14 hours old", and the QA patrol raises a condition when a location goes quiet. The artifact is sealed with an owner-held key that is not in the database it protects, and every credential carries a blast-radius record — what it unlocks, what goes dark if it is revoked, which copies of it exist and where — so a leak becomes an ordered rotation list instead of a panic. Every external dependency is a declared first-class object bound to the butler capabilities that rest on it, so the owner can see which parts of their life the system would forget if a vendor closed an API, and which parts are already captured locally and safe. Every infrastructure condition episode is a door: it reconstructs, from sessions, notifications, approvals and audit rows inside its window, what the fleet said and did while it was in a bad state, so an outage ends with a report rather than a shrug. And one page states the whole posture in the owner's language, generated from those real inventories, with a last-verified age on every line and an explicit, honest section naming what cannot be made resilient at this scale.

findings.title: The restore drill's pass state is unreachable by construction — every drill aborts on line 29 of its own artifact
findings.evidence: src/butlers/jobs/backup_health.py:196-207 (psql ... -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1); scripts/init-db.sql:270-271 (REVOKE restore_drill_executor FROM butlers; REVOKE butlers FROM restore_drill_executor); deploy/backup/pg_dump.sh:230-241 (pg_dump invoked with no --no-owner); live dump butlers_2026-09-12T02-00-00.sql.gz line 29 = 'ALTER SCHEMA calendar OWNER TO butlers;'; tests/scripts/test_pg_restore_definer_ownership.py:311-336 measures exactly this abort; scripts/pg_restore.sh:180-200 documents it ('ON_ERROR_STOP=1 does not work ... line 29 of 17291')
findings.detail: _run_restore_drill_sync pipes the plain dump into psql with ON_ERROR_STOP=1 as the restore_drill_executor role. init-db.sql explicitly revokes membership between that role and the migration login 'butlers' in both directions, and pg_dump emits ALTER ... OWNER TO butlers before a single table exists. ALTER ... OWNER TO requires SET ROLE ability, so the first statement fails, ON_ERROR_STOP aborts, and the drill records 'restore failed: permission denied' — the same class of failure already observed under bu-kqnum.8, but now permanent and independent of the CREATEDB grant that change fixes. The whole protected apparatus (dedicated role, secret mount, TCP proxy, firewall wrapper, result ledger, cadence) can only ever emit fail or pending. The in-flight openspec change restore-drill-recovery-truthfulness does not mention ownership at all (grep of its proposal/design/specs finds only unrelated 'ownership transfer' of the executor interface).
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: a proof mechanism whose pass state is unreachable by construction — the ceremony is fully built and the verdict it exists to produce can never be emitted

findings.title: Two application-plane tables are silently absent from every backup, and their NOT-NULL child is not — a restore lands referentially broken
findings.evidence: deploy/backup/pg_dump.sh:127 (BACKUP_EXCLUDE_TABLES includes public.fleet_cases public.fleet_case_links); alembic/versions/core/core_217_fleet_case_file.py:126-127,209-210 (FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY on both), :148-151 (fleet_case_evidence.case_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES public.fleet_cases(id)) — fleet_case_evidence has no RLS and is therefore dumped; docs/operations/backup-restore.md exclusion table (grep 'fleet_case' → no match, same for task_continuity and runtime_probe_control_receipts); openspec/specs/deployment-hardening/spec.md:179-186 ('Objects it omits SHALL be limited to the trusted-bootstrap control plane ... Every omission SHALL be documented with its cost in docs/operations/backup-restore.md')
findings.detail: fleet_cases is an alembic core-chain application table (the run-11 fleet case file), not trusted-bootstrap control plane, and init-db.sql does not reconstruct it — so its omission exceeds the bound deployment-hardening sets, and it is undocumented in the operations doc the spec names as the required place. The exclusion is mechanically forced by FORCE RLS plus pg_dump's row_security=off, and tests/scripts/test_pg_dump_backup.py:205-232 keeps the set green because it derives 'fenced' from catalogue flags, not from whether the data is recoverable — so the guard that exists to make omission a decision instead certifies it. Worse, the child table fleet_case_evidence carries a NOT NULL FK to the omitted parent and is itself dumped, so restoring the artifact produces either a failed ADD CONSTRAINT or orphaned evidence rows. The manual path (scripts/pg_restore.sh:159-170) runs psql without ON_ERROR_STOP and exits 0 regardless, so this failure is silent on the one path a human would take in a disaster.
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: an omission set that outgrew its own charter — the guard verifies the list against catalogue flags instead of against the recoverability claim, so silent data loss passes as policy

findings.title: Reading the backup tile takes the whole dashboard API offline for minutes
