findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/backup_facts.py:101-122 (_verify_backup_artifact gunzips the entire artifact), :246-249 (loops over stamped[:7]); src/butlers/api/routers/system.py:881 (facts = read_backup_facts_from_dir(...) — a fully synchronous call inside an async handler, no to_thread); src/butlers/core/qa/sources/infra_state.py:52-69 (the QA patrol calls the same function every tick); live: cold GET /api/system/backups >120 s with concurrent GET /api/butlers timing out at 15 s, warm 0.010 s
findings.detail: On a cold process the endpoint decompresses the seven newest artifacts end to end — ~12.6 GB at the measured 1.8 GB apiece — on the asyncio event loop. Every other dashboard request is starved for the duration; I reproduced this against the live dev stack, and the dashboard-api container is currently reporting unhealthy. The memo cache is keyed on (path, mtime, size) and process-local, so it is cold after every deploy, every hot-reload, and inside the QA staffer process; and backup_facts.py:118-120 clears the entire cache wholesale when it reaches _VERIFY_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES, guaranteeing a periodic full re-verification storm rather than an eviction. A verification whose cost is an outage is not a health check.
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: a read-side integrity check whose cost is the outage it was meant to detect

findings.title: A green 'Healthy' badge sits over a recovery that has never once been proven
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/system/BackupTile.tsx:94-142 (BackupStatusBadge ranks corrupt/empty > last_run failed > backup_stale > healthy; restore_drill is never consulted), :211-222 (a pending drill renders as a muted 'No drill yet' line), :321 (RestoreDrillRow is a sibling row, not an input to the badge); live GET /api/system/backups: last_backup_status 'healthy', restore_drill.result 'pending' across 15 artifacts
findings.detail: The tile's own header comment states the badge 'now reflects the REAL verified state' and that a failed drill is 'never silently folded into a green badge' — but a drill that has NEVER passed is folded in exactly that way. Fifteen consecutive nightly dumps with zero proof of recoverability render as a green Healthy pill with a grey subordinate line. A pass is likewise never aged out: a drill that passed six months ago still renders green 'Passed', with only a relative timestamp to disclose it. Absence of proof is being displayed with the authority of proof.
findings.taxonomy_shape: failure impersonating health at the read side

findings.title: A drill pass is a bare table count with no denominator; the manual verifier certifies on five checks
findings.evidence: src/butlers/jobs/backup_health.py:32-35 (_INTEGRITY_QUERY = SELECT count(*) FROM information_schema.tables ...), :216-223 (table_count == 0 fails, anything else is 'restored N tables' and ok=True); scripts/pg_verify_restore.sh:143-232 (three table-existence checks, contacts >= 1 row, model_catalog >= 1 row, row-count parity on public.contacts and public.contact_info only), :234-246 ('RESTORE VERIFIED ... The restored database is structurally sound')
findings.detail: Nothing compares the restored table count to the live one, and no row-level content is compared at all in the automated path. A restore that landed four tables of several hundred is recorded as a pass and rendered green. The manual verifier's summary line, 'N checks — N passed, 0 failed, RESTORE VERIFIED', denominates over a hand-picked list of five assertions about contacts and model_catalog; memory facts, entity_facts, sessions, chronicles, approvals, conversations — the owner's actual brain — are never checked by either path.
findings.taxonomy_shape: aggregates denominating nothing

findings.title: The nightly artifact is an unencrypted plaintext credential dump, and the doctrine that exempts it reasons about a premise the artifact breaks
findings.evidence: live: `gzip -dc butlers_2026-09-12T02-00-00.sql.gz | grep -o 'COPY [a-z_]*\.butler_secrets'` → COPY chronicler.butler_secrets; alembic/versions/core/core_001_foundation.py:317-327 (secret_value TEXT NOT NULL, no encryption, no RLS); deploy/backup/pg_dump.sh:127 (butler_secrets is not excluded); about/heart-and-soul/security.md:267-282 ('Why Encryption at Rest Adds Minimal Value ... the encryption key would be stored on the same machine as the database'); docs/operations/backup-restore.md:46-49 ('Keep a separate, owner-controlled off-host copy'); src/butlers/api/routers/data_ops.py:29-52 (the 7-table export is AES-256-GCM sealed)
findings.detail: Every butler schema's butler_secrets rows — Tier-1 LLM API keys, bot tokens, OAuth client secrets, S3 credentials — plus Tier-2 owner credentials in entity_info, are dumped in cleartext into a 1.87 GB file that is retained 14 days and that the operations doc instructs the owner to copy off-host. The security doctrine's exemption rests on 'key and data are on the same machine anyway', which is precisely the premise a portable artifact destroyed. The asymmetry is stark: the 7-table /api/data/export is sealed with AES-256-GCM under an owner-held key, while the file containing everything is not sealed at all.
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: a doctrine premise outlived by the artifact it exempted — the exemption's stated condition stops holding the moment the data becomes portable

findings.title: The infrastructure patrol has four checks and none of them is recoverability
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/qa/sources/infra_state.py:22-73 (the four checks: connector-offline, heartbeat-stale, backup-stale/backup-run-failed, external-deadman-stale), :78-95 (reconcile_snapshot into public.infra_conditions with source 'infra_state'); live restore_drill.result 'pending' produces no finding and no condition
findings.detail: The patrol reuses read_backup_facts_from_dir and raises BackupRunFailed the night a run dies — genuinely good — but it never reads the restore-drill ledger. A drill that has never run, or that has been failing for ninety days, generates no QA finding, no infra_conditions episode, and no attention. The only surface that mentions it is a muted line on /system that a calm owner has no reason to open. The substrate (a durable, episode-shaped condition ledger with an existing dashboard door) exists and this signal never reaches it.
findings.taxonomy_shape: substrate shipped / consumer never

findings.title: Nothing in the system knows whether a second copy of the owner's life exists
findings.evidence: docs/operations/backup-restore.md:46-49 (instructs an off-host copy; no mechanism, no ledger, no check); repo-wide grep for offsite|off-host|restic|borgbackup|rclone|s3:// over *.py/*.sh/*.yml/*.md finds no backup-replication code path; src/butlers/core/backup_facts.py:220-283 (facts are derived from exactly one directory); .env.example:63-75 (BACKUP_CRON, BACKUP_RETAIN_DAYS, BACKUP_DIR, BUTLERS_BACKUP_DIR — no replica target); live: 25.5 GB of dumps in the butlers_backups volume on the same host as the database
findings.detail: Every claim the system makes about backup health is a claim about a Docker volume that dies with the host. The operations doc names the risk in one sentence and hands it to the owner, and the fleet then reports 'Healthy' with no awareness of whether the owner ever acted on it. There is no replica registry, no attestation, no staleness clock on a second location, and no way for /system to distinguish 'one copy on this disk' from 'three copies in two places'. This is the single largest exposure to the literal pursuit question: if the host died tonight, the answer is total loss and the dashboard would have been green the whole way.
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: a stated operator responsibility with no ledger — the doc delegates the risk and nothing in the system ever asks whether it was discharged

findings.title: Credential 'used by' is a hand-maintained 14-key map that names modules, not consequences
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/secrets_v2.py:1960-2016 (_SYSTEM_KEY_USED_BY: 14 static entries, comment 'Runtime dependency tracing does not exist'), :2010-2016 (_used_by_for_key); frontend/src/components/secrets/passport/pages.tsx:2028-2050 (renders the honesty line for an empty list), :2121-2125 ('usedBy ... /butlers/{usedBy[0]} would 404 for every real entry')
findings.detail: The passport is admirably honest that an empty list means 'not tracked', but the map covers fourteen keys, names implementation consumers (a module or subsystem), and answers neither of the two questions a compromise raises: what stops working if I revoke this right now, and what else does this credential unlock. The last hop has no door either — the rendered consumer is deliberately not a link because it would 404.
findings.taxonomy_shape: last hop has no door

findings.title: The fleet-wide data-deletion verb is disabled with no replacement and no owner-visible statement of that fact
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/data_ops.py:102 (_WIPE_ENABLED = False  # disabled pending atomic + authenticated reimplementation), :549-561 (all calls return 503 wipe_disabled before any DB access); no frontend caller (grep of frontend/src for data/wipe finds none)
findings.detail: Not a rendered lie — there is no button, so nothing fabricates the capability — but sovereignty has two halves and the second one is currently absent: the owner has no working way to make the system forget. The disablement is recorded only in a Python comment; no doc, spec, or surface states that the system cannot presently delete itself.
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: an absent verb whose absence is recorded only in source

moves.title: Proof of recovery that names the brain: role-neutral artifact + content manifest + a drill that can actually pass
moves.why: The single fact that grounds this whole lens: 15 nightly dumps and, live, restore_drill.result = 'pending' — no backup has ever been proven to restore, and the drill cannot emit a pass because psql runs ON_ERROR_STOP=1 as a role that init-db.sql:270-271 deliberately bars from the ownership statements at line 29 of the artifact (src/butlers/jobs/backup_health.py:196-207). Even if it passed, the verdict is count(*) > 0 over information_schema.tables (backup_health.py:32-35) — an aggregate with no denominator. openspec/specs/deployment-hardening/spec.md:167-186 already demands 'a restore drill that proves a backup can be restored to a working state' and that a backup be 'a stated coverage claim, not merely a zero exit status'; today it is neither. The General butler's manifesto promises 'Reliability. Once you tell us something, it's safe. We never lose what matters to you' (roster/general/MANIFESTO.md, Our Promise). Owner-visible payoff within a week: the /system Backups tile changes from a green pill with 'No drill yet' to 'Proven recoverable 6h ago — 312/312 relations, 4.1M/4.1M rows, 3 omitted by policy', and the first drill failure names the relation that was lost rather than a permission string.
moves.manifesto: roster/general/MANIFESTO.md ('Reliability ... we never lose what matters to you') and roster/qa/MANIFESTO.md (QA staffer as system-wide SRE, patrol → condition → finding). Implies an amendment to openspec/specs/deployment-hardening/spec.md § Backup And Restore Verification Path: a restore drill SHALL reconcile restored content against a per-run manifest, and its published verdict SHALL carry a denominator.
moves.integration_points: deploy/backup/pg_dump.sh (add --no-owner --no-acl to the published artifact; emit ownership.json + manifest.json siblings recording per-relation row counts at dump time and every omission with a reason code; extend the atomic publish/prune to the sidecars); src/butlers/jobs/backup_health.py (_INTEGRITY_QUERY replaced by a manifest reconciliation; RestoreDrillResult gains relations_expected/relations_restored/rows_expected/rows_restored; _SAFE_RESTORE_DRILL_DETAIL vocabulary extended with fixed shortfall codes); restore_drill_executor.record_result + the restore_drill_executor ledger schema (scripts/init-db.sql, scripts/provision_restore_drill_executor.sh) for the new coverage columns and their audit_log projection; src/butlers/core/backup_facts.py RestoreDrillFacts; src/butlers/api/routers/system.py GET /api/system/backups; frontend/src/components/system/BackupTile.tsx + api/types; scripts/pg_restore.sh and scripts/pg_verify_restore.sh (the manual path restores the same role-neutral artifact and reconciles the same manifest, replacing the five hand-picked checks); docs/operations/backup-restore.md (the supported recovery order becomes init-db.sql bootstrap → data restore → ownership reconciliation from ownership.json); tests/scripts/test_pg_dump_backup.py and tests/scripts/test_pg_restore_definer_ownership.py.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: the nightly run publishes artifact + manifest + ownership map; the executor restores with ON_ERROR_STOP=1 and no ownership statement to trip on, reconciles counts, records pass with full coverage; /system shows a proven age with a denominator. Failure — shortfall: any relation or row-count gap records a fail naming the relation from a fixed vocabulary (never raw psql text), and cadence falls to the 24h retry the in-flight restore-drill-recovery-truthfulness change defines. Failure — no manifest (an artifact from before this ships): recorded as 'unverifiable: no manifest', never a pass, and rendered as such. Failure — ownership map missing on the manual path: pg_restore.sh refuses to certify, exactly as its existing SECURITY FAILURE audit does. Concurrency: the drill keeps its existing fixed-name scratch DB and single-deployment guard; the manifest is written to a .tmp and mv'd like the artifact, so a dashboard read never sees a half-written manifest; a drill reading a manifest whose artifact was pruned mid-run fails on the missing artifact, not on a mismatched pair (manifest name is derived from the artifact name). Idempotence: re-running the drill on the same artifact is safe — the scratch DB is dropped with --if-exists first, and record_result appends an episode rather than mutating one. Rollback: revert pg_dump.sh to owner-preserving output and the drill to the table-count check; the ledger's new columns are nullable and read as 'unknown coverage' by the API, so a rollback degrades to today's behavior instead of erroring. Explicit risk to state in the spec delta: --no-owner means the artifact no longer carries ownership, so the recovery runbook must reconcile it from ownership.json — this is not a loss, since tests/scripts/test_pg_restore_definer_ownership.py:346-430 already proves ownership cannot be restored by a non-member and that trying launders SECURITY DEFINER functions onto the restorer.
moves.verification: (1) A testcontainer test that bootstraps with the real scripts/init-db.sql, migrates core@head, seeds rows in memory.facts / public.entities / public.fleet_cases, runs the real pg_dump.sh, then runs the real _run_restore_drill_sync as a freshly provisioned restore_drill_executor and asserts result.ok is True with relations_restored == relations_expected — the test that today would fail and that no current test attempts. (2) A negative twin: drop one relation from the artifact before the drill and assert the result names that relation and is a fail. (3) A test asserting the published artifact contains no 'OWNER TO' statement and that ownership.json names every object the previous artifact would have claimed. (4) An API test asserting GET /api/system/backups renders coverage fields and that a manifest-less artifact yields 'unverifiable', not 'pass'. (5) A BackupTile test asserting a coverage shortfall never renders green.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1 (S): pg_dump.sh emits manifest.json + ownership.json beside the artifact; tests pin the format; nothing consumes them yet. Slice 2 (M): switch the published artifact to --no-owner --no-acl, rewrite the recovery runbook and pg_restore.sh's ownership audit to reconcile from ownership.json, prove the manual path end to end in a testcontainer. Slice 3 (M): drill reconciles the manifest; ledger + audit projection carry coverage; the fixed detail vocabulary grows shortfall codes. Slice 4 (S): API + BackupTile render 'proven recoverable' with its denominator and age. Slice 5 (S): retire the five hand-picked checks in pg_verify_restore.sh in favour of the manifest reconciliation.

moves.title: The last-copy ledger: off-host replica attestation the fleet can see
moves.why: docs/operations/backup-restore.md:46-49 tells the owner to keep an off-host copy and then the system never asks again; every 'Healthy' the dashboard has ever rendered is a claim about a Docker volume that dies with the host (live: 25.5 GB of dumps in butlers_backups, one location, zero replicas known). Vision non-negotiable 1 makes the owner sovereign over their data; sovereignty over data that exists in exactly one place, on one disk, is a claim the system cannot back. Owner-visible payoff within a week: a new line on /system that reads 'Off-host copy: 14h old at nas-attic' or, honestly, 'No second copy — every copy of your life is on this host', and a standing infra condition while that stays true.
moves.manifesto: roster/qa/MANIFESTO.md (system-wide SRE; the patrol already owns backup-stale and external-deadman-stale, so replica-stale is the same shape). Implies a deployment-hardening spec addition: 'Backup Copy Locations And Attestation'.
moves.integration_points: New core table public.backup_replicas (location_key, label, kind ∈ {volume, off-host-pull, off-host-push}, last_attested_at, last_attested_artifact, last_attested_bytes, expected_cadence_seconds, attestation_method) in a new core migration; src/butlers/core/backup_facts.py (BackupFacts gains replicas: list[ReplicaFacts] read from the ledger, keeping the DB-free directory read intact for the sidecar case); src/butlers/api/routers/system.py GET /api/system/backups; a narrow authenticated POST /api/system/backups/attest that an off-host puller calls with the artifact name and its own sha256 of the local copy (the only write, gated by the runtime auth surface bu-0uqgo hardens); src/butlers/core/qa/sources/infra_state.py (a fifth check, replica-stale, reconciled into public.infra_conditions like the other four, with 'no replica configured' as its own durable condition exactly as ExternalDeadmanUnconfigured already is); frontend/src/components/system/BackupTile.tsx; docs/operations/backup-restore.md.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: an off-host job pulls the newest artifact, verifies its sha256 against the manifest, POSTs an attestation; /system shows the location and its age. Failure — no replica configured: not an error and never a QA finding (acquiring a second location is an operator action), but a durable infra_conditions row and an explicit 'no second copy' line on the tile, matching the ExternalDeadmanUnconfigured precedent. Failure — replica stale past expected_cadence: infra condition opens, escalates L0→L3 through the existing condition ledger, tile shows an age in red. Failure — attestation names an artifact the host has since pruned: recorded as attested-but-superseded, shown as an age, never as fresh. Concurrency: attestation is an upsert keyed on location_key; two pullers for the same location produce one row, last write wins with a monotonic guard (an attestation older than the stored one is ignored, not applied). Idempotence: re-attesting the same artifact is a no-op beyond refreshing last_attested_at. Rollback: drop the fifth patrol check and the tile section; the table becomes inert; nothing else depends on it.
moves.verification: (1) An infra_state test asserting that a configured-but-silent replica produces a replica-stale finding and reconciles into infra_conditions, and that an unconfigured one produces a condition but no finding. (2) An API test asserting a stale replica never renders as a current copy and that an out-of-order attestation is ignored. (3) A test asserting a superseded attestation renders as an age against the artifact it actually attested, not against the newest artifact. (4) A BackupTile test asserting the 'no second copy' line renders when the ledger is empty.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1 (S): the table, the facade, and the honest 'no second copy' line on /system driven by an empty ledger. Slice 2 (M): the attestation endpoint plus a reference puller script (documented, not deployed) and its sha256 contract against the manifest from move 1. Slice 3 (S): the fifth patrol check and its condition-ledger reconciliation.

moves.title: Sealed backup envelope and a credential blast-radius map
moves.why: Live-confirmed: the nightly artifact contains COPY chronicler.butler_secrets — plaintext Tier-1 credentials (core_001_foundation.py:317-327, secret_value TEXT) — in an unencrypted 1.87 GB file retained 14 days, while the seven-table /api/data/export is AES-256-GCM sealed (data_ops.py:29-52). about/heart-and-soul/security.md:267-282 exempts encryption at rest on the premise that key and data share a machine — a premise the operations doc destroys the moment it tells the owner to copy the artifact off-host. And when a credential does leak, secrets_v2.py:1960-2016 can answer 'which module reads this' for fourteen keys and nothing about consequence. Owner-visible payoff within a week: every credential row on /secrets gains a blast-radius line — what it unlocks, what goes dark if revoked, where copies of it exist — and the nightly artifact stops being a portable copy of every key the owner owns.
moves.manifesto: openspec/specs/butler-secrets/spec.md (the passport is the owner's credential surface) plus a required amendment to about/heart-and-soul/security.md § Why Encryption at Rest Adds Minimal Value: the exemption is scoped to the live data plane and explicitly does NOT extend to portable artifacts, which SHALL be sealed under a key not stored in the database they protect.
moves.integration_points: deploy/backup/pg_dump.sh (pipe through an envelope step — age/AESGCM with a public recipient key mounted read-only, so the sidecar can seal but cannot open; the artifact extension changes and backup_facts._verify_backup_artifact learns the sealed shape); src/butlers/core/backup_facts.py (integrity verification of a sealed artifact becomes a header + size + tag check, which also fixes the 12.6 GB gunzip in finding 3); scripts/pg_restore.sh (unseal step with the owner's private key, refusing to proceed without it); a new declared blast_radius block per credential in src/butlers/api/routers/secrets_v2.py replacing _SYSTEM_KEY_USED_BY (fields: unlocks[], capabilities_lost_on_revoke[], copies_at[] ∈ {butler_secrets, backup artifact, connector env, CLI token file}, rotation_procedure_ref); frontend/src/components/secrets/passport/pages.tsx (the used-by band becomes a blast-radius band with real doors); docs/operations/backup-restore.md and about/heart-and-soul/security.md.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: the nightly artifact is sealed; /system still reports recency and integrity; the drill unseals with the private key mounted only into the protected executor; /secrets renders per-credential blast radius. Failure — recipient key missing at dump time: the run fails loudly with a new fixed reason code (sealing_key_unavailable) and publishes nothing, exactly as the existing failure branches do; the tile shows Run failed. Failure — private key missing at restore: pg_restore.sh refuses before touching the target and says so; the drill records a fixed 'artifact sealed, key unavailable' fail, never a pass. Failure — a credential has no declared blast radius: renders 'not declared' (never 'nothing depends on this'), preserving the honesty line the passport already gets right. Concurrency: sealing is inside the same atomic tmp→mv publish, so a partially sealed file is never visible. Idempotence: blast-radius declarations are static data, validated at import; re-declaring is a no-op. Rollback: drop the seal step (old unsealed artifacts remain readable by both paths since the reader sniffs the header) and revert the passport band; the security.md amendment stays as documentation of the decision either way.
moves.verification: (1) A testcontainer test that runs the real pg_dump.sh with sealing enabled, asserts the published artifact is not a gzip stream, and asserts a grep for 'butler_secrets' over the raw bytes finds nothing — the exact check that today finds a plaintext COPY. (2) A round-trip test: seal → unseal → restore into a scratch DB → manifest reconciliation (composes with move 1). (3) A test asserting the dump fails with sealing_key_unavailable and publishes nothing when the recipient key is absent. (4) A blast-radius completeness test asserting every key present in butler_secrets in a bootstrapped DB either has a declaration or renders 'not declared', and that no declaration names a capability that does not exist. (5) A passport test asserting an undeclared credential never renders as unused.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1 (S): the security.md amendment stating the artifact exemption boundary — the doctrine decision before the code. Slice 2 (M): sealing in pg_dump.sh, header-sniffing verification in backup_facts, unseal in pg_restore.sh and the drill. Slice 3 (M): the blast-radius declaration structure, the API field, and the passport band replacing used-by. Slice 4 (S): the rotation-order view — given a compromised credential, the ordered list of what to rotate and what will go dark while you do.

moves.title: Incident ledger: what the fleet said and did while it was in a bad state
moves.why: public.infra_conditions is already a durable, episode-shaped ledger with detected_at/resolved_at, an L0-L3 escalation lifecycle, five producers, and a rendered door at GET /api/system/conditions (src/butlers/api/routers/system.py:1320-1388; core_182). What it cannot answer is the only question the owner actually has after an outage: what did you tell me while you were blind? Nothing joins an episode's window to the sessions, notifications, approvals and actions that ran inside it. The substrate is shipped and the consumer was never built. Owner-visible payoff within a week: every resolved condition gains an 'During this' report — 47 sessions ran, 6 briefings went out, 2 of them cited a source that was already dead, 1 approval was decided on stale data — reachable from the Standing Conditions panel the owner already reads.
moves.manifesto: roster/qa/MANIFESTO.md (patrol, journal capture, 'every QA decision is recorded as an event'; the incident report is the owner-facing counterpart) and roster/switchboard/MANIFESTO.md (the staffer that sees all routing). Implies a QA staffer contract amendment adding 'incident reconstruction' as a responsibility, since the QA dossier is case-shaped and this is a case.
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/core/condition_ledger.py (episodes already carry detected_at/resolved_at and a stable fingerprint — the join key); a new read model src/butlers/api/read_models/ that unions, over an episode window, public.sessions, the notification/attention ledger (notifications router), approvals decisions, and public.audit_log, attributing each to the butler that produced it; a new GET /api/system/conditions/{id}/impact returning a degraded envelope per docs/api_and_protocols/response-conventions.md; the Standing Conditions panel on the frontend gains a per-row door; a core tool (condition_impact) so a butler session can read its own blind-window report and say so — which composes directly with the shipped blind-spot preamble (core_229).
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: an open or resolved episode returns counts plus a bounded list of the most consequential items in its window, each a link to the existing session/notification/approval detail surface. Failure — one source query fails: the envelope marks that source unavailable and reports the rest, never a fabricated zero (the fleet-wide degraded-envelope convention). Failure — an episode with no resolved_at: the window is open-ended and the report says 'still true, as of now', never implying closure. Concurrency: the report is a pure read over immutable-by-then rows; an episode resolving mid-read changes the window end, so the response carries the window it actually used. Idempotence: read-only, no writes, cacheable per (episode_id, window_end). Rollback: remove the route and the door; the ledger is untouched.
moves.verification: (1) A read-model test over a seeded database: one episode spanning a window with sessions, notifications and approvals inside and outside it, asserting exact membership at both boundaries (inclusive detected_at, exclusive resolved_at). (2) A degraded-envelope test asserting a failing sub-source yields availability=false for that source and real counts for the others, never zeros. (3) A test asserting an unresolved episode's report is labelled open-ended. (4) A frontend test asserting the door renders on both open and resolved rows and that a zero-impact window says 'nothing ran' rather than rendering an empty panel.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1 (M): the read model and the API route, sessions + notifications only. Slice 2 (S): approvals and audit rows folded in with per-source availability. Slice 3 (S): the Standing Conditions door and the impact panel. Slice 4 (S): the condition_impact core tool so a session can narrate its own blind window.

moves.title: Dependency sovereignty: what dies when a vendor dies
moves.why: public.expected_signals carries producer as opaque TEXT with no vendor dimension (core_210_expected_signals.py:64-84), and switchboard.connector_registry keys on connector_type/endpoint_identity/replay_safe with no external-dependency identity (src/butlers/core/ingestion_events.py:174-205). So the fleet cannot answer the question a sovereign owner most needs answered: if Google shuts the Health API tomorrow, what exactly stops, what did I already capture locally and keep, and what was only ever a view onto someone else's server? Vision's anti-pattern list already forbids 'designing features that require an always-on internet connection to function at the daemon level' — this move makes the fleet able to state where it violates its own rule. Owner-visible payoff within a week: a dependency map on /system where each external vendor lists the butler capabilities resting on it, the data already captured locally versus the data that is only a live view, and its current liveness — so a vendor deprecation email becomes a scoped decision instead of a surprise.
moves.manifesto: openspec/specs/connector-base-spec (connectors are the cost and dependency boundary per about/heart-and-soul/architecture.md) plus each affected butler's manifesto, since the map states which promises rest on a third party. Implies an architecture-doctrine addition: every connector SHALL declare the external dependency it rests on and whether the data it brings is retained locally or only proxied.
moves.integration_points: A declared dependency block per connector in src/butlers/connectors/* (vendor key, auth credential key linking straight into move 3's blast-radius map, retention ∈ {captured, proxied, hybrid}, capabilities_supported[] naming butler tools/skills); a new public.external_dependencies projection populated at registration from those declarations; public.expected_signals gains a vendor/dependency reference so the shipped liveness spine denominates per vendor; GET /api/system/dependencies; a frontend panel on /system; a core tool (dependency_status) so a butler can tell the owner in words that a capability is degraded because a vendor is down rather than reporting an empty result.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: the map renders per vendor with live liveness from the connector registry and expected_signals, and a per-capability list. Failure — a connector declares no dependency: renders 'undeclared' and raises a build-time lint (declaration is required for new connectors, grandfathered with an explicit undeclared list, never silently treated as dependency-free). Failure — expected_signals has no row for a declared dependency: the map says 'liveness not measured', reusing the existing unmeasurable vocabulary rather than inventing a green. Concurrency: the projection is rebuilt idempotently at connector registration; concurrent registrations upsert on the vendor key. Idempotence: declarations are static; the projection is a pure function of them plus the registry. Rollback: drop the route and panel; declarations remain as inert metadata.
moves.verification: (1) A test asserting every connector under src/butlers/connectors either declares a dependency or appears on the explicit grandfathered list — a mechanism, not a symptom list. (2) A test asserting a declared dependency with no expected_signals row renders 'not measured', never 'healthy'. (3) A test asserting the capabilities named in a declaration resolve to real registered tools. (4) An API test asserting a dead vendor's capabilities render as at-risk with the correct retention class.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1 (S): the declaration structure plus the completeness lint over existing connectors, no surface. Slice 2 (M): the projection, the expected_signals vendor reference, and the API. Slice 3 (S): the /system panel. Slice 4 (S): the dependency_status core tool so a session can say why it has nothing to report.

moves.title: The Backups tile tells the recovery truth, and reading it stops taking the dashboard down
moves.why: Two defects on one surface, both live-confirmed. The badge ranks corrupt > run-failed > stale > healthy and never consults restore_drill (BackupTile.tsx:94-142), so 15 dumps with zero proven restores render as a green 'Healthy' pill above a muted 'No drill yet' — the tile's own header comment claims it 'never defaults to green'. And read_backup_facts_from_dir is called synchronously inside the async handler (system.py:881) where it gunzips the seven newest artifacts end to end (backup_facts.py:101-122, 246-249): my first cold request did not return in 120 s and starved a concurrent /api/butlers, warm it is 10 ms. Owner-visible payoff within a week: /system loads instantly and always, and the badge stops claiming health it has not earned.
moves.manifesto: docs/frontend/purpose-and-single-pane.md and the north star clause 'failure never impersonates health, staleness never wears current-data authority'; roster/qa/MANIFESTO.md for the patrol half.
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/components/system/BackupTile.tsx (add unproven-recovery and stale-proof branches above 'Healthy' in BackupStatusBadge); src/butlers/core/backup_facts.py (verify only the newest artifact inline and persist per-artifact verification results in a small ledger keyed on (name, mtime, size) so history renders from recorded verdicts rather than re-decompression; replace the wholesale _verify_cache.clear() at line 118-120 with LRU eviction); src/butlers/api/routers/system.py:881 (await asyncio.to_thread for whatever verification remains inline); src/butlers/core/qa/sources/infra_state.py (a fifth check on the restore-drill ledger: never-run past a grace window, or failing, is a finding and an infra_conditions episode — the substrate the patrol already reconciles into).
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: badge is green only when the artifact is fresh, verified, the run succeeded, AND a drill proved recovery within its cadence; the tile renders from the verification ledger in milliseconds. Failure — never proven: amber 'Unproven', with the artifact facts still shown truthfully. Failure — last proof older than cadence: amber 'Proof stale (N days)'. Failure — verification ledger unreadable: history renders 'not verified' per row, never 'healthy'. Concurrency: verification writes are upserts keyed on artifact identity; two processes verifying the same artifact converge. Idempotence: re-verifying an unchanged artifact is a no-op. Rollback: the badge branches and the to_thread wrapper are independently revertible; the ledger is additive.
moves.verification: (1) A BackupTile test asserting a fresh, healthy, successfully-run backup with restore_drill.result='pending' renders amber Unproven, not green — the exact live state today. (2) A test asserting a pass older than cadence renders as stale proof. (3) An API test with a directory of large artifacts asserting the handler returns under a fixed budget and that history rows come from the ledger. (4) An event-loop test asserting the handler does not block (concurrent request completes while the backups request is in flight) — the reproduction of the live failure. (5) An infra_state test asserting a never-run drill past the grace window becomes a finding and a condition.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1 (XS): the badge branches — the honesty fix, shippable alone. Slice 2 (S): to_thread plus newest-artifact-only inline verification. Slice 3 (S): the verification ledger and LRU eviction, so history is recorded rather than recomputed. Slice 4 (XS): the fifth patrol check.

moves.title: The sovereignty statement: what you own, what you could take today, what we cannot protect
moves.why: Every fact this pursuit needs exists in a different corner — backup facts in a directory, replicas in a ledger, export scope in a Python dict (data_ops.py:113-127), credentials in butler_secrets, dependencies in connector code, the threat model in a static doc (about/heart-and-soul/security.md) that nothing keeps current and no owner surface renders. Doctrine says the owner owns the instance, the data, the credentials and the agents (about/heart-and-soul/vision.md, non-negotiable 1); nothing in the running system ever states what that ownership currently amounts to. Owner-visible payoff within a week: one page that answers, from live inventories with a last-verified age on every line, where every copy of their life is, what they could walk away with today and in what format, what would be lost, and — in its own honest section — what cannot be made resilient at this scale (a single host, a single Postgres, a vendor that can revoke an API, an LLM provider that can change a model).
moves.manifesto: No existing manifesto owns the owner's sovereignty posture — the General butler promises 'Export and share: take your data with you' for its own domain only, and the QA staffer's contract is infrastructure SLAs. This move implies a doctrine amendment: a new § Sovereignty Posture in about/heart-and-soul/security.md (or a sibling sovereignty.md) defining what the system SHALL be able to state about copies, portability, blast radius, dependencies and honest limits — plus a QA staffer contract amendment making the freshness of those statements a patrol responsibility.
moves.integration_points: A new GET /api/system/sovereignty composing: backup facts + replicas (moves 1-2), the restore-proof age and its denominator (move 1), the export scope map read from _SCOPE_MAP rather than restated (data_ops.py:113-127), the credential inventory and blast-radius declarations (move 3), the dependency map (move 5), and a checked-in limits.md whose 'last reviewed' date is rendered and whose staleness past a threshold is itself an infra_conditions episode; a new /sovereignty route or a /system section per docs/frontend/purpose-and-single-pane.md; a Concierge-readable shape so the owner can ask the dashboard chat 'what would I lose if this host died tonight' and get this, not a paraphrase.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: every line carries a value and a verified age, all derived — no line is authored prose about a mechanism. Failure — a contributing source unavailable: that line renders 'unknown' with its own reason, never an optimistic default, and the page states how many of its lines are unknown. Failure — the limits document is older than its review threshold: the page says so and opens a condition; the limits still render, marked as unreviewed. Concurrency: pure read composition; per-source degradation is independent. Idempotence: read-only. Rollback: remove the route and page; every underlying inventory stands alone.
moves.verification: (1) A test asserting every rendered line traces to a live source and that no line is a hardcoded claim — the mechanism check that keeps this from becoming a brochure. (2) A degraded test asserting a failing contributor yields 'unknown' plus an accurate unknown-count, never a green summary. (3) A test asserting a stale limits document renders as unreviewed and opens a condition. (4) A Concierge test asserting the chat answer to 'what would I lose if this host died' is grounded in this payload with its ages, not generated prose.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1 (S): limits.md — the honest-limits document written first, reviewed, with its freshness contract. Slice 2 (M): the composing endpoint over whatever inventories exist at the time, with explicit 'not yet measured' for the rest. Slice 3 (S): the page. Slice 4 (S): the Concierge binding so the question can be asked in words.

audits.jarvis_gap: Today the fleet has two honest halves of time and no spine between them. Forward: a real Google Calendar sync (`calendar_events`/`calendar_event_instances`), a workspace grid with dedup, a conflict radar, a proposals lane, a prep rail, a day-briefing over overlay contributions, and free/busy find-time — all deterministic reads, all fail-open. Backward: Chronicler projects 1,443 completed calendar instances plus OwnTracks, sessions, comms, Spotify and Steam into intent/activity/evidence layers, mines weekly routines, closes days, and correctly refuses to count a calendar block as lived time (openspec/specs/butler-chronicler/spec.md:531-545). But the two halves never meet as a product, and three classes of dishonesty sit on the owner's live screen. (1) The forward calendar is *incomplete*: a provider recurring master is projected as exactly one instance (src/butlers/modules/calendar.py:8184-8191, 2961-2962), so the live fortnightly "Housekeeping" series appears once in a 90-day window and never again — grid, radar, day-briefing and the chronicle of the past all lose every later occurrence. (2) The radar's arithmetic denominates nothing: a 4-day timed hold is charged whole to its start day ("106.0 h of meetings in one day", live), a 6h flight is reported as "6.1 h of meetings", and a declined invite still counts as load, because `ConflictCandidate` carries no kind, no RSVP and no day clipping. (3) The one question the owner actually asks — "when am I free?" — answers "No open slots match those constraints" when free/busy authentication fails, because the module's structured error envelope is dropped at the API seam. And the one thing only this system could say — "you planned X, the evidence says Y" — is computed inside `reconcile_day` for the day-close bundle and then thrown away; nothing persists an attendance verdict, so no surface, no aggregate and no week review can ever answer it. A world-class time butler would perceive planned-vs-lived as durable, first-class state; the current system perceives it for the length of one LLM prompt.
audits.live_verification: Dev stack live at http://127.0.0.1:42200, read-only GETs only. Live-confirmed: /api/butlers (chronicler + 10 butlers ok); /api/calendar/workspace?view=user over three 90-day windows on the owner's real calendar (25/42/74 entries) — exactly one row carries an `rrule` ("Housekeeping", RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=2;BYDAY=SU at 2026-05-24) and it appears once, with zero later occurrences in the adjacent window, proving provider recurrence is never materialized; /api/calendar/workspace/conflicts 2026-09-13..27 returned `overloaded_day` "106.0 h of meetings in one day" from a single 2026-09-21T03:00Z→2026-09-25T13:00Z hold, and 2026-10-01..11-01 returned two `overloaded_day` issues whose sole event is a flight ("6.1 h of meetings in one day" for SQ 800) plus one true overlap; /api/chronicler/routines returned mined rows whose `label` ("Mon 08:00-10:00") contradicts their own `window_start_local`/`window_end_local` (09:30-11:30); /api/chronicler/projection-health showed google_calendar.completed=1443, owntracks.points=1323, occupation_inferred=6262 rows — real substrate on both sides; /api/calendar/workspace?view=proposals returned zero pending proposals. Source-confirmed (not reproducible read-only): the find-time error-envelope discard, and the discarded `reconcile_day` verdicts. First-time tiering of this lens (not on the run-12 tier board): **functional** — both halves are real and non-fabricated with honest degraded envelopes in most places, but load arithmetic misleads on live data, recurring events silently vanish, and the forward/backward spine does not exist.

findings.title: A provider recurring event is projected as exactly one instance, so every later occurrence silently vanishes from the forward calendar and from the chronicle
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/calendar.py:2961-2962 (sync_incremental sends singleEvents=False, fetching recurring masters only); :8170-8191 (one instance per event at the master start, then _prune_superseded_provider_instances keeps a single row — the comment states "A provider event projects to exactly one instance per sync"); :10518-10560 (_materialize_native_reminder_instances expands RRULE, called only from the native/reminder paths at :8550, :10495, :10689); src/butlers/chronicler/adapters/calendar.py:1-30 (the backward projection reads calendar_event_instances, so it inherits the loss); live: /api/calendar/workspace?view=user 2026-03-17..2026-06-14 returns one entry with rrule=RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=2;BYDAY=SU at 2026-05-24, and the adjacent 2026-06-15..2026-09-11 window returns zero rrule entries
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: the store holds the rule but never the occurrences — a periodic commitment is rendered once and then absent, so every downstream reader (grid, radar, briefing, chronicle) is confidently incomplete
findings.detail: Google is queried with singleEvents=False, which returns the recurring master plus its RRULE. The projection writes one calendar_event_instances row keyed on the master's own start and prunes any other instance of that event. Nothing expands the rule for provider events; only native butler reminders get a materialized rolling window. Consequence on live data: the owner's fortnightly housekeeping is on the calendar in Google, absent from the workspace grid for every occurrence after the first, invisible to the conflict radar and the day-briefing, and — because Chronicler's calendar adapter reads the same instances table — absent from the record of what was scheduled in the past. Any recurring 1:1, standing meeting or weekly class is affected identically.

findings.title: Overloaded-day load charges a multi-day event's whole duration to its start day, producing "106.0 h of meetings in one day"
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/temporal/conflicts.py:265-289 (_detect_overloaded_days buckets by _local_date(c.start_at) and sums c.end_at - c.start_at with no clipping to the day window); rendered verbatim at frontend/src/components/calendar/ConflictRadarBanner.tsx:124; live: GET /api/calendar/workspace/conflicts?start=2026-09-13&end=2026-09-27 → {"kind":"overloaded_day","date":"2026-09-21","summary":"106.0 h of meetings in one day"} from a single 2026-09-21T03:00Z→2026-09-25T13:00Z hold
findings.taxonomy_shape: aggregate that denominates nothing (run-11/12 theme; new instance) — 106 hours cannot occur inside a 24-hour day, and the same bug leaves days 2-4 of that hold showing zero load
findings.detail: The detector neither clips an event to the day it is measuring nor spreads a multi-day span across the days it covers. So one long hold both fabricates an impossible number on its start day and hides real load on the following days. The spec scenario (openspec/specs/calendar-conflict-overcommitment-radar/spec.md:64-71) says only "total confirmed/tentative meeting time on a calendar day", which the implementation does not compute.

findings.title: The radar calls anything timed a "meeting": flights count as meeting-hours and a declined invite still counts as load
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/read_models/calendar_workspace_v1.py:1289-1300 (ConflictCandidate built with only entry_id/title/start/end/timezone/status/all_day — no event kind, no attendee RSVP, though src/butlers/modules/calendar.py:8130-8140 persists metadata.attendees with each attendee's response_status and self flag); src/butlers/core/temporal/conflicts.py:158-162 (only all_day and status='cancelled' are excluded), :281 ("{hours} h of meetings in one day"); live: 2026-10-01..11-01 scan returns two overloaded_day issues whose only event is a flight — "6.1 h of meetings in one day" for "Flight to Beijing (SQ 800)"
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: a vocabulary the data does not support — one predicate ("meeting") asserted over a heterogeneous store that already carries the discriminating fields (attendees/RSVP, travel provenance) and never reads them
findings.detail: The owner's real October is mostly travel; the radar reports it as an overloaded meeting schedule. Because the owner's own responseStatus is available in event metadata and never consulted, a meeting the owner declined is indistinguishable from one they accepted in every conflict, back-to-back and load verdict. The result is a radar that cries wolf on exactly the weeks the owner most needs it to be precise.

findings.title: find-time answers "No open slots match those constraints" when free/busy actually failed — the module's error envelope is discarded at the API seam
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/calendar.py:11296-11315 (_find_free_slots catches CalendarAuthError and returns _build_structured_error(...) with slots=[] — the dict carries status='error' and error text, see :652-675); src/butlers/api/routers/calendar_workspace.py:2965-2991 (the success path reads only result['slots'] and result['calendar_ids'] and sets available=True; only an HTTPException reaches the degraded branch at :2996-3013); frontend/src/pages/CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx:1443-1458 (available===false renders "Free/busy is unavailable", slots.length===0 renders "No open slots match those constraints in the selected window.")
findings.taxonomy_shape: failure impersonating health at the read side (run-11/12 theme; new instance) — the fail-open envelope exists one layer down and is dropped by the consumer that renders the sentence
findings.detail: A revoked or expired Google token, or any CalendarAuthError inside the freeBusy call, produces a well-formed MCP result whose status is 'error'. The dashboard route ignores status/error, marks the answer available, and the page tells the owner they have no free time. The degraded UI copy that would tell the truth already exists three lines away and is unreachable for the most likely failure mode.

findings.title: Plan-vs-actual reconciliation is computed inside the day-close bundle and then discarded — no attendance verdict is ever persisted or readable
findings.evidence: src/butlers/chronicler/reconciliation.py:262-322 (reconcile_day returns activities, kept_intents, dropped_intents); roster/chronicler/modules/__init__.py:642-708 (the only caller: recomputes per invocation, serializes dropped intents into the LLM bundle, returns; nothing is written); src/butlers/chronicler/bundle_assembler.py:424-425 (dropped_intents only decorate the prompt payload); no chronicler route exposes it — roster/chronicler/api/router.py:279-3782 has no reconciliation/attendance endpoint
findings.taxonomy_shape: computed then discarded at the seam (run-12 theme; new instance) — the one adjudication that joins forward intent to backward evidence exists only for the length of one prompt
findings.detail: reconcile_day already decides which calendar intents were contradicted by rest-lane activity and which activity candidates corroborate each other, exactly the arithmetic a plan-vs-actual answer needs. It runs only when the day-close tool is called, is never stored, is not idempotent-readable, and has no API. So "did I actually go?", "how much of last week's plan survived?" and "this recurring block never happens" are unanswerable even though the evidence is projected and the adjudicator is written and unit-tested.

findings.title: A mined routine's headline label is frozen at first detection while its window is refreshed on every re-mine, so the live UI shows a row contradicting itself
findings.evidence: src/butlers/chronicler/routines.py:138,303 (label is machine-generated by _format_label(dow_mask, window_start, window_end)); src/butlers/chronicler/storage.py:1077-1110 (upsert_mined_routine refreshes window_start_local/window_end_local but "deliberately never touches label" on the grounds that it is the owner's to edit); frontend/src/components/chronicles/WorkScheduleSettings.tsx:261 (label rendered as the row headline) and :279-283 (true window rendered directly beneath); live: GET /api/chronicler/routines → {label:"Mon 08:00-10:00", window_start_local:"09:30:00", window_end_local:"11:30:00"} and {label:"Tue 09:30-12:00", window_start_local:"08:00:00", window_end_local:"10:00:00"}
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: a machine-authored value protected as if owner-authored — the write path cannot distinguish "the owner named this" from "we named it once", so a stale generated string outranks the fact it was generated from
findings.detail: The preservation rule is right for owner-edited labels and wrong for generated ones, and nothing records which is which. On the live stack every mined row now displays a time range in its title that disagrees with the time range printed one line below it. The fix is a label provenance flag (or a null label rendered from the window) so re-mining re-renders machine labels and still preserves owner edits.

moves.title: Recurring events become occurrences: materialize provider RRULE into the rolling projection window
moves.why: vision.md "What Success Looks Like": the owner's calendar is maintained without manual entry — today a standing weekly commitment exists in the store as a rule and is rendered exactly once (live: fortnightly "Housekeeping" visible only on 2026-05-24). Every forward surface (grid, radar, day-briefing, find-time context) and the entire backward record inherit the loss, so this is the precondition for anything else in this lens. Owner-visible within a day of shipping: recurring meetings reappear on the grid where they belong.
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/modules/calendar.py: the provider sync projection path (:8122-8191) and _prune_superseded_provider_instances; reuse _rrule_occurrences_in_window (:469) and the existing rolling-window materializer pattern of _materialize_native_reminder_instances (:10518-10560) with RECURRENCE_PROJECTION_WINDOW_DAYS=90; _recurrence_lines_append_exdate (:522) for EXDATE and the existing is_exception/_mark_instances_exception machinery for Google's cancelled/modified occurrences; table calendar_event_instances (alembic core_003) keyed on (event_id, origin_instance_ref) with origin_instance_ref = f"{google_event_id}:{occurrence_start_iso}"; a new deterministic re-materialization tick registered in the existing _DETERMINISTIC_SCHEDULE_JOB_REGISTRY (pattern: src/butlers/jobs/calendar_overlay.py) to roll the window forward; spec openspec/specs/module-calendar (new requirement: Provider Recurrence Materialization) and openspec/specs/connector-google-calendar (document singleEvents=False + local expansion as the deliberate contract).
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: a WEEKLY;INTERVAL=2 master projects every occurrence inside [now-lookback, now+90d]; each occurrence is its own instance row with its own status; the grid, radar and chronicler adapter all see them. Failure: an unparseable RRULE materializes the master occurrence alone and records a parse warning on the event's metadata rather than dropping the event (never silently); a Google instance-level exception (moved or cancelled occurrence) arriving via the master's exdate/instances marks is_exception/cancelled on the matching row, never deletes history. Concurrency: materialization runs inside the same transaction as the master upsert and uses ON CONFLICT (event_id, origin_instance_ref) DO UPDATE, so two overlapping syncs converge; the window-roll tick takes the existing force-sync-style advisory lease. Idempotence: re-running over the same window produces zero row churn (assert on updated_at). Rollback: the expansion is gated by a runtime_config flag; disabling it stops new occurrence rows and a single DELETE of rows whose origin_instance_ref is not the master's own restores today's behavior.
moves.verification: tests/modules/test_module_calendar.py: a WEEKLY;INTERVAL=2 master with 90-day window yields 6-7 instances; an EXDATE occurrence is absent; a cancelled instance is marked, not deleted; re-sync is row-stable. tests/chronicler/test_calendar_adapter.py: each materialized past occurrence projects one scheduled_block episode with a distinct source_ref. tests/api/test_calendar_conflict_radar.py: a weekly series colliding with a one-off produces one overlap per colliding occurrence, not one for the series. Live read-side proof after ship: GET /api/calendar/workspace?view=user over two adjacent 90-day windows returns the Housekeeping occurrences in both.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Pure expansion + dedup keys unit-tested against RRULE fixtures (no DB). 2) Wire into the provider sync upsert behind a runtime_config flag, default off; backfill one calendar in dev and diff instance counts. 3) Add the rolling-window re-materialization tick + exception/EXDATE handling; flip the flag on. 4) Spec deltas for module-calendar and connector-google-calendar.
moves.manifesto: No butler owns forward time; the calendar module is cross-butler infrastructure, so this serves the repository's vision non-negotiable #4 (the daemon is deterministic infrastructure) rather than a single manifesto. Chronicler's manifesto benefits directly: "I read; I project; I preserve provenance" is currently reading an incomplete surface.

moves.title: The attendance ledger: persist plan-vs-actual verdicts and give the owner "what I planned vs what I did"
moves.why: The pursuit question's core: Calendar (forward) and Chronicler (backward) become one spine only if the join between them is durable state. openspec/specs/butler-chronicler/spec.md:531-545 already forbids treating a calendar block as attendance and requires corroboration; reconciliation.py:262-322 already computes the adjudication — and roster/chronicler/modules/__init__.py:682-702 throws it away after one prompt. Owner-visible within a week: a week view that says "you planned 14 blocks; 9 are corroborated by evidence, 2 are contradicted, 3 have no evidence either way", and a per-event door on the calendar grid answering "did this actually happen?" with the evidence that says so.
moves.integration_points: New Chronicler-owned table chronicler.intent_outcomes (intent_episode_id, source_ref='calendar:{origin_instance_ref}', local_date, verdict ENUM('corroborated','contradicted','unevidenced'), corroborating_episode_ids uuid[], contradicting_episode_ids uuid[], overlap_fraction, decided_at, decider='deterministic'|'owner', override_id) via roster/chronicler/migrations; writer = a deterministic day-close-adjacent job reusing src/butlers/chronicler/jobs.py + reconciliation.reconcile_day (extended to also return corroborations, not just drops); reads = new GET /api/chronicler/intent-outcomes (range + verdict filter) and GET /api/chronicler/plan-vs-actual?start&end returning per-day and per-lane planned vs corroborated seconds, in roster/chronicler/api/router.py alongside /rollups and /balance; corrections reuse the existing overrides layer (chronicler.overrides, POST /episodes/{id}/corrections) and the gap-interview one-tap transport (src/butlers/chronicler/gap_interview.py) so "I did go" is an owner testimony row, never a rewrite; forward-side door: the calendar workspace entry detail (GET /api/calendar/workspace/entries/{entry_id}) gains a read-only outcome badge sourced over MCP/the chronicler read surface, and frontend/src/pages/CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx + ChroniclesPage render it; spec deltas: openspec/specs/butler-chronicler (new requirement: Durable Intent Outcome Ledger) and openspec/specs/chronicler-intent-evidence-activity.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: at day close every intent episode in the closed local day gets exactly one verdict row with the evidence episode ids that produced it. Failure: an adapter that has not caught up leaves the day's coverage below a threshold — the day is written with verdict='unevidenced' AND a coverage note, and the day is re-decidable (a later run may upgrade unevidenced→corroborated but never silently flips a contradicted verdict without recording the prior one). Concurrency: one row per (intent_episode_id, decided_for_date) with ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE guarded by decider precedence — owner testimony always outranks the deterministic decider and is never overwritten. Idempotence: re-running day close for the same date is row-stable (assert decided_at unchanged when inputs unchanged). Rollback: the ledger is additive and read-only to every other butler; dropping the table restores today's behavior and no aggregate depends on it (lived-time totals keep coming from the activity layer only).
moves.verification: roster/chronicler/tests: reconcile_day extended to emit corroborations, property-tested for symmetry with the existing drop rule. tests/chronicler/test_day_close_reader_api.py sibling for the new endpoints: a contradicted intent, a corroborated intent and an unevidenced intent each render the correct verdict and evidence ids; an owner override flips the verdict and the deterministic re-run does not undo it. tests/api/test_calendar_workspace.py: an entry with a chronicler verdict renders the badge; a missing verdict renders "not yet closed", never "attended". Named honesty test: no code path may report an intent as attended without at least one corroborating activity episode id.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Extend reconcile_day to return corroborations with evidence ids (pure, unit-tested). 2) Table + writer at day close + backfill the last 90 days from existing episodes. 3) Read endpoints + plan-vs-actual aggregate. 4) Owner correction path over the existing overrides/gap-interview transport. 5) Calendar grid entry badge + Chronicles week panel.
moves.manifesto: roster/chronicler/MANIFESTO.md — squarely inside "Answer retrospective questions" and "Support corrections through an override layer", and it strengthens "I will never claim a certainty I do not have". No new message is sent, so the one-message-per-day promise is untouched. Implies a small amendment to make the pull-only forward use explicit: Chronicler may answer forward-facing questions with backward evidence when asked, and still never nudges.

moves.title: Honest day load: an owner-declared time contract the radar and find-time both enforce
moves.why: vision.md's bar is that failure never impersonates health and an aggregate must denominate something. Live, the radar tells the owner they have 106 meeting-hours in a day and calls a flight a meeting, while the owner's declared availability (public.owner_scheduling_preferences: earliest/latest meeting time, allowed days, no-meeting blocks) is honored by find-time (src/butlers/modules/calendar.py:11316-11325) and completely ignored by the radar. Owner-visible within a week: the radar stops crying wolf on travel weeks and starts flagging the thing that actually matters — "this Thursday booking sits inside the focus block you declared", "you are at 5.5 of your 4-hour Wednesday meeting budget".
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/core/temporal/conflicts.py: ConflictCandidate gains kind (meeting|travel|personal|butler), owner_response (accepted|declined|tentative|needs_action|none) and day-clipped duration; _detect_overloaded_days clips each candidate to the local day window and spreads multi-day spans across the days they cover; new issue kinds availability_violation and budget_exceeded. src/butlers/api/read_models/calendar_workspace_v1.py:1289-1300 populates the new fields from event_metadata.attendees (self+response_status, already persisted at src/butlers/modules/calendar.py:8130-8140) and from travel provenance (BUTLER: travel-authored events and the travel butler's journey rows). src/butlers/core/temporal/scheduling.py: SchedulingPreferences gains daily_meeting_budget_hours (per weekday) and protected_windows, with allows() reused by BOTH the radar and _find_free_slots so one contract governs both sides. API: GET /api/calendar/workspace/conflicts stops taking overloaded_day_hours as an unowned query default and reads the owner's contract (query param remains an override for debugging). Specs: openspec/specs/calendar-conflict-overcommitment-radar (amend the overloaded-day requirement to day-clipped, kind-aware, RSVP-aware and contract-denominated) and openspec/specs/owner-timezone-context/time-aware-delivery are untouched (this is availability, not delivery).
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: a 6h flight is classified travel and reported as travel load, not meeting-hours; a declined invite contributes zero load and no overlap; a 4-day hold contributes only its clipped hours to each covered day; exceeding the declared Wednesday budget yields budget_exceeded with the denominator in the summary. Failure: no owner contract configured → the radar falls back to today's 6.0h default and says so in the issue summary ("default budget, none declared") rather than implying the owner set it; metadata without attendees → owner_response='none' and the event counts as load (fail conservative, disclosed). Concurrency: the contract is a singleton row read per request; a mid-scan edit affects only later requests. Idempotence: pure detector, same inputs same issues. Rollback: kind/RSVP/clipping are pure-function changes behind unit tests; the new issue kinds are additive and the FE ignores unknown kinds.
moves.verification: tests/api/test_calendar_conflict_radar.py: a 4-day hold produces per-day clipped load and no impossible hour count (regression fixture built from the live 2026-09-21 event); a declined invite produces no overlap and no load; a travel-provenance event never appears in a meeting-hours summary; a booking inside a declared protected window produces availability_violation. tests/config or tests/core: SchedulingPreferences.allows() is exercised by both the radar and _find_free_slots in one shared test so the two surfaces cannot drift. frontend/src/components/calendar/ConflictRadarBanner.test.tsx: new kinds render with their denominator.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Day clipping + multi-day spreading (pure, fixes the live 106h today). 2) kind + owner_response on the candidate, sourced from existing metadata. 3) Contract fields on owner_scheduling_preferences + settings UI. 4) availability_violation / budget_exceeded issues and banner copy. 5) Spec amendment.
moves.manifesto: No single butler manifesto owns the calendar workspace; this serves vision.md non-negotiable #4 and the north-star clause that nothing is fabricated. It touches roster/travel indirectly (travel provenance as the discriminator) without crossing a schema boundary — the classification reads the calendar module's own metadata.

moves.title: Travel-feasible time: conflicts you can only find by knowing where the owner will be
moves.why: The pursuit question asks what conflicts today's system cannot see. It sees two events at the same instant and nothing else — it cannot see that a 15:00 meeting downtown and a 16:00 meeting at home are impossible, and the owner's real October (flights on the 8th, 9th, 10th, 13th, 15th, 25th, live) is exactly where this bites. Distinct from the deferred leave-by feed: no routing connector and no notification — this is a read-time feasibility verdict derived from evidence the fleet already holds, and it refuses to guess when it has no basis. Owner-visible within a week: "these two are 45 minutes apart in reality and 0 minutes apart on your calendar", and an explicit "cannot judge — never observed this transition" instead of false confidence.
moves.integration_points: New deterministic contribution job src/butlers/jobs/calendar_travel_feasibility.py following the calendar_overlay/calendar_prep precompute pattern (state keys under calendar/feasibility/, cross-schema read via the same v_*_contributions approach) so no request-time cross-schema SELECT occurs; evidence sources: Chronicler's owntracks.place_cluster and owntracks.points episodes (live: 1,323 points, 4 clusters) read over the chronicler read API/MCP, plus travel-butler journey rows for flight legs; matching key: normalized calendar_events.location text → observed place cluster, with an explicit unresolved state; src/butlers/core/temporal/conflicts.py gains issue kind travel_infeasible carrying observed_transition_minutes, gap_minutes, sample_count and basis ('observed'|'same_place'|'unknown'); src/butlers/api/routers/calendar_workspace.py conflicts route joins the precomputed feasibility envelope; spec: openspec/specs/calendar-conflict-overcommitment-radar new requirement Travel-Feasibility Candidate Pairs.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: consecutive events whose locations resolve to two place clusters between which the owner has been observed transiting in >= N minutes (median of >= 3 observations) and whose calendar gap is smaller than that median yield travel_infeasible with the sample count shown. Failure: either location unresolvable, or fewer than the minimum observations → NO issue and a basis='unknown' note on the pair (the radar never invents a travel time and never claims all-clear for that pair); the OwnTracks source stale beyond its freshness bound → the whole feasibility layer reports unavailable and the radar's other kinds still render. Concurrency: precompute job holds the standard job lease; the read is a pure join. Idempotence: recomputing over unchanged evidence produces identical envelopes (assert). Rollback: the layer is a separate state key prefix and a separate issue kind; deleting the keys removes it with no effect on the existing radar.
moves.verification: New tests/api/test_calendar_travel_feasibility.py: three observed transitions of 40-50 min between clusters A and B make a 15-min gap infeasible; two observations produce no issue and an 'insufficient evidence' basis; an unresolvable location produces no issue; a stale OwnTracks watermark degrades the layer without touching overlap/back-to-back issues. tests/jobs: the precompute writes bounded state and prunes past dates like calendar_overlay does. Live read-side check after ship: the 2026-10-08 pair on the owner's calendar renders either an evidenced verdict or an honest 'never observed' note.
moves.manifesto: roster/travel/MANIFESTO.md (movement between places is its domain — it contributes the journey legs) and roster/chronicler/MANIFESTO.md (it supplies observed transitions as retrospective evidence, on pull, with provenance and precision — no nudge, no planning). The verdict is rendered by the calendar workspace, which owns no manifesto, so the cross-butler contribution stays MCP/precompute-shaped per vision.md rule #3.

moves.title: History as a scheduling constraint: Chronicler's mined routines answer "when am I really free?"
moves.why: The system already mines the owner's actual weekly rhythm (src/butlers/chronicler/routines.py; live rows with support_count/confidence/evidence_summary) and then uses it only to infer occupation backwards. Forward planning ignores it entirely, so find-time will happily propose a slot inside the window the owner has in fact spent at a desk 4 of the last 6 weeks. Distinct from the deferred rhythm-deviation producer (that is a proactivity alert): this is a pull-only constraint feed consumed by an existing tool. Owner-visible within a week: find-time slots carry "history says you are usually working then (4/6 weeks)" and the owner can ask it to respect that; the radar flags a booking that lands on a high-confidence kept routine.
moves.integration_points: Chronicler MCP surface: a read-only chronicler_routine_windows(start, end, min_confidence) tool exposed through roster/chronicler/modules (existing module registration) returning windows with support_count, confidence, staleness and evidence_summary — no writes, no other butler's tables; consumer: src/butlers/modules/calendar.py _find_free_slots (:11268-11330) ranks/annotates slots against the returned windows via the Switchboard MCP path, and src/butlers/api/models/calendar_workspace.py CalendarSuggestedSlot gains routine_conflict {label, confidence, support_count, stale}; frontend/src/pages/CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx find-time list renders the annotation and an "avoid routine windows" toggle that maps to a hard filter; the radar reuses the same feed for a routine_collision issue; spec: openspec/specs/module-calendar (find-time annotation contract) + openspec/specs/butler-chronicler (Routine Windows Read Tool).
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: a slot overlapping a mined window of confidence >= threshold is annotated (soft) or excluded (hard, when the toggle is on) with the evidence attached. Failure: chronicler unreachable or the tool errors → slots render unannotated with an explicit 'history unavailable' note, never silently unfiltered-as-if-checked; a stale routine (missed_mine_cycles > 0, already tracked) is annotated as stale and never hard-filters. Concurrency: pure read; a routine edited mid-search affects the next search only. Idempotence: same window + same routines → same annotations. Rollback: annotation-only by default; removing the tool call restores today's ranking exactly.
moves.verification: roster/chronicler/tests: the new tool returns only rows meeting the confidence floor and marks stale rows; it performs no write. tests/modules/test_module_calendar.py: a slot inside a high-confidence window is annotated; with the hard filter it is excluded; a chronicler failure yields unannotated slots plus the unavailable flag (asserting the find-time honesty contract from move 6 is not bypassed). frontend CalendarWorkspacePage.test.tsx: annotation and toggle render and are keyboard reachable.
moves.manifesto: roster/chronicler/MANIFESTO.md — it answers a question and refuses to plan: the routine feed is read-only and Chronicler neither creates events nor sends a message, so "I do not plan. I do not schedule. I do not nudge you." holds. It does require the same small amendment as move 2 (Chronicler may answer forward-facing questions on pull with backward evidence), which is worth writing once and citing from both.

moves.title: The free-time answer states what it consulted — and never reports a failure as an empty schedule
moves.why: North star: failure never impersonates health and staleness never wears current-data authority. Today a free/busy auth failure renders "No open slots match those constraints in the selected window" (src/butlers/api/routers/calendar_workspace.py:2965-2991 discards the module's status='error' envelope), and even on success the answer never says which calendars were consulted or whether one of them is unsynced — the live workspace meta shows sources with sync_state 'stale' and last_synced_at null. Owner-visible immediately: the panel says "checked 4 calendars, 1 unreachable" instead of quietly implying a complete answer.
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/api/routers/calendar_workspace.py find_time (:2940-3013): inspect result.get('status')/result.get('error') and map to available=False with the sanitized reason; add consulted: [{calendar_id, display_name, sync_state, last_success_at, consulted: bool}] to CalendarWorkspaceFindTimeResponse (src/butlers/api/models/calendar_workspace.py) sourced from the same calendar_sources projection the /meta endpoint already returns; src/butlers/modules/calendar.py _find_free_slots returns the resolved calendar id list and a per-calendar consulted flag; frontend/src/pages/CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx:1433-1470 renders a one-line receipt under the slot list and keeps the existing degraded branch; spec: openspec/specs/module-calendar / calendar-availability-find-time — add the requirement that an availability answer discloses its basis and that an error envelope MUST NOT render as an empty result.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: slots plus "free/busy checked across N calendars at HH:MM". Failure: CalendarAuthError → available=false with the sanitized provider reason (credential redaction already handled at src/butlers/modules/calendar.py:624-651); partial per-calendar failure → slots returned with available=true and a consulted list marking the missing calendar, plus copy that says the answer may be incomplete. Concurrency: none (stateless read). Idempotence: repeated identical searches produce identical envelopes; the audit row logged at :2991 records the outcome either way. Rollback: additive response field plus one branch; reverting restores current behavior.
moves.verification: tests/api/test_calendar_workspace.py: a mocked MCP result carrying status='error' and slots=[] yields available=false and never the empty-slot copy (this is the named regression test for the defect); a partial consult renders the receipt; a clean run lists every consulted calendar. frontend CalendarWorkspacePage.test.tsx: the degraded branch renders for the error envelope, and the receipt line is present on success.
moves.manifesto: No butler manifesto owns the workspace panel; this serves vision.md's reliability bar and docs/frontend/purpose-and-single-pane.md — a consequential clause must be a door on an unbroken signal-to-evidence spine, and "you have no free time" is a consequential clause.

moves.title: The recurring-series ledger: what a standing commitment has actually cost, with a verb
moves.why: Once occurrences exist (move 1) and attendance verdicts are durable (move 2), the system can say what nothing today can: "this fortnightly block has taken 18 hours of your last quarter and the evidence corroborates 5 of 13 occurrences." That is the sharpest possible answer to "where does my time go", it is grounded in evidence rather than intent, and it ends with an action the owner can take. Owner-visible within a week of shipping: a Series panel ranking standing commitments by hours consumed and corroboration rate, each row offering "shorten", "make fortnightly" or "decline the series" as a staged proposal.
moves.integration_points: Read model: a new aggregate over calendar_events.recurrence_rule + its materialized instances joined to chronicler.intent_outcomes (move 2) — exposed as GET /api/calendar/workspace/series (src/butlers/api/routers/calendar_workspace.py, read_models/calendar_workspace_v1.py) returning per-series occurrences_in_window, hours_planned, hours_corroborated, corroboration_rate, attendee entity ids and last_corroborated_at; the action path reuses the shipped prepared-actions/approval spine and calendar_event_proposals (src/butlers/modules/calendar.py:5470-5570) so "shorten to 30 min" or "end this series" is a staged, human-confirmed proposal, never an inferred provider write (openspec/specs/calendar-event-proposals Subcalendar Routing Prerequisite still applies to butler-authored events; a change to a user-lane series is proposed with an explicit confirm); FE: a Series panel on frontend/src/pages/CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx with j/k traversal per the Dispatch keyboard contract; spec: new openspec capability calendar-series-ledger (or a requirement inside calendar-overlay-aggregation) documenting the denominator explicitly.
