moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: each series in the window reports planned vs corroborated hours with the occurrence count as an explicit denominator and a link to the evidence for each corroborated occurrence. Failure: no verdicts yet for a window (chronicler behind, or move 2 not backfilled) → hours_planned renders with corroboration shown as 'not yet closed', never as 0% attendance; a series whose occurrences are not materialized (move 1 flag off) is excluded with a disclosed reason rather than reported as a one-occurrence series. Concurrency: read-only aggregate; the proposal write is idempotent on source_event_id (existing producer guarantee). Idempotence: the aggregate is a pure function of instances + verdicts. Rollback: a read endpoint plus a panel; the action path is the existing proposals lifecycle with its own accept/dismiss audit.
moves.verification: tests/api/test_read_models_calendar_workspace_v1.py: the series aggregate denominates over materialized occurrences only and reports 'not yet closed' rather than 0% when verdicts are absent; a partial fan-out sets the honest-partial flag like the conflict scan does. tests/api/test_calendar_workspace.py: the shorten/decline action stages exactly one proposal and performs no provider write. Named honesty test: no response field may present a corroboration rate whose denominator is not the occurrence count returned in the same row.
moves.manifesto: Serves roster/chronicler/MANIFESTO.md's "Answer retrospective questions" for the evidence half and the human-in-the-write-loop doctrine (openspec/specs/calendar-event-proposals) for the action half. Depends on moves 1 and 2; it is the payoff that makes the spine worth building.

audits.live_verification: Dev stack reachable and used read-only throughout (http://127.0.0.1:42200). Live-confirmed: GET /api/spend/summary?period=7d ($85.16, 703 ledger sessions, 24.96M input / 171.16M cached-input, cache_read_cost $58.13, cache_hit_rate 0.873); GET /api/spend/forecast (mtd $134.07, projected EOM $335.18, ceiling_usd NULL, days_elapsed 12); GET /api/spend/breakdown?by=butler (travel $115.13 of ~$134 MTD) and ?by=purpose (qa $113.81 = 84.9% MTD); GET /api/spend/rules ([]); GET /api/spend/ceiling (405, no reader); GET /api/spend/by-schedule (top: chronicler_day_close $11.56/mo projected, retired flag present and false — the run-12 ghost-schedule bug is fixed); GET /api/sessions/aggregate with and without params (period= silently ignored; all-time 23,667 vs real 7d window 685 sessions / 682 success / 3 failed / 24.86M input); GET /api/sessions/{id} on the four most expensive 7d sessions (all butler=travel, trigger_source=qa, complexity=specialty, model=gpt-5.6-sol, 872k–1,535k ms); GET /api/dispatch/attempts by outcome (success 5,702; runtime_failure 1,491; quota_skip/permission_denied/breaker_open/capability_skip/fleet_halt all 0) and failure_reason prefix distribution over the 200 most recent runtime_failure rows (rate_limit_before_work 100, provider_unavailable 65, provider_auth_error 31, empty_runtime_response 2, timeout_before_work 2); GET /api/settings/models (36 rows, 11 enabled, max_context_tokens NULL on all 36; specialty tier = gpt-5.6-sol pri 30 / ollama/qwen3.5:9b pri 10); GET /api/secrets/inventory (39 credentials, expires NULL on all 39); GET /api/audit?limit=10 (empty); GET /api/butlers/{n}/analytics/friction?period=7d for 8 butlers (all zero friction kinds); GET /api/spend/breakdown?by=model billing_classes (ollama classified 'local' — run-12 finding fixed). Source-confirmed by reading the decisive mechanism: spawner.py ceiling/per-call/guardrail seams, spawner_guardrails.py, model_routing.py ceiling+ledger SQL, dispatch_intent.py, sessions.py error-marker SQL, spend.py routers, model_settings.py override writes, SpendPage.tsx, alembic core_094 and the core_231 head, docs/runtime/model-routing.md field-ownership section, openspec core-spawner / dashboard-spend-dashboard / dispatch-intent. Nothing inferred without a citation; no write of any kind was issued.
audits.jarvis_gap: Today the fleet has exactly one governance primitive — a fleet-wide singleton monthly USD ceiling (`public.spend_ceiling` id=1, alembic core_094:88-104; PUT-only at spend.py:2242) — and it has never been set, so it has never fired (live ceiling_usd NULL; `outcome=quota_skip` attempts total 0 across all time) while the month projects to $335.18. The reason it is unused is structural rather than negligent: the only thing the owner can say is "halt everything", and 84.9% of the bill is one lane they would never want to halt the fleet for. Live, $113.81 of the $134.07 month-to-date bill is `purpose=qa` — the QA staffer's investigation dispatches, which `dispatch_intent.py:88-101` already classifies as `Consequence.OBSERVE` ("produces an internal artifact nobody is waiting on") — running at `Complexity.SPECIALTY` (qa/dispatch.py:1716,3075), whose top-priority catalog entry is gpt-5.6-sol at $5.00/$30.00 per 1M (pricing.toml:68-73), for 14–26 minutes a session. The system already computes every fact needed to govern that ($ per butler, per `purpose`, per consequence class, all derivable from `public.token_usage_ledger`'s existing `butler_name`/`purpose` columns written at spawner.py:3293-3303) and then throws all of it away at the policy boundary: the ceiling has one scope, `Consequence` is consumed at exactly one line in the repository (dispatch_intent.py:299) to tolerate an unknown capability, `max_tool_calls` has had a value of 0 and no caller since it was written (spawner_guardrails.py:33; spawner.py:627,1228), `deadline_s` reaches `derive_dispatch_intent` only from QA and healing (spawner.py:1323) — the two classes where nobody waits — and the typed failure cause the failover classifier computes (`rate_limit_before_work`, `provider_auth_error`) is persisted per-row at spawner.py:2449 and aggregated by nothing. The consequence is that the fleet's actual binding constraint is invisible to its own budget spine: 100 of the 200 most recent dispatch failures are a provider-side "You've hit your usage limit" and 31 are an expired access token, and neither has a cost line, a cluster, or a door. Meanwhile the one number the owner does see points at the wrong owner: the Spend page's mover chip links to `/butlers/travel?tab=spend` (SpendPage.tsx:747) for spend that a staffer incurred. The gap is not measurement — measurement is unusually good here — it is that there is no governance *object*: nothing the owner can name, scope, price, and be answered by.
audits.ideal: A JARVIS-grade spend and dispatch governance system gives the owner one object — a scoped policy — and one promise: every dollar the fleet spends was admitted by a policy the owner can read, and every dollar it refused to spend is on a receipt. The object is a row keyed by a scope the owner actually thinks in (the fleet, a butler, a trigger class like `qa` or `route`, or a consequence class like `observe`), carrying the whole budget envelope for that scope in one place: a monthly ceiling, a per-call cap, a tool-call budget, a wall-clock SLO with a declared degrade mode, and whether an irreversible act in that scope must be independently verified. It lives in `public` beside the ledger it is evaluated against, is resolved most-specific-wins at spawn in the same round trip the ceiling already prefetches, and its resolved row id is stamped on the resolution receipt so a dispatch from last month can be read against the policy that actually produced it. The daemon stays deterministic: the policy is data, the resolver is arithmetic, and the only thing the session may do is knock — a bounded `request_escalation` door that the daemon, not the model, decides, re-admitting the continuation through the same gate so an escalation can never outrun its own ceiling and a guardrail termination never throws away work the owner already paid for. Every consequential edit renders, before it is written, the exact sentence the gate will enforce — computed by the same resolver, never by the frontend — naming who stops, when, and what the owner will stop receiving; and every edit lands in the audit log with a reason, no exceptions and no asymmetry between the cheap knobs and the expensive ones. On the read side spend stops being an aggregate and becomes a diagnosis: spend grouped by the same scopes the policy uses, the fleet's failures clustered by the typed cause the classifier already computes with the dollars each cluster consumed attached, retries priced as their own line, and credential failures joined to the credential that failed. And once a week the system hands the owner a receipt in its own words: what it refused and what that saved, what it escalated and what the tier hop cost, what changed in policy and who changed it — so that the calm on the Spend page is earned by arithmetic the owner can re-derive rather than asserted by a number with no denominator.

findings.title: 84.9% of the owner's month-to-date inference bill is the QA staffer, and no governance object can express a limit on it
findings.evidence: live GET /api/spend/breakdown?by=purpose (qa $113.81) vs GET /api/spend/forecast (mtd_usd $134.07); live GET /api/sessions/{f3255bc9-ead6-4109-891d-1ee44906ff01,15f16dc2-…,f81c1116-…,582cde9b-…} all butler=travel trigger_source=qa complexity=specialty model=gpt-5.6-sol duration 872,452–1,535,441 ms; src/butlers/core/qa/dispatch.py:1715-1720 and :3074-3079 (trigger_source="qa", Complexity.SPECIALTY); live GET /api/settings/models (specialty tier: gpt-5.6-sol pri 30, ollama/qwen3.5:9b pri 10); pricing.toml:68-73 ($5.00/1M input, $30.00/1M output) vs pricing.toml:82-87 (gpt-5.6-luna $0.20/$1.20); src/butlers/core/dispatch_intent.py:99 ("qa": Consequence.OBSERVE); src/butlers/api/routers/spend.py:2242-2289 (the only ceiling is a singleton row id=1 with a single monthly_usd column)
findings.detail: The lane the system itself classifies as producing an internal artifact nobody is waiting on runs on the most expensive model in the catalog for 15–26 minutes a session and carries $113.81 of a $134.07 month, projecting to ~$284/month. The only lever that exists is a fleet-wide ceiling; setting it low enough to bite QA would deny the owner's route replies as well (the exact sentence CeilingEdit already renders at SpendPage.tsx:714-717). Rerouting the observe class to gpt-5.6-luna at 25x lower input and output prices is a ~$109/month reduction with no owner-facing effect, and the system has no object in which to say so.
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: the risk classification the system already computes has no policy object to attach to, so the largest cost concentration is unsteerable by construction

findings.title: stale premise: /api/sessions/aggregate silently ignores period=, so run 12's fleet numbers (22,879 sessions, 3.3B tokens, 88.3% success 'in a week') were all-time; the real 7d fleet is 685 sessions at 99.6% success
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/sessions.py:503-542 (the aggregate endpoint declares butler / trigger_source / status / success / from_date / to_date / request_id / include_trigger_breakdown — there is no period parameter, and FastAPI drops unknown query params silently); live GET /api/sessions/aggregate?period=week and ?period=week&zzz=1 both return total 23,667 / 3,344,915,618 input tokens, identical to the bare GET /api/sessions/aggregate; live GET /api/sessions/aggregate?from_date=2026-09-06&to_date=2026-09-12 returns total 685, success 682, failed 3, input 24,862,188, output 1,551,721; same shape at src/butlers/api/routers/spend.py:1586-1594 (GET /api/spend/breakdown takes by/db/configs/pricing/mgr and no period; :1605 hardcodes month_start) with frontend/src/pages/SpendPage.tsx:179 fetching it without a period
findings.detail: Every dossier number sized off /api/sessions/aggregate?period=... is an all-time total wearing a period label — the exact 'aggregates denominating nothing' shape, here aimed at agents and at the run-12 dossier rather than at a page. It matters directly to this design: a per-scope ceiling sized from 23,667 sessions/week instead of 685 is 35x wrong, and the real fleet failure rate is 0.44% (3/685), not 11.7%. Any governance receipt that quotes a windowed denominator must resolve it from an explicit from/to, and the API should reject unknown query params rather than absorb them.
findings.taxonomy_shape: aggregates denominating nothing (run 11 theme), extended: the denominator is silently replaced by all-time because the parameter that would scope it does not exist and is not rejected

findings.title: The one governance primitive that exists has never been armed, and the gate it feeds has never fired in the fleet's lifetime
findings.evidence: live GET /api/spend/forecast → ceiling_usd null, ceiling_source_error false, projected_eom_usd 335.181358; live GET /api/dispatch/attempts?outcome=quota_skip → meta.total 0 (against outcome=success 5,702 and outcome=runtime_failure 1,491); live GET /api/spend/rules → {"data":[]}; live GET /api/audit?limit=10 → []; GET /api/spend/ceiling → 405 (src/butlers/api/routers/spend.py:2242 registers only PUT, no reader); alembic/versions/core/core_094_spend_tables.py:96-104 (CONSTRAINT spend_ceiling_single_row CHECK (id = 1))
findings.detail: Zero ceilings, zero spend rules, zero audit entries, zero denials — the entire governance surface is inert while the month projects to $335. The pre-spawn gate (spawner.py:1681-1719), its concurrent prefetch (spawner.py:1398-1400), the fleet-halt attention producer (dispatch_outcomes.py:283-289), the FleetHaltBanner and the over-ceiling attention row (SpendPage.tsx:2942-2969) are all real, tested and unreachable. The design conclusion is not 'the owner should set the ceiling' — it is that a ceiling whose only setting is 'stop the fleet' is not a ceiling anyone can responsibly arm, and the gate must gain scopes before the primitive gains a user.
findings.taxonomy_shape: substrate shipped / consumer never (run 12 theme), inverted: the consumer exists and is correct, but the policy vocabulary is too coarse for the owner to ever populate it

findings.title: The fleet's real binding budget constraint is a provider-side usage limit the budget spine cannot see, and the typed cause that names it is persisted and aggregated by nothing
findings.evidence: live GET /api/dispatch/attempts?outcome=runtime_failure&limit=200 → failure_reason prefixes: rate_limit_before_work 100, provider_unavailable 65, provider_auth_error 31, empty_runtime_response 2, timeout_before_work 2 (meta.total 1,491); error_message samples "Codex CLI exited with code 1: You've hit your usage limit.", "Codex CLI exited with code 1: Your access token could not be refreshed", "OpenCode CLI exited with code 1: UnknownError: Model not found"; src/butlers/core/spawner.py:2442-2455 (failure_reason=_failover_decision.reason is written to public.model_dispatch_attempts); src/butlers/core/failover_classifier.py:189-216 (_RATE_LIMIT_MARKERS incl. "hit your usage limit") and :105-147 (_PROVIDER_AUTH_MARKERS); src/butlers/api/routers/model_settings.py:1867-2060 (GET /api/dispatch/attempts returns a flat list; the only narrowing is reason_prefix at :1895/:1966); frontend/src/pages/SpendPage.tsx:2619 (failure_reason is rendered only inside the fleet-halt attempt list, which is empty because no ceiling exists)
findings.detail: The classifier computes a typed cause for every failure and the spawner stores it, so a same-cause cluster is a GROUP BY on an existing column — no new write path, no new vocabulary. Half of the fleet's recent dispatch failures are one external cause (the provider's own usage limit), 15.5% are an expired credential, and 32.5% are a catalog entry pointing at a model the runtime does not have. None of these appears as a cluster, as a cost line, or as an owner signal; the owner's only view of them is a flat reverse-chronological list on a settings surface. This is also why the USD ceiling has never been the constraint: the thing that actually stops dispatches is a limit denominated in someone else's currency.
findings.taxonomy_shape: computed then discarded at the seam (run 12 theme): the cause is typed, stored, and never grouped

findings.title: max_tool_calls remains unreachable: default 0, no non-passthrough caller, while the spec presents three live guardrails
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/spawner_guardrails.py:33 (_DEFAULT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS = 0) and :101-128 (_check_tool_call_budget returns None when max_tool_calls <= 0); src/butlers/core/spawner.py:627 and :1228 (default-valued parameters only), :834 and :866 (pure passthrough), :2598-2601 (the OR chain); openspec/specs/core-spawner/spec.md:621-660 (Requirement: Degenerate Session Guardrails — "Three independent budgets SHALL be enforced"; the tool-call scenario at :644-646 can never execute); src/butlers/core/sessions.py:822 and src/butlers/core/failover_classifier.py:267-275 both reserve a tool_call_budget_exceeded bucket; live per-butler friction for 8 butlers returns by_kind.guardrail_termination = 0 everywhere
findings.detail: Unlike max_token_budget, which reaches Spawner.trigger from ScheduleConfig, max_tool_calls has no TOML field, no runtime_config key, no catalog column and no API. The single defence against a runaway tool loop is the 6-consecutive-identical-call detector, which a loop that varies one argument walks straight past — and the two most expensive sessions on the fleet each ran 15–26 minutes. This is the guardrail the governance object exists to make reachable, and it is only safe to arm after bu-2jtfw.5's partial-output preservation lands, because today a trip discards the work (spawner.py:3019 output=None; :2795 store_session_episode on the success path only).
findings.taxonomy_shape: gates as metadata (run 11 theme): a documented budget with no control plane

findings.title: Consequence is derived for every dispatch and is still consumed at exactly one line in the repository
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/dispatch_intent.py:57-67 (the enum), :88-101 (_TRIGGER_PROFILES assigns OBSERVE/REVERSIBLE/EXTERNAL per trigger class), :299 (tolerate_unknown = intent.consequence is Consequence.OBSERVE); grep for `.consequence` / `Consequence.` across src/ outside dispatch_intent.py returns nothing, and the only other in-file reference is the receipt projection at :158
findings.detail: Verified unchanged on main after run 12. A dispatch that will send mail or actuate a light and a tick that will update a cache receive identical budget treatment, identical retry policy, identical verification (none) and identical model requirements; the one difference is whether an unknown capability disqualifies a candidate. Because the enum is a pure function of trigger class, a consequence-scoped governance row needs no new column anywhere — it is a policy keyed on a derived value the daemon already computes, which is precisely why it is the cheapest scope to add and the one that unlocks the QA case.
findings.taxonomy_shape: computed then discarded at the seam

findings.title: Butler model-tier override writes — the largest single cost lever on the settings surface — still leave zero audit trail and require no reason
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/model_settings.py:1542 (upsert_butler_model_overrides, PUT /api/butlers/{name}/model-overrides) and :1611 (delete_butler_model_override) contain no audit.append; grep for audit.append in that file returns only :723, :796, :869, :916, :994, :1020 — all global model_catalog CRUD; contrast src/butlers/api/routers/permissions.py:184-186 (422 {"error":"reason_required"}) and src/butlers/api/routers/spend.py:2280-2288 (audit.append("spend.ceiling.update"))
findings.detail: First observed in run 12's config-governance audit and still open on main. It is load-bearing for this design rather than a loose end: a weekly governance receipt that reports "what changed" reads the audit log, and the one write that can move a butler from a $0.20/1M tier to a $5.00/1M tier is the write it cannot see. The asymmetry is also the wrong lesson to teach the owner — the cheap knob (a spend rule) is gated and audited, the expensive one is not.
findings.taxonomy_shape: governance asymmetry on one surface (run 12 theme)

findings.title: Staffer spend is attributed to the domain butler it ran against, so the Spend page's top mover points the owner at the wrong knob
findings.evidence: live GET /api/spend/breakdown?by=butler → travel $115.13 (of ~$134 MTD), the largest row by 20x, while ?by=purpose → qa $113.81; the four most expensive 7d sessions are butler=travel / trigger_source=qa (live); src/butlers/core/spawner.py:3293-3303 (record_token_usage writes butler_name=self._config.name and purpose=trigger_source into the same ledger row — the dimensions exist, they are just never crossed); frontend/src/pages/SpendPage.tsx:747 (MoverChip links to /butlers/{name}?tab=spend) and :3096-3110 (MoversStrip is fed by the by-butler summary)
findings.detail: The by-butler and by-purpose dimensions are both computed from the same ledger rows and are never joined, so the page can say 'travel is your top mover' and 'qa is your top purpose' about the same $114 without ever saying they are the same dollars. An owner following the mover chip lands on the travel butler's spend tab and finds a domain butler that costs about $1.30 a month. Crossing the two dimensions is a single GROUP BY on columns that already exist.
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: two honest dimensions of one row, never crossed, so each is individually true and jointly misleading

findings.title: Retry and failover cost is unattributable from the ledger: token_usage_ledger carries no logical_session_id and no attempt_index
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/model_routing.py:1231-1235 (INSERT INTO public.token_usage_ledger (catalog_entry_id, butler_name, session_id, input_tokens, output_tokens, cached_input_tokens, cache_creation_tokens, purpose)); src/butlers/core/spawner.py:2439 and :2447 (attempt_index = len(_attempted_ids)) and :2453 (logical_session_id=effective_request_id) — both live only on public.model_dispatch_attempts; live GET /api/dispatch/attempts?outcome=runtime_failure meta.total 1,491 against outcome=success 5,702 (20.7% of all recorded attempts are runtime failures)
findings.detail: Each failover attempt is its own session row and its own ledger row, so on every spend surface a retried logical request reads as N independent sessions rather than one unit that cost N times. There is a join that recovers it — ledger.session_id -> model_dispatch_attempts.session_id -> logical_session_id — but nothing performs it, so 'what did retrying cost me this month' is unanswerable and a per-scope ceiling silently charges retries to the scope without ever showing them as a line.
findings.taxonomy_shape: last hop has no door (run 11 theme), on the cost spine

findings.title: The classification_timeout bucket keys on a model-name substring that matches no enabled model, so any governance receipt built on by_error_marker under-counts to zero
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/sessions.py:828-839 (_ERROR_MARKER_CASE_SQL: model ILIKE '%mini%' AND error ILIKE '%butler=switchboard%') and the mirror at :128-141 (_is_friction_classification_timeout: "mini" not in model.lower()); live GET /api/settings/models enabled entries: gpt-5.6-luna, opencode-go/mimo-v2.5, gpt-5.6-sol, opencode-go/kimi-k2.6, opencode-go/qwen3.7-plus, opencode-go/minimax-m2.7, opencode-go/minimax-m3, ollama/qwen3.5:9b — none contains 'mini' except minimax, which serves workhorse, not cheap; live GET /api/sessions/{id} rows carry trigger_source and complexity columns that state the fact directly
findings.detail: Carried forward from run 12 and unchanged on main. Noted here only because it is a prerequisite input: the weekly governance receipt's failure section and the friction ledger's classification_timeout kind both read this CASE, and both will report zero for the fleet's cheap-tier timeout mode regardless of how many occur. The fix is to key on the stored facts (trigger_source='classification' AND complexity='cheap') rather than a retired provider's naming convention.
findings.taxonomy_shape: writer's clock impersonating world's clock (run 11 theme), applied to a model naming convention

findings.title: dropped: credential-expiry-vs-ceiling-window correlation — every credential in the inventory has a NULL expiry, so the line would read 'unknown' 39 times out of 39
findings.evidence: live GET /api/secrets/inventory → 39 entries across cli/system/user/identities, expires: null on all 39 (states: ok 29, warn 7, expired 1, null 2); src/butlers/api/routers/secrets_v2.py:1286-1310 (_derive_state computes 'expiring'/'expired' from expires_at with EXPIRING_LEAD_TIME_BY_CATEGORY empty at :1277, so the default lead time applies to a field nothing populates)
findings.detail: Run 12 proposed a 'will this credential outlast the ceiling window' line in the tier/ceiling confirm dialogs. It is unbuildable: the field it reads is empty everywhere, including for the codex CLI auth that gpt-5.6-sol (89.8% of the weekly bill) depends on. The buildable correlation is the inverse and is already evidenced: join provider_auth_error dispatch clusters (31 of the 200 most recent failures, live) to the credential whose runtime raised them, so the owner sees 'this credential cost you N dispatches on these days' from observed failures rather than from a declared date nobody declares. That is folded into move 1 rather than filed as its own item.
findings.taxonomy_shape: dropped alternative

findings.title: dropped: a butler_name column on public.spend_ceiling (run 12's proposed per-butler ceiling)
findings.evidence: alembic/versions/core/core_094_spend_tables.py:96-104 (spend_ceiling is a CHECK-enforced singleton with one numeric column); src/butlers/core/model_routing.py:2690-2745 (check_monthly_ceiling reads that one row and compares one total); live evidence that butler is the wrong axis: the concentration is trigger_source=qa ($113.81) spread across butler rows, not a butler
findings.detail: Adding a butler dimension to the singleton solves the smallest case and misses the observed one: the fleet's cost concentration is a trigger class that runs *under* several butlers, and a butler-keyed ceiling on travel would deny travel's own owner-facing route replies to stop a staffer's self-test. It also forces a second gate (a butler ceiling and a fleet ceiling evaluated separately) where one scope-resolved envelope reads once. Superseded by move 2's scope_kind/scope_key table, which subsumes the butler case as one scope_kind among five.
findings.taxonomy_shape: dropped alternative

findings.title: dropped: putting spend ceilings or dispatch SLOs in {schema}.runtime_config or on public.model_catalog
findings.evidence: docs/runtime/model-routing.md:42-64 ("Do not look for model settings on the runtime-config surface, and do not add operational limits to the catalog"; runtime_config holds core_groups, max_concurrent, max_queued, catalog_read_sensitivity, tool_exposure_policy, seeded from [butler.runtime_seed]); about/heart-and-soul/vision.md Non-Negotiable Rule 5; src/butlers/core/model_routing.py:2586-2685 (price_mtd_from_ledger requires a pool with visibility into public.token_usage_ledger and public.model_catalog)
findings.detail: runtime_config is per-schema and per-butler, so a fleet-scoped or trigger-class-scoped policy has no home there, and evaluating a ceiling from a butler schema would require the dashboard to fan out across 12 schemas to render one number — reviving exactly the fan-out-versus-ledger divergence that price_mtd_from_ledger exists to prevent. The catalog is explicitly closed to operational limits. The governance table therefore belongs in public, beside spend_rules and the ledger it is priced against.
findings.taxonomy_shape: dropped alternative

findings.title: dropped for now: min_context_tokens as a governance/SLO field — supplying it today would exclude the entire catalog
findings.evidence: live GET /api/settings/models: 36 rows, max_context_tokens null on all 36; src/butlers/core/dispatch_intent.py:317-325 (CONTEXT_WINDOW_UNKNOWN excludes a candidate whose declared window is None whenever a floor is set)
findings.detail: Unchanged since run 12. DispatchIntent's third dead field stays dead in this design: the governance row deliberately carries deadline_s, max_cost_usd_per_call and max_tool_calls but not min_context_tokens, because undeclared-is-unproven means the first caller to supply a floor takes out every candidate in every tier at once. The prerequisite is a seed of max_context_tokens/max_output_tokens for the 11 enabled entries — a data task that belongs with the catalog owner, not in this design.
findings.taxonomy_shape: dropped alternative

moves.title: Slice 1 — Scoped spend truth and the same-cause cluster: read-only, no schema, ships alone
moves.why: docs/frontend/purpose-and-single-pane.md names the three loops as Detect / Diagnose / Act; on spend the fleet has Act (a ceiling) and a partial Detect, and no Diagnose at all. The north star's 'nothing fabricated' clause is being met number-by-number while the page as a whole misleads: by-butler says travel and by-purpose says qa about the same $113.81, and the mover chip sends the owner to the travel butler (SpendPage.tsx:747). Owner-visible payoff, in money from live numbers: this slice names $284/month ($113.81 MTD over 12 elapsed days, extrapolated) that is currently filed under a domain butler's name and is invisible as a lane the owner could govern, and it collapses 1,491 flat failure rows into three causes with dollars attached (100 rate_limit_before_work / 65 provider_unavailable / 31 provider_auth_error in the 200 most recent). It is the precondition for every later slice's decision and it changes no dispatch behaviour, so it can ship the day it is written.
moves.manifesto: Serves architecture.md § Why Connectors Are the Computational Cost Boundary (the cost boundary must be legible before it can be enforced) and the Switchboard staffer contract's SLA/failure-mode framing — a staffer's own consumption is an infrastructure fact the owner is entitled to read separately from their life domains. No manifesto amendment required; this slice only reads.
moves.integration_points: New read endpoints on the existing mount (src/butlers/api/routers/spend.py, prefix /api/spend, conventions per docs/api_and_protocols/response-conventions.md): (a) GET /api/spend/scoped?dimension=butler|trigger_class|consequence|butler_trigger_class&from&to returning per-scope cost, session count, projected EOM and the same unpriced_models / source_error degraded envelope every other spend response carries. Implementation is a group-by extension of the existing MTD SQL: public.token_usage_ledger already stores butler_name and purpose (written at src/butlers/core/spawner.py:3293-3303 with purpose=trigger_source), trigger_class is butlers.core.dispatch_intent.trigger_class_of(purpose), consequence is _TRIGGER_PROFILES[trigger_class].consequence (dispatch_intent.py:88-101) — pricing goes through the unchanged price_ledger_usage_rows (model_routing.py:2580-2645) so the scoped subtotals can never diverge from the ceiling total. (b) GET /api/spend/causes?from&to grouping public.model_dispatch_attempts by split_part(failure_reason,':',1) x butler x day, left-joined to the ledger on session_id for the dollars each cluster consumed, plus a retry line: the cost of ledger rows whose session_id belongs to a logical_session_id with more than one attempt row. (c) The credential join: provider_auth_error clusters annotated with the runtime_type of the catalog entry that raised them, linking to /secrets. Frontend: two new sections in frontend/src/pages/SpendPage.tsx between ByScheduleSection and BreakdownSection — a scope table with a dimension switcher (butler / trigger class / consequence) and a 'Same cause' strip; MoverChip (SpendPage.tsx:735-770) gains a staffer-lane marker and links to the scoped view instead of /butlers/travel?tab=spend when the mover's spend is dominated by a non-domain trigger class. Spec: openspec/specs/dashboard-spend-dashboard MODIFIED — new Requirement 'Scoped spend attribution' and 'Failure-cause clustering', both stating that an empty result is degraded evidence unless source_error is explicitly false (mirrors the existing Requirement at spec.md:19-22). No migration.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: the scope table renders butler / trigger_class / consequence rollups summing to the same total as GET /api/spend/summary for the same window, and the cause strip renders three rows with counts, days and dollars. Failure: the ledger query fails -> source_error true and a SourceDegradedNote, never an empty scope table read as '$0 in every scope' (the contract already enforced at spend.py:1608-1620); the attempts query fails independently -> the scope table still renders and only the cause strip degrades, because they are separate evidence. Unpriced models: excluded from the scoped subtotal and reported in unpriced_models per scope, so a scope's number is never silently short. Concurrency: pure reads against an append-only partitioned ledger; two concurrent callers may see a row count differing by in-flight sessions, which is correct and is why the window is explicit rather than a preset. Idempotence: pure functions of (window, dimension). Rollback: delete the two endpoints and the two sections; nothing else references them.
moves.verification: (1) tests/api/test_spend.py extended: an attribution test seeding ledger rows with butler_name='travel', purpose='qa' asserting the butler dimension and the trigger_class dimension report the same dollars and that the butler_trigger_class dimension reports one crossed row — the direct regression for the misattribution finding. (2) A consistency test asserting sum(scoped[dimension]) == GET /api/spend/summary total for the same explicit from/to, for all four dimensions. (3) A degraded test asserting a ledger failure yields source_error true with an empty breakdown, and that an empty breakdown with source_error false renders as a genuine zero (the three-way state contract). (4) A cause-cluster test seeding public.model_dispatch_attempts rows with failure_reason 'rate_limit_before_work: …' and 'provider_auth_error: …' asserting the prefix grouping and the joined cost. (5) A retry-line test asserting two attempts under one logical_session_id with two ledger rows produce one logical unit whose retry cost equals the non-final attempt's cost. (6) A window test asserting the endpoints reject an unknown query parameter rather than silently ignoring it (the /api/sessions/aggregate?period= shape). (7) frontend/src/pages/SpendPage.test.tsx: a mover-chip test asserting a staffer-dominated mover does not link to the domain butler's spend tab.
moves.slice_plan: Independently shippable as written. Order inside it: (a) the scoped endpoint and its consistency test; (b) the cause endpoint and the retry line; (c) the two page sections and the mover repair. Each of the three is separately revertible.

moves.title: Slice 2 — public.dispatch_governance: one scoped policy object, one resolver, one admission gate (core_232)
moves.why: vision.md Non-Negotiable Rule 5 puts operational tuning in the database and Rule 4 keeps the daemon deterministic; docs/runtime/model-routing.md:42-64 closes the catalog to operational limits and reserves runtime_config for per-butler daemon fields. Nothing in that split provides a home for a fleet-scoped, trigger-scoped budget, so the fleet has exactly one ungrained ceiling and it has never been armed (live ceiling_usd null; quota_skip attempts 0 all-time). Owner-visible payoff, in money from live numbers: a single row scope_kind='trigger_class', scope_key='qa', monthly_usd=40 caps the lane carrying $113.81 of a $134.07 month; a row scope_kind='consequence', scope_key='observe', max_cost_usd_per_call=0.25 pushes those dispatches off gpt-5.6-sol ($5.00/$30.00 per 1M, pricing.toml:68-73) onto gpt-5.6-luna ($0.20/$1.20, pricing.toml:82-87) — a 25x rate reduction on ~$284/month of observe-class spend, i.e. roughly $109/month or $1,300/year, with zero effect on any dispatch the owner is waiting for, because Consequence.OBSERVE is defined at dispatch_intent.py:59-60 as 'produces an internal artifact nobody is waiting on'. It also finally makes the enum load-bearing beyond dispatch_intent.py:299.
moves.manifesto: Serves vision.md Rules 4 and 5 and architecture.md § The Core Loop step 3 (the daemon decides admission; the session never sees the policy). Implies one amendment: the QA staffer contract (openspec/specs/staffer-qa, roster/qa/MANIFESTO.md) gains an explicit budget clause — a staffer's SLA section already names failure modes and escalation, and 'the owner may bound this service's monthly inference cost, and the service degrades by reducing investigation depth rather than by fabricating findings' belongs there.
moves.integration_points: Migration alembic/versions/core/core_232_dispatch_governance.py (down_revision = 'core_231', the current head at alembic/versions/core/core_231_filtered_events_id_index.py). Creates public.dispatch_governance (id UUID PK, scope_kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK IN ('fleet','butler','trigger_class','consequence','butler_trigger_class'), scope_key TEXT NULL, monthly_usd NUMERIC(12,6) NULL, max_cost_usd_per_call NUMERIC(12,6) NULL, max_tool_calls INT NULL, deadline_s INT NULL, degrade_mode TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'refuse' CHECK IN ('refuse','partial'), verification_required BOOL NOT NULL DEFAULT false, enabled BOOL NOT NULL DEFAULT true, reason TEXT NOT NULL, policy_version INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, created_at, updated_at) with UNIQUE (scope_kind, scope_key), a CHECK that scope_key IS NULL exactly when scope_kind='fleet', and the same _grant_best_effort role loop core_094 uses (alembic/versions/core/core_094_spend_tables.py:27-66). It migrates the existing public.spend_ceiling row into the scope_kind='fleet' row and DROPs public.spend_ceiling (backward compatibility waived). moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: a dispatch resolves an envelope; every field is within budget; the resolution receipt records the binding scope id and policy_version alongside DISPATCH_POLICY_VERSION (dispatch_intent.py:52-54) so the dispatch can later be read against the policy that produced it. Concurrency: rows are read per spawn in the same prefetched round trip, so an edit mid-flight affects the next dispatch only; the fleet-halt insert stays ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING against a partial unique index, now on (scope_id, month). moves.title: Slice 3 — Reachable max_tool_calls and a runaway budget the owner can arm
moves.why: openspec/specs/core-spawner/spec.md:621-660 states three independent budgets SHALL be enforced; one of them cannot fire in production and has not since it was written (spawner_guardrails.py:33; no non-passthrough caller at spawner.py:627/1228). Three downstream taxonomies reserve a bucket that is guaranteed empty (sessions.py:822, failover_classifier.py:267-275, qa/sources/session_records.py). The north star's 'failure never impersonates health' has a mirror: a documented guardrail that cannot trip is a claim of protection the system does not provide. Owner-visible payoff: the two most expensive sessions in the fleet's week ran 14 and 26 minutes on a $5/$30 model; a max_tool_calls bound on the observe scope turns 'this could run away' from a hope into a number the owner sets. It is small because the object and the resolver already exist after slice 2 — this is one parameter threaded through two call sites.
moves.manifesto: Serves vision.md Rule 4 (the daemon enforces deterministically) and openspec/specs/core-spawner's own guardrail requirement, which this makes true for the first time. No new manifesto.
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/core/spawner.py:1228 (_run's max_tool_calls parameter) is set from the resolved envelope rather than from the caller default when the caller did not pass one; the value flows unchanged into the existing OR chain at :2598-2601 and _check_tool_call_budget (spawner_guardrails.py:101-128). The resolution receipt records the applied bound and its binding scope. openspec/specs/core-spawner MODIFIED: the Degenerate Session Guardrails requirement gains a 'Control plane' clause naming public.dispatch_governance as the source of max_tool_calls and stating that the shipped default remains 0 (disabled) when no scope binds it. Hard ordering constraint: this MUST land after bu-2jtfw.5 slice S2 (partial-output preservation), because arming a guardrail that today discards result_text (spawner.py:2598-2612 raises with the text in hand; :3019 writes output=None; :2795 store_session_episode is on the success path only) would convert a runaway into a total loss of paid work. Do not re-implement S2 here; depend on it.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: no scope binds max_tool_calls -> the parameter stays 0 and the check is skipped, byte-for-byte today. Armed: a session exceeding the bound raises the existing tool_call_budget_exceeded RuntimeError, the failover classifier suppresses retry as it already does (failover_classifier.py:267-275), and — because S2 landed — the partial output and tool digest are preserved and the session reads as 'stopped at your budget with this much done', not as a bare error. Failure: the envelope read failed -> unbounded (fail open), same as slice 2. Concurrency: the bound is captured per attempt at resolution time, so a mid-session policy edit cannot retroactively terminate a running session. Idempotence: the check is a pure function of the merged tool-call list. Rollback: clear the field on the scope row.
moves.verification: (1) tests/core/test_spawner_guardrails.py extended with the first end-to-end reachability test: a governance row with max_tool_calls=3 and a scripted runtime making 4 calls produces a tool_call_budget_exceeded termination — the assertion that cannot pass on main. (2) A default test asserting that with no binding scope the parameter is 0 and a 500-call session is not terminated. (3) A preservation interlock test asserting the terminated session's result_text reached session_complete (depends on bu-2jtfw.5 S2; this test is the interlock that keeps the two from being merged out of order). (4) A receipt test asserting the applied bound and its scope id are persisted. (5) A taxonomy test asserting the session's by_error_marker bucket is tool_call_budget_exceeded rather than 'other' (sessions.py:820-822), closing the guaranteed-empty bucket.
moves.slice_plan: One PR, gated on bu-2jtfw.5 S2 being on main. Ship with max_tool_calls unset on every scope so the behaviour change is opt-in and the first arming is an owner decision made against the preview endpoint's 7-day counterfactual.

moves.title: Slice 4 — Dispatch SLOs: give the classes the owner waits on a deadline, and a named degrade instead of a spinner
moves.why: DispatchIntent declares deadline_s and evaluate_fit implements FitCode.DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, yet on the production path deadline_s is supplied only from timeout_override (spawner.py:1323), which only healing and QA set (healing/dispatch.py:670; qa/dispatch.py:1720,3079) — the two classes dispatch_intent.py:98-99 marks REVERSIBLE and OBSERVE, i.e. where nobody is waiting. The route and dashboard classes, the only EXTERNAL ones with an owner in front of them, always pass None, so the exclusion code can never fire for them. The north star's 'earned calm' has no expression today: the owner cannot say how long they are willing to wait, and the system cannot answer 'I cannot do that in your budget'. Owner-visible payoff, in minutes: the fleet's 248 route-triggered sessions in the last 7 days have no wall-clock contract at all, and the catalog's session_timeout_s is a uniform 1800s on all 11 enabled entries (live) — the owner's interactive turn and a 30-minute batch job share one clock.
moves.manifesto: Serves architecture.md § Why Connectors Are the Computational Cost Boundary, extending 'gate before the expensive thing' to the dispatch itself, and the Messenger/Switchboard interactive-reply contracts, which promise the owner a reply and today cannot promise when.
moves.integration_points: The resolved envelope's deadline_s and degrade_mode are supplied to derive_dispatch_intent at src/butlers/core/spawner.py:1323 when timeout_override is None, so the existing hard-fit machinery (dispatch_intent.py:137-150, 206-219) starts excluding candidates whose recent evidence proves they overrun — evidence that already exists via model_routing.get_routing_evidence and the duration_ms recorded on every attempt (spawner.py:2440,2454). For degrade_mode='partial' the same value becomes timeout_s at spawner.py:2109-2114, so the deadline is a real wall clock and the result is marked partial-within-budget rather than reported complete; for 'refuse' the dispatch is denied through the existing quota_skip denial path with a named reason. min_context_tokens is deliberately not wired (see dropped finding). openspec/specs/dispatch-intent MODIFIED (Hard Fit Evaluation: deadline_s has an owner-policy source) and openspec/specs/core-spawner MODIFIED (session timeout resolution order gains the governance envelope between timeout_override and catalog_timeout_s). Frontend: the Governance section's scope editor gains deadline and degrade-mode fields with the consequence sentence naming the effect ('route dispatches for finance that no model can prove it finishes in 15s will be refused with a named reason instead of running').
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: a route scope carries deadline_s=15; candidates with proven p95 over 15s are excluded by the already-implemented FitCode and the receipt names the exclusion. Nothing fits: degrade_mode='refuse' -> denial with 'no model can meet your 15s budget for route dispatches on this butler', written as a quota_skip attempt row so the existing denial vocabulary and surfaces carry it; degrade_mode='partial' -> the deadline becomes the session timeout and the result is honestly marked partial. Absence of evidence never excludes (dispatch_intent.py's existing rule) — a candidate with no duration history is admitted, because 'unproven slow' is not 'proven slow'. Failure: envelope read error -> unbounded, recorded on the receipt. Concurrency: the deadline is pinned per attempt; a failover to a second candidate re-evaluates fit against the same deadline, never a refreshed one. Idempotence: pure. Rollback: clear deadline_s on the scope.
moves.verification: (1) tests/core/test_dispatch_intent.py extended: a resolution test asserting that with a 15s deadline a candidate whose recorded evidence proves p95 > 15s is excluded with FitCode.DEADLINE_EXCEEDED for trigger_class='route' — the code path that cannot execute on main. (2) A no-evidence test asserting a candidate with zero duration history is not excluded. (3) A degrade test covering both modes: refuse produces a named denial with no invocation; partial invokes with timeout_s == deadline_s and marks the result partial rather than successful. (4) A precedence test asserting an explicit timeout_override (healing/QA) still wins over the envelope, so the two existing callers are unchanged. (5) tests/core/test_spawner_ceiling_enforcement.py-adjacent: a receipt test asserting the applied deadline and its scope are persisted alongside DISPATCH_POLICY_VERSION.
moves.slice_plan: 4a: deadline_s wired for the dashboard trigger class only with degrade_mode='refuse' (smallest blast radius; the owner is present to see the refusal). 4b: extend to route. 4c: the partial degrade mode and its honest result marking. 4d: the Governance-section editor fields and the counterfactual preview.

moves.title: Slice 5 — One re-dispatch mechanism, two doors: the session escalation request and the bounded continuation after a guardrail stop
moves.why: openspec/specs/complexity-classification fixes complexity at spawn (spawner.py:619-630) and its only named failure mode is 'default to workhorse'; there is no upward path anywhere in src/. Symmetrically, a guardrail or deadline stop today ends the logical request with no continuation (failover_classifier.py:267-275 suppresses retry by design, correctly — a runaway must not be replayed blindly, but a bounded continuation seeded with what it already produced is a different thing). bu-2jtfw.5 slice S3 is already building public.session_handoffs and the session-detail rendering of a preserved partial; this slice adds the second door and the one re-dispatch path both need, rather than a second mechanism. Owner-visible payoff: cheap-first becomes safe — the fleet's 54 classification sessions and 306 consolidation ticks in the last 7 days can be pushed down-tier because the loop self-corrects upward on evidence instead of on a pre-spawn guess, and a long job that hits its budget shows 'stopped at your budget, continued as <session>' instead of vanishing. Every continuation is re-admitted through slice 2's gate, so the escalation door can never outrun the ceiling that authorised the first attempt.
moves.manifesto: Serves architecture.md § The Core Loop (the session requests, the daemon decides and re-dispatches — intelligence in the session, determinism in the daemon, vision.md Rule 4) and the Switchboard MANIFESTO's message-classification responsibility. Explicitly named as a non-goal by bu-2jtfw.5, so this is the sanctioned owner of it.
moves.integration_points: Build on bu-2jtfw.5's public.session_handoffs rather than a new table: add handoff_kind TEXT CHECK IN ('guardrail','deadline','escalation'), to_complexity TEXT NULL, continuation_session_id UUID NULL, decision TEXT, with a UNIQUE (logical_session_id, from_session_id) key (migration core_233 or a column addition inside bu-2jtfw.5's own revision if it has not merged — coordinate, do not fork the table). New core tool module src/butlers/core_tools/_escalation.py registering request_escalation(reason, findings, confidence) in a new 'escalation' core group, gated through runtime_config core_groups per vision.md Rule 5 and the tool_exposure_policy contract (docs/runtime/model-routing.md:50-64). Spawner: Spawner.trigger gains escalated_from (spawner.py:619-700) threaded into session_create (core/sessions.py:115-180 gains continuation_of_session_id, shared with the run-12 task-continuity column if core_229 already added one — check before adding a second); one bounded re-dispatch at most per logical_session_id, enforced by the unique key plus a depth check, and admitted through resolve_governance so it consumes the same scope budget; _write_dispatch_attempt gains an 'escalation' outcome so the tier hop is visible in provenance and rolls up under one logical_session_id in /api/spend (the retry line from slice 1 prices it). Never for Consequence.EXTERNAL: a half-finished outward act becomes an owner-visible partial, not an automatic resumption. Specs: openspec/specs/complexity-classification MODIFIED (new Requirement 'Upward escalation'), openspec/specs/core-spawner MODIFIED (guardrail termination may produce exactly one bounded continuation), openspec/specs/core-sessions MODIFIED (continuation lineage).
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path (escalation): a cheap session calls request_escalation with typed findings; the tool returns a terminal marker; the session ends with success=true and an 'escalated' outcome, NOT a failure; the daemon re-dispatches once at the next tier with the original prompt plus the findings block. Happy path (continuation): a guardrail stop with a preserved partial (from bu-2jtfw.5) produces one continuation for REVERSIBLE trigger classes only, seeded with the handoff. Top tier: request_escalation at the reasoning tier returns a refusal naming 'no higher tier'; the session continues and must answer where it is. Budget: the continuation is admitted through the governance gate; if the scope is now over ceiling the continuation is denied with the scope-named reason and the handoff records decision='denied_by_governance' — the owner sees why the second half never ran. Concurrency: unique (logical_session_id, from_session_id) means a session calling the tool twice gets the first decision back and the daemon never spawns two continuations. Idempotence: replaying the termination handler returns the stored continuation_session_id. Rollback: disabling the 'escalation' core group removes the tool; a runtime_config flag disables continuation, leaving bu-2jtfw.5's preservation-only behaviour intact.
moves.verification: (1) A spawner integration test at the real seam: a fake cheap-tier runtime whose scripted tool call is request_escalation produces exactly one follow-up _run at the next tier, both sessions share logical_session_id, and the second session's prompt contains the findings block. (2) A depth test asserting a second escalation from the continuation is refused and no third dispatch occurs. (3) A concurrency test firing request_escalation twice from one session asserting one handoff row and one continuation. (4) A governance interlock test: the scope is over ceiling at continuation time -> no second dispatch, handoff decision recorded, quota_skip attempt written — the assertion that the door cannot outrun the budget. (5) A consequence test asserting an EXTERNAL-consequence guardrail stop produces a handoff and NO continuation. (6) A cost-attribution test asserting both attempts appear under one logical_session_id so slice 1's retry line prices the pair as one logical unit rather than two failures plus a success.
moves.slice_plan: 5a: the session_handoffs column additions and continuation lineage, no behaviour change. 5b: request_escalation behind the gated core group in record-only mode — the tool returns 'noted' and the daemon does not re-dispatch, so the owner can see for a week how often the cheap tier would have asked. 5c: enable the bounded re-dispatch for trigger_class='classification' only (highest volume, lowest blast radius). 5d: extend to schedule and to the guardrail door; session-detail renders the chain.

moves.title: Slice 6 — Consequence-gated verification: an independent check before an irreversible act leaves the system
moves.why: Consequence is derived for every dispatch and consumed at exactly one line (dispatch_intent.py:299). RFC 0028's physical-consequence gate proved the owner wants a door on actuation, but the only verifier behind that door is the owner. The north star requires that every consequential clause is a door on an unbroken signal-to-session-to-evidence spine; today an EXTERNAL dispatch that will send mail and a REVERSIBLE tick that will update a cache get identical treatment. Owner-visible payoff: outbound acts start carrying a verdict — 'verified against 3 evidence items' or 'verifier disagreed, held for you' — and a disagreement routes to the existing approvals spine instead of to the recipient. It is placed last among the enforcement moves deliberately: it is the only one that spends money to save trust, and it must be affordable, which it becomes once slice 2 can bound the verifier lane (a consequence:observe scope with a per-call cap covers the verifier's own dispatches).
moves.manifesto: Serves the north star's consequential-clause-as-door clause and architecture.md § The Core Loop step 5; requires an amendment to openspec/specs/module-approvals (a disagreement is a new approval source) and to whichever butler manifestos own an irreversible verb — respecting specialist ownership means the verb registry is sourced from the shipped RFC 0028 risk map, never re-invented here.
moves.integration_points: New table public.act_verifications (session_id, act_tool_call_ref, consequence, verifier_session_id, verdict, disagreement_reason, evidence_refs JSONB, decided_at) with UNIQUE (session_id, act_tool_call_ref) — a later core revision, after 232/233. A post-invoke hook in the spawner success path after the tool-call merge (src/butlers/core/spawner.py:2540-2585, before the guardrail block) firing only when intent.consequence is Consequence.EXTERNAL AND the merged tool calls contain a verb in the RFC 0028 risk map AND the resolved envelope's verification_required is true (the governance object's fifth field, added in slice 2's migration and inert until now). The verifier is a bounded dispatch with a new 'verification' entry in _TRIGGER_PROFILES (dispatch_intent.py:88-101) carrying Consequence.OBSERVE and no MCP wiring beyond a read-only evidence tool; it carries the parent's logical_session_id so spend rolls to the act, and it is admitted through resolve_governance like everything else. A disagreement creates an approval through the existing modules/approvals spine rather than a bespoke surface. Specs: openspec/specs/module-approvals and openspec/specs/core-spawner MODIFIED; openspec/specs/dispatch-intent MODIFIED (the verification trigger class).
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: an EXTERNAL session proposes an irreversible act; the verifier agrees; the act proceeds and the receipt carries the verdict and verifier session id. Disagreement: the act is held and an approval is created naming the reason — a door, not a silent block. Failure: the verifier fails, times out or is denied by governance -> verdict 'unverifiable' and the act is HELD (fail-closed for irreversible acts; a verifier that could not run must never read as agreement — the deliberate inversion of every other fail-open gate in this design, and the one place where a budget denial must not simply wave the act through). Concurrency: keyed on (session_id, act_tool_call_ref) so a replayed hook cannot double-verify or double-approve. Idempotence: re-running the hook returns the stored verdict. Rollback: verification_required defaults false on every scope and the RFC 0028 verb map gates which verbs qualify; an empty intersection means zero verifications and the loop is unchanged.
moves.verification: (1) A spawner test asserting the hook fires for consequence=EXTERNAL plus a registered verb and does NOT fire for the same verb at REVERSIBLE — the proof that the enum is finally load-bearing beyond dispatch_intent.py:299. (2) A fail-closed test: verifier raises -> verdict 'unverifiable', act held, approval created, no egress tool call executed. (3) A governance-denial fail-closed test: the verifier is refused by its scope ceiling -> the act is still held, not released — the interaction between two safety systems must resolve toward caution. (4) An idempotence test replaying the hook asserting one act_verifications row and one approval. (5) A cost test asserting the verifier attempt shares the parent's logical_session_id so /api/spend attributes it to the act. (6) An approvals integration test asserting the disagreement lands in the existing spine with the reason as its dossier.
moves.slice_plan: 6a: the verb registry sourced from RFC 0028 plus public.act_verifications in shadow mode — record what WOULD have been verified, verify nothing. 6b: run the verifier and record verdicts without holding anything; measure the disagreement rate before granting authority. 6c: grant holding authority for one verb class the owner picks (home actuation, already gated by RFC 0028). 6d: extend to outbound message egress through the Messenger contract; surface the verdict on the act receipt.

moves.title: Slice 7 — The weekly governance receipt: what was refused, what was escalated, what it saved
moves.why: vision.md § What Success Looks Like measures the system by the mental labour it absorbs, and architecture.md § The Core Loop step 6 promises the outcome is recorded whenever tokens are. Governance is the one subsystem where the owner's confidence must be earned by arithmetic they can re-derive, and today there is nothing to re-derive from: the audit log is empty (live), no denial has ever been written, and the Spend page reports only what was spent, never what was refused. Owner-visible payoff, in minutes per week: one page that answers 'did my policies do anything, and did they cost me anything' without opening four surfaces — replacing the manual cross-read of /spend, /settings/models, /secrets and the flat attempts list that the run-12 config-governance journey described as a monthly errand. It is small because slices 1, 2 and 5 already produce every input.
moves.manifesto: Serves the north star's earned-calm clause and openspec/specs/dashboard-audit-log; distinct from bu-6jv4m.6 (proactive calm receipts, which is about insight quiet) — this one is about policy, and it should link to that rather than duplicate it.
moves.integration_points: GET /api/spend/governance/receipt?from&to composing, with no new write path: refusals from public.model_dispatch_attempts (outcome='quota_skip', grouped by the scope named in failure_reason, with the counterfactual dollars from the resolved envelope); escalations and continuations from public.session_handoffs with their tier-hop cost from slice 1's retry line; savings from spend_rules.saved_7d plus the local-tier share from GET /api/spend/breakdown?by=model billing_classes (live: ollama/qwen3.5:9b correctly classified 'local'); policy changes from public.audit_log filtered to spend.governance.* / spend.rule.* / spend.ceiling.* / model.override.* — which requires slice 2's audit closure at model_settings.py:1542,1611 to be complete or the 'what changed' section is provably incomplete and must say so. Prerequisite repair inside this slice: src/butlers/core/sessions.py:828-839 and :128-141, whose classification_timeout branch keys on model ILIKE '%mini%' (matching no enabled model live) — re-key to the stored facts trigger_source='classification' AND complexity='cheap' so the receipt's failure section is not structurally zero. Frontend: a receipt panel at the top of the Governance section on frontend/src/pages/SpendPage.tsx, and a link from the Overview attention surface when a scope crossed 80% of its ceiling during the week. Specs: openspec/specs/dashboard-spend-dashboard MODIFIED (new Requirement 'Weekly governance receipt', with the explicit clause that an unavailable input is named rather than omitted).
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: the receipt renders four sections with counts, dollars and deep links to the evidence (each refusal links to its attempt row, each escalation to its session chain, each policy change to its audit entry). Nothing happened: the receipt says 'no scope was bound this week and nothing was refused' as an explicit known-zero, never a blank panel — and it still reports the spend the policies did NOT stop, so an inert governance layer reads as inert rather than as protective. Failure: any one of the four inputs is unavailable -> that section renders a SourceDegradedNote naming which evidence is missing and the totals suppress rather than under-report (the three-way state contract already enforced across this page). Incomplete audit coverage: if any governance-relevant action type is known to be unaudited, the 'what changed' section says so by name rather than presenting a partial list as complete. Concurrency: pure reads over an explicit window. Idempotence: pure function of (window, rows). Rollback: remove the endpoint and the panel.

audits.ideal: A Situation is the owner-facing object the fleet reasons in: the owner says one sentence in Telegram or dashboard chat — "Dad's in hospital until Friday", "Tokyo 12-19 Oct" — and the fleet answers with a named case of a declared kind, a horizon it can plan against, and a roster of butlers that each accepted their role in git. Five archetypes the roster can actually staff (trip led by travel; illness led by health; visit led by relationship; money_event led by finance; home_disruption led by home) declare, fleet-side, which contributions a situation of that kind needs, and each butler's own declaration accepts or omits its role, so a required-but-unaccepted role projects as unclaimed and the readiness denominator can never be fabricated. Each contributor writes typed clauses — known, pending, decision — every one carrying a resolvable door, a basis (measured/reported/derived/absent) and an as_of, enforced at write time so an undoored clause cannot be persisted; the daemon composes them deterministically into one honest paragraph per open case, which is what the owner sees on /situations/:id, what the digest folds five separate pings into, and what Telegram sends as one message per situation rather than one per butler. A git-declared question registry lets the chat lane answer "is anything unhandled about Tokyo?" from that case with a typed answer stamped with its read instant, or with one of six typed refusals — no_such_situation, archetype_unknown, role_unclaimed, contributor_silent, instrument_blind, outside_horizon — each of which is itself a door to the repair. Nothing about a situation is inferred where the owner could simply say it, nothing is reported satisfied that was merely never asked, and the whole plane has one writer (Switchboard), one spec, and one paragraph the owner can read in ten seconds and then stop carrying.
audits.jarvis_gap: Today the fleet has a situation object that no situation can enter. RFC 0032 is marked "Implemented (Slices 1-7 landed)" and the live instance holds zero cases: the only running consumer is fleet-case-lapse-sweep, a job whose sole purpose is closing cases, firing daily against an empty table. The proximate cause is not missing design but a stranded one — Switchboard, the RLS-designated sole writer of fleet_cases, has a runtime_config row seeded 2026-04-07 whose core_groups list predates the git addition of "fleet_cases" to roster/switchboard/butler.toml, and seed_if_empty is ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so open_case / propose_case_posture / close_case / record_case_link are not registered on the one daemon allowed to execute them; every other butler's write dutifully forwards through route() to a tool that is not there. The gate is inverted on top of that: the three butlers that explicitly opted in are the only three excluded, because a butler with no core_groups declaration gets every group by the NULL-means-all default. Above the mechanical fault sits the conceptual one: a case has no name, no kind, no horizon, no origin, no owner. correlation_key is an operator key, the read model projects nothing else, and nothing declares what a situation of a given kind needs — so a Tokyo trip and a respiratory illness are the same shape of row, no butler knows it is expected, no denominator exists for "unhandled", the chat staffer (Concierge) is not even in core_217's grant list so it cannot SELECT a case, and the owner cannot tell the fleet anything it did not infer. The distance to the ideal is one page, one git taxonomy, one verb, one clause table and one question registry — but none of it is reachable until the write path is unstranded.
