findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: git-declared capability stranded behind a seeded-once operational row — identity changed in git, the DB row that actually gates it was written once at first boot and never reconciled, so the capability is inert with no error anywhere
findings.detail: RFC 0032 makes butler_switchboard_rw the only role that may INSERT/UPDATE fleet_cases and fleet_case_links (RLS, core_217), and _fleet_cases.py routes open_case / propose_case_posture / close_case / record_case_link from every other butler to Switchboard. Switchboard's live core_groups does not contain "fleet_cases", so those four tools were never registered on its MCP server and the forwarded call resolves to a missing tool. No case can be opened by any butler by any path. This is why the live table is empty and why the lapse sweep — the one wired consumer — has nothing to sweep. Any situation design that assumes the S3 contribution tools work is building on a premise that is false in production.

findings.title: The core-group gate is inverted: only the three butlers that opted in are excluded
findings.evidence: src/butlers/daemon.py:1251 comment "When core_groups is None (default), all groups are enabled"; grep core_groups roster/*/butler.toml -> only roster/finance/butler.toml:11, roster/relationship/butler.toml:11, roster/switchboard/butler.toml:15; live runtime-config shows relationship and finance seeded 2026-04-07 without fleet_cases and the other ten butlers with core_groups null
findings.taxonomy_shape: governance asymmetry on one surface (run 12 theme) — explicit opt-in is punished, silence is rewarded
findings.detail: The three butlers that explicitly listed fleet_cases in git are exactly the three whose DB row pins an older list, so they alone lack the tools; the ten that never declared core_groups get every tool by the NULL-means-all default. The archetype contributors this design needs most (health, travel, home, general) can therefore call contribute_case_evidence and read_case but can never open a case, because open_case forwards to a Switchboard that cannot execute it. Per-butler role acceptance in this design must therefore not be expressed through core_groups alone.

findings.title: Concierge — the dashboard-chat read staffer — has no SELECT on any fleet-case table
findings.evidence: alembic/versions/core/core_217_fleet_case_file.py:39-52 _ALL_RUNTIME_ROLES lists twelve roles and omits butler_concierge_rw; core_217 is the only migration touching fleet_case tables (grep -l fleet_case alembic/versions/core/); butler_concierge_rw exists (alembic/versions/core/core_198_runtime_attention_outbox.py:274, core_221_dashboard_messages_search_index.py:113); roster/concierge/butler.toml:4 "System-plane read staffer: answers fleet status, spend, and session questions for the dashboard chat"
findings.taxonomy_shape: last hop has no door (run 11 theme) — the read surface exists, the reader whose whole job is using it was left off the grant list
findings.detail: RFC 0032 states "All roles retain SELECT on both tables — a case file is a shared read surface." The role enumeration silently makes that false for the one staffer that answers the owner's questions from the dashboard chat. An answerable-question registry over cases is unimplementable until this grant exists, and no test asserts the role list is complete.

findings.title: RFC 0032 reads as Implemented while its only live consumer is the job that closes cases
findings.evidence: about/legends-and-lore/rfcs/0032-fleet-case-file.md:3-6 "Status: Implemented (Slices 1-7 landed)"; same file's S7 text admits "the insight broker itself still does not call any fleet-case tool"; grep -n 'fleet_case|open_case|contribute_case' roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py -> zero hits; docs/concepts/fleet-case-file.md ends "No broker wiring or dashboard surface exist yet"; live schedules -> fleet-case-lapse-sweep enabled, last_run 2026-09-11T20:17Z; live /api/switchboard/cases -> []; live /api/system/conditions shows resolved episodes that src/butlers/core/fleet_cases.py:657 backfill_from_owner_conditions would have converted
findings.taxonomy_shape: substrate shipped / consumer never (run 12 theme), with the status field asserting the opposite
findings.detail: Seven slices of schema, tools, attention, sweep, backfill and link binding are marked landed. In the running instance the aggregate behaviour is a daily sweep querying an empty table. The status line is itself the stale premise: a reader planning work on top of the RFC reasonably assumes cases exist. The backfill is an idempotent script, not a job — nothing schedules or receipts it, so 'landed' means merged, not ran.

findings.title: A case cannot be named: no title column, and the synthesized sentence the broker pays for still has nowhere to go
findings.evidence: alembic/versions/core/core_217_fleet_case_file.py:83-101 (fleet_cases columns: id, correlation_key, state, posture, outcome, opened_at, updated_at, closed_at — no title, kind, or horizon); roster/switchboard/api/models.py:876-892 FleetCaseSummary projects exactly those; RFC 0032 Context: the broker "pays an LLM call to synthesize a one-sentence summary for each cluster ... then discards both every delivery cycle"; roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py:1022 _synthesize_cluster_sentence, :1147 interpolated into a digest string and never persisted
findings.taxonomy_shape: computed then discarded at the seam (run 12 theme) — the naming problem RFC 0032 was written to fix survived the RFC
findings.detail: The one thing an owner needs to recognise a situation — a name — is the one field the table lacks. correlation_key ('health:owner:respiratory-illness') is explicitly an operator-readable key, not owner prose. Any narrator, dashboard row or Telegram line must therefore either render an internal key at the owner or fabricate a name at read time. This is a schema-level blocker for every remaining piece of the situation design.

findings.title: Case evidence carries the writer's clock and no basis, so a narrator built on it would stamp stale facts with fresh authority
findings.evidence: alembic/versions/core/core_217_fleet_case_file.py fleet_case_evidence columns (id, case_id, contributor, kind, ref, payload, contributed_at) as projected at roster/switchboard/api/models.py:896-906; src/butlers/core/fleet_cases.py:65 _EVIDENCE_COLUMNS; src/butlers/core_tools/_fleet_cases.py:206-240 contribute_case_evidence takes only (case_id, kind, ref, payload)
findings.taxonomy_shape: writer's clock impersonating the world's clock (run 11 theme)
findings.detail: contributed_at records when a butler wrote the row, not when the fact it cites was true, and there is no basis field distinguishing measured / reported by the owner / derived / could-not-observe. A paragraph composed from evidence alone cannot honour the north star's staleness clause. The design below therefore puts as_of and basis on a separate append-only clause table rather than mutating the immutable evidence ledger.

findings.title: No openspec capability spec exists for fleet cases — the feature has a HOW and no WHAT
findings.evidence: grep -rl 'fleet_case' openspec/ -> only openspec/specs/runtime-config-api/spec.md, openspec/specs/runtime-config-dashboard-ui/spec.md and openspec/changes/add-runtime-tool-surface-discovery/* (all merely naming the core group); no fleet-case or situation capability directory under openspec/specs; CLAUDE.md routing table puts WHAT in openspec/ and HOW in RFCs
findings.taxonomy_shape: gates as metadata (run 11 theme) — a design contract with no required-behaviour spec to reconcile against code
findings.detail: Seven slices shipped against a single RFC with no spec requirements or scenarios, so a spec-vs-code reconcile could not detect that the write path is dead. Every move below names the spec section it must add.

findings.title: Switchboard's manifesto never mentions case arbitration, though RFC 0032 makes it the sole arbiter
findings.evidence: roster/switchboard/MANIFESTO.md:15-27 Responsibilities (ingress, classification, routing, buffer, agent registry, connector registry, butler-to-staffer routing) and Non-Responsibilities — no case, situation or arbitration clause; RFC 0032 'Write authority' makes butler_switchboard_rw the "sole arbiter of a case's existence, state, posture, and ledger bindings"; about/heart-and-soul/vision.md non-negotiable #6 makes the governing document binding and requires formal amendment
findings.taxonomy_shape: ownership asserted in an RFC but never written into the binding document
findings.detail: Switchboard also now owns the fleet-case-lapse-sweep schedule (live) with no SLA or failure-mode row in its contract. Adding archetype projection, situation declaration and narration on top compounds an unamended contract; the design carries the amendment as an explicit slice rather than a footnote.

findings.title: dropped: an LLM-composed case narrator
findings.evidence: about/heart-and-soul/vision.md non-negotiable #4 (daemon deterministic, intelligence in ephemeral sessions); roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py:1022-1116 _synthesize_cluster_sentence is best-effort and its output is unverifiable against its inputs
findings.taxonomy_shape: rejected alternative
findings.detail: The earlier proposal composed the owner paragraph with the broker's synthesis machinery. Rejected: a synthesized sentence cannot guarantee that every clause is a door, cannot carry per-clause as_of and basis, and can smooth an absence into a reassurance. The design instead makes each contributor write a typed clause with a mandatory resolvable door and composes deterministically. The LLM's job moves upstream — a butler session decides what its clause says; the daemon only orders and stamps them.

findings.title: dropped: a general public.context_windows table as the situational horizon
findings.evidence: src/butlers/context_bus.py:73-85 _WRITE_PERMISSIONS (butler names only, no owner writer) and :90-104 _TTL_CONFIG (belief expiry doubling as situation duration); src/butlers/jobs/context_producers.py:329-355 (trip end_date read and discarded)
findings.taxonomy_shape: rejected alternative
findings.detail: A second dated-fact substrate parallel to the case would create two answers to 'what will be true on 14 Nov'. A situation already is the window's owner and has a lifecycle, an arbiter and an outcome, so the horizon belongs on fleet_cases (horizon_start/horizon_end/horizon_precision/owner_timezone) with one read, situations_at(ts). The context bus keeps its meaning — true now, believed for a TTL — and can gain a case-derived producer later, outside this design.

findings.title: dropped: fanning a declaration out as a new switchboard.situation_declared domain event
findings.evidence: no roster/switchboard/domain_events.toml exists (only finance, health, home, travel declare one); roster/finance/domain_events.toml:19, roster/health/domain_events.toml:18, roster/home/domain_events.toml:18 all set permitted_subscribers = [] (undeliverable by construction); src/butlers/core/domain_event_contracts.py:83,372,438
findings.taxonomy_shape: rejected alternative
findings.detail: Routing the ask through the domain-event bus would make an owner declaration depend on five butlers first landing subscription declarations in git, on a bus where three of five existing contracts are already write-only. The design uses the expectation ledger as the ask record and Switchboard's existing route() primitive as the wake — one mechanism, MCP-only, with the receipt being the expectation row's own state transition.

findings.title: dropped: move, new_job and bereavement archetypes
findings.evidence: ledger: place registry has zero place rows and home spaces were deferred; no employment or estate substrate anywhere under roster/; openspec/specs has no housing, employment or estate capability
findings.taxonomy_shape: rejected alternative
findings.detail: Declaring an archetype the roster cannot staff manufactures a denominator: a 'move' case would report 0 of 5 contributions forever, exactly the fabricated-aggregate failure the north star forbids. The registry ships only kinds where every required role maps to a butler with real data today; unstaffable kinds are refused by the loader with the list of known kinds rather than silently accepted as free text.

findings.title: dropped: a deadline_crunch archetype owning its own due date
findings.evidence: openspec/changes/commitment-lifecycle/proposal.md (owner-declared commitments as a class on owner_conditions with an explicit resolution path); openspec/specs/deadline-tracking; ledger: forward horizon on owner_conditions is a known deferred item
findings.taxonomy_shape: rejected alternative / boundary statement
findings.detail: A situation must not become a third forward-obligation mechanism beside owner_conditions and the deadline lane. The boundary: a commitment is one obligation with one owner; a situation is a multi-butler reframing with a horizon. A dated obligation binds INTO a case as a clause with door_kind='condition', and the case never owns the due date.

moves.title: S2 — The archetype registry: five git-declared situation kinds, per-butler role acceptance, and a denominator that cannot be fabricated
moves.why: vision.md non-negotiable #6 makes each manifesto binding, so no fleet-level file may conscript a butler; and 'What Success Looks Like' measures the system by the mental labour it absorbs — a case that cannot say what it is missing absorbs none of the worry. The archetype is the shared vocabulary the case plane has never had: today a Tokyo trip and a respiratory illness are the same shape of row. The five kinds are chosen against real substrate — trip (travel trips/legs/PNR, home away, finance spend, general calendar, health medication supply, relationship plans), illness (health symptoms/conditions/medications/measurements, home climate, general calendar, relationship, lifestyle), visit (relationship entities, home, general calendar, lifestyle), money_event (finance transactions/budgets/anomaly/subscriptions/obligations, lifestyle, travel, home), home_disruption (home HA + maintenance, finance cost, general calendar). Owner-visible payoff: 'Trip · Tokyo · 12-19 Oct — 4 of 6 · Health has not confirmed medication supply through the 19th · Home has no away plan · Lifestyle: no role in a trip.'
moves.manifesto: Each contributing butler's MANIFESTO.md gains one line under its scope naming the archetypes it accepts a role in and what it contributes; the acceptance in roster/<butler>/case_roles.toml is valid only if the manifesto covers it, which is the review gate (one PR per butler so each is reviewed against its own binding document). Switchboard's contract gains 'archetype projection' under the Responsibilities row added in S1.

moves.title: S3 — Owner-declared situations: Lane E, the declare verb, and the horizon a case plans against
moves.why: Every situation-recognition path in this repo is inference-only, and the dashboard classifier has exactly four lanes — statement, bug, action, question (src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:540-640) — so 'Dad's in hospital until Friday' is classified as a data statement and routed to one butler, losing the fact that it reframes six domains. The highest-value situations are the ones the owner already knows and the fleet cannot infer; today the owner re-explains them to five butlers one channel at a time, exactly the labour vision.md says the system exists to absorb. Owner-visible payoff: say it once in Telegram or dashboard chat, confirm the proposal, and every accepted contributor is asked, with a receipt per butler and a horizon the whole fleet can plan against.
moves.manifesto: Switchboard's contract gains 'Situation declaration intake' under Responsibilities and an SLA row (a declaration produces asks to every accepted contributor within one dispatch cycle). No domain manifesto changes — declaration is arbitration, not domain logic, which is why it lives on the staffer.

moves.title: S4 — The case narrator: typed clauses with a mandatory door, composed deterministically into one honest paragraph
moves.why: When five butlers each notice one facet of an illness the owner gets five pings and assembles the situation themselves — the labour vision.md says the system exists to absorb. RFC 0032 S4 dedupes the quiet-hours bypass per case (a rate concern) and does not touch authorship, so even inside quiet hours the owner still receives five paragraphs in five voices. A budget decides how many messages; a narrator decides who speaks and in whose words. The north star's 'every consequential clause is a door on an unbroken signal-to-session-to-evidence spine' becomes a write-time database constraint here rather than a review convention. Owner-visible payoff: one block per open situation — 'Tokyo, 12-19 Oct. Known: flights confirmed (PNR QX7T2R, 2h ago) · hotel paid (Fri) · passport valid to 2029. Pending: Home has no away plan (asked 3d ago) · Health has not confirmed medication supply through the 19th. Decide: Sam's dinner Thu 16th falls mid-trip — move it or decline? Blind: Finance cannot see card spend (SimpleFIN stale 6d) [Reconnect].'
moves.manifesto: Messenger's contract gains a clause that a case block is delivered as one message per situation, never one per contributor. The narrator_butler field in the archetype registry names which specialist's voice frames the block, honouring specialist manifesto ownership without letting it author other butlers' clauses.

moves.title: S5 — The answerable-question registry: the chat lane answers from a situation, with typed answers and typed refusals
moves.why: The classifier's Lane D offers exactly two question scopes — one butler's domain data, or the system itself (src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:604-616) — so 'is anything unhandled about Tokyo?' has no home: it is not one butler's domain and not infrastructure, it is the fleet's situation plane, and the staffer that would answer it (Concierge) has no SELECT on any fleet-case table until S1 lands. Prose answers also cannot distinguish 'no' from 'I have no data' — the honesty distinction the fleet already got right for expected_signals (present|absent|unmeasurable) and for reaction receipts (ignored vs unreported). Owner-visible payoff: ask in chat or Telegram and get 'Tokyo: 4 of 6. Home was asked 3 days ago and has not answered [Home]. Finance cannot see card spend — SimpleFIN stale 6 days [Reconnect].' instead of a confident paragraph or a shrug.
moves.manifesto: roster/concierge/butler.toml:4 and Concierge's contract are amended from 'fleet status, spend, and session questions' to include the situation plane — a scope widening that must be written down before the tool is added, per vision non-negotiable #6.
moves.integration_points: Declaration: NEW roster/switchboard/case_questions.toml — the registry of question types the situation plane can answer, each with args, an answer schema, a required as_of, and its permitted refusals. Six types: situation.open_list (-> [{case_id, kind, title, horizon, posture, satisfied, total_required}]), situation.readiness(case_id) (-> the five-state expectation vector with a reason per non-satisfied cell), situation.what_must_i_decide(case_id?) (-> decision clauses with their doors), situation.on_date(date) (-> situations_at from S3), situation.who_is_working_on_it(case_id) (-> per-butler last_contribution_at and state), situation.history(case_id) (-> evidence + clause timeline). Loader: extend src/butlers/core/case_archetypes.py with the same fail-closed pattern, projecting into public.case_question_types (migration core_236, switchboard-fenced, concierge-readable). Refusal vocabulary, typed and each carrying a door: no_such_situation, archetype_unknown (with known_kinds), role_unclaimed (nobody assigned — door to the archetype registry), contributor_silent (accepted but pending past cadence — door to that butler's page), instrument_blind (contributor reported unmeasurable with a repair door — door to /ingestion/connectors/:type/:endpoint), outside_horizon (no case covers that date). A refusal is an answer with a door, never 'I don't know'. Classifier: src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:604-616 — answer_question gains scope='situation' beside domain and system, targeted at concierge, with cannot_answer keeping its scope_checked contract. Concierge: NEW read tool read_situations(kind=None, open_only=True, case_id=None) in the dashboard_read module (roster/concierge/butler.toml [modules.dashboard_read]), backed by the S1 SELECT grants and the S2 readiness read; it never writes. Telegram: the same question types answer over the normal route path with no transport knowledge in any butler (vision non-negotiable #7). Spec: openspec/specs/fleet-situations/spec.md Requirement 'Answerable questions and typed refusals'; amend openspec/specs/dashboard-chat-ui (scope='situation') and openspec/specs/module-dashboard-read.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: a situation question resolves to one typed answer with as_of on every field. Failure: the case DB is unreachable -> the typed refusal 'situation plane unavailable' with the degraded envelope, never a confident 'nothing is open'; a question type outside the registry -> refused with the list of answerable types, so the chat lane never improvises a case read. Concurrency: answers are pure reads at one snapshot and each carries its read instant, so two answers seconds apart are comparable rather than contradictory. Idempotence: reads only; no state change, no cooldown consumed, no attention budget spent — a question the owner asked is not an insight the fleet volunteered and must never compete in the delivery budget. Rollback: core_236 down() drops the projected type table; scope='situation' falls back to the existing cannot_answer path with scope_checked naming the situation plane, itself an honest answer. Quiet hours: not applicable — the owner initiated the exchange; an answer is never suppressed and never bypasses anything.

audits.live_verification: Read-side live verification against http://127.0.0.1:42200 only (no frontend dev server is listening on this host — `ss -ltnp` shows 42200/42173/42086 API-side ports and no Vite port; every frontend claim below is therefore source-confirmed from files, not browser-reproduced). Live-confirmed: `GET /api/butlers` returns 13 agents (chronicler, concierge, education, finance, general, health, home, lifestyle, messenger, qa, relationship, switchboard, travel), which is the multiplier for every per-butler destination count. `GET /api/butlers/{name}/schedules` across all 13 returns 303 schedule rows, 191 enabled (finance 36, chronicler 33, relationship 21, travel 18, switchboard 16, home 15, health 13, education 13, general 12, lifestyle 10, qa 3, messenger 1, concierge 0). `GET /api/schedules` → 404 (no fleet-wide schedule route exists). Static analysis: parsed `SHELL_CAPABILITIES` programmatically (48 capabilities, 36 `discoverability: "global"`, 15 chords, 21 chordless globals, 9 globals with `placement: null`); transitively walked each capability's lazy loader import graph (depth 6) to find which destinations register any page verb.
audits.jarvis_gap: The shell's discovery spine is real and well-built — one typed capability manifest (`shell-capability.ts`) projecting the router, rail, chords, chunk prefetch, query warmup and page-context policy; one command menu; two registries; one `usePageActions` primitive designed so a verb's key and its palette entry can never diverge. What is missing is coverage and generalization: the spine addresses 48 destinations while the product is roughly 250 addressable states, and every newest surface was built outside it. The butler console alone is a second, unmanaged route table — 195 distinct `?tab=`/`&section=` URL states across 13 butlers, none of them a capability, none findable in the command finder, none chorded, none prefetched, none in the page-context registry — which is where Finance, Travel, Home, Lifestyle, General, Messenger and Switchboard live in their entirety (those seven butlers own zero rows in the rail). The manifest's own `keywords` field, the one thing that would let an owner find a page by what they want rather than by its label, is silently discarded before it reaches the finder's fuzzy matcher. Sub-navigation is solved four incompatible ways: manifest-driven for `/ingestion`, hardcoded for `/entities`, sidebar-only for `/health`, and not at all for `/settings`. Detail pages — where the consequential, irreversible verbs live (EntityDetailPage carries `onForget`, `onArchive`, `onPromoteTier`, `onDemoteTier`, `onOpenMergeReview` among 52 click handlers) — register zero keyboard or palette routes; 10 of 12 dynamic destinations have no verb at all. `usePageActions`, shipped 2026-07-26 precisely to prevent shortcut/palette drift, has 8 call sites seven weeks later, six of them from a single PR, while 14 sites still register palette-only commands and 7 register keyboard-only shortcuts. There is no catch-all route and no `errorElement`, so any stale bookmark or mistyped path drops the owner outside the shell entirely — no rail, no finder, no chat, no door. And the two questions an owner most wants to ask — "what does my system do for me on its own?" (303 standing orders, no index) and "how do I / can you…?" (16 `dashboard_read` tools, none describing a capability, a route, a schedule, or a manifesto) — have no answer anywhere in the product. Movement vs run 09 (which tiered this lens "solid"): no discoverability mechanism has shipped since (bu-7exe4.12 still OPEN behind gate bu-xf54r), the manifest grew 33→36 globals so chordless destinations grew 18→21, and four shipped destinations (`/chat`, `/chat/:conversationId`, `/decisions`, `/beads/:beadId`) entered the product without entering the documented IA table. The spine did not degrade; the product outgrew it. Hence a drop to functional.
audits.ideal: One manifest is the single authority for every addressable state — top-level routes, family sub-routes, and the parameterized tab/section states inside a console — each declaring its label, owner-language synonyms, family membership, chord, page verbs, empty-state door, and lazy loader. Every projection (rail, family strip, command finder, chord table, `?` sheet, prefetch, page-context policy, the docs IA table, and the chat's capability index) is generated from it, so a destination cannot exist without being findable and cannot be findable in one surface but not another. Page verbs are declared once through a single primitive that emits both a binding and a palette entry, and a destructive verb on a detail page is as reachable by keyboard and by fuzzy search as it is by mouse. The command finder is browsable before the first keystroke — families and their destinations, ranked by recency — and matches synonyms, not just labels, so "prescriptions", "vitals", "forecast", "bills", "flights", "lights" each open a door. An unmatched URL never leaves the shell: it renders inside the rail with the closest capability offered. Empty pages state the fact and offer the one action that fills them. Each butler's manifesto — the binding governing document under vision Rule 6 — is a first-class product surface saying what that butler promises and refuses, indexed by the finder. Every standing order the fleet runs is listed on one page in owner language with its next fire, last outcome, and a door to the session that produced it. And the ChatDock is a discovery surface of last resort: "how do I…", "where do I see…", "can you…", "what will you do tonight?" each return a sentence and a door, grounded in the same manifest. All of it is held by the repo's existing enforcement seams — `no-restricted-syntax` layers, the custom eslint plugin, the lint-as-test files under `frontend/src/lib/*-eslint.test.ts`, and `route-registry.test.ts` invariants — not by discipline.

moves.title: Standing Orders: one page and one endpoint for everything the fleet does on its own
moves.why: vision.md:120-137 defines success as scheduled tasks firing on time and the owner trusting the system with progressively more autonomy; 303 standing orders (191 enabled) exist live and there is no surface on which that trust can be inspected. purpose-and-single-pane.md:17-27 makes the dashboard the single pane for cross-butler status and the Detect/Diagnose/Act loop; the autonomous half of the system is currently absent from it. Owner payoff: 'what will you do for me tonight, and did last night's run work' becomes a five-second read instead of 39 interactions.
moves.manifesto: Serves every domain manifesto's scheduled-contribution promises simultaneously; no manifesto amendment needed — this is a read projection over work each butler already declares in its own butler.toml. The page must render each butler's schedules under that butler's own identity mark and never re-word a specialist's job description.
moves.integration_points: New fleet-wide read route `GET /api/schedules` in src/butlers/api/ (mount-boundary + cursor-pagination + degraded-envelope conventions per docs/api_and_protocols/response-conventions.md — per-butler fan-out must name unavailable butlers in `meta`, never zero-fill, mirroring the existing /api/spend/by-schedule contract at frontend/src/pages/SpendPage.tsx:1241-1250). New capability `/standing-orders` in frontend/src/lib/shell-capability.ts with a chord, a `queryWarmup`, and a PAGE_CONTEXT_REGISTRY descriptor. New frontend/src/pages/StandingOrdersPage.tsx. New `dashboard_read_standing_orders` tool in src/butlers/modules/dashboard_read/tools.py. Doors out: each row → /butlers/:name?tab=system&section=schedules and → /sessions/:id for the last run. Spec: new requirement in openspec/specs/dashboard-domain-pages/spec.md (or a new dashboard-standing-orders capability spec).
moves.slice_plan: 1) Fleet-wide read endpoint with degraded envelope + contract test. 2) Read-only page: butler, owner-language name, cadence rendered in the owner's timezone, next fire, last outcome, enabled state; disabled schedules visibly disabled, never omitted. 3) Register each schedule name as a command-finder entry so 'weekly health summary' is a door. 4) Concierge read tool + chat answer. 5) Enable/disable from the row, routed through the existing approval spine — not before slices 1-4 are green.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: 191 enabled + 112 disabled rows render, ordered by next fire, each with last-outcome and a session door. Failure: one butler's schedule fan-out fails → that butler is named in the degraded note and its rows are absent-with-cause, never silently missing, and the count states what it excludes. Concurrency: a schedule toggled from the butler console while the page is open reconciles through the existing event bus invalidation, not a poll race. Idempotence: the read is side-effect-free; the slice-5 toggle is the existing idempotent schedule mutation. Rollback: the page and endpoint are additive; removing them restores today's per-butler-only reachability.
moves.verification: Backend contract test asserting the fan-out envelope names unavailable butlers and that totals are consistent with the sum of per-butler `GET /api/butlers/{n}/schedules`. Frontend test asserting a disabled schedule renders as disabled rather than being filtered out, and that a degraded butler suppresses any 'all schedules' claim. A route-registry test asserting /standing-orders is a global capability with a unique chord. Live read-side check against the dev stack: the page's total equals the 303/191 measured here.

moves.title: Sub-destinations become first-class capabilities: one `family` projection, one FamilyNav, and the butler console's 195 states enter the manifest
moves.why: th-design/discoverability: 'search over navigation once a surface is large' and 'everything in menus is in the palette'. Today 195 URL states — the entire home of seven butlers — are outside the manifest, and the `subnav` field that would have carried them was generalized to exactly one family (shell-capability.ts:46, used at :139/:173/:174). architecture.md's daemon-deterministic doctrine has a UI analogue: the route table is infrastructure and must be declared, not improvised in query state. Owner payoff: typing 'trips', 'bills', 'devices', 'routing log' opens the door.
moves.manifesto: Respects specialist manifesto ownership by construction: a butler's domain tab is declared alongside that butler's capability, labelled in that butler's own vocabulary (ButlerEducationReviewsTab.tsx:11 already records 'Reviews (manifesto rule — NOT Decks)'), so promoting tabs to capabilities makes manifesto-owned naming enforceable rather than incidental.
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/lib/shell-capability.ts — replace `subnav?: {...}` with `family?: { of: string; order: number; label?: string; end?: boolean }` on every capability, and add a `SUB_CAPABILITIES` projection for parameterized states (`/butlers/:name?tab=…&section=…`) generated from frontend/src/pages/butler-detail-tabs.ts + ButlerSystemSection.tsx:26 + ButlerActivitySection.tsx:24. New frontend/src/components/layout/FamilyNav.tsx replacing components/relationship/SubpageTabs.tsx and components/ingestion/IngestionSubNav.tsx. frontend/src/lib/route-registry.ts and EntityFinder's ALL_PAGES consume the sub-capability projection. frontend/src/lib/page-context-registry.ts gains descriptors for the new families (the existing shell-capability.context.test.ts already enforces one-to-one coverage). Spec: openspec/specs/dashboard-shell/spec.md gains a Family Navigation requirement; the legacy `?tab=` compatibility note at :753-758 is superseded.
moves.slice_plan: 1) `family` field + FamilyNav, migrating /ingestion (already manifest-driven) and /entities (kills the hardcoded TABS array, adds the missing Contacts destination). 2) /health and /settings adopt FamilyNav. 3) Butler-console tabs declared as sub-capabilities, indexed in the finder with butler-scoped labels ('Travel → Trips'). 4) `?tab=system&section=` states declared. 5) Prefetch and page-context descriptors for the new entries.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: every family renders one strip from one source; every sub-destination is fuzzy-findable by its own label and its butler's name. Failure: a butler absent from the roster hides its sub-capabilities exactly as EntityFinder.tsx:370-376 already hides butler-gated pages; a butler-list fetch failure falls back to showing all rather than hiding real destinations. Concurrency: none (static projection). Idempotence: navigation only. Rollback: `family` is additive metadata; FamilyNav renders nothing for a capability with no family, so a partial migration degrades to today's behaviour per family.
moves.verification: New invariant in frontend/src/lib/route-registry.test.ts: every capability whose path is a strict prefix-child of another capability's path must declare `family`, and every family must have exactly one strip renderer. New eslint rule `no-hardcoded-navlink-list` in frontend/eslint.config.js (alongside the existing visual-role plugin at :2565-2570), backed by a lint-as-test file matching the frontend/src/lib/*-eslint.test.ts pattern, forbidding a module-level array of `{label, to}` consumed by NavLink outside FamilyNav. EntityFinder test: searching 'trips' returns the travel console's Trips sub-capability.

The synonyms already exist in the manifest and are thrown away at EntityFinder.tsx:96-101/:377-384, and the surface refuses to list destinations at all until a character is typed, so a first-run owner meets eight session-spawning verbs and nothing else.
