moves.title: One sanctioned path for a page verb, enforced by lint; detail-page destructive verbs get keyboard and palette routes
moves.why: th-design/discoverability: 'every frequent mouse path has a keyboard path'; 'shortcuts are advertised where the action lives'. usePageActions exists precisely to make the two halves inseparable (use-page-actions.ts:1-33, shipped 2026-07-26) and has 8 call sites while 21 sites register one half only — the drift its own docstring predicts, with nothing enforcing the rule. The sharpest cost is at the last hop: forget an entity, retract a fact, retire a rule, promote a tier are mouse-only on ten of twelve detail destinations. Owner payoff: the tenth use of a consequential verb needs no mouse, and every such verb is fuzzy-findable by name.
moves.manifesto: Relationship and Memory manifestos both treat retraction and forgetting as owner-sovereign acts; making them keyboard- and palette-reachable (behind their existing confirmation gates) is manifesto-aligned. No amendment.
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/hooks/use-page-actions.ts (the mechanism's home) and frontend/src/hooks/use-list-triage.ts remain the only two sanctioned composers. frontend/eslint.config.js gains a `no-restricted-syntax` block (following the existing layered pattern documented at :18-62) forbidding `useRegisterCommands`/`useRegisterShortcut` imports outside those two hooks and an explicit exemption list, backed by a lint-as-test file beside frontend/src/lib/no-window-confirm-eslint.test.ts. Migration touches the 21 call sites; the detail-page slice touches frontend/src/pages/EntityDetailPage.tsx:2094-2115/:2203-2248, FactDetailPage.tsx:101-123, RuleDetailPage.tsx:86, ConnectorDetailPage.tsx, QaPatrolDetailPage.tsx, QaInvestigationDetailPage.tsx, SessionDetailPage.tsx.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Migrate the 7 shortcut-only sites (SessionsPage, ChatPanel, ButlerDetailPage tab rail, ButlersPage, CalendarWorkspacePage, ChroniclesPage, RootLayout) so every key gets a palette entry. 2) Migrate the 14 command-only sites so every verb gets a binding or an explicit, reviewed no-binding exemption. 3) Detail-page verbs: one PageAction per consequential verb, each preserving its existing confirmation gate. 4) Land the lint rule and its test once the tree is clean.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: every registered verb appears in both the palette (with its kbd chip) and the `?` sheet's 'On this page'. Failure: a verb whose handler is unavailable (loading, permission-gated) must not register a dead key — the action list is derived from the same enabled predicate the button uses. Concurrency: page-scoped bindings already suspend under modals and inputs per dashboard-shell/spec.md:797-813 — unchanged. Idempotence: a destructive PageAction opens the same confirmation dialog the button does; the key never bypasses a confirm. Rollback: the lint rule is the only irreversible piece and is a config revert.
moves.verification: The lint-as-test file asserts the rule fires on a bare `useRegisterCommands` import in a page module and does not fire inside the two composers. Per-page tests asserting that each detail page's consequential verbs appear in `useShortcutHintEntries()` output and in the command-menu actions context. A registry test asserting no destination with a registered ShortcutBinding has zero PaletteCommands.

moves.title: Capability index: one generated self-description the finder, the docs, and the chat all read
moves.why: th-design/discoverability: 'every feature is reachable from the product surface without reading external docs — if a wiki is the only path, the feature is hidden'. Today the chat has 16 telemetry tools and no capability knowledge (dashboard_read/tools.py:55-380), each butler's binding manifesto is four navigations deep behind a collapsed accordion (ButlerConfigTab.tsx:518-536), and the documented IA table has drifted four destinations behind the manifest (information-architecture.md:76-113 omits /chat, /chat/:conversationId, /decisions, /beads/:beadId). Owner payoff: 'where do I see my medication supply', 'can you track my sleep yet', 'how do I stop the finance digest' each return a sentence and a door.
moves.manifesto: vision.md:103-111 Rule 6 makes each manifesto binding; this move makes the promises and refusals it defines into product surface rather than a config file, and makes them the grounding for every capability answer. Implies a small amendment shape: each roster MANIFESTO.md gains a machine-parseable Promises / Refuses section so the index never paraphrases a specialist's scope.
moves.integration_points: New `GET /api/capabilities` in src/butlers/api/ serving (a) the frontend manifest projection, (b) per-butler manifesto promises/refusals parsed from roster/{butler}/MANIFESTO.md, (c) the per-butler standing-order names from the move-1 endpoint. New `dashboard_read_capability_index` tool in src/butlers/modules/dashboard_read/tools.py. frontend/src/lib/shell-capability.ts is the frontend half of the index; a build-time emitter writes the same shape into docs/frontend/information-architecture.md's route table. New 'What <butler> promises / refuses' panel on the butler overview tab (frontend/src/pages/ButlerDetailPage.tsx), sourced from the same parse. Spec: openspec/specs/module-dashboard-read/spec.md gains the tool requirement; openspec/specs/butler-base-spec/spec.md gains the manifesto Promises/Refuses section shape.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Manifesto Promises/Refuses section shape + parser + a contract test over all 13 roster manifestos. 2) 'What <butler> promises / refuses' panel on the butler overview tab, indexed in the finder. 3) `GET /api/capabilities` + the docs IA generator and its drift check. 4) Concierge tool, answering with a route the chat renders as a door.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: asking 'where do I see medications' returns one sentence and /health/medications; asking 'can you track my sleep' returns Health's promise or its refusal, never an invention. Failure: a manifesto that does not parse must make the index state that butler's promises are unavailable — never fall back to the butler's one-line `description`, which is a summary and not a binding promise. Concurrency: none (git-sourced, read at request time). Idempotence: read-only. Rollback: additive endpoint, tool and panel.
moves.verification: Contract test: every roster/{butler}/MANIFESTO.md parses into a non-empty promises set, and the served index contains every SHELL_CAPABILITIES path (the test fails the moment a capability ships without an index entry). A docs-drift check in CI comparing the generated IA route table against the manifest — the seam that would have caught /decisions. A chat-lane test asserting a capability answer carries a route the frontend renders as a navigable door and that an unknown capability produces a refusal, not a guess.

moves.title: Nothing leaves the shell: catch-all route with a nearest-capability door
moves.why: The north star requires every consequential clause to be a door on an unbroken spine; today any unmatched URL renders React Router's default error page outside RootLayout — no rail, no finder, no chat, no way back (router-config.tsx:86-217 has no `*` and no `errorElement`; the only ErrorBoundary is inside RootLayout at :171-173 and never mounts). The router already carries nine deliberate compatibility redirects, which proves stale bookmarks are treated as real; every other stale path dead-ends. Owner payoff: a mistyped or retired link lands inside the product with the closest real destination offered.
moves.manifesto: No manifesto implication; this is the shell's own contract.
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/router-config.tsx — add `errorElement` on the RootLayout route and a terminal `{ path: '*' }` child rendering a new frontend/src/pages/NotFoundPage.tsx. The page fuzzy-matches the attempted pathname against SHELL_CAPABILITIES via frontend/src/lib/fuzzy-match.ts and offers the top three, plus a 'search everything' button dispatching `dispatchOpenEntityFinder()` (frontend/src/lib/entity-finder.ts). Spec: openspec/specs/dashboard-shell/spec.md gains an Unmatched Destination requirement.
moves.slice_plan: 1) errorElement + catch-all rendering inside the shell. 2) Nearest-capability suggestions from the manifest. 3) An honest line naming the attempted path, so a bad deep link is diagnosable rather than merely apologised for.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: /helth renders inside the shell with /health offered. Failure: a route that matches but whose chunk fails to load must keep using RouteSuspense's existing boundary, not this one — the two must not be conflated, or a transient chunk error would read as a nonexistent page. Concurrency: none. Idempotence: navigation only. Rollback: two lines in router-config.tsx.
moves.verification: Router test rendering an unmatched path and asserting the sidebar landmark, the command-finder trigger and the chat surface are all present. A test asserting a nearest-capability suggestion is produced for a one-character typo of each global capability path. A test asserting a lazy-chunk load failure still renders the RouteSuspense error, not the NotFound page.

moves.title: The `?` sheet stops advertising chords the current page has taken over
moves.why: th-design/discoverability: 'a shortcut listed only in a help page doesn't exist' — and one that is listed there and does not fire is worse, because the help sheet is currently the only place chords are advertised at all. On /calendar the sheet renders both `c → Open chat` and the page's own `c` verb; only the page's fires (shortcut-hints.tsx:18-23 hardcodes the global list; use-keyboard-shortcuts.ts:59-63 suppresses global `c` when `isBareKeyClaimedByPage('c')`; CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx:4728 claims it).
moves.manifesto: None.
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/components/ui/shortcut-hints.tsx — replace the hardcoded `STATIC_SHORTCUTS` array with a projection over a new `SHELL_SHORTCUTS` table exported from frontend/src/hooks/use-keyboard-shortcuts.ts (the module that actually installs them), and render a shadowed row as struck-through-with-reason using the registry predicate `isBareKeyClaimedByPage` already exported at frontend/src/hooks/use-register-shortcut.tsx:199-203.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Export the shell shortcut table from the module that installs it and project the sheet from it. 2) Mark shadowed globals with the page verb that claimed them. 3) Registry test forbidding a shell bare key from being silently shadowed without a sheet annotation.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: on /calendar the sheet shows `c → Create event (this page)` and marks the global chat binding as shadowed here. Failure: registry snapshot unavailable → render the global list unannotated rather than hiding it. Concurrency: the claim set changes on navigation; the sheet already re-reads it per render via useShortcutHintEntries. Idempotence: display-only. Rollback: one component.
moves.verification: A test mounting the sheet on a page that claims bare `c` and asserting exactly one actionable `c` row plus a shadow annotation. A lint-as-test assertion that `shortcut-hints.tsx` contains no literal shortcut table (the hardcoding that caused the earlier g-h drift the file's own docstring records).

findings.title: `text-destructive` (177 non-test sites, 90 files) resolves to the fill token `--red` at 3.84:1 — the `--red-text` split it was supposed to consume has 12 adopters
findings.evidence: frontend/src/index.css:52 `--destructive: var(--red);` → frontend/src/index.css:396 `--color-destructive: var(--destructive);` (Tailwind v4 `@theme inline`, so `text-destructive` paints `--red`). Measured: light `--red` vs `--bg` = 3.84:1, vs `--bg-elev` = 4.01:1 (recomputed with the repo's own oklch→sRGB→WCAG pipeline mirrored from frontend/src/lib/contrast.ts). The text-safe sibling exists at frontend/src/index.css:141 `--red-text` (5.60:1) and frontend/src/lib/contrast.test.ts:254-265 documents base `--red` as deliberately sub-AA "because text sites use --red-text" — a claim the utility alias falsifies. CONFIRMED COUNT on main @37121b939: `grep -rn "text-destructive" --include=*.tsx --include=*.ts frontend/src | grep -v "\.test\." | wc -l` → 177; `grep -rl ... | wc -l` → 90 files (193 including tests). Run 12's "~170" was low.
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: the fix landed as a token and the utility alias routed around it — a guarded value with an unguarded spelling
findings.detail: bu-f310e minted `--red-text` and repointed every `text-[var(--red)]` site (0 remain). It never touched the shadcn alias chain, so the far larger population — the bare Tailwind spelling `text-destructive` — still paints the fill red. The token-level test is green and the codebase is 177 sites sub-AA. The root cause is structural, not a missed sweep: `frontend/src/lib/contrast.test.ts` grades TOKENS against `--bg`/`--bg-elev`; it has no model of which token a given *utility spelling* resolves to, so no amount of token hygiene can catch an alias. Dark theme passes (5.55:1), so this is a light-theme-only failure — exactly the theme the design-language spec names as the AA floor obligation (openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md:18-19).

findings.title: The axe gate that shipped certifies the loading skeleton: every one of 30 route cases is rendered with `fetch` held pending forever, `color-contrast` is disabled in every axe run, and the entire app shell is outside all eight a11y suites
findings.evidence: frontend/src/test/axe/route-pages.a11y.test.tsx:50 `vi.stubGlobal("fetch", vi.fn(() => new Promise<Response>(() => {})))` — the suite's own docstring (lines 6-8) calls this "its real loading contract". Every axe invocation disables the one rule that can fail on color: route-pages.a11y.test.tsx:38 `{ rules: { "color-contrast": { enabled: false } } }`, and skip-manifest.ts:20-21 makes that disable the documented house style. The eight a11y suites are ButlersPage / ButlerDetailPage / BeadDetailPage / DecisionsPage / TimelinePage / TimelineTab / route-pages / route-sweep — `grep -rn "Shell\|Sidebar\|RootLayout" frontend/src/**/*.a11y.test.tsx` returns one comment and zero mounts, so Shell.tsx, Sidebar.tsx, RootLayout.tsx, EntityFinder.tsx, ChatDock.tsx, ShortcutHints and Toaster are axe-unreachable. Playwright has zero a11y: `grep -rn "axe|a11y" frontend/tests/` → empty across 19 specs; `@axe-core/playwright` is not a dependency (frontend/package.json:56,66 carry only jest-axe/@types/jest-axe). frontend/.github → .github/workflows/ci.yml:2244 `frontend-e2e` exists and is explicitly not a required check (.github/workflows/e2e-main-schedule.yml:5-14).
findings.taxonomy_shape: failure impersonating health at the read side — applied to the verification layer itself
findings.detail:
bu-qvnce.10 built a genuinely good structure: `ALL_ROUTES` drives a completeness check, silence is impossible, skips need a reason >20 chars. What it verifies is a page with no rows, no buttons, no dialogs, no badges and no live regions. Proof that the gate is empty rather than merely narrow: axe-core 4.11.4 flags `
` as `aria-prohibited-attr` (serious) — verified by running axe 4.11.4 against that exact markup — and the codebase carries 59 such sites (finding below) with the whole suite green. Real-browser-only checks (1.4.3 contrast, 1.4.11 focus-indicator contrast, prefers-reduced-motion, 1.4.10 reflow, 1.4.4 200% text) have no home at all: jsdom cannot compute them and the Playwright job that could is a) assertion-free for a11y and b) not required.

findings.title: `text-white` on the state-color fills is 2.10:1 (light) / 1.82:1 (dark) on amber — the badges that say "Stale", "Unverified", "Corrupt", "Run failed" are the least readable text in the product
findings.evidence: 25 sites: `grep -rnE "bg-\[var\(--(red|amber|green)\)\]" --include=*.tsx frontend/src | grep -v "\.test\." | grep text-white | wc -l` → 25. Worst offenders are the fleet's own failure vocabulary: frontend/src/components/system/BackupTile.tsx:99,109,119,129,138 ("Corrupt" / "Run failed" / "Stale" / "Healthy" / "Unverified"), StoredFunctionsTile.tsx:116,141, DeploymentTile.tsx:172, ButlerStatusBadge.tsx:33, Sidebar.tsx:163,165,815,817. Measured white-on-fill: light amber 2.10:1, dark amber 1.82:1, light red 4.01:1, dark red 3.57:1, dark green 3.41:1 — only light green (5.57:1) clears AA. Root mechanism: frontend/src/lib/visual-token-roles.ts:52-62 — the `state` role in `VISUAL_TOKEN_ROLE_REGISTRY` is the only role in the registry with no `foregrounds` key; `local-category` (line 71) has `--categorical-fill-foreground` and `owner-custom-color` (line 86-90) has the on-light/on-dark pair, both graded in contrast.test.ts:172-216. State fills were never given the same contract.
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: every role in the registry got an accessible-foreground contract except the one that reports failure
findings.detail: openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md:166-170 requires exactly this contract ("Filled category and owner labels keep an accessible foreground") and scopes it to category and owner labels only. The state role — the vocabulary the north star cares most about ("failure never impersonates health, staleness never wears current-data authority") — is out of the spec's scenario and out of the test. A `Stale` badge at 1.82:1 does not wear current-data authority; it wears no authority, because it cannot be read.

findings.title: 59 accessible names are written and silently dropped: `aria-label` on role-`generic` elements, including the collapsed sidebar's fleet-health indicator whose only other content is an `aria-hidden` colored dot
findings.evidence:
59 sites across 47 files (AST-ish scan of `` carrying `aria-label` with no `role`, tests/stories excluded). The decisive one: frontend/src/components/layout/Sidebar.tsx:504 and :535 — `
{expanded && {titleText}}
`, where `titleText` is the honest aggregate ("2 errors · 1 degraded · Spend source unavailable" / "All systems ok", lines 522-533) and `dotColor` is `bg-destructive` / `bg-[var(--amber)]` / `bg-[var(--green)]` (lines 515-519). In the collapsed 56px rail `expanded` is false, so the text span is not rendered: the only DOM content is an aria-hidden dot, and the aria-label on a role-generic div is name-prohibited. Verified live: axe-core 4.11.4 reports `aria-prohibited-attr` (serious) on precisely this shape. Others of the same kind: components/system/ButlerHeartbeatTile.tsx:108, chronicles/SourceStateBadgeStrip.tsx:226, chronicles/DayRibbon.tsx:165,198, chronicles/StreakCallouts.tsx:70, qa/StateTrack.tsx:37, overview/AttentionList.tsx:155 (`aria-label={`Severity: ${item.severity}`}` on a span), ui/Pill.tsx:89, ui/Provenance.tsx:98,151,160, ui/ButlerMark.tsx:176, timeline/TimelineDensity.tsx:30, DashboardPage.tsx:482,549,571, HealthOverviewPage.tsx:232,404,490.
findings.taxonomy_shape: computed then discarded at the seam — applied to the accessibility name itself
findings.detail: This is the a11y analogue of the pursuit's recurring defect: the honest string is computed, attached, and never delivered. Nothing in the toolchain objects — `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y`'s recommended set (frontend/eslint.config.js:2582) has no rule for prohibited ARIA attributes, and axe would catch it but never renders the shell. The fleet-health rail is the worst case because it is also color-as-sole-signal: in the collapsed rail, red vs green is the entire message, and there is no name, no text, and no shape difference.

findings.title: The shared triage cursor is invisible to assistive tech on 11 of 12 adopting surfaces — it is not DOM focus, not `aria-activedescendant`, not announced, and not scrolled into view — so `a` approves a row the screen-reader owner was never told about
findings.evidence: frontend/src/hooks/use-list-triage.ts:110-133 — `moveSelection` computes `next` and calls `onSelect(next)`; the hook holds no element refs, emits no `aria-activedescendant`, calls no `.focus()`, no `scrollIntoView`, and never imports `lib/shell-announcer`. Consumer matrix (grep per file for `resolveSelectedId` / `aria-activedescendant` / `scrollIntoView` / `.focus()`): ApprovalsPage, DashboardPage, DecisionsPage, IssuesPage, NotificationsPage, QaOverviewPage, AuditLogPage, components/overview/AttentionList, components/notifications/notification-feed, components/issues/IssuesPanel, components/education/ReviewTimeline → all four counts zero (AttentionList has one unrelated `.focus()`). Only components/timeline/TimelineLedger.tsx passes `resolveSelectedId` and drives real DOM focus (shipped #4140). The verbs bound to that invisible cursor are consequential: ApprovalsPage.tsx:1941-1966 binds `a`→approve, `d`→deny, `x`→defer against `selectedId`.
findings.taxonomy_shape: built twice unified never — inverted: the generalization happened and carried the defect into ten more surfaces
findings.detail: Delta vs run 09 (which filed the visual-only cursor scoped to the entity index): `useListTriage` did not exist then. bu-qvnce.11 slice 4 extracted ApprovalsPage's hand-rolled j/k into a shared hook and eleven surfaces adopted it — extracting the keyboard half and leaving the focus/name/announce half behind, so one hook now codifies the defect fleet-wide. Meanwhile the correct pattern shipped separately in TimelineLedger (#4140) and was never folded back into the hook it sits next to. Secondary consequence for sighted keyboard users: with no `scrollIntoView`, holding `j` walks the cursor off-screen with nothing to look at.

findings.title: `attention_add` / `attention_remove` / `header_delta` reach the browser on the shared bus and die inside one page's local state — nothing anywhere announces an attention or health change
findings.evidence: Producer: src/butlers/api/routers/settings_console.py:683-685 emits `attention_add` (full item payload) / `attention_remove` / `header_delta` on every delta tick, independent of any client. Consumer: `grep -rn useBusEvent frontend/src` → exactly three subscribers, all in two files — hooks/use-settings-console-live.ts:186,193,201 (feeds SettingsConsolePage's local list only) and hooks/use-spend-ticker.ts:69. `lib/shell-announcer.ts`'s `announce()` has seven call sites (RootLayout stream/client-link edges, ui/page.tsx:347 page title, timeline/NewEventsPill.tsx:27, chat/FloatingChatWidget.tsx:423, SpendPage rule reorder, EntityDetailPage merge) — none of them attention, degradation, approval, or butler health. LIVE (GET http://127.0.0.1:42200/api/settings/console): the items already carry owner-ready prose — `{"id":"auth_renewal:claude","tone":"red","text":"CLI runtime 'Claude (Anthropic)' needs re-authentication.","action_route":"/secrets?focus=c:cli-auth/claude"}` — a fully formed sentence plus a door.
findings.taxonomy_shape: substrate shipped / consumer never
findings.detail: The hardest parts are already built and running: a server-side delta loop, a single multiplexed socket, a fan-out API, a mounted sr-only live region, and per-item prose with an action route. What is missing is eleven lines of subscription. Today an owner on /health learns that their Claude CLI credential expired only by navigating to /settings; an owner who cannot see the page never learns it at all. This is the largest new *capability* in this lens: the system already knows what changed and has a channel to say it.

findings.title: Single unmodified letters commit owner decisions page-wide with no way to disable or remap them (WCAG 2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts, Level A)
findings.evidence: frontend/src/hooks/use-register-shortcut.tsx:100-170 — bindings are matched on a document-level listener (`matchesBinding`, line 183-192, requires `!ctrlKey && !metaKey && !shiftKey && !altKey` for a bare key) and suppressed only by `isShortcutTargetSuspended`: editable field, `<select>`, or inside/underneath an open `[role=dialog]`. There is no owner setting, no remap surface, and no focus-scoping — `activeBindingsSnapshot` (line 194) is module-global. Bound consequential verbs: ApprovalsPage.tsx:1941 `a` Approve, :1951 `d` Deny, :1961 `x` Defer, :1929 `u` Undo; NotificationsPage.tsx:413 `a` Mark read; IssuesPage.tsx:272 `a` Restore, :285 `a` Acknowledge.
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: the shortcut registry advertises its keys but owns no off switch — discoverability shipped, conformance did not
findings.detail: SC 2.1.4 requires at least one of: turn it off, remap it, or activate it only while the relevant component has focus. None is present, and the guard that exists (`isShortcutTargetSuspended`) is a double-fire guard, not a conformance mechanism. ApprovalsPage routes its verbs through `scheduleDecision` + an undo window, which limits the blast radius there; NotificationsPage's `a` and IssuesPage's `a` do not visibly do so. For an owner using speech input or with a motor tremor, a stray consonant is an approval.

findings.title: Two live-region announcers: chat's sentence-batched streaming announcer has exactly one consumer, while the shell's announcer is a whole-string clobber shared by seven
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/chat/live-announcer.ts:24-100 — `LiveAnnouncer` class with sentence-boundary batching, 1500ms idle flush, a 3000ms-gated "Reply complete" marker, and append-only spans rendered with `aria-atomic="false"` (MessageThread.tsx:537-540). Its only importer is components/chat/MessageThread.tsx. frontend/src/lib/shell-announcer.ts:35-39 — `announce()` overwrites a single module-scoped string and no-ops on a duplicate; RootLayout.tsx:54 renders it with `aria-atomic` unset (defaults to true), so two announcements inside one paint cycle silently replace each other.
findings.taxonomy_shape: built twice unified never
findings.detail: The sophisticated announcer is locked to one surface; the naive one carries everything else and will drop messages the moment a second source (the attention narration above) starts writing to it. Any move that widens what the shell says has to fix the queue first — a page-title announcement and a 'butler degraded' announcement racing into one string is exactly the clobber `announce()`'s duplicate-suppression comment does not cover.

findings.title: AttentionList gives the harmless link an item-scoped name and leaves the three consequential verbs generically named
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/overview/AttentionList.tsx:264-265 — the row's navigation link carries `aria-label={`View: ${item.title}`}`. Twelve lines earlier the decision verbs in the same row carry only their own text: :231-238 `Approve` / `{item.approvePending ? "Approving…" : "Approve"}`, :241-248 `Deny`, :251-258 `Defer`, :216-226 `Undo`. In a list of N attention items the accessible name of every approve button is the string "Approve".
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: the door that changes nothing is named for its destination; the doors that commit the owner are named for themselves
findings.detail: The per-item naming pattern is present in the same JSX block, so this is not an unknown technique — it is an inconsistent application of a local convention, on the wrong side of the consequence line. Same shape recurs wherever a triage row exposes verbs (see the useListTriage finding); the fix belongs in the shared hook's row contract, not in this file.

findings.title: `role="grid"` wraps a real `<table>` on the entity index — a grid that owns no rows
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/relationship/EntitiesIndexPage.tsx:1539-1546 — `<div ref={listRef} tabIndex={0} role="grid" aria-label="Entity list" onKeyDown={handleListKeyDown}>` whose sole child is `<EntityTable .../>`, which renders an HTML `<table>` (implicit role `table`). ARIA requires `grid` to own `row`/`rowgroup`; `table` is not an allowed owned element, and the wrapper contributes no rows of its own. `/entities/index` is in ROUTE_AXE_CASES (frontend/src/test/axe/route-page-cases.tsx:42) but is only ever rendered with fetch pending, so `aria-required-children` never evaluates against a populated table.
findings.taxonomy_shape: gates as metadata — the ARIA contract is declared, the structure does not keep it
findings.detail: The keyboard map is correctly bound to the container rather than to `window` (the comment at :1537-1538 says so deliberately), which is the right instinct; the role added to make it feel legitimate is the part that breaks. Either drop to a focusable region with the table's own semantics intact, or make the table itself the grid.

findings.title: The console KPI strip conveys "this number needs your attention" with text color alone
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/SettingsConsolePage.tsx:245-252 — `KpiCell` renders its value with `tone === "red" ? "text-[var(--red-text)]" : "text-foreground"` and nothing else changes; there is no icon, word, prefix, or position shift. `tone` is server-supplied — LIVE GET http://127.0.0.1:42200/api/settings/console returns `"open_approvals"` with `"tone":"red"` today. Same pattern at SpendPage.tsx:318.
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: a server-computed severity arrives typed and is rendered as a hue
findings.detail: openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md:154 and :159 both require that "color is never the only signal" — scoped, again, to the categorical and chart ramps, not to state. The server already sends a discrete `tone` enum and, for attention items, a full `text` sentence; the surface throws away the discreteness and keeps only the color.

audits.ideal: A JARVIS-grade Butlers dashboard treats accessibility as the same honesty contract the rest of the system is held to, expressed once and enforced mechanically. Color is a role, never a message: every state token declares both its fill and the graded foreground that may sit on it, and the only legal way to spell a color is through a resolver the lint layer can read, so a sub-AA pair is a compile-time error rather than a visual audit finding. Every accessible name is either delivered or refused loudly — a name attached to an element that cannot carry it fails lint, exactly as a fabricated denominator fails review. The verification layer measures the product an owner actually touches: axe runs against populated pages and the mounted shell in a real browser, where contrast, focus-indicator contrast, reduced motion and reflow are computable, and the completeness registry distinguishes "covered populated" from "covered empty" so the gate can never certify a skeleton. Keyboard operation and screen-reader operation are one path, not two: a single list-traversal primitive owns the cursor, and moving the cursor moves real focus, scrolls it into view under the reduced-motion contract, and speaks the row and its position — so every consequential verb names its target before it fires, and every bare-key verb has an owner-visible off switch. And the shell is a narrator, not a mirror: the fleet's own attention and degradation deltas, which already arrive on one multiplexed bus carrying owner-ready prose and an action route, are spoken through a single priority-ordered live region and kept in a replayable "since you looked away" log — so the owner who is not watching the tab, or cannot see it, still hears "the Claude credential expired" the moment the fleet knows it.
audits.jarvis_gap: Every primitive this lens wants already exists in the repo, and almost none of them is load-bearing. There is a token-contrast test that reads the real CSS literals and grades both themes — and it grades tokens, not the pairs that meet in the DOM, so `text-destructive` paints `--red` at 3.84:1 across 177 non-test sites (90 files, main @37121b939) while the test's own comment asserts that text sites use `--red-text`, and `text-white` sits on `--amber` at 2.10:1 light / 1.82:1 dark on the badges that read "Stale", "Corrupt" and "Run failed". There is a visual-role registry in which every color role carries an accessible-foreground contract except `state`, the one role that reports failure. There is a route-registry-driven axe completeness sweep in which nothing can hide — and it renders all 30 pages with `fetch` held pending forever, disables `color-contrast` in every run, and never mounts Shell, Sidebar, RootLayout, the command finder or the chat dock at all, while the Playwright job that could measure any of it carries zero a11y assertions and is not a required check. There is a shell live region and a beautifully engineered sentence-batching streaming announcer — one has seven consumers and clobbers itself, the other has one. There is a shared j/k triage hook adopted by twelve surfaces, extracted from ApprovalsPage after run 09 filed the visual-only cursor: it took the keystrokes and left the focus, the name and the announcement behind, so on eleven surfaces `a` approves a row the screen-reader owner was never told about, and those bare letters have no off switch (SC 2.1.4, Level A). And the fleet already emits `attention_add`/`attention_remove` with owner-ready prose and an action route onto a single bus that the browser is already subscribed to — consumed by exactly one page's local state, announced nowhere. The gap is not knowledge or craft; it is that every mechanism stopped at the file that motivated it, and the gate built to catch that measures the loading skeleton.
audits.live_verification: The JSON API at http://127.0.0.1:42200 is up and was read read-only (GET /api/butlers → 13 butlers/staffers; GET /api/settings/console → header_counts + two live attention items). No dashboard UI is served locally — ports 42201/42210/5173/4173/3000/8080 all refused, and http://127.0.0.1:42200/ returns 404 {"detail":"Not Found"} — so no rendered-DOM or browser-level a11y verification was possible; all frontend findings are source-confirmed by reading the decisive mechanism. Two findings are live-confirmed on the data side: the attention-delta payload shape and prose (finding 6) and the server-supplied `tone` enum behind the color-only KPI (finding 11). Contrast ratios were computed out-of-tree with the repo's own oklch→linear-sRGB→WCAG pipeline transcribed from frontend/src/lib/contrast.ts, cross-checked against the ratios that file's test already pins (light --dim, light --amber, light --red-text all reproduced). axe behavior was verified empirically by running axe-core 4.11.4 (the version in frontend/node_modules) against synthetic markup matching Sidebar.tsx:504: it reports `aria-prohibited-attr` (serious), proving the 59-site class is machine-detectable and that the existing suites simply never reach it. No files were edited, no beads filed, no gates run.

moves.title: Grade the pair, not the token: give the state role a foreground contract and make the utility spelling the guarded surface
moves.why: openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md:18-19 makes the light-mode WCAG AA floor a binding obligation and :166-170 already specifies the fill/foreground contract — for category and owner labels only. The north star's "staleness never wears current-data authority" is falsified most literally by a `Stale` badge at 1.82:1. Owner-visible payoff: the failure vocabulary becomes readable in the theme the spec names, and 202 sites stop being one refactor away from silently regressing.
moves.manifesto: Dispatch design language (openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md) § Non-butler Categorical and Decorative Hue Ramp + § Semantic Visual Role Matrix. Implies a spec amendment: the "Filled labels keep an accessible foreground" scenario must be widened from category/owner labels to the `state` role, and a new scenario added for foreground *spellings* (which Tailwind utility prefixes a token may appear behind).
moves.integration_points: Tokens: frontend/src/index.css :52/:508 (`--destructive`), new `--green-text`, new `--state-fill-foreground` (both themes), and a new `@theme inline` entry `--color-destructive-text: var(--red-text)` alongside :396. Registry: frontend/src/lib/visual-token-roles.ts:52-62 — the `state` role gains `foregrounds: ["--state-fill-foreground"]` and `textTokens: { red: "--red-text", amber: "--amber-text", green: "--green-text" }`, mirroring the `local-category` (:66-73) and `owner-custom-color` (:79-95) shapes. Guard: frontend/scripts/visual-role-css-guard.mjs — its existing `TAILWIND_COLOR_UTILITY_SPELLINGS` recognizer (line 38) and named-alias grammar (`TAILWIND_IDENTITY_ALIASES`, line 31) already parse exactly the forms needed; add a `TOKEN_UTILITY_ROLE` table declaring which tokens are legal behind `text-`/`decoration-`/`placeholder-` versus `bg-`/`border-`/`ring-`, and export a `findTextRoleViolations()` sibling to `findPrivateIdentityReferences`. Wiring: frontend/eslint.config.js (the `no-restricted-syntax` guard family that already imports from that script). Grading: frontend/src/lib/contrast.test.ts — a new `describe` iterating the registry's declared (fill × foreground) pairs in both themes, replacing the hand-written `known gaps` block at :254-265. 202 call sites: 177 `text-destructive` + 25 `text-white`-on-state-fill.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Mint `--green-text` and `--state-fill-foreground`; add the pair-grading describe to contrast.test.ts and let it go red with the exact failing ratios named. 2) Declare the pairs in VISUAL_TOKEN_ROLE_REGISTRY and land the token/theme changes so the test goes green at the token layer. 3) Codemod the 177 `text-destructive` → `text-destructive-text` (or delete the spelling and use `text-[var(--red-text)]`) and the 25 `text-white`-on-state-fill → `text-[var(--state-fill-foreground)]`; one mechanical diff, reviewable by grep count going to zero. 4) Turn the lint rule on as an error and add its fixture cases to visual-role-css-guard.test.mjs.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: `text-destructive` no longer resolves; any new use fails lint with the sanctioned replacement named in the message. Failure: a token added to index.css without a registry entry fails the pair-grading test (fail-closed, same posture as the existing `requireToken` throw). Concurrency: none (build-time only). Idempotence: the codemod is a pure spelling substitution; re-running is a no-op. Rollback: revert the token diff — the guard is inert without registry entries, so the lint rule can be disabled independently of the token change.
moves.verification: contrast.test.ts asserts every registry-declared (fill, foreground) pair ≥4.5:1 in both themes, reading the real index.css literals (existing pattern). visual-role-css-guard.test.mjs gains fixtures for `text-destructive`, `text-[var(--red)]`, `bg-[var(--amber)] text-white`, and the legal counterparts. A repo-level assertion that `grep -c text-destructive` over non-test src is 0. Move 2's browser axe run then confirms the same pairs pass with `color-contrast` ENABLED against real rendered DOM — the only check that closes the loop.

moves.title: Make the axe gate measure the product: populated route fixtures, a mounted shell, and axe in the browser where contrast is computable
moves.why: The north star says failure must never impersonate health; a green gate that renders 30 pending-fetch skeletons and disables the contrast rule is that failure applied to verification itself (frontend/src/test/axe/route-pages.a11y.test.tsx:38,50). Owner-visible payoff: the a11y claim becomes true, and every subsequent move in this lens acquires a real regression net instead of a completeness ceremony.
moves.manifesto: openspec/specs/testing/spec.md (the repository verification bar) and the engineering bar's rule that a receipt without a positive terminator is not a pass — the axe sweep currently issues a positive terminator for a frame no owner sees. Implies a new normative scenario in openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md: focus-indicator and text contrast are verified in a real browser, not asserted at the token layer.
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/test/axe/route-pages.a11y.test.tsx (replace the pending-fetch stub with each page's existing populated `vi.mock` fixtures — every one of the 30 pages already has a `*.test.tsx` with them). frontend/src/test/axe/route-page-cases.tsx (each entry gains a `state: "populated" | "loading"` discriminant). frontend/src/test/axe/route-sweep.a11y.test.tsx (the completeness check gains a third axis: a route covered only in the loading frame must carry a skip-manifest reason, same honesty rule as today's `COVERED_ELSEWHERE`). New frontend/src/test/axe/shell.a11y.test.tsx mounting RootLayout with Shell + Sidebar collapsed AND expanded, EntityFinder open, ChatDock docked, ShortcutHints open — the surfaces zero suites touch today. New frontend/tests/e2e/a11y.spec.ts using `@axe-core/playwright` over the existing `page.route()` fixtures in frontend/tests/e2e/fixtures, running `color-contrast` and the focus-indicator checks with light and dark forced via `emulateMedia`. .github/workflows/ci.yml:2244 `frontend-e2e` promoted to a required check (and .github/workflows/e2e-main-schedule.yml:5-14's stated reason for the watchdog retires with it).
moves.slice_plan: 1) Add the `state` discriminant and the shell suite; land with every route still declared `loading` so the diff is pure structure and the sweep's new axis is honest on day one. 2) Convert routes to populated fixtures in batches by owning surface (health, ingestion, relationship, settings, chat), burning the loading-only skips down. 3) Add the Playwright a11y spec with `color-contrast` enabled in both themes over five representative routes plus the shell. 4) Make frontend-e2e required.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: a new page with no populated axe case fails the sweep's completeness check exactly as an unregistered route does today. Failure: a genuinely un-fixturable page is allowed only via an explicit skip entry with a >20-char reason (existing rule). Concurrency: Playwright already serializes workers in CI (playwright.config.ts:41). Idempotence: axe runs are pure reads. Rollback: the state discriminant defaults to `loading`, so reverting the fixture batches restores today's behavior without touching the harness.
moves.verification: The sweep's own tests, extended: (a) every ALL_ROUTES path is populated-covered, covered-elsewhere, or skipped with a reason; (b) a deliberately broken fixture (an unlabeled icon button injected into one page) fails the populated run and passes the loading run — the single check that proves the new gate measures something the old one could not. The shell suite must fail today against Sidebar.tsx:504 (`aria-prohibited-attr`) before move 3 lands; that red is the acceptance criterion. The e2e spec asserts zero `color-contrast` violations in both themes, which is the only place findings 1 and 3 are provable end to end.

moves.title: A name is delivered or it is a lint error: retire the 59 dropped `aria-label`s, starting with the collapsed rail's fleet-health dot
moves.why: Doctrine: nothing fabricated. Fifty-nine places assert an accessible name the platform silently discards — the a11y form of computing an honest string and dropping it at the seam. The Sidebar case is the north star's five-second fleet verification reduced to a colored dot with no name, no text and no shape (Sidebar.tsx:504,535). Owner-visible payoff: the collapsed rail, every status pill, every provenance chip and every severity glyph actually says what it means.
moves.manifesto: openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md § Semantic Visual Role Matrix — the `state` role's declared `requiredSignal: "state affordance"` (frontend/src/lib/visual-token-roles.ts:60) is unmet wherever the affordance is a dropped label on a generic element.
moves.integration_points: New rule in frontend/eslint.config.js's `no-restricted-syntax` family: `JSXOpeningElement` whose name is a lowercase host tag in the generic set (div/span/p/label/td/code/pre/b/i/em/strong/small/blockquote/caption) carrying `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` with no `role` attribute — message naming the two sanctioned fixes (add the role the name belongs to, or render an `sr-only` span). 59 sites in 47 files; the highest-blast are frontend/src/components/layout/Sidebar.tsx:504,535 (fleet health), components/system/ButlerHeartbeatTile.tsx:108, components/chronicles/SourceStateBadgeStrip.tsx:226, components/chronicles/DayRibbon.tsx:165,198, components/qa/StateTrack.tsx:37, components/overview/AttentionList.tsx:155, components/ui/Pill.tsx:89, components/ui/Provenance.tsx:98,151,160, components/ui/ButlerMark.tsx:176. The Sidebar fix is also a color-only-signal fix: the collapsed rail needs `role="status"` plus a visible non-color differentiator (glyph or count), not just a name.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Fix the four shared primitives (Pill, Provenance, ButlerMark, the sidebar status footer) — they account for the majority of rendered instances. 2) Sweep the remaining page/component sites. 3) Enable the lint rule as an error and add fixtures. Order matters: the shell suite from move 2 should be red on Sidebar.tsx:504 before slice 1 and green after, so the gate and the fix prove each other.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: an `aria-label` on a generic element fails lint with both sanctioned fixes named. Failure: an element that genuinely needs a name and has no natural role gets `role="img"`/`role="status"` — the rule accepts either, so it cannot force a wrong role. Concurrency/idempotence: build-time only, no runtime behavior. Rollback: the rule and the fixes are independent commits; either reverts alone.
moves.verification:
ESLint fixtures for `
` (fail), `
` (pass), `text` (fail — axe's own rule passes this because text content wins, but the *written name* is still discarded, so the repo rule is deliberately stricter than axe). The shell axe suite from move 2 independently confirms Sidebar.tsx:504 stops reporting `aria-prohibited-attr` (verified reproducible against axe-core 4.11.4). A test on the sidebar footer asserting the collapsed rail exposes the aggregate text and a non-color signal at both `expanded` states.

moves.title: The fleet narrates: subscribe the shell to the attention deltas already on the bus, behind one priority-ordered announcer
moves.why: Standing owner emphasis is feature-first — this is the one thing in this lens the system could newly SAY. src/butlers/api/routers/settings_console.py:683-685 already emits attention deltas with owner-ready prose and an action route (live-confirmed: "CLI runtime 'Claude (Anthropic)' needs re-authentication." → /secrets?focus=c:cli-auth/claude), the browser is already subscribed to that bus, and a mounted sr-only region already exists — and all of it dies in one page's local state (hooks/use-settings-console-live.ts:186-205). Owner-visible payoff: an owner anywhere in the app — eyes on another window, or blind — is told the moment a credential expires, a butler degrades, or an approval starts waiting, with the door to fix it.
moves.manifesto: about/heart-and-soul/vision.md § What Success Looks Like — "Butlers surface timely, relevant insights without being asked." Today that promise is kept only for whoever is looking at /settings. Also serves the north star's unbroken signal→session→evidence spine: the announcement carries the same `action_route` the visual card does, so the spoken clause is a door.
moves.integration_points: New frontend/src/hooks/use-fleet-narration.ts subscribing `attention_add` / `attention_remove` / `header_delta` via `useBusEvent` (lib/event-bus.tsx:150), mounted once in frontend/src/layouts/RootLayout.tsx alongside the existing stream-edge effects (:104-137). Announcer: promote frontend/src/components/chat/live-announcer.ts to frontend/src/lib/live-announcer.ts and rebuild frontend/src/lib/shell-announcer.ts:35-39 as a priority queue over it — `announce(text, { priority, source })` where an attention/health message outranks a page-title message and nothing is clobbered mid-paint; RootLayout.tsx:52-57 renders the region with `aria-atomic="false"` and append-only spans (the shape MessageThread.tsx:537-540 already proves). Replay: a bounded in-memory "since you looked away" list, surfaced as a command-menu entry via lib/command-registry.tsx so the log is reachable, not just spoken. Honesty guard: `meta.replayed` must suppress announcement on reconnect (the same trap use-settings-console-live.ts:187 and use-spend-ticker.ts:69 already handle) — otherwise a dropped socket re-announces the whole ring buffer as new.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Rebuild shell-announcer as a priority queue over the shared LiveAnnouncer and migrate its seven existing call sites; no new sources yet, so the diff is provably behavior-preserving. 2) Add use-fleet-narration for attention_add/remove only, replayed-suppressed, gated on a persisted owner setting defaulting to on. 3) Add header_delta (butler count, open approvals) with a debounce so a burst tick is one sentence. 4) Add the replayable log and its command-menu door.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: an attention item appears server-side → one polite announcement of its `text`, once, with the action route reachable from the log. Failure: bus down → nothing is announced and the existing stream-edge announcement already says so (RootLayout.tsx:118), so silence is never mistaken for calm. Reconnect: `meta.replayed` items are applied to state but never spoken — no re-announcement storm. Concurrency: two deltas in one tick queue rather than clobber; the queue drains at one span per flush. Idempotence: announcements are keyed by item id, so a repeated `attention_add` for the same id is dropped. Quiet hours / opt-out: the persisted setting suppresses narration without suppressing the visual surfaces.
moves.verification: use-fleet-narration.test.tsx driving a fake bus: asserts one announcement per non-replayed add, zero for replayed, zero for an add whose id is already announced, and ordering when an attention message and a page-title message race. shell-announcer.test.ts asserts the priority queue never drops a higher-priority message and never re-announces identical text. A RootLayout integration test asserting the live region's spans accumulate rather than replace. The seam is the real one: the test subscribes through EventBusProvider, not a mocked hook.

moves.title: The triage cursor becomes a real target: useListTriage owns focus, scroll, name and announcement for all twelve surfaces
moves.why: Eleven surfaces let the owner press `a` to approve a row that was never focused, never named and never spoken (hooks/use-list-triage.ts:110-133; ApprovalsPage.tsx:1941-1966). The north star requires every consequential clause to be a door on an unbroken spine — a verb whose target is a React state id and a background tint is not a door, it is a guess. Owner-visible payoff: keyboard triage speaks its target before it acts, and the selection stops walking off-screen.
moves.manifesto: openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md § Interaction Affordances (focus is visible via :focus-visible) — satisfiable only if the cursor IS focus. Serves the approval-command contract's premise that a decision names its subject.
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/hooks/use-list-triage.ts — signature change: `ids: TId[]` becomes `rows: ReadonlyArray<{ id: TId; label: string }>`; the hook returns `getRowProps(id)` supplying `id`, `tabIndex` (roving 0/-1), a ref callback into an internal element map, and `data-triage-row`. `moveSelection` additionally focuses the target element, calls `scrollIntoView({ block: "nearest", behavior: prefersReducedMotion ? "auto" : "smooth" })` via hooks/use-prefers-reduced-motion.ts, and `announce(`${label} — ${n} of ${total}`, { priority: "cursor" })` through move 4's queue. Verbs gain a required `subjectLabel` so `aria-label` on the rendered verb button is `${verb} : ${label}` (the pattern AttentionList.tsx:264 already uses for its non-consequential link). Twelve consumers: ApprovalsPage, DashboardPage, DecisionsPage, IssuesPage, NotificationsPage, QaOverviewPage, AuditLogPage, components/overview/AttentionList, components/notifications/notification-feed, components/issues/IssuesPanel, components/education/ReviewTimeline, components/timeline/TimelineLedger (already correct — it becomes the reference implementation and drops its bespoke `resolveSelectedId` path). components/ui/list-triage-footer.tsx unchanged (the `hints` coupling already works).
moves.slice_plan: 1) Land the signature change with `getRowProps` and focus/scroll/announce behavior, migrating TimelineLedger first (it already does this by hand — the diff is a deletion). 2) Migrate the four consequential surfaces (Approvals, Dashboard/AttentionList, Notifications, Issues) — the ones where a verb commits. 3) Migrate the remaining read-only lists. 4) Add the per-verb `subjectLabel` naming and the coupling test. Backward compatibility is waived: the `rows` rename makes every consumer a compile error, which is the enforcement.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: `j` moves focus to the next row, scrolls it minimally into view, announces "Deny reauth for Claude — 3 of 12"; `d` fires against the focused row and the verb button's own name says which. Failure: the row element is unmounted (virtualized list) → the hook falls back to selection-only and announces without focusing rather than throwing. Reduced motion: `scrollIntoView` uses `auto`, closing the JS-motion escape the global CSS floor at index.css:826 cannot reach. Concurrency: rapid `j` repeats coalesce — only the settled row is announced (the LiveAnnouncer's idle flush already provides this). Idempotence: moving to the already-selected id is a no-op (existing guard, line 131). Rollback: per-consumer, since each migration is an isolated diff.
moves.verification: use-list-triage.test.tsx: after `j`, `document.activeElement` is the expected row element; the shell announcer received exactly one message containing the row label and its 1-based position; `scrollIntoView` was called with `behavior: "auto"` under a mocked reduced-motion match and `"smooth"` without. A repo-wide coupling test (same file-scan shape as frontend/scripts/visual-role-css-guard.mjs) asserting every file importing use-list-triage also spreads `getRowProps`, mirroring the existing `ListTriageFooterHint bindings={hints}` contract. Per-consumer: an ApprovalsPage test asserting the approve button's accessible name contains the selected approval's subject. Move 2's populated axe run then covers these rows with real DOM.

moves.title: Give the bare-key verbs an off switch: consequential shortcuts become a declared, owner-governed class
moves.why: WCAG 2.1.4 (Level A) requires that single-character shortcuts be disableable, remappable, or focus-scoped; none is true today (hooks/use-register-shortcut.tsx:100-192). `a` approves, `d` denies, `x` defers, and the guard that exists is a double-fire guard, not consent. This is a trust defect as much as a conformance one: the pursuit's own doctrine is that a consequential clause is a deliberate door. Owner-visible payoff: an owner who uses speech input, or who once fat-fingered a denial, can turn bare-key verbs off without losing navigation.
moves.manifesto: Serves the approval/decision consent posture the fleet applies everywhere else (irreversible actions confirm). Implies a small amendment to the dashboard keyboard contract: bare keys split into navigation (always on) and consequential (owner-gated, advertised as gated).
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/hooks/use-register-shortcut.tsx — `ShortcutBinding` gains `consequential?: boolean`; the document listener skips consequential bindings when the persisted setting is off, and `useShortcutHintEntries` marks them so the '?' sheet shows the state and the toggle rather than advertising a key that will not fire. frontend/src/hooks/use-list-triage.ts — `ListTriageVerb` gains a required `consequential` field (mutating verbs must declare it), which the hook forwards. Persistence: frontend/src/lib/local-settings.ts (`readBooleanSetting`/`writeBooleanSetting`, the pattern RootLayout.tsx:22,80 already uses for the chat dock). Surface: a row on /settings and a command-menu entry so the toggle is reachable both ways. Declared consequential today: ApprovalsPage.tsx:1941 `a`, :1951 `d`, :1961 `x`; NotificationsPage.tsx:413 `a`; IssuesPage.tsx:272,285 `a`.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Add the flag and the runtime gate with the setting defaulting to on — no behavior change, pure structure. 2) Mark the six existing consequential verbs and make the field required on ListTriageVerb (compile-error enforcement across the consumers). 3) Add the settings row, the command-menu entry, and the '?' sheet's gated-state rendering.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy path: setting on → today's behavior, plus the '?' sheet says which keys commit. Setting off → j/k and every navigation chord still work; a/d/x are inert and the sheet says why. Failure: localStorage unavailable → defaults to on (matching Shell.tsx:22-28's best-effort read), so the feature never silently disarms navigation. Concurrency: the setting is read through the same module store the shortcut snapshot uses, so a toggle takes effect without remount. Idempotence: toggling is a pure boolean write. Rollback: the gate is one boolean check; reverting restores today's behavior with the flags harmlessly present.
moves.verification: use-register-shortcut.test.tsx: a consequential binding does not fire with the setting off and does fire with it on; a non-consequential binding fires in both states; the hint entries expose the gated state. A type-level test (or the compile itself) that a ListTriageVerb without `consequential` does not build. An ApprovalsPage test asserting `d` performs no mutation with the setting off while `j`/`k` still move the cursor — the exact separation the SC asks for.

audits.jarvis_gap: A JARVIS you carry answers on the device in your pocket: the butler pushes a consequential clause to Telegram, you tap, and the decision is the first thing under your thumb, sized for a thumb, titled with what it is, decidable in one tap with the evidence one scroll away. Today the fleet is desktop-only in fact while claiming a phone contract on paper. Measured live at 390x664 against the running dev API across 38 routes: 3,404 of 3,574 in-main interactive targets (95.2%) fall below the product's own written 44x44 floor, 20 of 38 routes render the browser/home-screen title as the literal string "frontend", and both routes the backend actually mints into Telegram are non-functional — /secrets?focus=u:<provider> (the OAuth return route, oauth.py:42) renders the credential page in a 46px-wide column beside a 296px hardcoded spine, and /approvals/<id> (notifications.py:98) puts the dossier the link exists for 1,792px below the fold of a 608px scroll viewport with no scroll-into-view and no focus move. The Viewport and Modality Contract that would forbid all of this has sat in an unarchived openspec change directory since 2026-09-03 and never entered openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md, so there is no normative text and no CI seam holding anything. Every phone-aware primitive the repo owns (useMediaQuery, useVisualViewportHeight, Tip, the single 320px e2e assertion) was built exactly once for exactly one caller and never generalized. The gap is not polish: the phone modality has no runtime representation at all. Responsive branching is CSS-class-only, which can restyle a layout but can never change what a surface composes — which is precisely what /secrets and /approvals/:id need.
audits.ideal: On a phone the dashboard is a different composition of the same truths, not a shrunken desktop. A device band is a runtime value every surface can ask for, so an entry route can render a different tree — /approvals/:id opens with the dossier under the thumb and the queue collapsed to a "7 more waiting" disclosure; /secrets?focus= opens on the credential page itself with a back-to-index affordance, never a spine beside a 46px sliver. Every backend-minted URL is a tested contract: the phone Playwright project walks the exact strings notifications.py and oauth.py produce and asserts the named resource is inside the first viewport and holds focus. Under (pointer: coarse) every verb is at least 44x44 by primitive, not by hand, with a frozen allowlist for genuinely dense grids that can only shrink. No fact is hover-only: Tip taps as well as hovers, and a lint guard with a frozen baseline makes the 94 remaining raw title= attributes a debt that cannot grow. Dialogs are bounded in dvh with internal scroll and a bottom-sheet posture at the phone band, so the confirm button is always reachable above the home indicator. Every route names itself from the router's own capability registry, so the tab-switcher card and the home-screen icon say what the surface is. One file owns the gutter. And the contract that says all of this lives in openspec/specs/, enforced by a lint script and a phone e2e budget in the frontend-e2e CI job, so the floor is a ratchet rather than a paragraph.
audits.live_verification: Live-confirmed READ-SIDE ONLY. The dev API (http://127.0.0.1:42200) was up; no frontend server was running, so I built the current main tree (npx vite build --outDir <scratchpad>/dist --emptyOutDir, exit 0, after npm ci because frontend/node_modules was empty) and served it from a scratchpad static server that proxies /api to 42200 and hard-rejects every non-GET/HEAD with 405. Playwright (chromium, devices['iPhone 12'] = 390x664, coarse pointer, no hover) crawled 38 static routes plus the three minted deep links, with a route interceptor that aborts any non-GET/HEAD request, so no write could reach the stack. Measurements taken in-page: getBoundingClientRect over every interactive element and every leaf inside #main-content, computed gridTemplateColumns of the secrets book body, dossier offsetTop against main scrollTop/clientHeight/scrollHeight, document.title, document.activeElement, and a screenshot of /secrets?focus=c:cli-auth/codex that I read. Everything else is source-confirmed by reading the decisive code: primitive class strings (button.tsx, dialog.tsx, alert-dialog.tsx, select.tsx, dropdown-menu.tsx, tip.tsx, page.tsx, Shell.tsx), breakpoint-prefix and title=/Tooltip/Tip counts by grep over non-test .tsx, playwright.config.ts projects, the openspec spec vs change directories, and the backend URL minters. findings.title: The Dialog primitive has no height ceiling: 38 of 43 dialogs can put their own confirm button off a phone screen
findings.detail: DialogContent is fixed top-[50%] left-[50%] translate-y-[-50%] with a width cap and no max-height and no overflow. A position:fixed box taller than the viewport cannot be scrolled by the page, so both ends become unreachable. AlertDialogContent carries the identical class shape. Of 43 non-test <DialogContent> call sites only 5 set a max-h, and all 5 express it in `vh`, which on mobile browsers measures the largest viewport including the collapsible URL bar — an 85vh dialog is roughly 100% of what is actually visible. By contrast the Select and DropdownMenu primitives already bound themselves with Radix's --radix-*-content-available-height: the fix exists in this codebase and was never pushed into the two primitives that hold the long forms (medication, meal, measurement, symptom and condition trackers, schedule form, rule editor, create-entity). PR #4042 removes only Shell's h-screen and SettingsModelsPage's min-h-screen; the other 10 raw `vh` sites survive it and no guard is added.

moves.title: Device band as a runtime value, and a phone posture for the two routes the backend actually mints
moves.why: vision.md's success markers are about the owner being served wherever they are; purpose-and-single-pane.md makes the dashboard the one operational pane. The north star's clause 'every consequential clause is a door on an unbroken signal-to-session-to-evidence spine' fails at the last hop when the door opens onto a 46px column (DirectionPassport.tsx:507) or 1,792px above the dossier (ApprovalsPage.tsx:2092). The contract's band clause cannot be honored by CSS prefixes, because these two surfaces must compose differently, not merely restyle. Owner payoff: a Telegram approval push or an OAuth re-auth return lands on the decision itself, readable and actionable, at the moment it matters.
moves.manifesto: dashboard-design-language § Viewport and Modality Contract (currently unlanded — see the archival move), plus the amendment it implies: a surface MAY change what it composes at the phone band, not merely how it looks. Respects Switchboard/Messenger ownership of the minted URLs (notifications.py:98, oauth.py:42) by consuming, not changing, them.
moves.integration_points: New frontend/src/hooks/use-device-band.ts exporting useDeviceBand(): 'phone'|'tablet'|'desktop' from the three canonical queries, generalizing the single-consumer frontend/src/hooks/use-media-query.ts:11; frontend/src/layouts/RootLayout.tsx:27,84 stops hand-rolling '(min-width: 1280px)' and asks for a band. New frontend/src/hooks/use-entry-focus.ts: when a route resolves a resource from params or ?focus=, on the phone band it scrolls the owning pane into view and moves focus to it. Consumers: frontend/src/components/secrets/passport/DirectionPassport.tsx:505-508 (phone renders spine XOR page — page whenever ?focus= resolves, with an explicit back-to-index control) and frontend/src/pages/ApprovalsPage.tsx:2092-2096 (phone with :id renders the Dossier first, rail collapsed to an 'N more waiting' disclosure). No API, schema or backend change.
moves.slice_plan: S1 use-device-band + use-entry-focus with unit tests and one adopter (RootLayout's chat-dock threshold moves onto the band). S2 DirectionPassport phone posture. S3 ApprovalsPage phone dossier-first posture. S4 sweep the remaining hardcoded two-pane composers; frontend/src/pages/ChatPage.tsx:189 already does this correctly and is the exemplar to copy.
moves.behavior_matrix: Happy: phone + :id or ?focus= → the named resource is the first thing rendered and holds focus; desktop unchanged pixel-for-pixel. Unresolvable id → the index posture with an honest 'that credential/approval is no longer listed' note, never a blank sliver. Band change mid-session (rotation, desktop resize) → posture switches without remounting the query, no double fetch. Concurrency: a background refetch that removes the focused row falls back to the index posture rather than an empty pane. Idempotence: entry focus fires once per resource id, not on every render. Rollback: the hook returns 'desktop' when matchMedia is unavailable, so jsdom/SSR/older browsers keep today's behavior exactly.
moves.verification: New frontend/tests/e2e/phone-entry-routes.spec.ts under the phone Playwright project (devices['iPhone 12'], real coarse pointer): for /approvals/<id> assert the dossier's bounding box intersects the initial viewport and document.activeElement is inside it; for /secrets?focus=u:<provider> assert the credential pane's width is at least 90% of the viewport. Unit tests for use-device-band at the 767/768/1023/1024 edges. The tested URLs are asserted against the backend minters so a change to notifications.py:98 or oauth.py:42 breaks the test rather than the owner.

moves.title: Bound the Dialog primitive to the dynamic viewport, give it a phone posture, and ban raw vh
moves.why: 38 of 43 dialogs can render their own confirm button off a phone screen because DialogContent (dialog.tsx:63) and AlertDialogContent (alert-dialog.tsx:52) set no max-height on a position:fixed centered box, which is unreachable by scrolling. Select and DropdownMenu already solve this with the Radix available-height variable — the fix exists in the codebase and was never pushed into the primitives that hold the forms. audits.jarvis_gap: Run 12 already tiered this surface solid on the strength of its honesty flags (heartbeat_unavailable, schema_unreachable, push_outcome/push_failed) and its keyboard triage coverage; that verdict still holds. What is new this run is a crack in exactly the mechanism run 12 praised: the prepared-actions feature (#4120) shipped a real 'origin=prepared' distinction in the domain model (a proactive draft parked by an insight-scan producer, deliberately never pushed to the owner) but the field never reaches either of the two response shapes the owner actually reads -- ApprovalSummary (the flat list backing ApprovalsPage's queue and, via the same shape, the dashboard's 'needs me' rail) and ApprovalDetail (the dossier opened on click) both omit `origin` entirely, and the frontend's generated ApprovalAction type has no such field at all. Because `_push_failed()` is origin-blind (it flags every still-pending action whose push_outcome is null or 'failed', and a prepared action's push_outcome is null by design, forever), every prepared draft renders with the same 'push_failed' banner text ('...was never attempted') built for bu-mda0r's original still-unresolved-alarm use case: a genuinely undelivered, time-sensitive approval the owner doesn't know exists. The ideal version of this journey keeps that alarm meaningful -- a prepared draft shows a calm 'proactive draft, browse at your leisure' badge sourced from `origin`, and the red 'push failed' treatment is reserved for `origin IS NULL` rows only, so the one banner the north star depends on ('failure never impersonates health') isn't itself diluted into crying wolf over a working-as-designed feature.

audits.ideal: One Autonomy view per butler composes permissions, tool exposure/core groups, model tier, and a per-butler spend ceiling as a single reviewable, reason-gated, cost-previewed decision; every write on that view lands a semantically-labeled audit row drawn from a registry that cannot silently drift stale, so the default privileged audit filter is guaranteed complete rather than hand-maintained; the owner opens one door, sees current-state-plus-consequence for all four levers together, confirms once, and can later filter the audit trail to that one butler and see every lever that moved, by whom, and what it has cost since -- with no page ever asking the owner to memorize which of several disconnected editors owns which capability.
audits.jarvis_gap: Run 12 already established that the ceiling/permission/rule half of this surface is gated-and-audited while the model-tier-override half is not; this run's deeper look at the audit filter mechanism shows the defect is worse and more systemic than "no audit call" -- a generic safety-net middleware DOES fire for every mutating request including model-overrides and runtime-config PATCHes, but the hand-maintained "privileged" allowlist regex that the Audit Log page defaults to (and that the journey's own words, "see afterwards exactly what changed", depend on) does not include either action family, so even a genuinely audited, genuinely consequential autonomy-widening edit (tool_exposure_policy, core_groups) is invisible by default and only surfaces if the owner already knows to disable the noise filter and guess the exact literal method+path string. Separately, the journey's "widen a permission" verb has no single door: the enforced permissions matrix (5 fixed capabilities) and the tool-exposure/core-groups runtime-config editor are two disjoint autonomy-control surfaces with no cross-link, no shared reason-gate, and no shared audit visibility, even though both are "give this butler more capability" actions the journey treats as one motion.

findings.title: The 'privileged' audit-log default filter excludes runtime_config_patch entirely, hiding tool_exposure_policy/core_groups autonomy changes
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/audit.py:86-98 _PRIVILEGED_CONSEQUENCE_SQL only matches action LIKE 'approval.%'/'approvals.policy'/'model.%'/'permission.%'/'data.%'/'webhook.%'/'spend.%'/credential-lifecycle-actions/result='error'. src/butlers/api/routers/runtime_config.py:249-256 emits its explicit audit row with operation="runtime_config_patch" (no dot-prefixed family match). frontend/src/pages/AuditLogPage.tsx:80-111 defaults every load to kind=privileged (the noise=all toggle is required to see anything else), and its action-filter placeholder text ('e.g. model.priority', AuditLogPage.tsx:301) gives the owner no hint that 'runtime_config_patch' is even a valid search term. Live-confirmed: GET /api/audit-log (default, no kind param) returns only heartbeat/verify rows in the last 100.
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: audit-completeness allowlist drift -- a real, explicitly-written audit row exists but the filter built specifically to surface consequential rows was never updated for a newer consequential action family, so the trust-bearing default view silently omits it (the gate fires correctly; the display discards it).

findings.title: Generic DashboardAuditMiddleware safety-net row for model-tier overrides is also invisible under the default privileged filter -- refines run12's 'zero audit trail' finding with the actual mechanism
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/dashboard_audit_middleware.py:108-121,178-198: every PUT/PATCH/POST/DELETE under /api/ (except /health prefixes) gets an unconditional emit_dashboard_audit with operation=f"{method} {path}", so a PUT to /api/butlers/{name}/model-overrides DOES produce a row -- contradicting a literal reading of run12's 'zero audit trail' claim. But that operation string is 'PUT /api/butlers/{name}/model-overrides', which does not start with 'model.' and so also fails audit.py:86-98's allowlist; the row is written but structurally unreachable from the default filtered view. Live-confirmed: GET /api/butlers/finance/model-overrides is empty and GET /api/audit-log?action=model-overrides returns total:0 (no override has ever been set in this environment, so no such row exists to point at directly); the code path guarantees one would be created and would fail the privileged predicate.
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: same family as the finding above -- the true defect is an audit-filter completeness gap, not (only) a missing audit.append call; corrects run12's root-cause attribution rather than restating it.

findings.title: 'Widen a permission' has two disjoint control surfaces with no cross-link and inconsistent consequence-gating
findings.evidence: The enforced permissions matrix is a closed vocabulary of 5 capabilities (src/butlers/core/permissions.py:68-73: calendar.write, cross_butler, email.send, notify, spawn), edited only on frontend/src/pages/SettingsPermissionsPage.tsx with a mandatory non-empty reason. tool_exposure_policy and core_groups -- both genuine autonomy grants (auto tool discovery vs eager_filtered; which core tool groups a butler can call at all) -- live only in frontend/src/components/butler-detail/RuntimeConfigCard.tsx (rendered from ButlerConfigTab.tsx on the Butler Detail page, not /settings). Grep of SettingsPermissionsPage.tsx confirms zero references to tool_exposure_policy/core_groups/runtime-config. RuntimeConfigCard.tsx's RuntimeConfigPatch model has no reason field (runtime_config.py:78-84) and Save (RuntimeConfigCard.tsx:126-137) fires the PATCH immediately with no confirm step, unlike the permissions matrix's required-reason gate.
findings.taxonomy_shape: NEW: one owner intent ('give this butler more autonomy') implemented as two unlinked, inconsistently-gated control planes -- a surface-level fragmentation distinct from run12's model-tier/ceiling findings and from the sibling deep-design agent's object-model scope (no cross-link exists today regardless of what the object model becomes).

themes.title: The frozen seed: runtime_config core_groups overrides git, so butlers lose tools they declare
themes.detail: runtime_config.py seed_if_empty (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) captured each butler's core_groups on 2026-04-07 and has governed ever since; daemon.py:1251-1282 reads the row, not butler.toml. Finance and Relationship therefore expose zero cross-butler tools, Switchboard never registers open_case on the only role that may write fleet cases, and Relationship runs 26 of its 66 tools. Four independent lenses (cross-butler, relationship, situation-archetypes, knowledge-graph) each rediscovered the same row. The fix is one reconciliation with an audit receipt, not four.

themes.title: Substrate shipped, consumer never (run-12 theme, now the dominant shape)
themes.detail: Fleet cases (read API, six tools, lapse sweep, zero frontend lines, zero cases), prepared actions (origin NULL on all 50 recent rows, one producer), task continuity (zero adopters), backfill (jobs table, two tools, six REST endpoints, no door), graph backfills (three, no caller), reconcile_day verdicts (discarded), review-card scheduler (zero schedules ever), graph_coverage (no consumer), blind-spot registry (one module), entity_graph_walk (zero invocations across 12 schemas).
